A row plays through stock's `player_start_queue` (`0x520df0`, which `mclSetPlayPos`es and starts the player) and closes the page. **Playing Next.** Play Next's list is queue indices in play order, at most 64 (`PEND_LIMIT`); Play Next past that drops the list's last entry, Play Last (the hold menu's, `qm_apply` with 2, in place of stock's Add to Queue) adds nothing more to it. Under advanced play Play Next's tracks go to pos+1 and the list's front, Play Last's to the queue's end and the list's end. Outside it, under List or Repeat All, the list is the run of rows right after the playing one (`plain_follow`): Play Next's go to pos+1 and start it, Play Last's to its end (pos+1+its length); a track played from it leaves it, and anything else (Previous, a pick elsewhere, a stock edit, another mode) ends it, its songs playing where they stand. ponytail: the plain snapshot keeps no run, so a restart forgets which songs were queued. Up Next's bump (a tap on a queued row's arrow, or a Play/Pause hold on it: `ringnav_keylong`'s `un_hold`) and its lift (Center held, the wheel, Center) move an entry within the list (`playback_next_move`): under advanced play only the list's order changes, so the queue, its indices, the order and every album or folder group stay as they were; outside it the row moves among the run's rows (`swap_rows`), and stock's shuffle pool, last pick, preload and `back_to` follow (`stock_remap`). Clear (`playback_next_clear`) takes the list's songs out of the queue: the rows kept close up in order, the others go last and are popped (`deque_pop_back`, which frees their strings), stock's indices and the position follow, and advanced play follows the queue by identity (`follow_queue`). The gapless preload is closed when the next track changes. Nothing toasts. A Play/Pause hold on a row of the rest of the queue does nothing. Playing one takes its order entry to the cursor, as a Shuffle Songs pick does (`commit`'s `play_now`). ponytail: a row from the next pass (Repeat All) still plays in that pass too. Its hook (`ringnav_start_queue`, `patch/playback.c`) commits the pick in advanced play first, so Previous returns to it. Under Shuffle Songs it goes through Play Next's path, moving it right after the cursor, so the order carries on after it: the pick does not play again later in the pass, and the tracks it jumped stay up next. An ordered queue (or Shuffle Albums, Folders, a category) moves the cursor to it, so the tracks after it follow. A pick inside a pending Play Next takes only its entry off the list; the rest stay pending. Stock's own View Queue delete under advanced play is followed on the UI thread (`follow_queue`: each UI pass, a View Queue row, and Next, Previous or a preload when they run there): `rebuild` keeps each entry's identity (its path's hash and CUE start, `ids`), so the entries left keep their seen marks, history and Play Next places, shifted down as `playback_insert` shifts them up, and the order is drawn again over them as an insert's is. The playing entry deleted, stock's position names the one after it, which joins the history, so Previous goes back to the track before the deleted one; with none after it (the last row), Previous goes there too and Next ends the queue. A size change that isn't a deletion takes a new order as a new load gets, Play Next and the history dropped. Off the UI thread (headset keys, a natural change) a resized queue takes stock's way for that one Next or Previous, and the next UI pass follows. ponytail: only a size change is seen (a delete always makes one); a same-size swap would need the identities compared every pass. Stock Shuffle draws each next track at random, so it has no order to list: Shuffle Songs and a collection's Shuffle save stock's Shuffle mode, then hand the loaded queue to advanced Shuffle Songs with Repeat All (`playback_shuffle`). View Queue does the same on a stock Shuffle chosen elsewhere (Now Playing's mode button; `playback_listable`, only while advanced play is off), then opens Up Next, a Play Next stock's Shuffle was holding (`qm_forced`) moved to the front of the pending list; ponytail: the order is fresh, so songs stock's shuffle already played can come round again. On Now Playing's hold menu a last row, More…, sends Now Playing's own `img_more` a click (stock's handler opens `playermore_page`), only while that page is open (`np_more`). Playlist add mode 2 uses the playing queue; its existing row click handlers are guarded again before the stock callback, with the captured row selected. Browsing state is independent.

## Home carousel

Home is an ordinary list ([ipod.md](ipod.md#home)) that bumps and wraps like a ring list. In Home: Carousel (below) the carousel uses `HOME_SLIDE_MS` (200 ms) for isolated ticks and `HOME_FAST_SLIDE_MS` (120 ms) when consecutive same-direction ticks arrive at most `HOME_FAST_WINDOW_MS` (200 ms) apart. There is no extra home input gate; stock filtering and audible ticks stay stock-controlled. Each accepted tick retargets one animator from its live offset, extending the intended destination by one icon. Reversal discards that destination and heads toward the adjacent card in the new direction at normal speed. Stock completion handles wrapping and card selection; center confirmation follows the intended final icon. Touch, native clicks, center presses, leaving home and unavailable navigation reset speed tracking; wheel input cancels pending center confirmation. Allocation failure settles on the requested icon without retaining an animator.

### Home: Carousel

Display's Home: Carousel (`IPOD/HOME=2`) shows stock's carousel in place of Home's lists. `ipod_home` (`tools/ipod.py`) keeps stock's `slide_menu` and its `img_left`/`img_right` arrows in `home_page.bin`, after the lists, hidden and insensitive, with clones of the Local Music card for Coverflow and the Shortcut (`home_card`). Stock binds the stock cards and arrows by name; `coverflow_home` binds the carousel's own Coverflow and Shortcut images, as `widget_lookup` from the window finds the lists' rows first. `coverflow_home_layout` swaps the carousel and the lists at runtime (`home_show`: visible and sensitive together, since hidden widgets keep their taps), hides the art, and on leaving Carousel shows the main list. The wheel, Center and touch take the carousel path above (`home_step`); Return keeps stock's. The cards' art (stock's, and `assets/icons/menu_coverflow*` and `menu_rockbox*`) keeps its own colors: the image hook leaves every `menu_*` image but the white arrows (`menu_left`, `menu_right`, which flip in Light Mode as other glyphs do) alone, so no Theme, accent or Light Mode reaches the cards. ponytail: the Shortcut card stays when Home's Shortcut row hides (Shortcut: Rockbox with no Rockbox on the card; its tap toasts that) and under Shortcut: None, where it names and opens the default (`shortcut_target`): `slide_menu` lays out hidden cards too, so leaving it out would mean removing and re-adding the clone with the setting. `IPOD/SHORTCUT` 11 is None, after Groovebox, so every stored value keeps its meaning; a build before 1.8.2 reads 11 as out of range, no choice, and shows the row, and this build reads 12 and up the same way.

## Coverflow

Coverflow (`patch/coverflow.c`) follows Rockbox PictureFlow: albums and tracks come from the stock library queries, never from tags, and the payload owns only a thumbnail cache. Audit (V1.32, 2026-09-28; the addresses are V1.36's, carried by `tools/rebase.py`); every entry point is exported, and the builder pins the executable through the stock ZIP's SHA-256:

| Stock entry                                       | Address                 | Size      | Prologue                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `home_page_init` (hook)                           | `0x534b6c`              | 1028      | `50001c3c3c309c2721e09903`                              |
| `getAllAlbum`                                     | `0x507a20`              | 800       | `53001c3c109e9c2721e09903`                              |
| `getMusicByAlbum`                                 | `0x50a348`              | 480       | `52001c3ce8749c2721e09903`                              |
| `toolsThumbSpecCover`                             | `0x5d71a8`              | 264       | `46001c3c70279c2721e09903`                              |
| `toolsGetAlbumCover`                              | `0x5d709c`              | 268       | `46001c3c7c289c2721e09903`                              |
| `window_create`                                   | `0x67d824`              | 72        | `3c001c3c4cca9c2721e09903`                              |
| `widget_factory` / `widget_factory_create_widget` | `0x67a218` / `0x67a4b4` | 24 / 188  | `3c001c3c58009c2721e09903` / `3c001c3cbcfd9c2721e09903` |
| `image_create` / `image_set_draw_type`            | `0x627b8c` / `0x62810c` | 112 / 116 | `41001c3cc41f9c2721e09903` / `41001c3c441a9c2721e09903` |
| `image_base_set_image`                            | `0x656d04`              | 228       | `3e001c3c2c359c2721e09903`                              |
| `widget_load_image` / `widget_unload_image`       | `0x66f75c` / `0x66fdf4` | 196 / 124 | `3d001c3cd4aa9c2721e09903` / `3d001c3c3ca49c2721e09903` |
| `bitmap_create_ex` / `bitmap_destroy`             | `0x642f34` / `0x642ae4` | 248 / 256 | `3f001c3cfc729c2721e09903` / `3f001c3c4c779c2721e09903` |
| `bitmap_lock_buffer_for_read` / `_for_write`      | `0x643570` / `0x6435e8` | 120 / 120 | `3f001c3cc06c9c2721e09903` / `3f001c3c486c9c2721e09903` |
| `bitmap_unlock_buffer` / `bitmap_get_line_length` | `0x643660` / `0x64302c` | 60 / 88   | `3f001c3cd06b9c2721e09903` / `3f001c3c04729c2721e09903` |
| `canvas_draw_image`                               | `0x6487c4`              | 260       | `3f001c3c6c1a9c2721e09903`                              |
| `slide_menu_set_spacer` / `widget_to_local`       | `0x608270` / `0x66df24` | 116 / 220 | `43001c3ce0189c2721e09903` / `3d001c3c0cc39c2721e09903` |

Data: `tools_pdeq_directory` (`0xa3a8a0`, 4), `parse_cover_mutex` (`0xa4bc28`, 24) and `g_playcover_mutex` (`0xa4db88`, 24) are size-checked `CONTEXT_DATA`; the scan thread handle `0xa3b0c8` and done flag `0xa3b0c4` have no symbol (`offsets.inc`).

**Albums.** `load_localclass_list(0xf003)` (`0x51357c`) is `getAllAlbum()` followed by `deque_assign(*p_deque_showlist, *tools_pdeq_directory)`, so the payload calls `getAllAlbum` itself through `staged`, into a deque of its own: no private state, and a Local Music page underneath keeps its showlist. `getAllAlbum` runs `select id,album,songer,fileurl from songtable group by album COLLATE NOCASE` on `/mnt/data/database.db` through `toolsQueryDbTable` (`0x5dad14`: the lazily opened shared handle at `0xa50114`, `deque_clear`, `sqlite3_exec`, then `algo_sort_if` with the stock comparator). Its row callback (`0x506e94`) skips empty albums and fills `+0` id, `+0x10/+0x14` album, `+0x18/+0x20` artist and `+0xc` the group's `fileurl`, which is the first-track path the art build uses. When any album exists it then appends an "Unknown Album" row (id -1, no path). It returns the query count: -1 without a database, 0 when empty. That grouping is by name alone (stock's Albums list shares it), so Coverflow then runs `ALBUM_SQL`, the same columns plus `albumsonger`, grouped by album, then album artist, or for songs without one the folder (`rtrim(fileurl, replace(fileurl, '/', ''))`), through `split_row`: `album_row` on the first four columns, then the album artist into `+0x24` (`REC_ALBUM_ARTIST`), which the `stSongInfo` copy (`0x5c65ac`) duplicates. An album's path, which its art comes from, is the song `ALBUM_TRACK` picks: the lowest disc, then track, then path, each number padded to four digits, a missing one taken as 0 and one outside 0-9999 (a date as the track, or -1) as its bound, so the prefixes stay four digits and the path whole. A bare `fileurl` was whichever row SQLite read last, so an album whose songs carry different covers showed a random one. Covers already made from another song stay until **Refresh Coverflow** (`coverflow_refresh_art`), which empties Coverflow's cache and stock's `.sldp` (Library's album covers, made once per name, which otherwise only a settings reset, `init_usersetting`, clears) and drops AWTK's cached bitmaps, as the cover thread writes the same names again. Each stock row is replaced in place by its name's rows (`split`), one per `album_cmp` album, so same-named albums by different artists are separate covers with separate art keys; `album_cmp` tells albums apart the same way everywhere else (tracks, Sort ranks, play counts, playback's album groups). Its folder fallback takes a trailing disc folder (`CD1`, `Disc 2`, `Disk_03`: cd/disc/disk, an optional space, `_` or `-`, digits) as its parent, so an untagged multi-disc album is one; the SQL keeps disc folders apart and `split` merges them. Shuffle Folders (`folder_cmp`) keeps each folder apart. The stock Albums list gets the same split (`ringnav_localclass`), and a row's album page (`load_album_detaillist`, hooked to keep the row) and resume (`memeory_startplayer`'s 0xff10 rebuild) keep only that album's songs from `getMusicByAlbum`. Its art cache, `/mnt/mmc/.sldp/<md5 of the name>0.jpg`, adds the album artist, else the album folder, to a name that adjacent rows share (`art_key`): the row renderer (`0x4a52bc`), the page's `albumcoverinfo_init` cover tasks the art thread hashes, and the album page's big cover (`0x4a910c`). An artist's albums tab (`load_localartist_list(1)`, hooked) groups by name too, and has one row of a name another artist shares, so adjacency can't tell: `ringnav_artist_list` splits a copy of the tab as Albums is and gives each row its album's `art_key`, the same-named album in its folder, else with the row's artist as album artist. Its renderer (`0x4adb4c`, the row in `$s2`) and three `albumcoverinfo_init` calls (Album tab entry `0x4aeb70`, page return `0x4b07f0`, which V1.32 had twice, init `0x4b12ac`) use those keys, and the album page's big cover follows its cover task as before. Local art completion (`0x4f84c0`) passes the worker's copied key (`sp + 0x1688`) to `ringnav_cover_done`; the folder-cover path, which branched to the call itself (`0x4f94fc`), now enters one word earlier so it passes the key too: under `aclist_mutex`, it sets the small/big ready flag only if that row still has the key. A job finishing after navigation rebuilt the list therefore cannot mark a different album ready and make later requests skip its missing cover. When `rename_covers` changes a row's key, it clears both ready flags under the same lock, including a completion arriving between stock initialization and renaming. The grids' scroll start (`0x14e`: `0x4ace30` an artist's albums, `0x4a3910` Library Albums) set the worker's shared `albumcover_taskstate` to 2, which it sleeps through, and their scroll end resumed it (`local_albumcover_task`) only when the first row in view changed; a wheel tick within the same rows, or the return to a scrolled grid (its `scroll_view_set_offset` sends `0x14e` alone), left every grid without art until reboot. Library Songs (`music_table_client`, scroll start `0x4a9c00`) did the same, so returning to a scrolled Songs list showed every row's placeholder until the wheel moved. All three stores are `nop` (`COVER_PAUSE`): the worker keeps going, and each scroll end replaces its queue as before. An artist's albums scroll end (`0x4b0adc`) took its first row as `yoffset / 256 * 3`, though its rows are 160 px as Library Albums divides; it divides by 160 (`ARTIST_COVER_ROW`), so the nine covers it requests, and the renderer (`0x4adae0`) draws, are the ones in view. Coverflow keeps this order and shows the Unknown row with the placeholder, only when its card's query, `getMusicByAlbum(NULL)`, finds a song (`drop_unknown`, as [Unknown rows](#unknown-rows)): before V8.6 it showed even with every song tagged.

The copy outlives the page, because the query is the slow part of an open: `toolsQueryDbTable` sorts with a stock comparator (`0x5cd188`) that runs `utf8_to_pinyin` on both names, four `snprintf`s and several `memset`s per comparison. Only `scanAllMusicFile`, `scanSpecFolder` and `deleteMusicFromMusicDb` write `songtable` (every other `toolsInsert/Delete/UpdateDbTable` caller writes the favorites, playlist and play-record tables); their hooks step a generation before and after stock runs, and an open queries again only when the generation moved since the list was taken, or on Refresh. A list taken while a writer runs is never kept, and an empty or refused result is not kept at all. **Opening.** A cold open (none kept, or the generation moved) runs that query with Home still up, in three steps (`query_step`): `getAllAlbum`, then `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`'s grouping, then `split` and `music_albums` on its rows; the page opens after the last, as a warm open does at once. Each step runs on a thread of its own while the UI thread waits for it (`step_turning`, as `name_order.c` sorts), so only that thread touches the library and its staging pointer meanwhile. Once the open has taken `OPEN_SPIN_MS / 2` (75 ms), the selected row's chevron is the spinner (`coverflow_spinner`, drawn by `paint_chevrons` through `spinner_icon` on a `CHEV_ICON` theme, OLED; its eight frames are `tools/art.py`'s `spinner`): within a step the waiting UI thread repaints its box at each spoke itself (`spinner_turn`, then `ringnav_wm_paint`), so it turns through `getAllAlbum`'s seconds on a large library, and each further step waits for a main-loop pass (`open_step`), so Home takes input between them; meanwhile `ringnav_input` drops keys, wheel ticks and touches (`coverflow_wait_input`), Return's release giving the open up (`open_end`), as does any other window over Home. Half of 150 ms is the cue because what follows `getAllAlbum` costs at least half as much again: in the emulator (QEMU, 2,018 albums of 20,106 songs) `getAllAlbum` took 110–380 ms and the rest of the query 290–690 ms, and on a Q2 with 6,175 albums `getAllAlbum` was 524 ms of an 878 ms open ([server-library](server-library.md)). The emulator's 18-album card opens cold in under 100 ms and never shows it. ponytail: the spinner moves between steps, not within one: each query holds the UI thread for its whole statement and stock's sort, and demo imports no `sqlite3_progress_handler` to paint from inside them (an import through `sqlite3_exec`'s GOT entry and the rebuilt library's offset, as `localtime_r` is reached, would let it turn smoothly). Cover Flow's own open groups the library once, not twice: `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`'s rows split `getAllAlbum`'s names as `ALBUM_SQL`'s would, since a name's `ALBUM_SQL` rows are its music rows and more (the `WHERE` drops songs, never a group's key), and `music_albums` drops the more; a name with no music keeps its stock row, which `music_albums` drops as it would that name's `ALBUM_SQL` rows. `split_by` leaves the grouping's Unknown rows (`REC_ID` -1, `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`'s untagged songs) out of the names, so an album tagged "Unknown Album" is split as before. That cut the emulator's cold open (press to the covers' first frame) at 2,018 albums from 1,230–1,340 ms to 860–1,080 ms, the two builds alternated across reboots (784–907 ms to 470–560 ms on a quieter host), and with Local + Server's 834 more albums from 1,250–1,290 ms to 970–1,090 ms; a warm open, 40–140 ms, is unchanged. The Albums list (`coverflow_split`) and the rated albums still split with `ALBUM_SQL`.

**Folder tag refresh.** Scan specified folders keeps stock's recursive scan and cancellation, but its `toolsCheckItemExist` call (`0x5dc4d8`) goes through `ringnav_scan_refresh`: existing `songtable` rows re-read tags and update in place, matching filename, full path and CUE start/end. IDs, creation time and song count stay intact; a file the library doesn't have yet is stock's to add, at any count. CUE entries use the freshly parsed CUE metadata; ordinary files use `toolsGetMusicInfo`, including the FLAC album-artist fallback, after checking TagLib can read them. Tag validation and refresh disable TagLib audio-property reads, so rescanning existing tags does not probe the audio duration. The title’s stock pinyin initial is refreshed too. SQL text is bounded and quotes apostrophes; an unreadable tag leaves the existing row intact. The existing scan writer hooks invalidate cached album groups. New songs keep stock's insert path. Update Local Music drops `songtable` (`scanAllMusicFile`'s second argument is `toolsInitDatabase`'s drop flag) and dates every song again from `toolsGetFileCreateTime` (`0x5d0954`): `st_ctime` on FAT32, the directory entry's creation time, but the file's `st_atime` when `getDiskMemoryInfoAndSetFormat`'s format byte says exFAT or NTFS, where stat has no creation time and a fresh copy's access time stood in for it. The update's own tag reads move it (relatime, once a day), so each full update dated the whole library to its last update or play, and `getAllRecentAddRecord`'s `order by time_create desc limit 100` (Library → Recently Added; Coverflow's Recently Added sort reads the same column) filled with those songs, the album added that day lost among them (#170, #188). `ringnav_file_created` hooks the function: `statx` with `STATX_BTIME` (`ringnav_statx`, the o32 syscall; demo imports none) reports the creation stamp the exFAT directory entry keeps, which reads never move (stock's 5.10.21 kernel has the mainline driver, which fills it), so every full update dates the library the same way; the first one on this version replaces the dates 1.6.1–1.6.3 kept and repairs those lost before them. Windows and Linux stamp a copy with the time of copying; a Mac keeps the file's own creation date. A file whose filesystem reports no stamp, or a failed call, takes stock's date (the stock kernel mounts no NTFS, so only exFAT takes the access-time path). 1.6.1's keyed `ringnav_added` copy of `time_create` across the drop is gone; one left by an update interrupted on 1.6.1–1.6.3 stays in the database, unused. The query hook keeps that `ORDER BY` outside its `songtable` subquery.

**Scan Folders' rows.** Stock's row click (`0x53f9b4`) ticks the row for a tap left of x 81 and opens the folder for one past it. The list holds folders only, so `specfolder_enter` refuses a folder with none inside, and stock answered "Folder not found" (`msg_notfolder`, #254), which left no way to reach an album's folder without knowing the column is there. `ringnav_specfolder_click` (`patch/scan_folders.c`) asks stock's `toolsLoadDirectory` and `toolsCheckTypeDeque` first, the same check, so a tap on such a folder moves to x 0 and stock ticks it; Center's click already arrives at x 0. Limits: a folder that does open is listed twice on the tap, and a folder holding only folders stock hides (`.Trashes`, `System Volume Information` and the like) ticks rather than failing. Stock's `unselect` ring is emptied (`ringnav_image_add`), so the tick column shows nothing on a row until it is ticked.

**Indexes.** Stock's `songtable` has only its primary key, so `getMusicByAlbum` (`album like '%s'`: an album's page, Go to Album, an artist's All albums card, and twice for each album of Era's Play All), `toolsCheckItemExist` and `toolsDeleteDbTable` (`filename='%s' and fileurl='%s' and time=%d and time_end=%d`: the folder scan's check and `ringnav_scan_refresh`'s update for each file, and each song a delete removes) and `getAllRecentAddRecord` (`order by time_create desc limit 100`) each read the whole table. Both scans' hooks end (`library_scan`) with `create index if not exists` of `songtable_album` (`album collate nocase`), `songtable_filename` and `songtable_time_create` (`time_create desc`), through `toolsUpdateDbTable` on the scan thread and stock's shared handle: after stock's writes, as Update Local Music drops the table and its indexes with it (so a full scan inserts into a bare table and builds each index once), and before `wait_scan` sets the done flag, so the library reads as scanning meanwhile. `like` takes a `NOCASE` index on a text column (stock's `VARCHAR`) while `case_sensitive_like` is off, which nothing sets. The query hook's `MUSIC_WHERE` subquery is flattened into the query, so the scoped queries use it too; a pattern that starts with `%` or `_` still reads the table. With stock's libsqlite3 3.19.3 under QEMU (instructions on a cold connection, the row callback's fill included), an album's songs take 1.2 M instead of 257 M at 65,000 songs (9 tracks), and 1.4 M instead of 1.56 G at 400,000 (16), so Era's Play All on the 65,000-song library's largest decade (760 albums, 1,520 queries) is about 1.8 G of queries rather than 0.39 T; a file's check, delete or refresh 0.6 M instead of 50 M, and 0.6–0.7 M instead of 306 M; Recently Added 4.2 M instead of 780 M at 65,000 and 4.77 G at 400,000. The build costs 1.04 G at 65,000 songs and 7.30 G at 400,000, adds 5.4 MB and 33.6 MB to `database.db` (21.4 MB to 26.8 MB, 106 MB to 140 MB) and sorts through up to 2.6 MB and 15.9 MB of temporary file in `/tmp` (RAM) an index; a folder scan's new song then costs 40 k (65,000) to 64 k (400,000) more to insert. A library no scan has run on since has none and reads as before: a build anywhere else would hold the database's write lock for seconds while stock's library pages query it. A connection still reading when the build writes (a count started before the scan) fails the create with `SQLITE_BUSY` once the 500 ms the shared connection waits (`stock_db_open`) run out, and the indexes wait for the next scan. A full scan (`drops`, Update Local Music) adds three more first, when `/mnt/data` has `DATA_ROOM_MB` (8 MB) free (`card_room`): `songtable_group` on `ALBUM_GROUP`'s three terms as their text (`album collate nocase`, `ifnull(albumsonger,'') collate nocase` and the folder `case`; SQLite matches an index's expression to the query's), which Albums' grouping (`ALBUM_SQL` and the other `ALBUM_GROUP` queries) walks in group order with no temporary B-tree, `songtable_album_exact` on `album` and `songtable_artist` on `ifnull(nullif(albumsonger,''),songer)`, which the [Unknown rows](#unknown-rows) checks (`album=""`, the album-artist one) search instead of scanning the table. In the emulator at 20,103 songs (instrumented build, three opens each, back to back): the grouping 240-347 ms to 171-273 ms, each Unknown check 37-67 ms to 0-2 ms, Artists' and Songs' queries unchanged; 786,432, 487,424 and 413,696 bytes of `database.db` (1.69 MB; 4.87 MB without them), each built in 0.14-0.54 s by q2-coda's SQLite under QEMU. They go before the other three because SQLite takes the most recently created of two indexes that serve a query equally: made after `songtable_album`, `songtable_group` took `getAllAlbum` and stock's other `group by album COLLATE NOCASE` queries and picked another song as each group's bare-column row (its `id`, `songer`, `fileurl`); made before, all 17 of stock's grouping queries give the rows they gave without it, on 3.54.1 and on stock's 3.19.3, checked over a library with albums and artists in two cases. A folder scan adds none, so they come with the next Update Local Music. Stock's 3.19.3 misplans the payload's own `group by ifnull(nullif(albumsonger,''),songer) COLLATE NOCASE` over the binary `songtable_artist` and splits artists that differ in case (402 groups for 202); q2-coda runs SQLite 3.54.1 ([third-party](third-party.md)), which groups them right, and stock never runs that query. ponytail: a full scan whose drop failed keeps `songtable_album` older than `songtable_group`, so the album groupings take the wider index until the next full scan.

They change other plans, for the same rows. An index keeps equal keys in rowid order, as stock's sort did, so with `desc` songs of one second (a CUE image's tracks, files copied together) keep their order newest first (Recently Added, `getAllMusic(3)`: Time added (descending), and the payload's unsorted reads). Oldest first (`getAllMusic(4)`, Time added (ascending)) would walk the index backwards and reverse them, so `library_query` adds `, id` to its `order by`; an ascending index would reverse the newest-first lists instead, and Recently Added would keep the other end of an album its `limit 100` cuts. `count(*)` counts `songtable_time_create` (5.2 MB at 400,000 songs) instead of the table (99 MB): 1.9 M instead of 22.6 M, so the count Update Local Music's message takes before the scan holds its lock for less of the scan's start. `getAllMusic(3)` walks `songtable_time_create`: 1.51 G instead of 2.02 G at 65,000 songs, and no sort spilled to `/tmp` (15 MB). `getAllMusic(4)` walks it too and sorts only each second's songs. The album groupings walk `songtable_album`, a row lookup each in album order: `getAllAlbum` 386 M instead of 889 M at 65,000 (2.32 G instead of 6.26 G at 400,000) with no 10 MB spill, `ALBUM_SQL`, Era's and Home's album count 5–14% fewer, their three-term `group by` still sorted through `/tmp`, an artist's albums tab 13% more (328 M instead of 289 M), and the other `like … group by album` queries (album artist, composer and genre tabs, album search) walk it the same way. Each reads its pages out of order, over twice a scan's (227 MB rather than 99 MB at 400,000). ponytail: those reads are unmeasured on a Q2; `not indexed` puts a grouping back on the table if they prove slow.

**Empty or scanning.** Only the modal Update Local Music dialog (`dialog_updatemusic_dialog_init`) starts the scan: `tk_thread` `wait_scan` → `scanAllMusicFile` (`toolsInitDatabase`, `toolsLoadAllFile`, commit), storing the handle at `0xa3b0c8` and clearing `0xa3b0c4`, which `wait_scan` sets when it ends. The same init sets the byte at `0xa3b0c0` (`SCAN_WHOLE`): 1 for the whole library's scan, 0 for a folder's, as we read stock's code; no device run has checked it. Its Back button stops the scan and quits the dialog before the thread ends. Coverflow shows an empty page while a scan runs (handle set, flag clear) or when `getAllAlbum` returns ≤ 0, as PictureFlow's `check_database()` does: under OLED the empty state (`feedback.c` `empty_state`, its tiles, words and row on a view the page's painter reads, `empty_state_paint`) by cause (`patch/cf_empty.c`): music on the card but none in the library (a walk of the card, dot-folders left out, at most 6 deep and 4,000 entries, stopping at the first song file) is "No Albums Yet" with Scan Music Now (stock's `dialog/updatemusic_dialog`); else a catalogue app signed in (`catalogue_signed`: its card folder holds its `credentials` file, which is looked for and never opened, since the app's status file is in `/tmp` and gone at boot, and signing out deletes it) is "No Albums", "Streaming albums can show here", with Turn on Streaming while Streaming Songs is off (`library_needs`, which asks first); else "No Albums", "Copy music to the SD card". The page's timer (`empty_poll`) loads the covers again once `library_gen` moves (a scan, an import, Streaming Songs turned on). Other themes keep stock's words, "Update Local Music first". Stock's own limit on a scan went with V1.36: until V1.34 `toolsLoadAllFile` (`0x5dc330`) stopped, as Back does, once the song count (`toolsGetMusicNum`) reached 20,000; now it scans until `/mnt/data` is full, which its insert (`tools_insert_song_to_db`, `0x5da07c`) finds with `toolsGetFreeSpace` after each 100 songs' commit and reports by setting the stop flag to 2 (`toolsStopUpdateMusic`'s byte, `0xa50528`, which Back sets to 1; the scanner looks at it before each folder entry and stops above 0), and the scan dialog then says `msg_no_storage`. Q2 Muse's own limit, 65,000 songs while stock's was 20,000, went with it: nothing counts the scan's songs now. The queue's `QUEUE_LIMIT` is 65,536, and a larger queue (a larger library's Songs, a folder's, a playlist's) gets no advanced play: `rebuild` refuses it before it takes its tables, 36 B a song. Play Next or Add to Queue past it (`playback_insert`), or a stock edit that grows the queue past it (`follow_queue`), still takes a 4 B a song `seen` first.

**Update during a count.** `toolsInitDatabase` drops `songtable` and creates it again on the connection every `tools*` function shares (`0xa50114`), which since playlist art waits up to 500 ms for a reader (`stock_db_open`, [Songs' hashes](#playlist-art)): a count outlasts that. A count reading `songtable` on its own connection, the dialog's `msg_count` or Home's `count_worker`, holds a read lock on the database until it ends, and a count reads every page of the table. So the drop could not commit: it failed with `SQLITE_BUSY` (stock ignores the result, `0x5d9d9c`), the create then failed as the table existed, `toolsInitDatabase` closed the handle and returned -1, and `scanAllMusicFile` skipped the update: the old library stayed and nothing said so. `coverflow_scan_all` now waits on the scan's thread, before the marker walk and stock's body, while either count runs (`library_counting`: `home.counting` or `st.msg_counting` 1), looking every 100 ms. Each flag is set on the UI thread before its worker starts: `msg_open` sets the dialog's as the dialog loads, before stock's init starts the scan's thread, and `home_counts` starts no count while a scan runs (`library_scanning`). The wait is outside SQLite and holds nothing, so no statement on the shared connection waits with it. The UI thread waits on it only when the dialog opens again over a running scan: stock's init stops the old thread and joins it, and the stop ends the wait within 100 ms. It can't deadlock: the counts' connections are their own, and a count takes no lock the scan's thread holds. Back ends the wait (`toolsStopUpdateMusic`'s flag, `toolsGetUserStop`) and skips stock's body, returning its 1, as `wait_scan` skips a scan stopped before it starts (`0x4a24a4`): the drop would otherwise commit in a count's last 100 ms and `toolsClearDbCount` erase the Back, leaving a scan running behind a closed dialog, or fail and close the shared handle with a count still running. A folder scan never drops the table (`wait_specfolder_scan` passes a 0 drop flag) and does not wait. `test/patch.py` runs stock's `scanAllMusicFile` and `toolsInitDatabase` on a real SQLite file while the dialog's count holds a read lock on it. ponytail: the dialog stays on its first line for as long as a count runs: Home's album count runs about 14 billion instructions on a 400,000-song library.

Coverflow's main, artist and rated views keep only albums with a track outside `/mnt/mmc/Audiobooks/` and without an `.m4b` extension, case aside (`music_albums`, `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`). Filtering precedes the SQL grouping so a mixed album uses a music track for its artwork. The stock library lists keep their audiobook entries.

**Tracks.** A cover opens `getMusicByAlbum(id == -1 ? NULL : album)`, which is what a stock Albums row opens (`load_localclass_list(0xff10)` with `g_local_classinfo_save+0xd`, `+9` flagging Unknown); it returns stock-ordered songs (`algo_sort_if`). The Albums list has no -2 row; that one only occurs in an artist's albums (queue menu). The result comes through `staged` the same way, keeping only the cover's own album (`album_cmp`: the query matches the name alone). Coverflow then re-orders the copy into album order, disc then track then path then CUE start, so an untagged album keeps its file-name order. Its row callback (`0x506428`, `select *` from `songtable`) fills `+0x08` the file name, `+0x10` the tag's title, `+0x3c` `track` and `+0x40` `cd_num` (`REC_NAME`, `REC_TITLE`, `REC_TRACK`, `REC_DISC`). Each row shows the title tag when present, otherwise the file name less its file's extension; a CUE track's name, which does not end in it, stays whole. Folder play gets the re-ordered deque, so playback follows the list.

**Play class.** `0xff10` would resume the wrong album: memory-play re-runs `getMusicByAlbum` from `g_memory_info+0x611` (`memeory_startplayer` `0x5211f4`), which only `player_load_songlist` (`0x51e31c`) fills, from the live `g_local_classinfo_save`. Coverflow therefore plays the cover's songs as `0xff10` through `play_folder`, after `album_memory` has written the cover's album (or the Unknown flag, `+0x60d`) into `g_memory_info`, so that rebuild finds the cover's own album, and `playing_page` gets `{tracks, index, 0xff10, 2}`. `mclLoadPlayList` copies the deque synchronously. A restart resumes the saved queue whole from `ringnav_queue`; stock's rebuild (`stock_memory`, then `album_only`) runs only when no snapshot exists, in practice a queue of more than 999 songs (`SAVE_LIMIT`). The Unknown Album card's rebuild keeps every untagged song the card lists, whatever its folder (spoken and scoped-out ones left out, and the playing song kept). ponytail: the rebuilt queue is stock's order (name), not the card's file-name order, so Next and Previous after such a restart follow stock's; sort with `album_before` in `album_only` if that shows.

**Art.** Every stock caller holds a lock around the art calls, and none nests the two: `parse_albumcovertask_thd` (`toolsGetAlbumCover` `0x4f8638`/`0x4f9728`/`0x4f97f0`, `toolsThumbSpecCover` `0x4f9080`/`0x4f99f0`) and the UI-thread online thumbnails (`0x536248`/`0x536260`) hold `parse_cover_mutex`; `player_parsecover_thd` holds `g_playcover_mutex` around `toolsGetAlbumCover` (`0x51dc90`) and `parse_cover_mutex` alone around its Tidal/Baidu downloads. `toolsGetAlbumCover` writes and removes the shared `/tmp/.tmp_picture`, so both stock threads can already race on it; Coverflow takes both locks, parse then play. `taglib_album_picture` (`libtag_c` `0x12508`) dispatches by extension to the C++ `get*_file_albumpic` helpers, none of which touches `libtag_c`'s unlocked string list (`taglib_tag_free_strings`), which the UI thread's `toolsGetMusicInfo` uses. That list is what failed the first design; embedded art is only as concurrent as stock's own player thread already is. `toolsThumbSpecCover(src, dst, w, h)` decodes JPEG (≤ 6 MB; libjpeg scales by the longest side, 1/1 to 1023 px, 1/2 to 2048, 1/4 to 4096, 1/8 beyond, `0x5cb198`, so a baseline 3000×3000 cover is cheap, while a progressive one still holds its full coefficient planes, about 27 MB at 4:2:0, in demo) or PNG (≤ 1 MB and at most 1024 px on either side, `slti 0x401` at `0x5c9358`, but only after `png_read_png` at `0x5c9308` has expanded the whole image in demo, about 64 MB at 4000×4000 RGBA), by their magic bytes (`toolsGetPictureInfo`), and encodes, or `cp`s a source already small enough, straight to `dst` with no extension check, so `<key>.jpg.tmp` is safe. Both return 1 on success. Stock's own cover cache (`/mnt/mmc/.sldp/<md5>{0,1}.jpg`) and folder-image finder (`toolsGetExternCover`, `0x5d7640`) are not used: the first fills lazily as the album grid scrolls, and the spec fixes cover.jpg → folder.jpg → embedded. Coverflow tries embedded art, then `cover`/`folder` `.jpg`, `.png`, `.webp` (none from a folder so deep that the image's path would not fit 1024 bytes: the cut name is a prefix, another file's at best), then ffmpeg on the embedded art (last: a process for every album without art). Whatever stock refuses (WebP, a PNG over 1 MB or 1024 px, a JPEG over 6 MB) goes to stock `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` (`ff_thumb`: fork and exec, its first picture or embedded `attached_pic` fitted into the box, written as a baseline 4:2:0 JPEG). `ff_thumb` has ffmpeg write `<dst>.ff` and renames it onto `dst` only on exit 0 with a non-empty file; otherwise it removes `<dst>.ff` and leaves `dst` alone, as stock's grid cache takes any file at its path for art. ffmpeg creates its output before decoding, so a picture it can't decode leaves an empty file even on exit 0, and a killed run a partial one. `-xerror` ends the run at a picture's first decode error instead of demuxing the rest of the audio file, and `waitpid` is retried on `EINTR` so the child is always reaped. That covers the embedded picture in `build_art` and every `thumb` caller with a readable source (playlists' art, Tidal, Spotify). It writes no shared file and takes no lock. `thumb` reads the source's header first (`big_picture`: a PNG's IHDR, or a JPEG's frame header within its first 64 segments, a fill byte before a marker counting as one) and gives a PNG over 1024 px either way, a progressive JPEG (SOF2) over 1024 px, or a JPEG whose frame header it didn't find (it may be either, [GHSA-w54x-mvfw-c7v3](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/security/advisories/GHSA-w54x-mvfw-c7v3)), to `ff_thumb` alone: stock would hold the whole picture in demo, which the OOM killer then takes ([#216](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/issues/216)). A baseline JPEG, a smaller picture and another type it can't size stay with stock, and so do the arithmetic and hierarchical progressive frames (SOF6, 10, 14), which ffmpeg 4.2 can't decode. ponytail: a progressive cover cut short, which libjpeg shows with a warning, fails ffmpeg's `-xerror` and has no art now; fall back to stock when ffmpeg exits by itself if such covers turn up. Embedded art gets no such check, as its picture reaches a file only inside `toolsGetAlbumCover` (`/tmp/.tmp_picture`, between `taglib_album_picture` and the decoder's `jalr` at `0x5d7140`), so a large embedded PNG or progressive JPEG still decodes in demo. Neither do stock's own callers of a folder image: Now Playing's `toolsGetExternCover`, tried before Coverflow's fallback, and the album grid's `parse_albumcovertask_thd`, so a big `cover.png` still decodes in demo when its album plays or its grid row shows; trampolining `toolsThumbSpecCover` itself would cover both. Stock's decoder also refuses palette and grayscale PNGs (its PNG reader, `0x5c91bc`, takes only color types 2 and 6). Now Playing gets the same fallback: `player_parsecover_thd` tries `toolsGetAlbumCover` (embedded) and then `toolsGetExternCover` (folder images) under `g_playcover_mutex`, and that second call (`PLAYER_COVER`, `0x51dccc`) becomes `jal coverflow_player_cover`. That runs stock's call first, then `ff_thumb` on the same `cover`/`folder` names and then on the embedded picture. It never calls `thumb`, whose `parse_cover_mutex` would nest under the player's lock in the opposite order from `build_art`'s. Folder images cost a process only when one exists. The embedded probe costs one for every track without art, so it is skipped when `g_play_id3_info` holds the track's path (`player_get_id3info` parses it before the cover thread runs) and Coverflow's cache file for those parsed tags, keyed as Home's art is, is an empty marker. ponytail: the marker records one track's result, so another disc's tracks, or tracks of a same-named album, whose only art is embedded WebP or a large PNG show none on Now Playing; tracks on albums Coverflow hasn't built, or by another artist than the album's key (compilations), still pay a probe per play. Albums already marked empty need **Refresh Coverflow** (Display → Coverflow). ponytail: one process per refused cover; a resident decoder if first builds drag. Library Albums grids and Folder view get the Ogg case: `parse_albumcovertask_thd`'s three `toolsGetAlbumCover` calls (`GRID_COVER`, `0x4f863c`/`0x4f9738`/`0x4f97f4`: an album's cover, a folder's first track with art, a track row) become `jal coverflow_album_cover` (the first), `jal coverflow_folder_cover` (the second) and `jal coverflow_grid_cover`, each stock's call and then, for an `.opus` or `.ogg` track only (stock's libtag reads no Ogg picture), `ff_thumb`. All three run on stock's one cover thread (`platform_init` starts it) under `parse_cover_mutex`, which the UI thread also takes for Library's online thumbnails (`localmusic_page_init`, `0x536248`/`0x536260`) and Spotify's art (`thumb`), so the lock is dropped for the ffmpeg run and taken again before returning. That is safe: each call's source and destination are the thread's stack paths (`.sldp/<md5>{0,1}.jpg`, `.downpic/fd_<md5>.jpg`), which no other lock holder writes (the UI thread's are `.downpic/s_<md5>.jpg`), and what stock does after it (`toolsGetExternCover` on the album call) runs with the lock held again. The album call's stock fallback is `toolsGetExternCover`, which scans the folder for any `.jpg`, `.png` or `.jpeg`, `folder`/`cover` names first; `coverflow_album_cover` calls it before ffmpeg, so an Ogg album whose art is a folder image costs no process, and its Ogg art is ordered as Coverflow's. The folder-row call already runs it first, and the track-row call has no folder fallback, so neither does. Stock caches only a hit (`.sldp`, `.downpic`), so a track ffmpeg found no picture in is remembered in memory (an FNV hash of its path; not when the track itself is gone, the fork was refused or ffmpeg was killed) and its rows ask no further process. ponytail: 1024 misses remembered until reboot, the oldest overwritten; a picture added to such a track since shows after a reboot. Stock's folder row reads the folder in directory order, the order its files were copied to the card, and keeps the art of the first audio file that has any (folder images, then that file's own), cached as `.downpic/fd_<md5>.jpg`, which stock deletes at every Return in Folder view. So an album copied out of order showed a later song's cover. `coverflow_folder_cover` lists the folder itself and tries its first song by name, as Folder view lists it, before the song stock passed: regular files with the extension of stock's song, no dot files (a Mac's `._` copies). The folder, its first song and whether that song had art are kept for stock's next call; a hit ends stock's walk and clears them, so the next walk lists the folder again. ponytail: names compared by `strcasecmp`, not the list's own comparator; a folder with no art at all stays kept until another folder is shown.

**Build.** On open, the UI thread copies each uncached album's track path (`strdup`) and FNV key (artist, album) into a job array. One pthread then renders 160×160 art to `/mnt/mmc/.coverflow/<key>.jpg.tmp` and renames it into place. Missing art leaves an empty `<key>.jpg` marker; a track that is gone, or an ffmpeg run that never reached its own exit (a refused fork, a kill), leaves nothing, so the next open retries it. Before each album the thread writes the album's key and its track's path to `/mnt/mmc/.coverflow/building`, synced in place (a sync per album; not through a rename, whose directory write a reset could lose; a torn note reads short), and removes it after the last. One still there at the next open names an album whose build never ended: demo died on it, or hung on it until the watchdog restarted the Q2, and as nothing marked it every open would try it again and end the same way (two testers' "Preparing artwork… 0/2" restarts, 2026-11-09). `art_strike` gives that album the empty marker, unless its cover is there (a death between the rename and the next note), so it shows the placeholder until **Refresh Cover Flow**, and appends the track to the card's `q2-crash.log` under `== cover flow skipped`: the boot hook's `== last art` names it only when demo itself died ([boot.md](boot.md)), and the tester's log was the watchdog's "demo did not end" with no stall record, demo alive and the Q2 frozen, which fits a swapless kernel thrashing on a large embedded picture decoded in demo (the unguarded path above). One strike per restart, so a card with several such albums restarts once for each. A clean end mid-build (`coverflow_clean_end`, from `ringnav_clean_end`) removes the note and sets the cancel flag, so the thread stops after the album it is on, with no note for the next, which the kill that follows would otherwise have left for `art_strike`: a power-off is no album's fault. ponytail: the battery running out mid-build strikes an innocent album, which Refresh Cover Flow puts back. A 3000×3000 cover costs ffmpeg tens of MB (a PNG frame 27-36 MB, a progressive JPEG's coefficients up to 54 MB) on a device with no swap, and the kernel's OOM killer takes the process with the most memory, which was demo, so the Q2 froze and the watchdog rebooted it mid-build ([#169](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/issues/169); only a dead demo reboots, see [boot.md](boot.md), a hung one never does). every child demo forks (`child_oom_first` in `patch/peq.h`: `ff_run`'s and the boot logo's ffmpeg, Audiobooks' chapter read, Tidal's tagger, q2video) writes 1000 to its `/proc/self/oom_score_adj` between fork and exec, so the kernel takes the child first; the album is then retried at the next open rather than marked artless, and Now Playing's `marked_empty` skip does not apply to it. Demo's own baseline matters too: `staged` keeps the staging deque's contents across a query by copying them out and back (`deque_init_copy`, `deque_assign`), so after Library → Songs on a 65,000-song library every `staged` call briefly holds two copies of that list (a `stSongInfo` is 0x58 bytes plus its strings), the likeliest link to Songs' deferred crash; a move would need the stock deque's layout. There is no build below `MIN_FREE_MB` (16) free on the card (`statfs`, o32 `f_bsize` word 1, `f_bavail` word 7). Progress and the cancel flag are volatile `.scratch` ints; a 250 ms timer polls until every job is done. Cancel and window destroy join the thread, a wait bounded by one album. A folder holding tracks of two albums gives neither its `cover`/`folder` image, which may be the other's: `folders_shared` finds those folders in one pass before the jobs, sorting the albums by folder (FNV hash, then the folder itself and the album key), replacing a check of every album against every other on the UI thread, albums squared: the likely cause (inferred from a tester's watchdog restarts, not reproduced) of a big library's first open stalling until the watchdog restarted the Q2. A cold open, one that queries the albums or finds albums with no art, also writes its phases (`start`, `staged`, `split`, `music_albums`, `drop_unknown`, `sorted`, every 1000th job and `done`, each with the milliseconds since it began) to `/mnt/data/q2-cf-trace`, synced, a few lines per open (a warm one writes nothing), and removes it when `load` ends, so after a forced restart `S90play` puts the phase it reached in `q2-crash.log` ([Watchdog](#watchdog)). Before each album the thread's `crash_note` names its track in `/tmp/q2-art-file` and, every 50th album, appends the count, demo's VmRSS and the track to `/tmp/q2-art.log`, for the crash log ([boot.md](boot.md)). **System settings → Display → Coverflow → Refresh Coverflow** (`coverflow_refresh_art`) first stops [playlist art](#playlist-art)'s build (a Playlists page can be open under Settings), then unlinks the cache directory and steps `library_gen`, so the next open queries the albums again and rebuilds their art.

**Page.** The Home card clones `btn_localmusic` at index 2 in the carousel, reusing its images, and is the third row of Home's list; `home_page_init`'s `widget_foreach` visitor (`0x534750`) binds `img_*` clicks and translates `label_*` by name and ignores unknown names. The Local Music card's label is renamed `label_library`, so it skips it too and its literal "Library" shows in every language. Since stock V1.34 the visitor knows `img_coverflow` and `label_coverflow`: its own Album Wall card's, which `ipod_home` deletes; the Cover Flow card's are `img_cover_flow` and `label_cover_flow`, so stock neither binds the card to its Album Wall nor names it so. The hook runs the stock init through `stock_home_trampoline` (`0x534b78`), then binds `widget_lookup(win, "img_cover_flow", 1)`, whatever stock returned. In iPod it also sets up Home's art ([ipod.md](ipod.md#home)). The card opens a runtime `window_create(NULL, 0, 0, 0, 0)` named `coverflow_page`; `window_base_create` opens it through `window_manager_open_window`, and the window-manager key handlers that `home_page_init` registers route it like any page (`CTX_DYNAMIC`, exempt from the rootfs window-name check). Covers are a factory `slide_menu` of `image_create` children, each item `h` square (`0x605ed0`); with depth (below) the children stay empty and the payload draws the covers. In the flat fallback they are stock images (`image_set_draw_type` 4, as stock cover rows). `slide_menu` dispatches `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED` (`0xe`, after `0xd` will-change, `0x60609c`) with the new index already at `+0x78`, which updates the captions (the album over its artist; with Artists set to Album Artist, `artist_type` 1, the album artist tag when it has one, `cover_artist`, so a compilation reads "Various Artists" or its compiler, and the Artist sort and its letter jump use the same name, sorting again when Artists changes); in the flat fallback only covers within ±3 then load their file, the stock way: `widget_load_image` → `image_base_set_image` → `widget_unload_image`. A failed load (the empty marker) shows `default_album_flow`. Clicks only schedule screen changes on a 0 ms timer, so no screen change destroys the widget whose click is running. Tracks hide the covers rather than destroy them, so Return restores the album.

Coverflow’s Album and Artist sorts, on ticks (a finger on the screen, the page sliding in or no depth frame; otherwise the thumb's letters apply, [Letters](#coverflow-thumb)), once a spin passes `CF_FIRST_MS` (700 ms, longer than the lists' `LIST_FIRST_MS`), jump to the first album of the next or previous populated initial group; with Fast Navigation on Year jumps the same way by year, the next or previous year that has albums, the undated last (`group`, below). The active sort key skips leading articles; numeric, punctuation, separator and missing-name initials share `#`, while other Unicode initials are retained. The same carousel animator is retargeted; utility cards and wrap edges remain individual stops. On ticks the big letter expires after 400 ms (`LETTER_MS`); with Fast Navigation on the thumb's letters hold it until the lift. Recently Added, Most Played and Random keep single-album stepping.

## Tag text

Stock reads a song's tags with its own `libtag_c` (`toolsGetMusicInfo`, `0x5d8b98`, for the library scan and the player): for each of six fields (title, artist, album, genre, composer, album artist) it asks for the field twice, `taglib_tag_<field>(tag, 0)` (TagLib's `String::to8Bit(false)`: one byte per character, Latin-1) and `(tag, 1)` (UTF-8), and whether TagLib found every character below U+0100 (`taglib_tag_islatin1`, `String::isLatin1`). `toolsFixId3ErrorCode` (`0x5d8950`) then took a field for GBK whenever it was "Latin-1" that way: it converted the Latin-1 bytes from GBK to UTF-8 (`toolsIconvConvert(s, "utf-8", "gbk")`, with an `iconv_open("gbk", "utf-8")` round trip as its check) and kept the result, so any Western title with an accented letter came out Chinese: "Lo que la música me enseñó" pairs `ú` and `s` (0xFA 0x73), `ñ` and `ó` (0xF1 0xF3) into GBK characters. That covers FLAC and Vorbis comments (always UTF-8) and UTF-8 ID3v2 frames as much as Latin-1 ID3 frames: the test is on the decoded text, not the tag's encoding. `TAG_TEXT` in `tools/build.py` turns that round trip's `strcmp` (`0x5d8ad4`) into `jal ringnav_gbk_tag`, which also asks that the Latin-1 bytes read as GBK (`gbk_text`): not UTF-8, and every byte from 0x80 one of a pair, lead 0x81–0xFE then trail 0x80–0xFE, with no pair between two ASCII letters. Western text puts an accented letter next to an ASCII one ("mú-s" is 0xFA 0x73) or a pair inside a word ("Can-çã-o", "Beyonc-é’-s"), so it fails and keeps TagLib's UTF-8 copy; a GBK-tagged MP3 (Chinese rips' Latin-1 frames holding GBK bytes) is all pairs and still converts. Limits: a GBK character with an ASCII-range trail byte (0x40–0x7E, the rarer GBK/3 and GBK/4 ones) or a single one inside a Latin word ("a周b"), makes its field read as Latin-1, and Western text whose accented letters only come in pairs at a word's edge ("ñó" alone) reads as GBK. Stock's conversion writes back over a CUE field unbounded, and GBK grows by half as UTF-8, so a CUE field over 340 bytes is read as Windows-1252 instead. The library keeps what the scan stored: **Library → Update Local Music** reads the tags again.

TagLib 2.0.1 joins multiple genre values with `" / "`. Stock copied the result unchecked into the 128-byte style field at `info + 0x200`, immediately before the title at `+0x280`, so a joined genre of 128 bytes or more replaced the title in the library and player (`toolsFixId3ErrorCode`'s `snprintf` stops the value at 255 bytes, so nothing goes past the title). `GENRE_COPY` changes that one copy to `ringnav_genre_copy`, which keeps the whole entries that fit 127 bytes, or as many whole characters of an oversized first entry as fit. Tag files are unchanged. Limits: only `" / "` is an entry boundary, so a single value joined with `;` or `//` over 127 bytes is cut at 127 (at a whole character), and an empty first entry followed by an oversized one stores an empty genre. The library keeps what the scan stored. Update Local Music drops `songtable` and inserts every row through `toolsGetMusicInfo`, and Scan specified folders refreshes existing rows (**Folder tag refresh**), so either repairs the title. Favorites, playlists and play records keep their own copy of a row, which neither touches: a bad title saved there stays until the song is added again.

Every scrolling text is a stock `hscroll_label`, and its holds and pace are set where every one of them passes. Stock's start (`hscroll_label_start`, `0x5fb4ac`, which a label's focus, its paint on a new text, its lull and the payload all call, PC-relative or through the GOT) waits the label's `delay` before its first step; nothing sets one but a page's XML, so most labels moved at once. A looping label then ends a pass by adding its `lull` timer (2000 ms from `set_hscroll_label_attribute`, 3000 by default), whose callback (`0x5fb658`) restarts it: the start's step put the text back at its start, so the lull held the end and the start never held. Its pace is `speed` in pixels per ms (`set_hscroll_label_attribute` sets 0.05 since V1.36 and 0.1 before, some pages 0.2, Now Playing's title and artist 0.05), or, with no speed, the whole overflow in its `duration`. The `hscroll_label_start` hook (`ringnav_hscroll_start`, `HOOKS` in `tools/build.py`) sets every label's `delay` to `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS` (1500) and caps its speed at `HSCROLL_PACE` (0.05, Now Playing's; a label with none takes it too) before stock's start runs. `HSCROLL_LULL` turns the end-of-pass `widget_add_timer` into `jal ringnav_hscroll_lull`, which adds its own timer, `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS` whatever the label's lull, through `hscroll_lull_end`: it sets `xoffset` to 0, then runs stock's callback, so the end holds `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS`, the text goes back to its start, and the start holds the same before the next pass. A looping `yoyo` label scrolls back instead: its lull is 0, since the delay holds whichever end it is at. A label that doesn't loop (`set_hscroll_label_attribute` leaves `loop` off, so most stock rows that scroll by themselves scroll once as their page opens) ended its pass at once, its timer removed, and stock painted its start with the ellipsis the moment it reached its end, or a `yoyo` one stayed on its end: `HSCROLL_ONCE` sends that pass to the lull too, whose end clears the label's timer id and stops it on its start, as stock's own lull callback clears it, so the timer ends by its `RET_REMOVE`. Since V1.36 `set_hscroll_label_attribute` (`0x4f1ed8`), which that release calls for most rows' labels, also gives a label a `loop_interval_distance` of its own width, AWTK's seamless loop: the label's range grows by that distance, so the text runs off the label and comes in again behind the gap, with no end to hold. `hscroll_label`'s range (`0x5fb1e4`), timer and paint honour it only from 0 up, and the default is -1, so `HSCROLL_GAP` drops the one call that sets it (`widget_set_prop_int`, `0x4f1f4c`) and every label keeps the pass described here. The same function sets `only_parent_focus` in Menu Mode alone, which `WHEEL_MODE` never lets stock be in. V1.36's Albums rows (`localmusic_album_on_prepare_row`) call it where V1.34's set a focus flag outright, the list row's artist line (`only_focus`) and each grid cell's title (`only_parent_focus`), so those four labels would have scrolled once by themselves as the page painted; their calls go through `ringnav_album_label` (`ALBUM_LABELS`), which sets `only_parent_focus` after stock's call. A row of Baidu Netdisk's download list lost its `only_focus` the same way and is left as stock has it: Q2 Muse takes that page's row off Streaming. While a label holds its start it is running, so stock paints it without its ellipsis. An `only_focus` label stock won't restart (unfocused) rests on its start rather than its end, and one started while unfocused holds its start before its first tick stops it, as stock's does. Stock counts a pass's time in its 16 ms ticks, so on the UI loop's idle passes (25 ms) every label runs about a third slower, as it always has.

**The ellipsis.** A label at rest with `ellipses` set ends a long text in stock's `"..."` (`canvas_draw_text_bidi_in_rect`, `0x64cc00`, which `widget_draw_text_in_rect` hands its text): it keeps the characters that fit, each measured alone, while the dots, those kept and the next are under the box's width. On its own a cut just after a word keeps the space, so a title reads `Wicked Garden (2017 ...`, a gap before the dots. `HSCROLL_ELLIPSIS` turns `hscroll_label_on_paint_self`'s one call that asks for the ellipsis (`0x5fc074`) into `jal ringnav_ellipsis_text` (`patch/navigation.c`), which runs stock's count itself and, when the kept characters end in spaces, hands stock a box one pixel wider than the dots and the characters up to the last that isn't a space: those still fit, and the space after them (wider than a pixel) doesn't, so the dots follow the word. A cut inside a word, a text that fits and a scrolling label (the other call, no ellipsis) are stock's as they were.

**Marquee fades** (OLED's `list.marquee.fade`). The text itself fades, onto whatever stands behind it, so no color is guessed: the selection's blue, a destructive answer's red, the page, a cover. When an `hscroll_label`'s text (`HSCROLL_TEXT_W`, 0x94) is wider than its column, the label's box inside its style's `margin_left` and `margin_right` (2 px unless the style says otherwise, as a folder row's does past its icon), `ringnav_paint_bg` calls `marquee_fade_under` (`patch/list_marks.c`) as the label's background paints, before stock draws its text: it copies the `MARQUEE_FADE_PX` (12) columns at each end that needs one out of the canvas's buffer (the lcd_mem's `LCD_OFFLINE_FB`, BGRA8888: what is behind the text), the right end while the offset (`HSCROLL_XOFFSET`, 0x90) is short of the overflow, the left while it is past 0, so a text at rest on its start is crisp. After stock has drawn the text, `ringnav_paint` calls `marquee_fade`, which blends each column back toward the copy by how near the end it stands: behind + (painted - behind) x i / 12, the end column exactly what was behind, which is the text's own coverage times a ramp over the real background, as an offscreen alpha mask would give. Only rows inside the frame's clip are touched (outside it the buffer holds an older frame), and a canvas whose buffer is not 32-bit (none on the Q2's screen) shows the text clipped, unfaded. A stopped label with `ellipses` (`HSCROLL_ELLIPSES`, 0x7c) set keeps stock's ellipsis untouched, so only a scrolling text pays: two copies of at most 12 x 24 pixels and a blend of them a frame. The status row's title is `only_focus` and never focused, so it never scrolls and a long one ends in its ellipsis. The text stays in its own box, which stock clips it to: OLED's boxes end on the right column, a row's before its chevron or value and Now Playing's on `np_grid`'s, so nothing runs under the glass.

**Now Playing's marquee** (OLED: `list.marquee.fade`). The title, artist and album move on one clock (`patch/np_marquee.c`), the way Spotify's do, not each on its own label timer. Every line that overflows its column holds at rest `NPM_HOLD_MS` (2750), then all slide left together until each line's end meets its column's end, hold there `NPM_END_MS` (`MARQUEE_HOLD_MS`, 1500) and go back to rest together: the longest line's overflow at `NPM_PX_S` (35 px a second), linear, and the others stretched to the same time. A line slides only what overflows, never past its end: V1.36's `hscroll_label` paint (`0x5fbd08`) draws a second copy of the text only when `stop_at_begin` (`+0x98`) is set (`0x5fc1a0`), and then at the range plus the gap, not behind the text, so a pass that slid the text its whole width plus a 40 px gap, expecting a copy, left the column empty: measured in the emulator, the title was blank for 1,416 ms of each 9.5 s cycle (frame capture of the title's box). Its ellipsis is cleared, and while it rests on its start or slides, its right end fades (`list_marks.c` `fade_ends`), its left once it has moved. `npm_tick` sets each `xoffset` from the clock, a frame each time the longest line moves a pixel (the timer rounded up to that pixel), and nothing runs while the lines rest, fit, or the page is dark or covered. Stock's own timer never runs for these lines: `ringnav_hscroll_start` hands an owned line's start to `np_marq_reset`, and the page's opening calls it too, which stops the title's timer that stock's page init started before the payload bound the lines. Left running, that timer moved the title through the hold and between the clock's frames (seen in the emulator: offsets 3, 42, 5, 0, 45 within 120 ms), which was the snap back. While a pass runs, `ringnav_sleep`'s idle sleep ends by the next frame (`np_marq_wait`). The bar does the same between the player's seconds: stock sets the slider's value once a second, and `paint_scrubber` runs the fill on from it by the time since it changed (at most a second, so it never goes back), with a one-shot repaint for each pixel (`bar_glide`, at least `GLIDE_MIN_MS` apart) and `np_glide_wait` in the idle sleep. Measured in the emulator: the title moves one pixel a frame about every 28.6 ms with no backward step, and the bar one pixel about every 760 ms on a four-minute track. The emulator's shim sleeps 16 ms in every `FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC`, so each paint there takes about 18 ms; a frame due during another paint (the times' each second) arrives that much late, and paints of 80 to 300 ms every second or two on a loaded host skip a few pixels at once.

The info page's Genre line (`genre_fill`) is a private `hscroll_label` at stock's label's place, in the style `s_scrlabel_white16c`, for every value: stock's plain 225-pixel centered label clips a long value at both ends, and stock rewrites it every 250 ms, which would reset an animation on it, so it stays hidden as the value source. The private label's text is set only when the value changes; a value that fits is centered and never moves. A wider one scrolls on `genre_step`, the album marquee's chained timer and pace (`np_marquee`: `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS`, then `MARQUEE_PX` every `MARQUEE_MS` to the end, `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS` there, back to the start), looping while Now Playing is the top window, lit, on its third slide (`view_info`, value 2). Otherwise the chain ends where it is, costing no timer and no repaint, and the next fill restarts it. AWTK's own scroller stays off (`only_focus`, with no focus); `hscroll_label_set_xoffset` moves the text. Stock measures `text_w` when it paints, so the first fill of a new label sees 0 and a later one starts the hold. A new page's `ringnav_playing` ends the last page's chain, since `np_gone` ignores a page already replaced. ponytail: `np_animating` doesn't count this chain, so after 2 s without input the loop's idle passes stretch a step past `MARQUEE_MS` and the line runs a little slower than the album's; counting it would hold the loop at its fast pace for as long as the line moves.

CUE sheets went through the same `toolsIconvConvert(field, "utf-8", "gbk")` in their parser (the unnamed function after `toolsFreeStSongInfo`, seven fields, `CUE_TEXT`): each call is `jal ringnav_cue_text`, which keeps UTF-8 (lead and continuation bytes, nothing overlong, no surrogate), passes GBK (`gbk_text`, as for tags) to stock's conversion, and reads anything else as Windows-1252, the code page Western rippers write, re-encoded in place and cut at a whole character to 511 bytes (the fields' buffers hold at least 512, and their lines 500).

`test/patch.py` runs the patched `toolsFixId3ErrorCode` on accented Latin-1 fields and on a Chinese one, and `ringnav_cue_text` on UTF-8, Windows-1252, overlong and surrogate input.

## English

Q2 Muse runs in English with nothing Chinese left in stock's interface:

- **Strings:** `en_US.bin`'s About row `system_prove` reads Certification (stock: 技术证明), with the other `LABELS`.
- **UI assets:** stock's `.bin` layouts carry Chinese `text` in about 40 of them, designers' placeholders that stock's code mostly replaces, but some shows in every language: Search's tabs (单曲, 歌手, 专辑, 风格), Now Playing's info labels, Folder's and Streaming's titles, Quick Settings' rows, the factory test pages. The build finds every asset with Chinese text (`CJK`) and `english_ui` gives each such `text` in English (`ENGLISH`, with per-asset choices in `ENGLISH_IN`), checking the round trip and that nothing Chinese is left. Layouts the build already rewrote (`patch_asset`) are given English after that.
- **Keyboard:** the T9 keyboard's EN key opened its Chinese pinyin page (`page:chinese`); it is a case key now (ABC on the lowercase page, abc on the capitals), so that page is never reached, and its 《》 key types «».
- **Streaming:** stock's Baidu Netdisk row (a Chinese cloud drive, signed in to from Baidu's app) is removed (`ringnav_stream` destroys the row whose image is `list_baidu`). That row is the only way into Baidu's pages (`baidu/netdisklogin_page`, `netdiskfolder_page`, `netdiskdownload_page`), and stock sends the sign-in's access token to `pan.baidu.com` over plain HTTP, so the boot (`BOOT_HOOK`, `tools/build.py`) also deletes a sign-in stock saved before, `/mnt/data/baidu_token.conf`; only stock's Baidu code reads it.
- **Tags:** [Tag text](#tag-text).

The Language row is hidden (`ringnav_systemset` hides stock's row 0, its page left whole): stock's other twelve string tables (`strings/*.bin`) are untouched, so they lack the relabelled keys and Q2 Muse's own pages stay English in all of them. A unit already set to another language keeps it until Reset. ponytail: no language is forced at boot; show the row again when translations ship.

## Sorting

Every name-sorted library list (artists, album artists, composers, genres, albums and songs: the `group by … COLLATE NOCASE` queries and `sort_first_alphabet`) is sorted in C, not SQL: `toolsQueryDbTable(…, 1)` and `toolsQueryDbTableAndSort` mode 0 pass `algo_sort_if` one of two comparators, `0x5cd188` or, with the flag at `0xa5011d` clear, the pinyin one `0x5cc870`. The `ORDER BY` queries sort by time, sample rate or id, and folders sort by file name in `toolsLoadDirectory`'s own comparators. Both name comparators `snprintf` the row's `+0x10` name into a local buffer and `bal toolsTrimLeft` on it, falling back to the file name when it is empty. Those four calls (`SORT_TRIMS`) become `jal ringnav_sort_key`, which trims and then drops a leading "The ", "A " or "An " (any case) when a name follows, as Apple does; the record is untouched. "Them", "Anthrax" and a bare "The" keep their place, and equal keys ("The Cure", "Cure") stay as stock's `algo_sort_if` leaves them. Coverflow follows this order. Stock has no A–Z jump index; on a `CTX_LOCAL` page iPod's fast-scroll letter skips the same article, and OLED's [A-Z index](#a-z-index) files rows past it too.

## Name order

A name sort costs the most on a large library's open: `algo_sort_if` with stock's comparator makes about 1.5 n log2 n comparisons, each copying both names into buffers, trimming them (`ringnav_sort_key`) and comparing them character by character. In the emulator, on a synthetic library of 20,103 songs, Library > Songs took 3.2-3.6 s from Center's release to the first paint, 2.4-2.7 s of it the sort (865,614 name copies), and it took that on every open: `load_localclass_list` loads the list again each time. With 10,000 server songs beside them (Local + Server) the sort was 1.9-2.0 s of 2.5 s. `patch/name_order.c` sorts those loads itself and keeps the order. `library_query`, on the UI thread (`ui_thread`, `playback_poll`'s), runs a sorted load (`toolsQueryDbTable` with its sort argument, or `toolsQueryDbTableAndSort` in any mode) as `toolsQueryDbTable` with sort 0: the same `sqlite3_exec` and row callback into the same staging deque, no sort. `name_order` then sorts the deque as stock would have, with the same call: `algo_sort_if(deque_begin, deque_end, comparator)` (`cstl_sort`; libcstl's imports, `cstl_iter` the 28-byte iterator they pass by value), the comparator the one stock picks for that sort and `NAME_SORT_FLAG` (`0xa5011d`): `NAME_CMP` or `NAME_CMP_PINYIN` for the name sort, `FILE_NAME_CMP` or `FILE_NAME_CMP_PINYIN` for mode 1, `PATH_CMP` for mode 2. `tools/build.py` reads each from the `lw`/`addiu` pair that loads it in stock (`NAME_COMPARATORS`, checked against demo's GOT at build time) and writes them into `stock.h`. The same records in the same order through the same comparator come out in the same order, equal names included: the order hash of Songs, Albums and Artists (an FNV-1a over the shown ids) was the same on stock's sort and on this one, `d94a25cf`, `8a3d8075` and `b55baf3d` at 20,103 songs, a third of the titles repeated. A list of 512 records or more (`NO_MIN`; below it the sort is a few milliseconds) is sorted on a thread of its own (`spin_sort`; in place when none starts) while the UI thread waits in 20 ms sleeps, and once the sort has run 250 ms (`SPIN_AFTER_MS`) draws a spinner straight onto the shown framebuffer page (`/dev/fb0`, its `FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO` y offset; 320 x 375, 32 bpp, rotated, so a square at the center is one either way): a 64 px `#1c1c1e` square with 12 px corners at the screen's center and eight dots 15 px out, the lit one stepping clockwise every 80 ms with the seven behind it dimmer (`spin_paint`, coverage from squared distances for the edges). What it covers is saved first and put back once the sort is done, before anything else paints: no frame is drawn while the UI thread waits, as none was while stock's sort ran on it. In the emulator the first Songs open at 20,103 songs showed it from about 1.0 s after Center's release to 2.3 s, and the screen under it came back pixel for pixel. Stock's comparators and `ringnav_sort_key` touch only their own buffers, and the UI thread runs nothing else meanwhile. The sorted list is then kept: each record's id in the sorted order, under a key of the query's final text (after every rewrite: the album-artist one, the music filter, the server union, the Library's scope), its sort (`toolsQueryDbTable`'s argument, or `0x100` and `toolsQueryDbTableAndSort`'s mode) and `NAME_SORT_FLAG`, with the count and a hash of the records as they came, in order (`list_hash`: each id and type, and what the comparator reads, the title and file name, or the path for mode 2; FNV-1a 64). Four slots, least recently used first out. The next load of that key whose records hash the same, in RAM or after a reboot, maps each record's id to its kept place and moves the records there whole (`rec_permute`, song_sort.c's cycle walk, their strings with them) instead of sorting. A changed record, a record more or fewer, or the same records in another order (which could settle equal names otherwise) sort again, as does an id not kept or an id twice. Each slot is also a file on the card, `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod/order0` to `order3` (`keep`, written whole through `blob_io`: a temporary file, synced, renamed over): a 32-byte head (`no_head`: a magic, `Q2POD_VERSION`'s hash, as the comparators run `ringnav_sort_key`, the key, the count, the records' hash and a hash of the ids) and the ids. The first sorted load of 512 or more after a boot reads the four heads; a slot's ids are read when a load matches its head, whole or not at all: a short or long file, another magic or version, or ids that do not hash to the head's are dropped, and the load sorts. A Songs open that sorts and keeps writes 80,444 bytes at 20,103 songs, Albums' 8,076. A kept Songs open took 300-330 ms from the load's start to the first paint (from 1.4-1.6 s at the same machine load; 550-610 ms from 2.5 s with the server's songs), Albums' `getAllAlbum` 55-70 ms from 125-135 ms. The first Songs open after a boot, with the order on the card, took 534 ms from the load's start to the first paint (414 ms its query, the card's file read included), against 1,855-2,930 ms sorting on the same build and emulator; Albums' `getAllAlbum` 76 ms against 173-189 ms. A load whose records differ from the kept ones (a scan, a server import or a deletion that changed them) sorts once. ponytail: the card's heads are read once a boot, so a card inserted after the first sorted load is not read until the next boot; the file is written on the UI thread after the sort, 80 KB at 20,000 songs on the card's write speed.

## Unknown rows

`load_localclass_list` (`0x51357c`) runs the class's query into `tools_pdeq_directory`, `deque_assign`s it to `*p_deque_showlist`, clears the staging deque and returns `deque_size(*p_deque_showlist)`, which its callers take as the row count (Playlists, `0xf00b`, and Baidu's `0xff26` fill their own deque and return its size). For `0xf003`–`0xf006` the query is `getAllAlbum`, `getAllArtist` (`GetAllAlbumArtist` when `g_artist_type == 1`), `getAllComposer` or `getAllGenre`, and each appends an Unknown row (id -1) whenever the list has any rows (`getAllArtist` `0x508034`: type 4, the "Unknown Artist" string), even when every song carries the tag. `ringnav_localclass` runs stock, and when that class's last row has id -1 it runs the query the row's press would run (`class_query`, shared with the [Queue menu](#queue-menu): `getMusicBySonger(NULL)` and its kin, `where songer=""`). With no song it `deque_pop_back`s the row and returns one less. Whether a song exists is all it asks, so `ringnav_localclass` sets `library_first` around that call and `library_query` ends the scoped query with `limit 1`: stock puts one record in the staging deque, not every song without the tag, and SQLite stops at that song. Once a full scan has added `songtable_album_exact` and `songtable_artist` ([Coverflow](#coverflow), Indexes), the album and album-artist checks are an index search; ponytail: the composer and genre checks still scan `songtable` up to the first such song, and all of it when every song has the tag. The Queue menu's query on the same row (`qm_query`) still takes every song. The staging deque is cleared again, as stock leaves it. Coverflow builds its own album list and drops an empty Unknown card the same way (`drop_unknown`), but its query has no limit.
