A list with no rows at all (no card, an empty library): `empty_class`, from a 0 ms timer so the page that loads it is up, closes that page (`album_page` or `localclass_page` on top with `g_class_type` the list's class) once the window manager has marked it opened (its `stage` property `WINDOW_STAGE_OPENED`, set after the open animation; the close path reads the same at `0x69d218`) with `window_manager_close_window_force`, polling every `EMPTY_POLL_MS` until then or until it stops being on top, then opens the empty state's page (`empty_class`, `feedback.c` `empty_open`: `empty_page`, titled Albums, Artists, Composers or Genres, "No Albums" and so on, or "No SD Card" with no card in). Stock opened the black page, and an empty Albums grid's Return then did nothing until a restart, though Hold Return: Home's `back_to_home` left it; where its `window_close` went was not found, so no Return reaches that page now. A page that is no longer on top, or is another, keeps the toast alone.

## Shuffle

`localmusic_page_init` (`0x535334`) destroys `scroll_view_localmusic`'s children and builds 11 rows (`0x535508`), each button named by its index; the shared row click (`0x53510c`) `atoi`s that name into a switch. Stock's rows, by index (`get_localmusic_showinfo`, `0x50bf30`), are Update Local Music, All Songs, Album, Artist, Genre, Hi-Res, My Fav, Frequent, Recent, Recently Added and Playlist. The hook runs stock through `stock_localmusic_trampoline`, appends its own rows in the same widgets and styles (`list_row`, also Display settings'; `library_into` adds stock's `list_into` chevron), then tags every row with its letter and `widget_restack`s them into the saved order ([Library order](#library-order)), by default the menu review's (2026-11-15): Shuffle (hidden), All Songs, Playlist, Artist, Album, Search, Genre, Years (see [Era](#era)), Ratings (My Fav hidden after it, see [Ratings](#ratings)); Recently Added, Recent, Most Played, Frequent (hidden: Most Played lists the same from every listen), Hi-Res (hidden), Long Songs (hidden); the media rows; Games; Upload Scrobbles (hidden); Update Local Music last. A hidden row is built and kept in its place, as My Fav is, so a later build that shows it again finds it there; nothing on the Q2 shows it. A page that doesn't hold exactly 11 rows is left as stock built it. The added buttons have no name, so stock's click never sees them. The Shuffle row carries the `local_shuffle` icon, a build-added copy of stock's 52 px `playset_playmode`, which iPod pre-sizes to 40 px for Settings, and opens `shuffle_page`, a runtime page (`page_list` and `page_row_detail`, as Most Played's). Its Shuffle Songs row runs `getAllMusic(3)` (`0x5079cc`, no title sort) through `staged`, scoped to music as the Library's Artists and Albums are (`MUSIC_WHERE`, see [Podcasts and Audiobooks](#podcasts-and-audiobooks)), saves shuffle with `config_playmode(2, 1)` (`0x4fe718`, as the play-mode setting does), clears advanced play (`playback_clear`, so stock Shuffle's keep-the-groups rule below doesn't rebuild group shuffle), and folder-plays the copy from `rand_below(n)` as Coverflow does with `toolsRandnum` (`0x5cc71c`). Shuffle Songs is one-shot: `playback_unshuffle` takes the stock mode it replaces (or the one an earlier Shuffle Songs still holds), and when the next other queue loads, `ringnav_load` applies it with `config_playmode` before stock does, ending the advanced shuffle; a mode choice in between (`ringnav_mode`) is kept instead, and a reboot mid-shuffle keeps Shuffle, as the mode is held in RAM only. Its Shuffle Albums and Shuffle Folders rows run `playback_groups(all, 0|1)`. Picks leave the page open for another, and a note under the rows says albums and folders take a moment to shuffle. A resume after reboot therefore reloads the last track's folder, not the library. An empty library shows "Update Local Music first". **Most Played** uses `local_frequentplay`, the icon of stock's Frequent; see [Play counts](#play-counts). **Upload Scrobbles** shows with an account set up; see [Scrobbling](#scrobbling). **Podcasts**, **Audiobooks** and **Videos** show with their folders; see [Podcasts and Audiobooks](#podcasts-and-audiobooks) and [Videos](#videos).

## Library order

The Library's rows go in the order the user last left in Edit Library (`patch/library_edit.c`; the theme's side is [oled-design](oled-design.md#edit-library)). `lr_default` is the one table of the default order: each row's letter (Search `S`, Shuffle `h`, Artists `a` and so on, its comment lists them), in the order the rows take with nothing saved. `ringnav_localmusic` (`patch/home.c`) builds every row, stock's and the payload's, tags each with its letter (`lr_put`, the `_lr_code` property) and restacks them in the saved order (`lr_apply`); Home's Library list, built by the same function, follows. The order is `/mnt/data/ringnav-library-order`: the letters in order, each led by `+` or `-` once the user has shown or hidden that row (below), NUL-ended in 64 bytes, written whole through `blob_io` (a `.tmp` beside it, `fsync`ed, renamed over it), so a power cut leaves the old order or the new one, never half of either; a missing or short file reads as nothing saved. `lr_resolve` reads it against `lr_default`: a letter it doesn't know, or one it has already seen, is dropped, and every row it doesn't name, one a later firmware adds, goes in at its default place, straight after the nearest row before it in `lr_default` that the saved order has (first if none), so new rows in a run keep their default order and the user's order is kept. A change to the default order is a change to `lr_default` alone; a new row takes a new letter, never one used before. Saving (`lr_save`) reads the shown rows' letters in the view's order and puts them in the places those rows held in the saved order (`lr_merge`): a row the editor doesn't list (My Fav and Frequent, always; Search or a media row when absent) is neither shown nor moved, and keeps its place.

**Which rows show.** Each row's visibility is Auto, Shown or Hidden. Auto, no mark in the file, leaves it to the row's own rule, its `_lr_auto` property: shown (`lr_put`'s default), hidden until the user shows it (`lr_auto_hide`: Shuffle, Hi-Res, Long Songs and Upload Scrobbles, the menu review's), or never listed (`lr_retire`: My Fav and Frequent, which Ratings and Most Played replace). Shown (`+`) and Hidden (`-`) are the user's and stick whatever the rule says (`lr_shows`); Home's Settings is locked shown, a mark or none. `lr_resolve_in` reads the marks into one byte a row by its place in the default order, a mark before a letter it doesn't know going with that letter; a firmware from before the marks reads them as unknown letters and drops them, so its order is kept. `lr_apply` shows each tagged row as its mark and rule say. In the editor every row with a rule shows, a hidden one's text in Text Tertiary (`lr_edit_dim`, from `ringnav_style_color`), and Play/Pause's release (`lr_edit_key`; not a release that ends a hold, `play_hold_released`, and the hold itself does nothing there, `ringnav_keylong`) or a tap in the first `LR_VIS_ZONE` (52) columns (`lr_edit_click`, with the press's x from `lr_edit_touch`, which starts no hold there) flips the selected row from how it shows now to the other, the user's from then on (`lr_toggle`), and saves. Leaving the editor (`lr_leave`, `lr_show`) hides the hidden rows again and keeps the selection on its row, or the next one shown if it went. Each row's words move right of its circle while the editor is open (`lr_edit_labels`: to x 52 on screen, their right end kept, and back after).

**Home.** Home's main list (`tools/ipod.py` `HOME_ROWS`) has its own order and visibility, `/mnt/data/ringnav-home-order` against `lr_home` (`plsfcqS`: Now Playing, Library, Streaming, Folders, Cover Flow, Search, Settings), its rows tagged by their names when Home is made (`lr_home_tag`, from `coverflow_home`). `coverflow_home_layout` calls `lr_home_apply` where it used to place Now Playing alone: the rows in the saved order, each shown as its mark and rule say, Now Playing only while something is loaded (its Shown cannot show it with nothing to play), and the hidden rows restacked last, as the list's layout keeps a hidden row's slot. Folders' rule (`home_folders`, `patch/home.c`) is the empty Folders page's test: stock's listing of the card's root (`toolsLoadDirectory` of `/mnt/mmc`, which leaves out what stock hides) holds a row. It is read again only when `/tmp/mmc_add` or the root's `st_dev` and `st_mtime` change, never during a library scan (which fills the same deque), and `coverflow_home_np` (each bar paint) asks only while Home is on top, laying Home out again when the answer changes; the card and its root are looked at again at most every `CARD_RECHECK_MS` (5 s), or at once when a library scan has rewritten the library (`library_gen`), not on every paint. The status row's Rockbox and Groovebox checks (`rockbox_seen`, `groovebox_seen` in `patch/theme_engine.c`, for `bar_sync` and `shortcut`) are kept the same way, and looked at again at once after the Shelf installs or removes an app (`card_bins_changed`); stat'ing them on each paint cost Now Playing about 150 syscalls a second. A card's mount, removal or new root folder shows on Home up to 5 s late, as `logo_poll`'s mount edge already does. Each row that comes or goes calls `home_keep` with its place among the shown rows, which keeps the selected row selected (`COUNT` moved with it, so the list's load doesn't start the selection over) and the rows in view, as Now Playing's coming and going always did. Edit Home is Edit Library on that list: `lr_view_of` takes Home's main list from `coverflow_home_edit_view` (Home on top, its main list shown, not Carousel), the status row reads Edit Home (`bar_title_sync`), `paint_chevrons` leaves the list's chevrons to the grips (`lr_edit_list`), and while it is open `ipod_home` answers Full for Split, so the list spans the screen under the hint and the art is hidden; Settings' circle is locked. Its lift's abort goes to the row's last child, Home's tap image (the Library's button is its only one).

**Edit Library**: on `localmusic_page`, Center's press (`ringnav_keydown` calls `lr_edit_keydown`) starts a `LR_HOLD_MS` (550 ms) timer; released sooner, the press is a row's click as before. When it goes off, Edit Library starts (or, in it, saves and ends), stock's own Center hold timer (`st.centre_hold`, Shut Down? at 1000 ms) is removed, and the release is taken (`lr_edit_key`, in `ringnav` before stock's key-up), with stock's wheel lockout (`KEY_LOCKOUT`) cleared so the wheel moves at once. In it the status row reads Edit Library (`bar_title_of` with `lr_edit_title`, refreshed with `title_gone` and `bar_title_sync`), `paint_into` draws no chevron on a Library row (`lr_edit_row`), and `lr_edit_paint` draws the rest (`list_marks.c` `grip_mark`, `check_circle`, `lift_card_paint`), clipped in screen coordinates within the paint's own clip (`clip_within`). From the rows' view's paint, before the list's fades go over it (`row_paint.c` `list_fade`, `home.c` `home_fades`), each row's grip where its chevron was and its check circle at its left, in the view's whole box, so a scrolled list's top row and the rows past its end fade with their marks; from the page's border paint, after everything, the hint's band (the ground from `LR_FOOT`), the hint, and the lifted row's card over all of it. The card is the selection bar's box (`LR_CARD_X`, 16 px in each side), `LR_LIFT` (108%) of the row's height about its middle, and its circle, grip and words (Inter Medium at the row's 20 px, from the label's own `LR_LABEL_PAD` margin) are drawn where the row's own stand, so a lift changes the row's look and moves nothing (the user, 2026-11-16, from the device: the card had grown 8% to x 2 to 372, its marks and words moving out with it). While the editor is open its list ends `LR_ROOM` (a row, 32 px) higher than the set's list end, so the hint sits under the rows with the room a list has above the screen's foot: `lr_edit_room` takes it off `navigation.c` `sel_height` (where a selected row stops), `list_fade`'s end and `home_rest` (Home's rows at rest: six in Edit Home, which then scrolls), and `lr_edit_foot` moves the fades' ground from y 316 to `LR_FOOT` (284), the band's top, as far below the raised end as 316 is below 282. Center lifts the selected row (`SEL`, its place among the shown rows) and puts it down again, saving; a tick of the wheel while one is lifted moves it a place (`lr_move`: restacked before the row it passes, which `widget_layout` lays out; it stops at either end) and selects it, clicking as a row change does when the press was silenced; Return while one is lifted restacks it at the child index it had when lifted, which puts it back exactly, as only it moved; Return otherwise saves and ends. A held Return's release (its latch set) is stock's: it leaves for Home, and the page's close ends Edit Library. The rows a moved row passes slide over `LR_SLIDE_MS` (150 ms, cubic out, a frame every `LR_STEP_MS`): `lr_place` notes where each row shows, restacks and lays out, then puts each back where it showed and moves its `W_Y` towards its new place each frame; the moved row itself goes at once.

**Touch.** `ringnav_touch` hands a press on the Library page under OLED to `lr_edit_touch` after stock's. On a row it starts the same timer, which a move past `LR_SLOP` (8 px) or a lift stops (the page's move-before, up-before and abort, bound once a page, `lr_event`); when it goes off, Edit Library starts if it hasn't and the finger takes the row (`lr_grab`). In Edit Library a press in the last `LR_GRIP_ZONE` (64) columns, on the grips, takes its row at once. Taking a row at a hold's end dispatches `EVT_POINTER_ABORT` through the page so the rows let go of the press, as the A-Z index does, and ends the pull to search the press began (`pull_cancel`); a press on a grip is taken before stock hands the press to the rows (`ringnav_touch` runs first), so the lift sends the abort to that row's button alone (`stock_dispatch_trampoline`): an abort through the page also reaches the scroll view, which then glides back to the offset it was pressed at, undoing the drag's edge scroll (seen in the emulator: its animator set straight after the abort, the list back at its top); from then the page's moves and lift stop at `lr_event` (`STOP`), and `ringnav_touch` passes moves straight to stock while `lr_edit_dragging`. `widget_to_local` on the view gives its content's coordinates, its scroll counted. The row's top follows the finger, kept within the list's box on the screen (never over the status row or the hint) and within the rows, and it takes the place its middle is over; within `LR_EDGE` (16) px of the list's top or bottom (the view's top to the set's list end) the list scrolls `LR_SCROLL_PX` (8) every `LR_SCROLL_MS` (40) while the finger stays. The lift slides the row into its place and saves. A tap in Edit Library selects its row and opens nothing (`lr_edit_click`, in `ringnav_dispatch`'s click observer).

## Coverflow depth

The shelf and caption values below are the theme's `cfs` (see Themes). Coverflow draws its covers in software, after Rockbox PictureFlow's renderer: the selected cover faces the viewer at its native 160 pixels, its neighbours are turned inward, pushed back and dimmed, and each has a reflection. Where the side covers stand is the iPod preset of the Cover Flow Parameter Lab in [#329](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/issues/329) (spghetti), in OLED: the lab's selected cover is 1000 units wide and the Q2's 160 px, so its numbers times 0.16, with the selected cover's pull forward (`front`) taken off the camera's distance and added to the side covers' depth, since the Q2's selected cover is the plane at its native size. `eye` (1650 - 50) × 0.16 = 256, `tilt` 90, `x1` 800 × 0.16 = 128, `xs` 220 × 0.16 = 35, `z1` (430 + 50) × 0.16 = 77, `zs` 0, and `horizon` 64: the lab's vanishing point is 34 px under the middle of its 250 px cover, 63.6% down it. Until 1.8.1 the side covers turned 60 degrees (`eye` 300, `x1` 112, `xs` 48, `z1` 90, `zs` 20, `horizon` 50). `patch/coverflow.c` owns the drawing; the stock `slide_menu` stays the navigation and animation controller, so the wheel (one retargeted animator, 200 ms or 120 ms fast, reversal), wrapping, center, the saved album and track positions all work as before. Touch is the payload's own (below): the `slide_menu` stays insensitive, so stock's drag and throw never run. Tunables are `coverflow.shelf` in OLED's `theme.xml` (the shelf's geometry and the thumb) and `CF_*` in `patch/offsets.inc`; adjust them together.

**Layout.** With depth the `slide_menu` spans the frame, 375 × `view_h` (`CF_VIEW_W`; `coverflow.shelf.view_h`, 220 by default as `CF_VIEW_H`, `CF_TOP` + 160 + `CF_REFLECT` and a row; OLED's `coverflow.shelf.reflect_top` is 0, so each reflection is the page's own color and none shows, and its caption, at `text_y` 173, has the artist's box `artist_y` 27 px under the album's, baselines 24 px apart and the artist's on y 277 on screen, so its tails (p, y, g, q) end on the lists' end, y 282) at the top of the page, so every animator step invalidates all of it. Its items stay `h` square (`view_h`), and `slide_menu_set_spacer` (a store at `+0x84` and an invalidate) sets the spacer to `CF_STRIDE - view_h`, so the stride that stock scroll, completion and ringnav's wheel steps use (item width plus spacer) is `CF_STRIDE` (110 px). The children are `image` widgets with no image, so stock paints nothing under the frame. The album and artist captions sit under the covers at `CF_TEXT_Y`, over the reflections' faint tail, and follow the center cover: when the album `coverflow_paint` drew in the middle changes, a zero-delay timer (`retitle`, never text set inside the paint) names it, once per change; `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED`, when a move commits, writes them again.

**Position.** `ringnav_paint`, the border hook, calls `coverflow_paint` for every widget after stock has painted it; only Coverflow's `slide_menu` on the covers screen draws. The visual position is the index less the live offset over the stride (stock completion commits `index - offset / stride`): center album `c` and `frac`, 16.16, in `[-1/2, 1/2)`. Every cover's rotation, place, depth, brightness and reflection come from that one continuous value, so an incoming side cover unfolds into the center as the outgoing one turns away.

**Projection.** All integer (the stock build is `-mfp64`, and integer arithmetic is also cheaper here). A cover `t` albums from the position gets a rotation that grows linearly to `tilt` at one album (a 17-entry sine table to `CF_ANGLE`, 60 degrees, and a second to 90 for any other tilt, OLED's among them), a center `x` that reaches `x1` then steps `xs` per album, a depth that reaches `z1` then `zs` per album, and a brightness of 256 at the center, `CF_BRIGHT1` (75%) one out, `CF_BRIGHT2` (50%) two out, and 0 three out unless `third`, so covers fade in and out at the edge of reach. A theme can turn its covers another way: `coverflow.shelf.tilt` other than 60 reads a second table, 0 to 90 degrees, stepped by the same interpolation. `horizon` puts the shared horizon that percentage down the cover (50 by default), and `third` (`CF_THIRD`, on in OLED) keeps every cover from the second out at `bright2`. Still (nothing moving: no thumb on the covers, no glide or step animating, no finger on them; `coverflow_paint` passes it, `cf_still`), the shelf draws the seven it always has, the same bytes. Moving, it draws all of the ring (`shelf_draws`), so the cover coming in at either edge is whole from its first pixel, its reflection too. A move's frame on a whole album is a moving one, and the frame is drawn again when the covers stop; a tap hits only the covers the frame on the screen draws (`coverflow_hit`, `fx_still`). The fold lands on the still shelf: its covers past the third out fade to nothing on the fold's ease, as they always have. With no thumb the ring is seven, and the third cover out is gone by half a step past it, so the ring's reach ends it without a pop (with `third` 0 it vanished as the covers came to rest). `swing` changes only the path between center and first slot. At 0 `x` is quadratic up to one album, so the two covers turning mid-step keep clear of each other on a 60 degree shelf; at 2, OLED's, it goes straight out as the cover turns, as the lab's does. 1 is for a near edge that would otherwise balloon on a short eye (not OLED's): depth follows the sine of the turn, less `lift` px at most mid-way, and the near edge's screen x is two parabolas meeting flat at 45% of the way, 3 px past its rest place (`cf_rest16`, with the sine at one album `cf_s1`, cached by `cf_restyle`), with `xc` derived from it, so the cover swings on its outer edge with no corner in the path. Every other reader (`unproject`, `coverflow_hit`, the reflection) reads the pose, and at whole albums the pose is the one without it. Left covers mirror right ones about the center line (between columns 186 and 187). For each screen column the renderer inverts the perspective (eye `eye` px away) to the cover column under it and the cover's projected height there, then steps down the texture column, top and bottom rows weighted by coverage. Only those two rows can step off the art, so only they clamp the texture row; at full brightness (the center cover) a texel goes in unshaded. At rest the selected cover is its texture pixel for pixel. Below each cover its reflection is the column mirrored, `CF_REFLECT` rows at native size scaled by perspective, from `CF_REFLECT_TOP` of its brightness down to nothing: no blur or glow. By default it is 46 rows from 90/256 (35%); OLED's `reflect_top` 0 starts it at none, so no reflection shows.

**Compositing.** The frame is drawn nearest cover first: each pixel's alpha byte holds the coverage so far and every layer fills only what is left, which composites as drawing back to front would, and per column a span of rows known to be opaque is skipped outright, so hidden parts of side covers cost nothing. A last pass makes every pixel opaque over black. The hit test walks the same order, nearest first, over cover bodies only.

**Frame and textures.** One `bitmap_create_ex(375, view_h, 1500, 3)` (`coverflow.shelf.view_h`, 220 by default; BGRA8888, the screen's format; `bitmap_t` is 0x48 bytes, flags `u16 @0xc`, format `u16 @0xe`, buffer `@0x14`) is created with the covers and marked `BITMAP_FLAG_OPAQUE` (bit 0, as `bitmap_init_from_rgba` sets it for opaque images); `bitmap_lock_buffer_for_write`/`bitmap_unlock_buffer` bracket each render and `canvas_draw_image(canvas, bitmap, src, dst)` (`0x6487c4`, `dst` relative to the canvas origin, which is the `slide_menu`'s) draws it 1:1. Stock's `lcd_mem_draw_image` (`0x6a6884`) copies an image whose format is the lcd's, opaque, unscaled, under a global alpha of at least 250, with `image_copy` (`0x688f18`: a `memcpy` a row; the lcd is turned without fast portrait, so not `image_rotate_ex`), and blends any other with `image_blend`, about 39 instructions a pixel against 3 (`opaque_frame`). The renderer works in the textures' order (RGBA8888, red low) and its last pass, which makes every pixel opaque, swaps R and B; the alpha stays `0xff`, as stock's later blends and Night Shift read it from the screen. It is re-rendered only when the position or a texture changes; a repaint in place only draws. Textures come from the existing JPEG cache: `widget_load_image`, `bitmap_lock_buffer_for_read` and `bitmap_unlock_buffer` read the decoded image (the stock loader, `stb_load_image` called with RGBA8888 for both formats at `0x69467c`, never premultiplies), fitted whole and centered (a non-square cover between black bars), sampled to 160 × 160 over black into the payload's own buffer, and the load is dropped at once with `widget_unload_image`, as stock cover rows do; the image manager's copy is only read. `fx_base()` slots hold the covers nearest the position, seven (`CF_RING`, within three albums) or 15 under a thumb theme (`CF_WIDE`, **Textures.** below); as movement crosses an album the one leaving is dropped and the one entering is decoded. A small library repeats round the ring as the `slide_menu` wraps, each album decoded once. Missing art and a card (an artist's All albums, the rated albums' Sort) use `default_album_flow`, a 160px copy of Home's disc resized with Lanczos at build time and decoded 1:1. Both are decoded once and left in the manager's cache as theme images. iPod clips each cover column to rounded corners at the Now Playing radius ratio (12/166), including the mirrored bottom in its reflection; the insets are computed once, with no alpha processing in the pixel loop. The frame and the textures (`fx_base()`'s and the placeholder: 16 under a thumb theme, every built-in's, about 1.6 MB) are allocated together when the covers are built; if either fails, Coverflow keeps the flat stock covers exactly as before. Closing the page destroys the frame and frees the textures.

**iPod artwork.** Home's 290px disc is the master placeholder for album rows, Now Playing, the full-screen art and AirPlay, pre-sized at build time to each stock asset's dimensions, keeping the disc's transparent corners so a selected row's bar shows through them (Now Playing's to the 166px art it fills; the full-screen `default_bigcover` to its `BC_ART` square, the centered art clear of the glass). The artist-person icon keeps its stock image. Library thumbnails (`file:///mnt/mmc/.sldp/`) get rounded alpha at radius min(width, height) × 12/166 in `ringnav_image_add`, before the image manager caches them. The hook clears the cached opacity flag and keeps straight RGB, so stock can blend the corners over wallpaper or selection panels. Alpha is clamped to arc coverage, making reuse idempotent. Stock's temporary playing covers (`coverpic.jpg`, `externpic.jpg`, `album_tidal.jpg` in `/tmp`) are not: Now Playing, Spotify and the full-screen art round them after scaling, in `paint_cover`; Home's Split art is cropped past its corners.

<a id="coverflow-touch"></a>**Touch.** The covers' view takes `EVT_POINTER_DOWN`, and the page (`open_page`) the move, the release and `EVT_POINTER_ABORT`, so a release off the covers still ends the touch (`touch`); the payload moves `SLIDE_OFFSET` itself and finishes through `carousel_glide` (`patch/navigation.c`), the wheel's one retargeted animator split out of `home_step`, with the run's easing set on the animator (`ANIM_EASING`, `+0x38`: `widget_animator_init` stores `easing_get(type)` there, so a reused animator would keep its first). Every finish commits through stock's completion as a wheel step does. On an album's tracks the view is hidden and made insensitive: stock's hit test (`widget_find_target_default`, `0x67d21c`) checks only the enable and sensitive bits (`+0x24` mask 9), not visibility, so a hidden covers' view over the list would take its taps and swipes.

- **Drag.** A move past `CF_SLOP` (8 px) more sideways than up or down is the covers'; one more up or down leaves the touch to stock (the Quick Settings pull-down). From there the offset follows the finger, one album per `CF_DRAG_PX` (90 px, about the center cover's own travel on screen), starting where it passed the slop so nothing jumps. An artist's albums give past an end as iOS's rubber band, `x · 0.55 / (1 + x · 0.55 / D)` with `D` two fifths of a stride, so the center never passes half a cover, where `visual` would wrap to the other end. A touch catching the band (or a wheel bounce) starts from its inverse (`unbound`), so the shelf doesn't jump.
- **Release.** The finger's speed is taken over its last 100 ms of moves, by each event's post time (`EVENT_TIME`; moves queued behind a frame are dispatched together) (0 if it rested `CF_STILL_MS`, 60 ms, before lifting; at most `CF_VMAX`, 6000 px/s, so a burst of queued moves can't throw the shelf). The covers glide to the whole cover that speed reaches in `CF_PROJECT_MS` (400 ms), and a flick of at least `CF_FLICK` (250 px/s) never settles back against its direction. The glide is `cubic_out` (`EASE_CUBIC_OUT`, AWTK's `easing_type_t` 5) for `3 d / v` whenever the goal lies ahead of the finger's motion, so it starts at the finger's speed and decelerates, between `CF_SETTLE_MS` (280 ms, also a still release or one that settles back) and `CF_GLIDE_MAX` (1.4 s); an artist's ends clamp it.
- **Tap.** A touch that never passed the slop hit-tests the drawn frame (`coverflow_hit`): the frontmost cover body under the finger, nearest first as drawn, rounded corners (`cf_inset`, where the arc crosses each texel column's middle) and reflections left out, and no cover under a quarter bright. The center cover at rest opens, as Center's click; a side cover glides to the center with the wheel's easing in `CF_TAP_MS` (320 ms). The flat fallback opens its center cover only.
- **Catch.** A touch while the covers move pauses the animator where they are. Lifting without a drag settles on the nearest cover and opens nothing; a drag carries on from there. A down while a touch is still open (a release the input queue dropped), or any key with the window manager no longer pressed (`coverflow_lost_touch`, in `ringnav`), ends the old one first, so Center opens the cover the shelf settles on; a touch ending after Center changed the screen still settles the covers on a whole one, and covers built anew drop it.

ponytail: no MIPS run of the gesture: `test/coverflow.py` drives the C on the host (`-m32`), and `test/patch.py` checks the MIPS renderer byte for byte. The drag scale, reach and glide lengths are `CF_*` in `patch/offsets.inc`, set by eye.

**Checks.** `test/coverflow.py` builds the renderer on the host and checks the selected cover pixel for pixel, that nothing is drawn outside the frame, mirror symmetry at rest and mid-turn, brightness one and two out, the reflection's rows and fade, that a small step changes little (including where the center album changes hands), the texture window's loads and releases, the center click, touch (the hit test against every drawn pixel at eight positions, taps, drags, flicks, a flick dispatched in one batch, a resting release, a vertical move, a catch and a dropped release), going by letters (`thumb_letters_held`: letters held through a slow turn, a still thumb and a turn back; `letters_entry` and `enter_frames`: the entry, with no cover turning and no hole opening; `held_row`: the held row's geometry, the formed row's, with no cover turning; `entry_handover`: no art change and no stop across the first letter; `fold_flow` and `fold_frames`: the fold's landing, its frames and paint order; `lift_handoff`: the lift's hand-off at `fold_near`; `fold_clearance`: every two covers kept clear), the arch (`arch`: its poses in every built-in theme, none nearer the eye than the side covers, and the follower forming it only at speed, with Fast Navigation off), one- and two-album libraries, missing art, Refresh, return from tracks and the allocation-failure fallback; `--captures DIR` writes the renderer's frames at rest and a quarter, half and three-quarter turn as PNGs. `test/patch.py` runs the MIPS payload's renderer against the host build byte for byte, and the page's paint, center click and fallback, and prints the payload's instructions per frame (about 3.5 million for a frame mid-turn under the mocks): a relative measure, not a frame time.

## Coverflow step

Cover Flow's two steps may name `easing="follow"` (`EASE_FOLLOW`, one past AWTK's 24 names), and `tools/theme.py` refuses it on any other kind: `easing_get` has no such id and a window's `anim_hint` no such name. Under it the row's `ms` is a time constant, 81 ms, and the run's length comes from the distance. Other themes, the carousel and touch's release and tap keep their easings.

**The curve.** A critically damped follow of the goal: a tick only moves the goal, so the speed carries on through it, and nothing overshoots. Over `s` time constants a run `d` px long leaves `(d + (d - v tau) s) e^-s` to go, `v` being the speed it started with. The share is `1 - (1 + a s) e^-s`, with `a = 1 - v tau / d`, floored at 0 for a goal right ahead of a cover too fast to stop for it. `coverflow_follow_aim` takes the speed from the last run at `ANIM_ELAPSED`, only when the animator's easing is still the follow (a touch's glide gives a start from rest), and returns the run's ms, until within half a px of the goal.

**The animator stays.** `carousel_glide` sets `ANIM_EASING` to `coverflow_follow` after `scroll_create`, which gets `linear`, so `ANIM_X_TO`, `EVT_ANIM_END` and `home_done` work as for any step. `widget_animator_time_elapse` (`0x679684`) calls the easing with `$25` set, `k` in `$f12` clamped to 1, and passes `$f0` to the update (`+0x3c`, `0x6954e0`), which writes `from + (to - from) p` truncated to whole px. That's AWTK's `float_t` as a plain single in this `-mfp64` build, so the easing is a float C function. It returns exactly 1 at `k` 1, so the truncated offset's last move is one whole px at most.

**The pose.** `coverflow.shelf.eye_turn` (0 in every built-in theme since the shelf became #329's) draws the eye back mid-turn by `eye_turn (1 - t^4)` px, in `pose()`, kept per cover in `pose_t.eye` for `project()`, `unproject()` and so `coverflow_hit`. Depth moves with it, which holds the near edge's place and height and lengthens the far edge. At `t` 0 and 1 no pixel moves, so rest poses are the same bytes.

**Frame gaps (`--dev`).** Each painted frame of a run goes to a ring in RAM, and at the first paint after the run to `/tmp/q2-cf-gaps.log`, if `/tmp/q2-cf-gaps.on` exists (off by default). `python3 tools/q2remote.py sh 'touch /tmp/q2-cf-gaps.on'`, turn the wheel, then `sh 'cat /tmp/q2-cf-gaps.log'`. Each run is a `== run` line, then a row a frame, all in ms: `gap`, since the frame before (a run's first row counts from the last run); `decode`, spent in `fx_ring` loading textures; `render`, spent in `coverflow_render`; then `offset`, the px when it was painted. The last row is the frame after commit. The crossing is where `offset` passes half a stride: a `decode` near that row's `gap`, with `gap` well over its neighbours, says the decode stalls the step. A big `gap` on the last row alone points at the commit.

## Coverflow thumb

OLED's covers are held by the thumb: `coverflow.shelf.thumb` is 1 and every number below is an attribute of that element, so retuning on the wheel needs no C change. The carousel isn't the covers' page, so `coverflow_wheel_poll` never takes the wheel there and it stays on ticks and the animator, as it does on the covers' page whenever the thumb isn't shown (a finger on the screen, the page sliding). A theme with `thumb` 0 is on ticks throughout, letters after `CF_FIRST_MS`.

**The wheel.** `thumb_poll` (`ringnav_sleep`, before `lyric_poll`) calls `coverflow_wheel_poll`. The wheel is raw only with the covers' page on top, not animating, `usable()` and no finger on the screen, and that's decided afresh each pass, so no way off the page can leave `wheel_raw` set. It's `WHEEL_THUMB` (2), not the `WHEEL_RAW` (1) of the lyrics and Vortex, for one reason below; each of the two pollers gives the wheel back only if the value is still its own, so neither clobbers the other's in the pass the wheel changes hands. A still thumb sends no frames, for seconds, so a gap in frames is never a lift: the thumb is `wheel_held`. `contact_ms` debounces it each way: a shorter contact is ignored with its travel, and a shorter lift changes nothing. A press only anchors (`wheel_sample`). Shake of `dead` units moves nothing. If a lift is lost (a known case: a thumb on the ring and a screen tap), `hold_ms` covers it.

**The goal.** A tick is `200 / ticks_turn` units at 50% Wheel Sensitivity, and `th_turn` scales the travel by `wheel_pct()`, so 100% has twice the ticks a turn. Every tick count and rate below (`ticks_album`, `fast_at`, `fast_full`, `jump_ticks`) is in those sensitivity-scaled ticks. `r` is the thumb's rate in ticks a second, filtered `rate_up` ms rising, `rate_down` falling. `speed = slow r + max(0, top_speed - slow r) smoothstep((r - fast_at) / (fast_full - fast_at))`, `slow = 1 / ticks_album`, and the goal moves `min(max(slow, speed / r), top_speed / max(r, r_pass))` a tick, `r_pass` being this pass's own rate, over a frame (`TH_FRAME_MS`, 16 ms) at least, so a pass a millisecond or two after the last doesn't read its ticks as a huge rate and throw them away. OLED's 36, 7, 23 and 90 make a slow album 39 units at 50% (70 degrees) and 19 at 100%, and the speed reaches `top_speed`, 20 albums a second, at 90 ticks a second: 2.5 turns a second at 50%, 1.25 at 100%. The cap holds at every sensitivity: without it, past `top_speed ticks_album` ticks a second the slow share alone would outrun it (31 to 62 albums a second at 100-200%), and while `r` is still rising to a quick spin's, `r_pass` keeps the share from overshooting. Turning back drops the goal to within `back` of the position, and `r` to 0.

**Letters, Fast Navigation off.** Fast Navigation is Display → Cover Flow's switch (`Q2POD BIGLIBRARY`, `ringnav_big_library`: the key and the code keep its first name, Big Library Mode; it was Large Library Mode until 1.8.1), off unless it is 1, read at once when the row changes it. Off, the letters are 1.7.6's (`th_beat`, `th.beat`), and nothing below them is used: no held row, entry or fold, no letters' slots, loader or half copies, and Year has no groups. The page holds 1.7.6's 16 textures either way; turned on with the page open, the half copies start at once. Loading is 1.7.6's too: `FX_DECODES` (two) a frame, and the row at speed draws and loads 1.7.6's window, round the facing cover (`row_window`). With `r` at `jump_at` for `jump_ms`, the spin goes by letters. The count stops at `jump_ms` and any pass under `jump_at` takes its ms off it, so a dip costs only its own time and speeding back up refills only that; a turn back drops it. A letter has no motion of its own: travel moves the goal and the covers follow exactly as on any fast turn, so the speed, the lead and the row's shape all go on. Each `jump_ticks` of travel, the first at once, none sooner than `jump_pace` (140 ms) after the last and only while the covers move over 4 albums a second (`th_moving`), `th_name_letter` asks `coverflow_letter_next` for the first album of the letter after the last one named, `jump_to` (the previous letter's first, turning back; round the ends as the covers go), and `th_name` moves `SLIDE_INDEX` so that album is the one named. It goes from `jump_to` and not from where the flow has got to: the covers travel about three albums between letters at `top_speed`, which would pass over a letter of fewer albums, and turning back, where the flow leaves a letter's first album at once, every other letter. Such a short letter steps the pictures back by that much instead, on a row still moving. Only the pictures change, and never on a still row; with one letter in the library, the flow goes round by itself. `jump_pace` is the beat of a turn a second, so spinning harder doesn't race the alphabet. `coverflow_letter` shows the big letter for `LETTER_MS` (400). Once in, letters stay while the thumb turns on the same way at `fast_at` or more, and a lifted thumb leaves `r` alone, so a lift for as long as a letter shows goes on from there with no second dwell. Only a pass that turned starts letters or moves them on. A thumb turning under `fast_at` or `LETTER_MS` with no tick ends them, and since the covers never stopped, the album named simply carries on under the thumb; turning back (`th_turn`) ends them too, dropping the goal as on any fast turn. A lift or a stop from speed with the covers still moving lands on the letter: as the goal goes to the album named, `th_albums` names `jump_to` (`th_name`), so the row runs down onto the letter's first album. With the covers already at rest it lands where they are. Nothing commits while letters last (`letters_176`).

**Letters.** With Fast Navigation on (the thumb's start of letters checks it, and so does `lettered` for Year): with the thumb down and `r` at `big_jump_at` (75 ticks a second, about two turns a second at 50%) for `big_jump_ms` (240), the spin goes by letters (`th.jump`). Off, 1.7.6's `jump_at` (32, a steady turn a second) for `jump_ms` (700, the 0.7 s the wheel's ticks had before 1.6.9) start its letters; on, they last until the lift, so a false start costs more, and at 1.7.6's trigger a brisk turn through a few albums set them off (75 and 240 were tuned on the wheel). A pass under `big_jump_at` but still at `fast_at` takes its ms off the count, and a lift or `r` under `fast_at` drops it. `th.lean` is set against the way the spin went (`-th.dir`) and holds through the entry, the letters and the fold. Once the row is in (the entry, below), travel stops moving the goal and counts towards the next letter, one each `jump_ticks` (5: one tick), at any rate and either way; turning back starts the count again and steps back a letter. Each `th_letter` asks `coverflow_letter_next` for the next letter's first album from the one the row is going to, never from where the row has got to, so no letter is passed over however fast the spin (`test/coverflow.py` `short_letters`, #276); it holds that letter (`coverflow_letter_hold`, shown until the lift), clicks, and sets the follower's goal there. The row slides through the albums between on its own follower, critically damped with time constant `slide_ms` (160), so a far letter flies past faster; speeding up, it grows by at most e^(ms / `slide_ms`) a pass from the entry's speed (`coverflow_enter_v`), or from `CF_ENTER_SPEED` turning round, so the spin's speed grows into the letters' (`real_spins`, `letters_turn_back`). A step before the row arrives only moves the goal: position and velocity carry over. The caption names the album nearest the middle as it passes (`th_named`). Within half a pixel the row is there, and `th_rebase` puts `SLIDE_INDEX` on the letter. Past the last letter `coverflow_letter_next` goes round to the first, and back past the first to the last, the goal set the short way through the seam (`letters_slide`); the row draws the other end's albums there, as `fx_window` takes the ring round modulo the count. With one letter there is no step. Only where `coverflow_jump` finds groups (`lettered`: the whole library by Album, Artist or, with Fast Navigation on, Year); elsewhere the cap alone (`unlettered_sorts`). In Year the groups are years (`group`): `sorted` keeps each album's year from `YEAR_SQL`'s year column (`REC_YEAR`) in `years`, 0 undated (so are a year outside 1 to 9999 and the albums the query missed), the undated last; the held letter is then `CF_YEAR` with the year in its low bits, and `ringnav_paint` (`cf_label`) draws its four digits, or an en dash (`by_years`). Only a lift (`!th.finger`) ends letters: no `r`, `stop_ms` or `hold_ms` does. A key other than the wheel's, a touch, the screen going dark or leaving the page lands at once on the caption's album (`coverflow_wheel_land`, `th_shown`). Nothing commits while letters last. `jump_ticks` 0 turns letters off; `big_jump_ms` 0 starts them at once at `big_jump_at` (`jump_ms` 0 at `jump_at`, off). `jump_at`, `jump_ms` and `jump_pace` are read only with Fast Navigation off.

**The entry.** Going into letters overtakes the facing cover. For `enter_albums` (8) albums of travel (`th.enter`) the row goes on the way it was going, at its speed and `CF_ENTER_SPEED` (12) albums a second at least (`coverflow_enter_v`), the wheel's travel dropped. `draw_row` (`row_at`, `entry_at`) places every cover on one clock, the share of the entry gone. In its first `ENTER_RUN` percent (99) the facing point runs on ahead the way the spin went, from its own speed and faster by the cube of that share, through the covers ahead, each turning as a cover passing the facing point does in the row (`row_quad_run`), and the shelf goes with it at the row's spacing, so the covers away from it keep their places. It runs until the cover `max(row_flat, row_edge)` albums behind it is wholly past the screen's leading edge (`entry_at`), so every cover on the screen keeps the formed row's side pose and none turns towards the eye; the covers left behind lean against the spin (`th.lean`). Then `th_letter` holds the row as it is (`coverflow_hold`: the facing point's lead and run and the shelf's shift in `th.hold_*`, the album at the middle in `hold_k`) and puts the position on that album, so no cover moves or changes its art. The goal is the first letter whose first album is `v slide_ms` or more on (`v` the entry's speed), where the follow from `v` lands with no overshoot, and none before the letter after the album the wheel had got to. A lift on the way in lets the entry end, then folds (`enter_frames`, `letters_entry`, `entry_handover`).

**The held row.** Going by letters `draw_row` (`row_at`, `hold_at`) draws the row as the entry left it, centered on the album at the middle, and the position slides it, so its first frame is the entry's last, cover for cover (`held_row`). About 13 covers show, each as wide, as far apart and as keystoned as the formed row's away from its facing point. The frame is rendered again only while the position moves (`fx.frac`, `fx.mode`).

**The fold.** After a lift the follower goes on until the row is within `fold_near` (50) hundredths of an album of the letter's first album, where the album nearest the middle, the caption's, is already the letter's (`lift_handoff`). `th_rebase` puts `SLIDE_INDEX` there, what is left and the row's speed go into `th.fold_off` and `th.fold_vel`, and the big letter goes. For `CF_FOLD_MS` (450) `fold_pose` glides each cover from the pose that draws it in the held row (`quad_pose`: its x, turn, eye and depth from its quad's edges) to its rest pose (`pose()`), by smoothstep of the fold's time, and `fold_push` adds the row's speed as a Hermite term shared by every cover, so the row goes on at its speed and stops at the landing. The landing cover turns to face the eye, and the covers on the side that already leans the right way turn to the shelf's `tilt`. Those on the other side turn their lean over: each swings out by `sin²(πt) (FOLD_OUT + (n - 1) FOLD_STEP) / 100` cover widths, `n` = |o| (53 and 87), and turns between `FOLD_FROM` and `FOLD_TO` percent of the fold (20 and 80). The fold's first frame is the held row's and its last the shelf's; a pose whose eye is past `CF_EYE_NEAR` is drawn as its quad (`pose_quad`). `fold_order` gives `draw_fold` its order: of two covers drawing a column in common, the taller there first. The wheel steers nothing during the fold; at `CF_FOLD_MS` `th_commit` lands on the letter's first album, where the covers already are. `coverflow_paint` renders every frame of the entry and the fold anew. `fold_clearance` checks from above that no two lit covers come within 4% of a cover's width of each other through the fold, both ways, in OLED. `tools/theme.py` requires `enter_albums` and `slide_ms` of a thumb theme, `fold_near` of 50 or less, and a `row_out` that puts no more than `CF_WIDE` of the held row's covers on the screen (`edge_drawn` holds the row at that least).

**The arch.** With Fast Navigation off the covers at speed bend in to the middle, as the lab's do (`th_arch`, `arch_pose`). `th.arch` goes from 0 to 1 as the covers' own speed goes from `arch_at` to `arch_full` albums a second (8 to 16), times how far past one album the goal is ahead of them, up to two: a step of one album never forms it, and it is gone as the covers land. It follows that by `arch_in` ms rising (100) and `arch_out` falling (62). Formed, every cover within `arch_span` (5 albums) of the middle is at the side covers' depth, the middle one too, so none swings towards the eye, and is turned `tilt` × smoothstep of its share of the span instead of standing at `tilt` from the first out; partly formed, depth and turn are that far between the shelf's and the arch's. Each cover's place across and its brightness stay the shelf's, the covers are drawn nearest the middle first as at rest, and at `th.arch` 0 the pose is `pose()`'s to the byte. There is no facing point ahead of the covers (`lead` stays 0), so the texture window stays round the middle and none of the row below is drawn. The covers follow the wheel's goal by one time constant throughout, `arch_tau` (56 ms: the lab's spring, stiffness 18 a second), in place of `track`, `snap` and `spin`. ponytail: so a slow step settles in about 0.6 s instead of 0.3 s, and touch, which waits for the follower to stop (`th.on`), is ignored that long after a wheel step; `arch_tau` only while the covers move or arch would undo that. The lab's thresholds are 15 and 30 covers a second, which its key repeat reaches; the wheel tops out at `top_speed` 20, where the goal is 2 `arch_tau` `top_speed` = 2.2 albums ahead, so 8 and 16 form the arch between 9 and 18 albums a second: none at a turn a second, nine tenths of it at two. `arch_span` 0 leaves a theme the row at speed. With Fast Navigation on there is no arch: its entry and held row come in from the row at speed, with the follower that row was tuned on.

**The position** follows the goal, critically damped and exact over the real elapsed ms of the pass, so a slow frame costs no accuracy and speed stays continuous. With no arch its time constant is `max(base, min(tau, rest))`: `base` is `track` blending to `spin` with that smoothstep (`snap` with no thumb), `rest` is `snap` to `spin` by `smoothstep(left / far_left)`. Only the thumb raises it, which removes a snap: lag raising it would add lag, and the row would jump out at one speed. A detent of `detent (1 - smoothstep)` draws the target towards albums, thumb down only.

**Settling.** A lift, the hold's timeout, or no tick for `stop_ms` with more than `stop_left` left sends the goal to the caption's album, so a stop from speed lands on what's named, with speed only falling. Otherwise a slow cover stays part-way while it's held. `th_commit` ends it through `carousel_glide`'s immediate move, so `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED` and `changed()` run as for any step. The position and goal are albums from `SLIDE_INDEX`, so once the position is `TH_REBASE` (64) albums out, `th_rebase` moves `SLIDE_INDEX` by the whole albums (`slide_menu_set_value`) and takes them off the position, goal and click count: nothing moves, and a float keeps the 1e-4 its settling needs however long a spin goes (past about 1024 albums it didn't, and the covers settled a step short and stayed held). The pass names the album in the caption and keeps it as the one to reopen on whenever the caption changes, so `closed()`, which can come while the page is being destroyed, only lets go.

**The row** (Fast Navigation on, or a theme with no arch). `lead` is `l smoothstep((|l| - lead_from) / (lead_full - lead_from))`, `l = goal - pos`, through a `lead_ms` follow. `draw_row` measures each cover's `t` from `pos + lead`, on that side, and slides everything `lead row_shift` px. `b` is `smoothstep` from `row_from` to `row_full`: `row_shrink`% smaller, no receding past `row_flat` from the focus (`row_out` px an album instead), and `e = b smoothstep(t / row_edge)` narrows a cover by `row_width e` (40: a side cover of #329's shelf is 64 px across two albums out, where the 60 degree shelf's was 101, so 60 left gaps between the held row's covers) and flattens its keystone by `row_key e`. At lead 0 none of this runs and `coverflow_render` takes its own path, byte for byte. A cover's columns take the art through `cf_texel`, as `draw_cover`'s do, so the two paths meet with no jump: the near half `r` times as wide as the far half, `r` going from 1 (even) at `coverflow.shelf.art_persp` 0 to the plane's own near over far height at 100. At 100 it is `unproject`'s own texels to the byte.

**Textures.** The row shows about 11 covers, so a thumb theme keeps `CF_WIDE`, 15, around the facing cover (`fx_reach`, `fx_base`): 1.6 MB with the placeholder. The window (`entry_window`, through `row_window`, for `coverflow_paint` and `draw_row` alike; with Fast Navigation off the row at speed keeps 1.7.6's, round the facing cover) starts from the farthest cover behind the facing point that shows (`CF_SHOW_PAST`), so the covers the row draws are the ones loaded, a cover joins or leaves the window only where it adds nothing to the frame, and every cover any of which shows is drawn whole (`edge_drawn`). A decode takes 6 to 9 ms on the UI thread, so while the thumb holds the covers `fx_window` loads nearest the center first: with Fast Navigation off `FX_DECODES` (two) a frame, as 1.7.6; in it, within a frame's budget: `FX_BUDGET_MS` (8), `FX_ENTER_MS` (2) in the entry, `FX_LETTERS_MS` (1) going by letters, or `FX_SLACK_MS` (10) in a frame `FX_LATE_MS` (30) or more after the last. A frame's first load always starts, and each after only if the last load of its kind (`fx.half_ms`, `fx.full_ms`) would still end within the budget; a copy asked for and missing is a full decode, costed and timed as one. At rest the seven the shelf shows load at once. A cover not yet loaded shows the placeholder, and `fx.todo` has the thumb's pass ask for frames until none is left.

**Half copies.** Every cover the held row shows is turned and narrow, so half the art draws it as well. Each album gets `<key>.jpg.half` beside its cache file: 80 × 80 texels, each the rounded mean of four, raw (25.6 KB, about 26 MB for 1000 albums; each file takes at least a cluster of the card, so on exFAT's 128 KB clusters 128 KB, about 128 MB for 1000), read with one `fread` into the last quarter of a texture slot and spread two by two (`half_load`, `half_spread`). Only the idle passes at rest make them, only with Fast Navigation on, never a frame: `coverflow_wheel_poll` (the covers shown, no touch, nothing gliding or loading) calls `coverflow_halves`, which makes one a pass, decoded into 100 KB of heap freed once it is written, no sooner than `HALF_GAP_MS` (100) after the last, since a decode is 6 to 9 ms of the UI thread, written to `.half.tmp` and renamed, none with the card's free space under the larger of `HALF_KEEP_MB` (512 MB) and `HALF_KEEP_PCT` (5%) of its size (`card_room`; the art build and the rest keep `card_space`'s `MIN_FREE_MB`), so they stop short of filling the card and stay until Refresh Cover Flow, and once every album has one returns before asking the card for space. A copy cut short reads as none, and the cover's own art decodes instead. Refresh Coverflow empties `.coverflow`, the copies with it. Going by letters the pool grows to `FX_POOL` (64) slots (`fx.more`), and `fx_window` wants, in order: the window of the letter gone to, where the row will stop; the window on the screen; up to `CF_WIDE` albums ahead towards that letter; and the next and previous letters' windows, so a step finds its letter loaded. Covers load from their half copies in the entry, letters and the fold, then full art over the screen's copies where it shows face on: at rest, and in the held row once it is there, but not during the fold, whose covers sharpen after it lands, the landing cover first (`half_art`). At any landing, `fx_unletter` drops the covers kept away from the landing album, so its window, wherever it was loaded, takes the shelf's slots (a touch or Center mid-letters, not only the fold: `loader_test`), moves those in `fx.more`'s slots to the shelf's free ones and frees it.

**The loader.** A half copy's read is about 4 ms of card, so the copies are read on a thread of their own (`loader`), on the Q2's second core, started at the first copy asked for. Each frame `ld_ask` asks for the copies of the covers `fx_window` wants and lacks, in its order, up to `LD_SLOTS` (32) at once, each into its own 25.6 KB of `fx.stage`; a request no longer wanted is taken back, and one the frame has not reached gives up its place to a nearer one. The loader reads the one asked for first (`ld_step`). A request goes `LD_FREE` to `LD_WANT` (the UI thread), `LD_READ` and `LD_READY` (the loader) and back (the UI thread) by atomics, so neither thread waits on the other; the loader sleeps on a semaphore when nothing is asked. The UI thread spreads a copy that is there into its texture within the budget (`ld_take`), decodes the art of a cover with no copy whole. Its first call (`thread_lower(1)`) puts it at nice 19 and its reads in the idle I/O class, else best effort's lowest level. At any landing, painted or not (a window over the covers, the screen going dark), `fx_unletter` (from `coverflow_wheel_land`, or the next frame) asks it for nothing more (`ld_ask(0, 0)`), so it parks after the read in hand and the UI thread never waits on it; the next letters use the same thread. Only closing the page stops it (`ld_quit`), joined after the read in hand, and frees the stage, so the stage's 0.8 MB stays while the page is open once letters have run (a known limit: joining at a landing with no request `LD_READ` would give it back). `fx.more`'s 5 MB calloc is an mmap that the kernel's overcommit grants whatever is free, so it never fails on the Q2 and its pages, filled as covers load, would end in the OOM killer: it isn't tried with `MemAvailable` (`mem_available_kb`, shared with `mp4_fits`) under its size plus `MP4_SPARE_KB` (16 MB), and refused that way or by a failed calloc, it isn't asked again until letters end (`fx.no_more`), the letters loading the screen's window alone. Full art stays on the UI thread: `cf_decode` goes through AWTK's image manager, which is not thread safe. If the thread or its stage can't be had, the copies are read on the UI thread (`loader_test`; `test/patch.py` runs its body as MIPS).

**What ticks gave.** Each is rebuilt, and `test/patch.py` holds a case for it:

- `KEY_LOCKOUT`: its first `LOCKOUT_KEEP` tenths drop travel, as `ringnav` keeps it for ticks.
- `tick_gate`: no frame in `WHEEL_FRESH_MS` drops travel read after a stall.
- Two Returns: `wheel_sample` counts `WHEEL_THUMB`'s travel into `wh_since` a tick's worth at a time, so the second Return stops it, and the poll honours `wheel_mute`. The lyrics and Vortex stay out of it, as before.
- `chord_gate` works as it did: it is on key events, and dark isn't `usable()`, so the wheel is ticks.
- `hold_wheel`: a turn begun during the page's slide is ticks, raw being off. They play in as a step, and the next travel takes that animator over, goal kept (`th_grab`). A tick still queued as the wheel goes raw is dropped.
- Letter jumps: after `jump_ms` at `jump_at` (Fast Navigation: `big_jump_ms` at `big_jump_at`), not `CF_FIRST_MS` of any turn, so a slower spin never jumps and lands where the caption says, and letters, once in, last until the lift ([Letters](#coverflow-thumb)).
- The end bounce: an artist's albums clamp the goal, and the first push past an end in a contact kicks the covers out `1 / CF_BOUNCE` of a stride.
- The click: once an album of the goal (`buzzeer_switch`). A turn also resets the screen's timeout and the idle clock.

Wheel Sensitivity scales the travel (`wheel_pct`), as it does other lists' ticks. Center lands at once on the album named, then opens it. A touch during a spin settles first: its press does nothing, and the covers run down to the album named (`coverflow_hit` only ever runs at rest).

The `--dev` frame gaps ([above](#coverflow-step)) go on working: `th.on` is a run, and its frames go to the log at the first paint after it.

## Cover Flow browsing position

`coverflow_position.c` draws an optional position bar, off by default. Display → Cover Flow's **Position Bar** persists `Q2POD/CFPOSITION`. The track matches the central cover's 160 px width, and its center is halfway between the last caption's bottom and the page's bottom. The 2 px track and 9×4 px gray thumb share a centerline. Virtual Sort/All Albums cards hold at the last album; wrapping to the first album returns the thumb to the left, at the half cover where `visual()` wraps. A bounded list's bounce or rubber band past its first album holds the thumb at the left. Zero or one album hides it.

The painter reads the wheel thumb's follower (`th`) while it holds the covers, otherwise the slide's live offset (touch and stock's step), so wheel and touch movement update it before settling. It stays opaque during movement, holds for 800 ms and fades over 300 ms. A temporary 33 ms UI timer invalidates only the 160×8 px footer strip; queuing that damage outside painting avoids the toolkit consuming it in paint cleanup. The timer stops after clearing, when disabled, or at page teardown. There is no worker, image cache, scan, or music-file access.

`test/coverflow_position.py` executes the production painter against a native canvas boundary; it also models shelf-only invalidation and paint cleanup. `test/patch.py` checks the real MIPS painter's placement in both halves, plus the persisted setting.

## Position memory

Position memory is a bounded 64-entry table keyed by the audited top-window context in `patch/contexts.inc` and a content fingerprint. Selecting a row updates its entry and moves it to the front; a full table evicts the least recently selected entry. Restoration alone does not promote an entry.

Local folders use the full bounded `g_folder_path`; local music lists use the stock browsing class, saved query and artist/album modes (`g_class_type`, `g_local_classinfo_save`, `g_artist_type`, `album_modetype`). Root Albums, Artists, Composers and Genres lists ignore the saved detail query: opening an artist overwrites it without changing the parent collection. `playlist_page` keys on none of these: opening a playlist writes the browsing state, so `context_now` scopes it by the page's add mode alone (`PL_MODE` + 1), and back from a playlist keeps its row while the Add to Playlist picker keeps its own. These are the inputs used by the stock folder and local-list loaders, not playback metadata. The builder verifies each object's size against the stock ELF. A changed fingerprint resets selection even if a surviving surface has the same row count, then restores the matching recent position and reveals it, or keeps the stock viewport if none is remembered. Fixed settings menus can restore by window name alone, but for Display's sub-pages (Appearance, Cover Flow, Controls: `display_page` opened again by `ringnav_display`, which marks each with its `DISPLAY_SUB`), whose scope is that mark + 1, so each opens on its own first row rather than on the row Display was left at; multi-pane and other dynamic pages without an audited content identity keep their live widget selection but do not restore across recreation.

Under a theme with `list.reopen.top` (OLED's), Return's release forgets the entry of the list being left (`forget_left`, before stock leaves the page, so `context_now` still names it): choosing that list again opens it at the top, as an iPod's menus and stock's own pages do (stock keeps no row of its own but Folder's, whose `folder_enter` pushes the parent's position and `folder_back` pops it), while the page Return lands on keeps its row. Home's own lists (Library, Streaming and Settings sliding in over its menu) are hidden rather than closed and Home keys no position memory, so Return there (`coverflow_home_back`) drops the row its view keeps and scrolls it back to its top (`forget_rows`). A theme that turns it off restores every list.

Memory lasts until power-off, with no filesystem writes. The table occupies 1,280 bytes. Ordinary paints do not search it; repeated selections in the current scope match its first entry and shift nothing. Lookup and promotion are bounded by `POS_MEM` (64).

Non-virtual lists also remember hashes of the selected row's first two text values, read through the stock `widget_get_text` UTF-32 accessor. A matching second text outranks proximity; equal matches choose the occurrence nearest the remembered index. Rows without text fall back to the index within the same content scope. The stock rows expose no stable item id. Both scroll views and virtual music tables protect an interrupted recall glide from silently replacing the remembered selection with a currently visible row. A real tap cancels the glide and selects its target; a wheel step advances from the remembered logical row. Pointer-down and synchronous click delivery load rows without recall, so native touch sees the widget it pressed and a rebuilt list cannot move or rebind that row first. Synchronous table rebinds discard the old row-pool snapshot before resolving the selected entry.

## Touch mode

A session-wide touch-mode flag suppresses only custom drawing, independently of logical selection and gesture state. Touch-down and native clicks (including clicks without touch-down) set it and invalidate the visible window. A touch on the keyboard (a `keyboard` top window) or the lock window (`g_lockscreen_pageflag`) leaves it as it was: it touches no row, so the list shown after it (a playlist just named, the page under the lock) keeps its bar. It persists through settling and page changes. Accepted wheel input, including a turn at a boundary, center selection or an accepted Return release restores drawing, so the page Return goes back to shows its row; iPod's Home list ignores the flag and always draws its bar; synchronous center-generated clicks bypass the native-click observer.

## Drawing

The canvas hook intersects the existing clip with the viewport and restores the clip, the LCD fill color and the LCD stroke color; this firmware's `canvas_save/restore` do not save those properties. The outline is one translucent fill (`0x402b2b2b`, a per-color alpha) plus two concentric one-pixel `canvas_stroke_rounded_rect` calls, a dark separator at radius 9 and the 70%-opaque white line at radius 8, with `bg_r = NULL`. The separator is the stock dark surface at `0xb32b2b2b`, so it disappears on the dark theme and only shows over bright artwork. It never calls `canvas_set_global_alpha`, so the shared alpha is untouched. A rounded call that reports failure (either stroke) or a row too small for the corner radius, keeps the square separator-plus-white outline instead.

iPod draws a selection bar instead of the outline. `widget_paint` (`0x6727fc`) calls `widget_on_paint_background`, then the widget's own paint, its children and `widget_on_paint_border`, so the background hook paints the bar behind the rows. The border hook then draws nothing, and the selection is loaded and settled once per frame, in the background hook. The bar spans the full surface width at the selected row's height and position, leaning with the wheel's tug (`patch/tilt.c`); an entry narrower than half the surface, a grid tile, gets the bar in its own rectangle. `paint_selection` draws it ([Themes](#themes)): on a list row the accent's flat bar (`gradient()` in the scheme's tones), `list.selection.inset` in from each side, its ends rounded by `list.selection.radius` at most (OLED's 16 and 8), under the rows' own ink, which stays white on it (`sel_accent`, resolved from paint ancestry by `ringnav_style_color`, without mutating recycled widget styles); a grid tile gets a square card in the accent's tone, `TILE_INSET` inside it, and the theme insets a grid tile's cover, so the card frames it. The bar uses the same clip, color restore and touch-mode rules as the outline. Rows only show it where they are transparent: after the iPod style edits, list rows, table rows, grid tiles (`s_btn_listblack`) and the settings rows (`s_btn_listitem`) are.

The iPod border hook draws the chevrons. Windows flagged `DRILL` in `patch/contexts.inc` get the stock `list_into` image on every row, over the bar as well: `widget_load_image` (`0x66f75c`, served from the image manager's cache) once per paint, then `canvas_draw_icon` (`0x64c20c`: canvas, bitmap, center x, center y, relative to the canvas origin like the fills) per row, placed as stock rows place their `img_into`: left edge `CHEVRON_W` (58) from the row's right edge, inside the same viewport clip, which hides rows outside it. A playlist button spans the same 20 to 355 pixels as a category or album button, so the glyphs cover the same screen columns (317 to 327); Local Music's own images sit 5 pixels further right at a fixed x. On a drill window the row layouter lays out as if that image were the last child, so the title and a playlist's "more" button end before it. The widget's own window, found through its parents, decides, so a window painted during a transition keeps its own rows. Rows narrower than half the surface (tiles) get none, and none are drawn while `g_navbar_status` is set, as stock hides its own chevrons in multi-select. The Add to Playlist picker (`playlist_page` with its add mode, `PL_MODE`) gets none either: its rows add in place and close, so they open nothing (`drill`), and its status row reads Add to Playlist (`pl_rows`).

The iPod border hook also draws the fast-scroll letter over the list. A step of more than one row (so the list has more than `SHORT_LIST_MAX` rows and the run has reached `LIST_FIRST_MS`) restarts a one-shot `LETTER_MS` (400 ms) timer. While it runs and the spin run is still past `LIST_FIRST_MS`, the surface draws the selected row's first non-space character, past an article on a library page ([Sorting](#sorting)). `paint_letter` draws none on a list OLED's [A-Z index](#a-z-index) shows on (`az_on`), which lights the letter itself. The letter is opt-in, by the list's page: the wheel handler arms it only when `name_sorted` (`patch/az_index.c`, the same rule as the A-Z index's) names the top window's list a name-sorted Library list, and every other list, however long, never arms it (Wi-Fi's networks, which come by signal, showed a letter until 2026-11-16; Bluetooth's devices, Settings, Up Next, View Queue, Chapters, Most Played, Era's albums, Internet Radio, card apps, Spotify and Tidal, the downloads, search results). The name-sorted lists: `localclass_page` and `album_page` (the Library's class lists), `artistinfo_page`, `folder_page` (a folder sorts by its file name), `coverflow_page` (its covers: `paint_letter` draws none over an open album's tracks, `coverflow_tracks` of the widget's own window, which `in_order` puts in disc and track order), Edit Playlist's Add Songs picker (`playlistedit_page` while `ple_listing` is 0, the whole library A to Z), and Library's song list, `allmusic_page`, while its class and Sort put it in name order. The wheel handler tests the top window's name where it arms the letter, not at paint, where the top may already be the page a Return brings back. An album's songs in the Library are not among them: stock shows them only in `albuminfo_page` (its init, `0x4a9a48`, is `load_album_detaillist`'s one caller: classes `0xff10`, `0xff11`, `0xff12` and `0xff14`) and `playerjumpinfo_page` (Album info and Go to Album, `0xff10`), and `getMusicByAlbum` and its kin sort them by disc, then track (comparator `0x5063f0`). `allmusic_page` shows lists of both kinds, so there the class decides, and its list is in an order of its own while it shows Recent, Frequent or Recently Added (`0xf007` to `0xf009`: `ORDER BY id DESC`, `getAllOftenRecord`'s own sort `0x506414` and `ORDER BY time_create desc limit 100`, each without the name sort), a playlist's songs under its Sort's Time added (`0xff13`, passed by a playlist row's click at `0x4b4bdc`, under a Sort of Time added, `g_playlistsort_flag` not 0: `getMusicByPlayList` `0x50b6c8` then lists them through `sort_playlist_addtime`, to which `library_query` adds `order by id`, the playlist's own order; sorted by name, 0, the list is A to Z and keeps the letter), Songs under Sort's Time added (`g_sort_flag` 3 or 4, or `song_sort.c`'s own orders), or an artist's Songs tab or a genre's songs from Genres (`0xff07` and `0xff09`: `getMusicBySonger`, `getMusicByAlbumArtist` and `getMusicByGenre` have no `ORDER BY` and ask for no sort, so the rows come as the database holds them). Songs A to Z, Hi-Res and My Fav are in name order (`getAllHr` and `getAllFav` ask `toolsQueryDbTable` for the name sort whatever their SQL's order). The class is the page's own, which its init stores (`0x4acd3c`) and its return handler puts back when another page changed it (`0x4ab728`); a class would not do on other pages, since `g_class_type` keeps its last value on pages that do not set it. That handler returns early while a song delete started on the page still runs (`g_delsong_state`, `0x4ab6c0`), so a class left by a page opened meanwhile can outlast the return; no other page stores a class tested here, so that can only leave the letter on. Edit Playlist, `playlistedit_page`, while it shows the playlist's songs (`ple_listing`: `ple.mode` 0, listed by `sort_playlist_addtime` whatever the playlist's Sort) is in the order they were added. The text is the row's first non-empty `widget_get_text`, taken from the same `row_id` walk as the position-memory hashes, and a virtual table finds its logical row in the recycled pool; an offscreen or textless row draws nothing. The box is `LETTER_BOX` (80) square, `canvas_fill_rounded_rect` at radius `LETTER_RADIUS` (12) in the stock dark surface at `LETTER_ALPHA` (85%), or a square fill without a vgcanvas. The glyph is `LETTER_PX` (60) in the system default font (`canvas_set_font` `0x6473dc` with a null name), white (`canvas_set_text_color` `0x64730c`), centered by `canvas_draw_text_in_rect` (`0x64ca94`) with the canvas alignment fields (`+0x34` horizontal, `+0x30` vertical) set to center and middle. The clip, fill and text colors and alignment are restored afterwards; the font is not, since stock sets it before drawing its own text. The expiry repaints the live surface, which then draws nothing.

## A-Z index

OLED's A-Z index ([oled-design](oled-design.md#a-z-index)) is `patch/az_index.c`. It indexes a `table_client` over `p_deque_showlist` with more than `AZ_MIN_ROWS` (50) rows whose count is the deque's: `allmusic_page` while `name_sorted` says its list is in name order (not Recent, Frequent, Recently Added, Time added, nor an artist's or a genre's songs, see [Drawing](#drawing)), and `localclass_page` or `album_page` for classes `CLASS_ALBUMS` to `0xf006`, whose rows name the album, artist, composer and genre at `REC_ALBUM`, `REC_ARTIST`, `+0x20` and `+0x1c`, as `class_query` reads them. A song row's name is `track_name`'s (the title, else the file name), which is what the name comparators sort on. `az_initial` gives a name's letter as the sort sees it: through `ringnav_sort_key` (trimmed, its article dropped), A to Z in either case, anything else `#` (0), as `catalogue.c`'s `initial` files a title; a class list's Unknown row (`REC_ID` -1, last) has none.

**Touch.** `ringnav_touch` hands a press to `az_touch` after stock's, before it marks the touch on the list. A press in the last `AZ_EDGE_PX` (28) columns of an indexed list takes the touch the way a claimed pull does ([Pull-to-search](#pull-to-search)): `EVT_POINTER_ABORT` dispatched through the page lets go of the rows it pressed, and `az_event`, bound once per page to its move-before, up-before, abort, close and destroy, swallows the moves and the lift (`STOP`), so the list neither scrolls nor takes a tap; `ringnav_touch` passes moves straight to stock while `az_held`; a press while it holds (a lift it never saw) ends the hold, and the strip fades as after a lift. The press is on the edge by its place in the list's view: `widget_to_local` gives it in the content, the scroll added, so `az_touch` takes the table's offset (`TABLE_TOP`) off again; a scrolled list once took a press low on the strip for one below the list. On the press `az_touch` walks the deque once and keeps each letter's first row (`az.first`); the finger's screen row picks a letter evenly over `AZ_TOP` to `AZ_BOTTOM` (80 to 240), all 27 whether or not the column is folded (`az_letter_at`), and `az_target` takes that letter's first row, else the next letter's that has rows, else the last before it. `ringnav_jump` (`patch/navigation.c`, where `load`, `select` and `wheel_offset` live) selects it and sets the table's offset to put it at the top, as far as `max_top` allows, with `touch_mode` cleared so the bar shows.

**Wheel.** The list tick calls `az_wheel` after `select` and `reveal`. With the strip hidden it costs one test of `wheel_speed` (degrees a second, [Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)); at `AZ_SPIN_DPS` (300) or more the strip comes up on the list with the selected row's letter lit and the bubble beside it. 300 is where Rockbox's acceleration, `(speed / 270)^4` rounded, first gives 2 (`vol_accel`'s step 2): the averaged speed needs about a turn to get there, so a fast spin shows the strip after half a turn or so, and a slow turn never does. A slower tick while it shows keeps the lit letter in step and drops the bubble, without putting the fade off.

**Showing and fading.** `az.list` is the table it shows on and `az.page` its window, compared and never followed. It shows until `UI_SHOW_MS` (1000 ms, `patch/ui_kit.h`'s show-then-fade, `ui_fade_alpha`) after the lift or the last fast tick, fading over the last `UI_FADE_MS` (200), as the scroll indicator does: `az_due` repaints the strip's columns of the top window every `UI_FADE_STEP_MS` (40) through the fade, then the whole window once it is gone, when the rows move back. `az_paint` draws it from the window's border paint (`ringnav_paint`), after everything in it, since Songs' table starts at y 90 under its Shuffle row, above `AZ_TOP`'s 80; it places itself by the canvas's own origin (`CANVAS_X`, `CANVAS_Y`). The column is `az_column`'s: 27 letters do not fit `AZ_SLOTS` (14) slots of `AZ_SLOT` (11) px, so it keeps seven, evenly from `#` to Z, with a U+2022 dot between each two, each in its share of the 160 px. While `az_on` a list, `az_right` moves its right column `AZ_RIGHT_IN` (4) px in (`song_row`'s lengths and right-hand artist, `paint_chevrons`' theme chevron) and `az_bar_in` takes `AZ_BAR_IN` (8) px off the selection bar's right end (`paint_selection`); `paint_letter` and `wheel_sb_alpha` draw nothing on it. The bubble is drawn, not `search_strip.c`'s key-pop art, which points down from a 30 px head.

## Accent

iPod's accent ([ipod.md](ipod.md#display-settings); OLED's own Blue) replaces Shanling red wherever it is drawn:
the theme's style colors, inline `style:*` colors (a mutable style answers through the same
vtable), decoded images, and the payload's own selection bar and progress fill, which read
the active scheme's tones (`tones()`, [Themes](#themes)). `accent_map` (`patch/theme_engine.c`) is
a pure function on one `color_t` (bytes r, g, b, a). Stock uses `#FF1448`, `#7F0A24`, the
pressed tint `#3D1920` and `#FF144840`, all stock red blended with a neutral: each channel is
`t * red + k`. Least squares against red with
the mean removed gives `t` (in 1/4096), then `k`. A color within `RED_TOLERANCE` (8) of that
blend, with `t` between 1/16 and 17/16 and `k` not below the tolerance, becomes `t * tone + k`
for one of the preset's tones (`ACCENTS`): the red tone for text colors (a property name ending
`text_color`, `tk_str_end_with`) and image pixels, the light tone for every other color property
and gradient stop; alpha is kept, and anything else, grays and other hues included,
is returned as it was. Anti-aliased edges onto black, white or a transparent background are such
blends, so they follow. No preset's colors are red blends, so mapping twice changes nothing.

- `style_get_color(color_t *ret, style, name, default)` returns its color through the hidden
  first argument. The hook runs stock through a trampoline and maps `*ret`, comparing the
