  property name only when the color maps. Stock first asks `style_get_gradient` for every color
  (`bal` at `0x65d558`; `style_data_get_gradient` turns a plain color into a one-stop gradient),
  so the gradient hook leaves the call that returns to `0x65d560` unmapped, and the color hook
  alone picks the tone. The builder pins that `bal`.
- `style_get_gradient(style, name, gradient_t *out)` (`0x65d4ac`) is a 12-instruction leaf with
  no GOT setup: null checks on the style and its vtable, then a tail call to the vtable's
  `get_gradient` (+0x18). The builder pins its first three words (`0x10800009, 0, 0x8c820000`)
  and replaces the first two with the jump; the payload repeats the checks, calls `get_gradient`
  through `$t9`, and maps the stops only when it filled the caller's `out`: `gradient_t` is 0x4c
  bytes (`gradient_init`), with the stop count at +8 and up to 8 `{color, offset}` stops from
  +0xc (`gradient_add_stop`, `gradient_get_first_color`). Widget backgrounds come this way.
- `image_manager_add(manager, name, bitmap_t *)` copies a freshly decoded bitmap into the cache.
  The hook maps its pixels first, only for plain theme image names (no `/` or `:`, so covers by
  path, `file://` or online URL are never touched), and only when the format
  is one of the 32-bit ones: `bitmap_t` has w at 0, h at 4, the format as a u16 at 0xe
  (1 RGBA, 2 ABGR, 3 BGRA, 4 ARGB in memory order, 4 bytes each by `bitmap_get_bpp_of_format`),
  its row stride from `bitmap_get_line_length`, and the pixels from
  `bitmap_lock_buffer_for_write`/`bitmap_unlock_buffer`. Premultiplied pixels are red blended
  with black, so they map the same way.

The confirm pop-up's discs (`confirm_ok`, `confirm_cancel` and their pressed images, names
starting `CONFIRM_IMAGE`) go through the same mapping with `CONFIRM_SURFACE` (`#2B2B2B`) as the
tone under every preset, Crimson included ([ipod.md](ipod.md#pop-ups)). The quick settings'
control discs (names starting `DROPDOWN_IMAGE`, `drop_`, except the brightness suns, `DROPDOWN_SUN`)
take the preset's red tone; when that tone is brighter than `GLYPH_LIGHT_MAX` (Graphite's silver),
an image that holds red also maps its neutral glyph pixels to `CONFIRM_SURFACE`, so the white glyph
turns dark ([quick settings](ipod.md#quick-settings)). Gray discs hold no red and are unchanged.
Any other image that holds red and an opaque pure-white pixel (a switch's knob, a disc's glyph; `#7F7F7F`
on a pressed disc) takes
the light tone instead of the red one, as do button backgrounds (names starting `BUTTON_IMAGE`,
`btn_`), whose white label is a widget's text; an image with red alone (a tick, the time page's
colon) keeps the red tone. Only Graphite's two tones differ, so only it scans for white.
The settings rows' category icons (`settings_icons` in `patch/ipod.json`, which the builder
writes to `SETTINGS_ICON_NAMES` in `stock.h`) are never mapped: several use stock red as their
category color (Network, DLNA, Wi-Fi, Backlight), like the purple and orange ones.
`red_map` is the mapping with an explicit tone;
`accent_map` is it with the preset's tone.

Changing the accent saves it, sets the progress fill, calls `image_manager_unload_all(image_manager())`
(`0x658594`) and `widget_invalidate_force` on the window manager. Widgets ask for their style
colors, gradients and images on every paint, so the next frame decodes the images again through
the hook and shows every recoloured part; nothing needs a restart.

## Rounded corners

Every rounded thing the payload paints itself is anti-aliased from one table: `corner_cover(r)` (`patch/corner_cover.c`) gives a radius `r` corner's coverage, `r` rows of `r` pixels from the outermost, each the share of 16 x 16 sample points inside the circle, out of 255. It works a radius out the first time it is drawn (16 integer square roots a row of pixels) and keeps it on the heap, a pointer a radius up to 160 in the scratch page, so any radius costs one fill per boot and a table lookup after. `tools/art.py` `corner_cover` is the same table in Python, which `test/fw/test_corners.py` holds the C to at every radius to 40 and beyond. The readers:

- `round_row` and `round_ring` (`patch/nav/row_paint.c`): a box a row at a time, each corner pixel the colour at its coverage. The scroll bar, the sheet, artist discs and boxes, About's tiles and `fill_box` where AWTK will not round (no vgcanvas, or a radius of 2, which stock declines under 3).
- `gradient`: the selection's pill, its bands' ends at their corner pixels' coverage.
- `corner_mask`: what lies outside a box's corners painted in the colour behind at the share the arc leaves, which rounds a square cover already drawn: Now Playing's art (`paint_cover`), About's, Control Center's, Up Next's and the artist pages' covers (`ar_corners`). `modal_corners` blends the screen towards the sheet's material by the same share.
- `round_corners` (`patch/nav/theme_titles_paint.c`): a decoded list thumbnail's alpha clamped to its coverage.
- Cover Flow's `column` (`patch/coverflow.c`): in a corner's texel columns, each end row the corner covers in part takes that texel's coverage too, so the arc is smooth where it runs steep (across the columns) as well as where it runs flat; the reflection mirrors it. The covers are drawn a column at a time, so this costs only the corners' end rows.

AWTK's own rounded rects (`canvas_fill_rounded_rect`, `canvas_stroke_rounded_rect`, through vgcanvas) are anti-aliased already and are left to it at a radius of 3 or more.

## Themes

OLED is the one built-in theme: `themes[]` (`patch/theme_engine.c`, from the generated `themes.inc`; the
types are in `patch/theme.h`) holds its one row, `THEME_N` is 1, and `theme()` reads the settings first
(`accent()`) and returns `&themes[0]`; `scheme()` returns its scheme for the stored accent in the half
Light Mode picks. Code asks the theme for a field, never which theme it is. The stored `THEME` is always
3, OLED's number when there were four themes: `theme_boot` (`patch/navigation.c`) gives a unit an older
build left on another (0, 1, 2, or no key) OLED's preset once, through `theme_preset`, and writes 3
([ipod.md](ipod.md#theme)).

- `theme_t` holds the surface flags (monochrome icons, `art_final`, the theme's own art left final,
  Now Playing opacities), the fonts per role, the Home and settings geometry, the Now Playing bar
  heights, the selection bar's radius and inset, the scrollbar, the accent's slot and config key
  (`accent_slot`/`accent_key`: OLED's `OLED_ACCENT`, an own key in `st.own[]`; `ACCENT` for a theme
  that names none), its schemes, its options, the Cover Flow style and its art prefix (`art`, `"oled_"`).
- `scheme_t`: one per `ACCENTS` row and theme's own accent, indexed by the stored value; its tones are that row, or
  the own scheme's `tones` when it states them (`<id>_tones[]`), read through `tones()` or `tones_of(v)`. The roles
  `chevron` (a mono theme's icon gray) and `muted` (second lines) are `0xRRGGBB`, 0 meaning unused; `sel_text`
  is the text on the selection, `paper` and `ink` the half's ends, and `label` an own scheme's name ("Blue").
- `option_t`: the Appearance rows, in order. At the first read, a stored value outside
  `values` becomes `def`. `theme_preset` writes each option's `preset` unless the stored value is
  its `keep` (Light's Auto), and only values that change. The accent row cycles within `values`.

The table is generated. Each built-in theme is `assets/themes/<id>/theme.xml`. The format is a strict
XML subset: elements with double-quoted attributes, self-closing tags and comments, only whitespace
between tags, the entities `&amp; &lt; &gt; &quot;`, UTF-8, at most 32 KB. `tools/theme.py` fills
each theme in this order: the schema defaults, its `extends` base (a theme may extend another
in `assets/themes/`; OLED extends none), its own elements, then
`ROLE_MACROS`, which takes the numbers a theme leaves to `patch/offsets.inc` (OLED's: Home's Full
label end, the chevron gray, Cover Flow's `CF_*` and the motion), so a theme file never names a macro. Any unknown name or
value stops the build. The tool writes `themes.h` (the enums and macros, which navigation.h includes) and `themes.inc`
(the tables, which theme_engine.c includes after the accent tables, where the hand-written table
stood) into the build directory, and `THEME_N` into `stock.h`, because `setting_counts[]` uses it. `edit_paint`'s OK is an off-white card (`MINIMAL_FILL`). A theme's `art` attribute (its own id by default) names the theme whose generated images (`tools/art.py`, `<art_id>_*`) it draws, and the payload loads them by that prefix (`theme_art`, `patch/list_marks.c`): OLED's are `oled_*`. `art.theme_images` packages each name once, stopping the build if two themes would draw one name.

**Faces.** A theme names a face for each font role (`theme_t.font[ROLE_*]`: the list row's title, its second line and a two-line row's title, the bar's title, Now Playing's title, Home's rows, the small info text) by a key of `FACES` in `tools/build.py`, the one list of them: `regular` (stock's `default.ttf`, uncut), and `inter` and `inter-medium` (Inter 4.1 Regular and Medium, OLED's). Each entry gives the face's name on the device (`fonts/<name>.ttf`, and AWTK's `font_name`), its original in `assets/fonts`, the name its subset takes, its license files (`FONT_NOTICES`, shipped beside the fonts), and the face a text falls back to when this one lacks a character, with that fallback's size as a percentage of its own (the two faces' cap heights' ratio: 98 for Inter's to stock's), and for Inter the suffix of its tabular figures' glyph names (`.tf`). `subset_font` cuts each face but stock's to its Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and punctuation, with a play mark at U+25B6, and points 0-9 and the colon (`TABULAR`) at a face's tabular figures, so a clock or a song's time keeps its width as it counts; `stock.h` then holds `FONT_<NAME>` (its index, in `FACES`' order), `FONT_NAMES`, `FONT_FALLBACK`, `FONT_FALLBACK_PCT` and the faces' cmap runs (`FONT_RANGES`, a face's from `FONT_RANGE_AT[i]` to `[i + 1]`, and `<NAME>_RANGES` each). `tools/theme.py`'s `FONTS` is the same keys. navigation.c's `face_has` looks a text's characters up in those runs (stock's has none listed, and every character), and `theme_font` (a label, in its role's face) and `theme_face` (canvas text, in the list title's face) walk the fallbacks from the theme's face until one has them all, scaling the px at each step.

**Cover Flow.** `theme_t.cf` (`cf_style_t`: `coverflow.shelf` top, x1, xs, z1, zs, eye, bright1,
bright2, reflect, `reflect_top`, stride, radius, tilt, horizon, third, swing, lift, `view_h`, the thumb's and the arch's; `coverflow.caption` `name_px`, `artist_px`, `text_y`) is
copied to coverflow.c's `cfs` by `cf_restyle` at every page open, so the stride is in place before
`slide_menu_set_spacer`; a radius change refills `cf_inset`, and a render before any page restyles
once. OLED takes the top, brightness, reflection, stride and frame height from offsets.inc's `CF_*` and the radius from `NP_ART_RADIUS` (`ROLE_MACROS`); where the side covers stand (x1, xs, z1, zs, eye, tilt, horizon, swing), `reflect_top`, the captions, the thumb and the arch are its `theme.xml`'s. An arch (`arch_span`) needs `arch_in`, `arch_out` and `arch_tau`, a span of an album at least, and `arch_full` past `arch_at`.
tools/theme.py checks each range, top + 160 + reflect ≤ `view_h` ≤ the client height, eye + z1 > 80 sin(tilt) (a first side cover's near edge in front of the eye), with swing 1 also eye - max(0, 80 - z1 / sin(tilt)) - lift / 4 > 0 (and all through a step), bright2 ≤ bright1, and
the caption's lower box, `text_y` + the greater of `CF_NAME_H` and `artist_y` + `CF_ARTIST_H`, ≤ the client height. A caption may overlap a taller frame: its labels draw
over it. `CF_EDGE`, `CF_VIEW_W`, `CF_CX` and `ART_SIZE` stay fixed. The frame's paper is the scheme's, as is a
placeholder's corners', so a theme's own white paper meets the page with no band.

**Bar and client height.** The grid's bar height is in `geom_vals` (`themes.inc`, the `V_*`
columns), 58 for OLED's. `client_h()` (theme_engine.c) is `320` less that bar, the window's height under
the bar. Cover Flow's views, Home's art panel, its pan frame, render loop and clip read it, and the
battery slot (`bar_sync`) takes the same bar. The page fallbacks
(`widget_get_prop_int(page, "h", 290)`) stay sized for 290, and `DRIFT_TEXELS` for a pane the screen's height (a `split_art_up` as tall as the bar). On the
build side `Geometry` and `with_geometry(g)` (`tools/ipod.py`) drive `ipod_home`, `status_bar`,
`playing_page` and `patch_asset`.

**Geometry set.** The build bakes one set, the theme's (`tools/theme.py built_geometry`): `patch_code` writes its
values into stock's row immediates (`ipod.json`), and `ui_pages` (`tools/ipod.py`) builds every page under it, each
written over stock's own. `themes.inc` holds the same values for the payload: `geom_words` (the immediates' words,
`G_*`, which `geom()` reads) and `geom_vals` (the values that are not immediates, `V_*`, which `geom_val()` reads).
The Library and Edit Playlist rows the payload builds follow the set: `list_row_core`
reads the Library constructor's body and icon x words, and Edit Playlist's row
takes the set's `pitch` and `body` (`geom()`).

**Geometry fields.** OLED is the one theme and its grid the one the build bakes: its theme.xml states it in one `<geometry bar="58" …/>`, each omitted field stock's own (`STOCK_GRID`, the `Geometry` defaults: stock's page measurements) or, for a theme that extends another, that theme's; `tools/theme.py` checks each field's range (`GEOM_RANGES`) and that the themes share one grid (`built_geometry`). The build writes it into stock's row immediates (`patch_code`) and pages (`ui_pages`), and the payload reads the values that are not immediates from `geom_vals`; nothing is patched at boot, and no other grid is built.

- Values that follow the grid but are not immediates (the bar, the settings rows, the battery body, the text inset) are `geom_vals[V_*]`, and `client_h()` is `320 - geom_val(V_BAR)`.
- `list_end`: list boxes take the whole window, so rows draw down to the glass (OLED's end their rows at `list_end` instead, the strip below black), while the selection's scroll limit (`sel_height`, `max_top`) stops at `list_end` so a selected row never lands where the glass hides its text. A last row selected leaves the glass's strip below it empty. A list ends after the last row whose text clears the glass at `text_x` (`fit_bottom`).
- `action_row`: Songs' action bar as a plain row. Stock rebuilds that view's children on each refresh (0x4a9e78: the label, Play All's image, Sort's image only on some pages), so the assets shape only the boxes around it and `action_row()` shapes its children as it paints, once per rebuild. They stay stock's widgets with stock's handlers.
- `home_lib`: Home's Library row, in Split (OLED's grid has `home_lib` 0), slides in a list of the Library's rows (`list_view_homelib`, filled by the same `library_rows` the page uses, `home_library`) instead of opening the page; each row opens its stock page and Return comes back to the list. The bar's title names the open list (`coverflow_home_title`). Full keeps stock's page. Its Streaming row does the same (`list_view_homestream`, `home_streaming`, `stream_rows`): stock's `stream_page_init` takes the list for its window, finds no `view_navbar` there and rebuilds the rows in the view of that name, its timer stopped by `STREAM_BG` and its handlers dropped, and the rows take Home's height (`home_fill`). Full's page still follows it through `stream_row`. `svc_toggle` looks in every window, as Home's list comes first and is empty under Full.
- Songs' rows have their own immediates (`song_pitch`, `song_body`, `song_title24_y`, `song_meta_y`) and page kind `song`. With no text art (the grid's `text_art` 0), a row taller than the pitch whose leading image has no width is two lines (`two_lines`): art and playing gif hide, the second line stays, and the artist is what stock's bind (0x4ab208) writes, "Unknown Artist" when untagged. A playlist's songs are the same page and list; album tracks and an artist's songs are other constructors, title only.

**A theme's own options.** A theme declares them in theme.xml (OLED's `<option key="SONGARTIST" label="Song Artist" default="Inline" preset="Inline">` over its `<value label="..."/>` rows). The payload draws, cycles and stores them generically (`SETTING_OWN`, `theme_keys[]`, `st.own[]`) and reads their keys after the thirteen in declaration order. Each is a plain choice the payload reads as `st.own[OWN_<KEY>]` through `theme_own` (0 while the theme does not offer it), saved at once. `tools/theme.py` accepts only the plain keys in `PLAIN_KEYS`, the ones the payload reads: OLED's `SONGARTIST`, `SONGLENGTH` and `NPTIME` (`theme_engine.c` `song_artist`, `song_length`, `np_time_total`). An own option takes `preset` and `keep` as a payload setting does (into its `option_t` line), so `theme_preset()` writes it with the rest. Undeclared settings take the theme's value, and their stored keys are untouched.

**OLED.** `assets/themes/oled/theme.xml`, built to [oled-design.md](oled-design.md). It extends no other theme and is built on its own `oled` set: a 58 px bar holding a status row (`status_y` 23, its ends `STATUS_ROW_INSET` 62 px in from the sides: `tools/ipod.py` `status_row`) with no band, then 32 px rows from y 58 (52 for art lists and Search), the text at `text_x` 24 and the right column at `right_x` 28, and `list_end` 224, so a list's box (`patch_asset`, `fit_rows`, the settings lists' too, and the payload's own `page_list` pages through `fit_view` and `list_fit_end`) holds the whole rows that end by y 282 on screen and the strip below stays black. The status row's `label_title` and `label_clock` start in one box at `text_x`, in the bar's face at `bar_px`; `bar_title` (np_bar.c) keeps the clock beside a title whatever Time in Title says, and `clock_place` (navigation.c, each bar paint) moves it, its box sized to its text as measured in the bar's face, so the label's own alignment plays no part: with no title the text is centered on x 187.5 (unless centered it would reach the slots' edge), else (a title, or Home in Split, `coverflow_home_split`) its box ends `CLOCK_BESIDE` (7) left of the leftmost shown slot (`status_slots_left`, [Status row slots](#status-row-slots)), the title's box ending `CLOCK_CLEAR` (12) short of the widest clock, "00:00" as measured once, so its ellipsis stops there; over Split's art the clock takes Text Primary in each state its style names, so `home_ink` inks it whole, in the row's one ink; the color written last is kept and compared, so an unchanged clock never asks for another repaint. `bar_title_sync` gives Home's own list and Now Playing an empty title there (`coverflow_home_sub`), and names the Library (`localmusic_page`) and the whole Songs list (`allmusic_page` under class `0xf001`) by those words where stock's hidden toolbar says "Local Songs" for both; `allmusic_page`'s other lists keep stock's title (an album's, a playlist's). On a set with a right column the settings rows' trailing images end on it (`set_edge`, `list_toggle`'s switch), a feature's "Title: value" row (Crossfade, Resume Songs, Night Shift, Wheel Sensitivity, Folder Root and the Library & Folders rows, `row_value_text`) shows as a key/value row, and `value_fit` ends the value 21 px short of the column on a row that opens a page, so it stands beside the chevron, and splits the row between title and value as a [label/value row](oled-design.md#labelvalue-rows) does (`kv_row`). `list.art.radius` (OLED's 4) is a row cover's corner radius on screen at the set's art size, scaled to the thumbnail's own size when `round_corners` rounds it; 0 keeps `NP_ART_RADIUS`'s share. The right group is the battery; the play state, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and EQ are off-screen, and the payload paints the row's other glyphs left of the battery ([Status row slots](#status-row-slots)). Its own scheme (`oled-blue`, five equal tones) is the only one `OLED_ACCENT` offers, its faces are `inter` and `inter-medium` at 1.21 times the design's sizes (AWTK sizes a face by its line), and `settings.values.ink` gives its key/value rows their gray, final in each half (`list_value`, through `text_ink`, which the selection's `sel_text` still overrides), the value's right end on the right column. `settings.values.switch` (`theme_t.set_switch`) keeps an on/off row a switch where `set_text` would write On or Off: `list_toggle` makes its `switch_on`/`switch_off` image as on any theme, the image hook empties stock's switch art (and Gain's `gain_high`/`gain_low`, the Wi-Fi page's `wifi_sig1`..`4`), and `paint_into` draws `switch_mark` (`patch/list_marks.c`, vgcanvas: 40x24, the knob 20 px sliding over 200 ms when a switch at the same place flips (`sw_knob`, `SWITCH_SLOTS` places remembered), the on-bar pair white track and accent knob, or a 1.5 px white ring) on the image's right end, Gain's High or Low as a value (`paint_gain`), a disabled row's `list_intodown` as `chevron_muted` in Text Tertiary with its label's stock #777777 mapped to the scheme's `muted` (`ringnav_style_color`), and a picker's mark as the theme's 12 px `check_a`/`check_w` (`paint_radio`); settings rows' text starts at `text_x` less hscroll_label's 2 px (`set_text_x`). Under it stock's four slider windows take one form (`patch/slider_page.c`: `slider_page_open` from `slider_open` as the window loads, `slider_page_paint` after its children: the toolbar's title and switch as a selected row, the value from stock's label, which stays laid out but clear so its writes still repaint, the track, knob and range ends, `xfade_ends` for crossfade.c's pages), EQ's Simple tab draws rows and vertical sliders (`eq_rows_paint`, `eq_tabs_paint`, peq_ui.c's `e3_paint` and `e3_touch` on `EQ_*` rows), and the Wi-Fi page is restyled after each `wifimenu_rows_build` (`patch/wifi_rows.c`: stock's Scanning row, whose tap scans, reads Search Again with its spinner hidden; `wifi_rows_pre` and `wifi_rows_post` from `ipod_list_layout`, `wifi_mark` from `paint_into`, the scan records' flags from `wifi_showlist` for the lock, `wifi_searchtime` for Searching...). About is a key/value table (`patch/settings_pages.c` `about_rows`, from `ipod_list_layout`: each row split by `kv_row`; its rows take the selection, so the wheel walks them and a value cut off at its column scrolls on the selected row, as `marq_moved` takes a row's first cut-off label; stock's row click, `systemset_about_row_on_click` `0x4c12f8` and its serial-number QR code, gives way to `about_click`, which does nothing; keys in Text Primary and values in the value gray, white on the selection), Reset Settings' three rows lose stock's `list_into` (hidden and insensitive, as they open the card at once) and each takes its caption once (`reset_rows`, from `ipod_list_layout`; what each reset takes is stock's `init_usersetting` and `init_database`, called from reset_page's row click (unnamed, after `systemset_powermanager_page_init`), and the cards say it, `feedback.c` `asks[]`), Lock Screen's pictures sit three a row on the text and right columns without stock's blue default-picture corner (`lock_grid`, from `lockscreen_rows`), and EQ's Advanced list shows whole rows down to the set's `list_end` (`eq_list_end`), its box running on to the window's foot so the rows past it fade there (`list_fit_end`, navigation.c `list_fade`). The rest are drawn by `patch/list_marks.c`: stock's `list_into` is emptied and the theme's own caret drawn on every drill row's and every `list_into` row's right column (`chevron_icon`: `paint_chevrons`, `paint_into`), white on the selection; a theme with `list.scrollbar.w` (OLED's 4) draws the track (`list.scrollbar.track`) and thumb only while the wheel turns (`wheel_sb_arm` from the wheel's tick, `wheel_sb_alpha` in `paint_scrollbar`, a fade over the last 200 ms of a second, repainted every 40 ms by `sb_due`, and nothing while the [A-Z index](#a-z-index) shows on the list); `list.divider.ink` draws a 1 px divider under each row taller than the pitch, from its text column (`list.art.text_x` under a theme with art rows) to the right column, on neither edge of the selected row (`paint_separators`); the lists keep no reading margin (`reveal`), so they scroll a whole row at a time, and where a row of another pitch (Power's 12 px gap before Restart) would leave the view's end inside a row, cut at the top, the view stops on the next row's top instead, its content grown to allow it (`fit_top`); the battery is the iOS-proportioned one (`battery_slim`, vgcanvas), and the play state is `status_row.c`'s level bars. A theme's own images are named by its art prefix (`theme_t.art`, `"oled_"`, `theme_art`), which `art_final` reads in the image hook: OLED's are final in each half, drawn per half by `tools/art.py` from Phosphor's SVGs (`phosphor`, filled by the nonzero rule). A one-line song row shows what its list calls for (`patch/song_rows.c`): `paint_songs`, from the list's background hook after `paint_selection` and so before the rows paint, hands each row to `song_row`, which picks the list by its window (`song_list`: `allmusic_page`, Songs and the lists stock opens there such as a genre's, mixed; `artistinfo_page` an artist's, `albuminfo_page` an album; any other list keeps stock's row), fits the title's box to its measured ink (`song_fit`) and draws the rest in the meta face in the scheme's `muted` (Light Mode's flip turns it for paper), its `sel_text` on the selection. The artist is the text stock bound to the row's hidden second line; an album's track number (`REC_TRACK`) and a length (`duration_text`, so only once a durations pass has measured the song) come from the row's `p_deque_showlist` record, taken only when its `REC_TITLE` is the row's title, at the row's index or the one before. Song Artist (`SONGARTIST`: Inline, Selected Row, Right, Off) and Song Length (`SONGLENGTH`: Albums, All Lists, Off) are the theme's own plain options (`song_artist`, `song_length`); a length takes the right column, so a Right or Selected Row artist stands inline beside it. A grayed row's offline mark ([Server library](#server-library)) takes the right column's place: `ringnav_paint_bg` runs `grey_rows` before `paint_songs`, which passes `song_row` the mark's left (`offline_x` less half `CAT_MARK_W`) for a row `catalogue_row_greyed` names, and the length, a right-hand artist and the title's room then end `SONG_COL_GAP` short of it; `song_row` clears the title's `_catw` so `catalogue_fit` never gives back a width the row no longer has. Track Time (`NPTIME`: Remaining, Total) is a third: Now Playing's right-hand time (`np_sync`, `np_time_total`), switched by a tap on it (`np_time_tap`, `np_time_toggle`, which saves it under `theme_keys`' key). A box changed while its list paints repaints once (`widget_move_resize`); a relayout gives the title its full box back and the next paint fits it again. Folder view (`folder_page`, `SONGS_FOLDER`) reads as an album under it (`folder_row`): the set's `folder_pitch` and `folder_body` (OLED's 32; 0 takes `art_pitch` and `art_body`, the `folder_*` immediates in `patch/ipod.json`) make its rows one line, so the compact layouter hides their artwork. Once per listing (the folder path's hash, the showlist's size and first record) `folder_tracks` asks the library for the songs under the folder by `fileurl` (one `era_sql` query, the path's quotes doubled) and keeps each of the folder's own files' tag title and track by the record's `REC_PATH`; a file it doesn't know is named from `REC_NAME` without its extension, a leading track number (which becomes its number) and the longest "Artist - " every such name shares. A song's row then shows that title (written into stock's label once, as stock binds the file name), its number and its length (`duration_text`); a folder's, or any file's that isn't a song, the theme's `folder_d`, `folder_l` or `folder_w` glyph (`tools/art.py` `FOLDER_INKS`) with the name at x 52, stock's chevron left as it is. `list.shuffle.row` turns Songs' action bar (`view_navbar_allplay` on Songs' page, an album's and a playlist's songs: the pages `songs_action_row` sizes) into a Shuffle row the wheel reaches: `action_row` writes "Shuffle" into stock's label 28 px after the text column and centers Sort's bars in a 44 px pill inside the bar inset, and `shuffle_paint` (the bar's background hook) draws the theme's `shuffle_a` glyph (Phosphor's regular `shuffle`, 20 px, the accent's top tone) on the text column with the label in the accent, or, with the selection on it, the accent's bar and the white `shuffle_w`, the label white (`ringnav_style_color` gives the lit label the selection's text color, as a selected row's, so Light Mode's flip leaves it white). `shuffle_key`, ahead of the list's own wheel and Center in `ringnav`, puts the selection on the row (`st.shuffle_on`, `SHUFFLE_STOP`) on a tick up from the first song, and on Sort's bars (`SORT_STOP`) on another when the list has them (OLED hides the bars, and the stop with them: Sort is its hold menu's Sorting row, see [Inset modal](#inset-modal)); a tick down comes back, and the list's bar is hidden meanwhile (`paint_selection`). Center on Shuffle, and a tap on the row, which `ringnav_dispatch` takes before stock's Play All handler, run `shuffle_page`: the page's `p_deque_showlist`, when it holds the surface's rows one for one, through `shuffle_play` (Shuffle Songs: a random first song, the rest in a shuffled order Up Next lists, Now Playing opened); Center on Sort clicks the bars, so stock's sort picker opens. Any row's selection (`select`) and the action view's destroy (`shuffle_gone`) take the selection off the row; another page on top keeps it (`title_gone` and `shuffle_key` leave it), so Return from the Now Playing that Shuffle opened lands on Shuffle, the row that was left. ponytail: Sort stays on the row until the options menu has it (SPEC-next 2). Under it Streaming's rows are one line at the set's `stream_row` 32, and `stream_marks` (`patch/home.c`, from `ringnav_stream`, so Home's Streaming list too) hides each row's logo on its disc (`list_tidal`, `stream_spotify`, `stream_app`, `stream_radio`, `stream_airplay`, `stream_config`) and tags the row; `stream_mark_paint`, which `ringnav_paint` calls only for the rows of the two lists it tagged (`stream_mark_views`), draws the theme's 20 px mark for it centered on x 34 (`oled_stream_*_d`, `_l`, `_w` from `tools/art.py`: Phosphor's `spotify-logo`, `app-window`, `radio`, `airplay` and `sliders-horizontal`, TIDAL's four diamonds drawn there, and q2-coda's own `assets/icons/q2coda/subsonic.svg`) in Text Secondary, white on the selection (the row or, on a settings row, its button), and keeps the row's words at x 52, moving them where the settings layout (`set_row`) or Home's (`library_look`) put them. The settings layout hides every leading image on these rows (`set_child`: OLED's `stream_row` and `set_row` are both 32 and `set_icon` is 0), so a card app's row is marked too: `ringnav_stream` tags each with its app's index (`_stream_app`), and an app whose id `stream_apps` names (`subsonic`) takes that mark, with or without icon files; any other app's own icon (`addon_is_icon`) is hidden and drawn by `stream_own_icon` scaled into the mark's 20 px box, as the image hook leaves it (`icons.addon_mono` grays it); an app without one shows `stream_app`, so `app-window`. `patch/feedback.c` gives OLED its feedback forms: `feedback_toast_paint` (from the background hook, `ringnav_paint_bg`) takes `msginfo_dialog`, clears the dialog's background and fits its first line onto a `#1c1c1e` pill (y 236 to 268, the text's measured width and 16 px each side) in Inter at 16 px, so the page shows round it; `paint_selection` draws the page's held row under the toast as under a sliding page, and `bar_title_sync` treats the window under it (`feedback_under`, the window manager's last window before it) as the top, so the page keeps its title and Shuffle row. `toast` lasts 1.5 s under it. `confirm_prompt` hands `confirminfo_dialog` to `feedback_confirm_dress` on its first paint, which draws it as the confirmation card ([oled-design](oled-design.md#confirmation-card)): the prompt's lines are hidden and its text, through a table of stock's English prompts (`asks`, each with its title, verb and any body), becomes the card's title; the dialog's background is cleared so the page shows, with the status row painted under the card's scrim (`feedback_confirm_bar`, `confirm_paint`); `img_cancel` and `img_enter` become the card's answers, 8 px in from its sides (`confirm_surface` keeps their width in `paint_selection`), their words cleared and painted over the selection by `confirm_rows_paint` (the second the verb: `asks`, the prompt's first word when it is a verb, or `confirm_over`'s; red, after a 12 px gap, when it loses something). Delete Song's `msg_delcheckbutton` is the card's switch row above them: its words painted, a click handler that makes it a wheel stop (the check turns itself on any click, Center's too), and `switch_mark` by its value. `feedback_switch_bar` puts the selection's bar on Sleep Timer's switch row while its fields are hidden (the switch off), the row's words white through `st.sel_accent`. `ringnav_stream_row` opens `feedback_offline`'s page (`empty_open`'s `empty_page`, titled Streaming: the empty state, "Not Connected", **Turn on Wi-Fi**, which opens `systemset/wifi_page`) for Tidal's row with no link under OLED, in place of stock's toast. Playlists' action rows take the playlists' pitch (`pl_pitch`), and `pl_rows` sets the list's `item_height` to it, as the Add to Playlist picker lays its rows out by that. The page's list is built at the set's `playlist_pitch` (52, `page_detail`'s height: `tools/ipod.py` `page_rows`), so `fit_rows` ends its box on a whole playlist row and the list takes no `item_height` from the bin, which the 32 px `default_item_height` of a list beside the settings rows would add (`navigation.c` `settings_list`). The App Store's lone Check for Updates line is centered in its row. `qm_run` toasts what Play Next, Add to Queue and the favorite rows did. The empty state (`empty_state`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#empty-and-offline)) is one view over the page, named `_empty_state` and insensitive so the rows beside it keep their taps, holding the glyph, title, hint, button label and stack top in its props for `empty_state_paint` (from `ringnav_paint_bg`), and at most one button, a one-row list named `_empty_row` the capsule's height with blank words and no fill, whose capsule `empty_state_paint` draws (`ui_cta_paint`) and whose selection bar `paint_selection` leaves out (`empty_button`); Songs' Scan Music Now is stock's `btn_upmusic` made the same band, its capsule drawn by `feedback_scan_bar`; it is made once per page and written again on each call, and a call with no state hides it. `empty_list` is `page_list` with no rows, its caption hidden for the status row, and the empty state in the body (Most Played, Long Songs, Ratings' lists, Era, Downloads, Chapters, Internet Radio's station lists, Cover Flow); `empty_open` is a page of its own holding only that; `empty_paint` paints the stack for Search's sheet; and from the bar's paint an `allmusic_page` whose `p_deque_showlist` is empty (`feedback_songs`, by `g_class_type`, the Shuffle row hidden) and an empty `folder_page` (`feedback_folder`) show theirs. Playlists' sits under its rows (`image_wait`, stock's spinner, sized to nothing), and Car Remote's under its switch. The older note is two labels (`feedback_empty`, `feedback_note`) centered between the end of the page's rows and y 282: `page_empty` uses it in place of its first line (Internet Radio's Loading and Battery History), and so do Spotify's message, the App Store's Check for Updates row and a card app's empty page. `feedback_shuffled`, from `shuffle_play` and `shuffle_groups`, opens a window of its own over the Now Playing they open: the theme's `confirm_shuffle` art (Phosphor's bold shuffle at 56 px in the accent, `tools/art.py`), what was shuffled and the song count, closed by a 1.2 s timer or the first key. `paint_separators` draws `list.divider.ink` under a page_list's two-line rows too, and `page_fit` cuts a page_list's box to the whole rows ending by `list_end` (Era, Most Played, Long Songs, Ratings' lists), as `fit_rows` does stock's.

**A theme's own accent.** `<colorScheme name="oled-blue" base="cobalt" label="Blue" tones="#2160d8 #2160d8 #2160d8 #2160d8 #2160d8"/>` (OLED's) adds a scheme after the `ACCENTS` rows that only this theme has: it starts from its `base` row's roles, and `tones`, five colors in an `ACCENTS` row's order (selection top, bottom, light tone, red tone, highlight), replace that row's tones, so its selection, progress fill and mapped reds are exact without a shared row every theme would offer. Without `tones` it takes its base's. The tones are one row for both halves: Light Mode keeps a colored scheme's, and gives a neutral one its red tone (`tone_of`). `tones` on an `ACCENTS` row is refused. `<colorSchemes accents="oled-blue"/>` offers it alone. A theme holds at most 10 schemes, the nine rows and its own, so a theme has room for one scheme of its own. Ten is the format's own bound (`tools/theme.py`), not a reader's: `config_value` reads up to three digits and stock's `write_int_config` writes any; past 32 the accents mask (`option_t.values`) could not hold a scheme.

**The selection bar's shape.** On a list row the bar is `list.selection.inset` in from each side of the row (default `SEL_INSET`, 6; OLED's 16) and its ends round by `list.selection.radius` at most (default `SEL_MAX_RADIUS`, 160, more than half any row, which is the pill; OLED's 8): the radius drawn is the lesser of it and `pill_radius`'s, so a cover's corner still shrinks it, and 0 is square ends, still inset. A grid tile's card is square.

**The progress bar's track.** `playing.scrubber.track` (default `TRACK_COLOR`, `#1c1c1c`) is the plain bar's track: `np_theme` writes it into the slider's `bg_color` in each state, and writes `TRACK_COLOR` back after a theme with another, so a theme on the asset's color writes nothing. The volume over Now Playing and Spotify's bar draw it too. It is one value for both halves, which Light Mode treats as it treats `TRACK_COLOR`. OLED's is `#333333`.

**Rows.** `list.row.tall_font`/`tall_px` (`ROLE_TALL`) are a two-line row's title, and `list.divider.ink` the 1 px divider under each two-line row (`paint_separators`), final in each half. A final value a half leaves out is the other half's, flipped (`half()`).

**The bar's title.** On OLED's status row the bar's `label_title` names the top window by `bar_title_sync`'s rule, Home by the list it shows (`coverflow_home_title`: "Q2 Muse" on its own list, else "Library", "Streaming" or "Settings"); a page with no title leaves it empty and the clock centered. It is written during a paint, where an invalidate is lost, so `title_due` forces it on to the panel just after. The clock stays beside the title (`clock_place`) whatever Time in Title says ([ipod.md](ipod.md#status-bar-and-clock)). The title and clock are laid out at the set's `bar_px` (`tools/ipod.py` `status_row`) and drawn at `bar.title.font_size`, so `tools/theme.py` rejects a `bar.title.font_size` other than the `bar_px` of each of the theme's sets that has one.

**Stock details the slider pages lean on.** `playset_bootvol_page_init` makes `img_bootswitch` in `view_navbar` after the load, so `slider_paint` finds it at its first paint. Stock's slider fills its knob in `border_color` and draws none when it is clear (`0x62e290`).

**Message screens.** `msg_open` (`patch/scan_page.c`) takes Update Local Music's `updatemusic_dialog` as the loader hands it over (USB mode's page stays stock's); stock's `img_animation`, `label_msg` and `label_scanfolder` stay by name, hidden, and `btn_no` keeps its binding, laid unseen (no fill, no words) over the painted button. `oled_scan` adds a label for the folder's name, which scrolls as the house marquee; `msg_paint` paints the status row the dialog covers first (`widget_paint` of the system bar, as `cc_paint` does; `bar_title_sync` lets the dialog title it, "Update Library", through `msg_title`), then the rest as the empty states' stack ([oled-design](oled-design.md#update-library)): the figure, the title, the line and the shared button (`ui_button`), in screen rows. While the scan runs (`SCAN_DONE` 0), the figure is Software Update's spinner (a frame each 80 ms poll) and the title the count, "1,284 songs found", until it can be measured: stock gives no total, so `msg_sync` reads the first number in `label_msg` against the songs a detached worker counts as the dialog opens (`msg_count`, `library_count`, its own connection), and on a whole-library scan (`SCAN_WHOLE` 1, by our reading of stock's code) with the count at most that total the figure is a ring with the percent, held at 99%, and the title "312 of 704 songs". The line is the last name in the hidden `label_scanfolder` after a folder glyph (the card's root as it is). Stock's ending, read from its own code (`updatemusic_dialog_refresh`, `updatemusic_dialog_on_timer`): once `wait_scan` sets `SCAN_DONE`, each 200 ms tick writes `scan_updatefinish` with the count, or `msg_no_storage` when the stop flag (`toolsGetUserStop`) is 2 (`/mnt/data` full), and the third tick pauses the animation, sleeps 2 s on the UI thread and quits the dialog. So the page's ending (`scan_state`) is the check circle with "Library Updated" and the songs ("738 songs, 34 new" when a whole scan grew the library past the count before it), "Scan Stopped" after Stop (flag 1: stock's Stop only stops the scan while the counter is under 3, and the same ending follows), or the memory chip with "Not Enough Space" (flag 2), each with Done in the accent; it holds until stock closes the dialog. Stock has no card-removed state: with the card pulled mid-scan (emulator: its music moved away and `/tmp/mmc_add` removed, 2026-11-16) it ends as a finish with the songs it had read, which become the library (3,800 songs fell to 3,000), and toasts its own "SD Card Removed". A finish with `/tmp/mmc_add` gone (stock's mount marks the card with it) is therefore drawn as the card glyph, "SD Card Removed" and "Put it back and scan again", not as Library Updated. `msg_sync` also runs in the paint hook, so it writes the folder's label only when it differs, and marks any change (`msg_dirty`) for the next poll to repaint the whole stack: stock's own repaint of its hidden label's box can read the ending first, which left Stop under the check in the emulator. Center presses the button there (`ringnav`, a click on `btn_no`), as a tap does; Return stops the scan as stock's does.

**USB Storage's eject.** `ringnav_ui_load` adds `usb_poll` to USB Storage's `usbmode_page` (`g_usbmode` not 1) as a 500 ms widget timer, so it goes with the page. Stock's `storage_config.sh` exports the card as LUN 0 of the configfs gadget `storage_demo`. The computer's eject is a SCSI START STOP UNIT with LoEj set and Start clear. Linux 5.10's `f_mass_storage` answers it in `do_start_stop` with `fsg_lun_close`, unless the host holds PREVENT ALLOW MEDIUM REMOVAL ([f_mass_storage.c](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.10/source/drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_mass_storage.c#L1298)). After that, `functions/mass_storage.msg/lun.0/file` reads empty (`fsg_show_file`, [storage_common.c](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.10/source/drivers/usb/gadget/function/storage_common.c#L330)). Once that file has read a path, an empty read is the eject. A missing file (no gadget yet, or one torn down) is none. Stock's timer (0x542d44, every 500 ms) rewrites `scrlabel_info` "USB Connected" through `usbmode_showface`, so `usb_poll` hides it and puts an `s_scrlabel_white24c` label in its place. The LUN stays closed until stock rebuilds the gadget, so the poll ends there and the page never goes back to Connected. Stock's teardown (`storage_config.sh stop`, from `usbmode_exit` at the page's window close, on the UI thread) unbinds the UDC, which closes nothing, then removes `lun.0`, which closes the LUN and its file together, so no tick reads it empty there. Limit: only a host that sends LoEj counts (macOS Finder, Linux `eject` and udisks, Windows Explorer's Eject). Windows' Safely Remove Hardware may only stop the device, which leaves the page on Connected. The vendor kernel (5.10.21 X2000) builds `f_mass_storage` in, and its xImage carries mainline's eject and close-backing-file messages; its only visible change there is the `pc_check` parameter (stock's PC-link status).

**USB DAC on a host that never reads the card.** Stock's `check_usb_status` (`0x4f3744`, once a second from the idle loop `on_wm_idle_status`) starts a gadget as soon as a cable is in (`g_usbdet_value` 1, `g_usblink_status` 1): under Audio and DAC (`g_usbmode` 1) the UAC2 one (`uac_device_config.sh start`), otherwise the card's (`storage_config.sh start`). It waits there until `toolsGetpclinkStatus` (`0x5d1ebc`) returns 1 (`g_usblink_status` 2), and only then does `on_wm_timer_dialog` open `usbmode_page`. For the Q2 (device type 23, the word `platform_init` hands `initToolsModule`) the link is a UDC state (`/sys/class/udc/13500000.otg/state`) of `configured`, in both USB modes. A charger has no host, so the UDC never reads `configured` there. Up to stock V1.32 the gate was `/sys/module/usb_f_mass_storage/parameters/pc_check`, which the vendor kernel sets when the host sends the drive a SCSI command, and the storage gadget came up first in both modes: a Nintendo Switch 2 configures the gadget and never sends it a SCSI command, so stock stayed a drive nobody read (#290). Q2 Muse hooked `check_usb_status` for that until its base moved to V1.34 (`patch/usb_dac.c`, gone), which does the same itself.

**Motion.** A theme's `<view name="motion">` holds one `<element>` per kind, `ms` and `easing` (`linear`, `cubic_out` and the rest of AWTK's names, and `follow` on Cover Flow's two steps: see [its step](#coverflow-step)) on each, and defaults to 0 ms; OLED's come from `ROLE_MACROS` (`MOTION_ROLES`: `PAGE_SLIDE_MS` and the rest, `patch/offsets.inc`). A window kind (`page`, `playing`, `coverflow`) also takes `anim` (`htranslate` unless `fade` or another AWTK animation) and becomes the window's `anim_hint`, e.g. `htranslate(duration=300,easing=sin_inout)`, as it loads or opens (`motion_load`, `motion_open`); a kind with no ms writes nothing and leaves the asset's own hint. `page` is a stock page that slides, `playing` Now Playing's close (its open stays immediate), and `coverflow` its page. No kind hints a page that has no slide of its own, nor any dialog: a dialog's background is clear, and an animated window is two snapshots, so a fade over a clear one shows black first (see [Queue menu](#queue-menu)). Every dialog, popup and the hold menu opens and closes in one frame. A widget kind (`inplace`, `swap`, `step`, `step_fast`, `coverflow_step`, `coverflow_step_fast`) glides a widget's own property with an animator: a level inside a page, Home's lists to and from Settings, the carousel's wheel step, slow and fast (`step_fast` within `HOME_FAST_WINDOW_MS` of the last), and Cover Flow's, the same. `recall ms` is how long a remembered row's glide takes (0 jumps). Every reader takes these rows through `motion_row` (`patch/ui_kit.c`), which under Reduce Motion (`IPOD REDUCEMOTION`, `motion_reduced`) answers `fade(duration=150)` for a window kind (Page's too, whose slide is its windows' asset hint `SLIDE`, so `motion_load` writes the fade over it on each window it loads), ms 0 for `inplace` and `swap`, and the steps as they are; the recall goes through `motion_ms`. A window already loaded keeps the hint it took, so the change shows from the next window opened. The rest of the payload's animations, each with its own `*_MS`, take their duration from `motion_ms(ms, kind)`, their curve from `motion_ease` (AWTK's `easing_type_t` numbers) and, where they have no loop pass of their own, their frames from one shared timer (`anim_start`, `motion_frames`: a 16 ms `timer_add` that repaints the top window and removes itself 16 ms after the last run ends); overlays (a toast, the confirmation card) run through `ovm_t`. A toast's exit outlives its dialog: `toast_gone` (its `EVT_DESTROY`) starts the exit and `feedback_toast_leave`, from `ringnav_paint`, paints the pill over the page under it until the exit ends. The confirmation card and a toast fade through their dialog's `widget_set_opacity`, which the shared timer sets on each frame (`ovm_bind`, `ovm_opacity`; 255 at once for an enter under Reduce Motion), from `confirm` on for the card and from the toast's first paint, at stock's 255, for a toast; `ovm_bind` forgets the dialog on its `EVT_DESTROY`. Never from the dialog's own paint: stock's `widget_paint` (demo 0x672848) returns before any paint hook while a widget's opacity byte (+0x34) is under 9 (`OVM_PAINT_MIN`), so a dialog at 0 whose paint was to raise it was never painted again: the card showed only the status row's dim, and a toast nothing. The card's answer waits the exit's 120 ms. The marquee, the volume and slider eases, the progress fill, the scroll indicator's and A-Z index's fades and the spinners are feedback, kept under Reduce Motion, and keep their own timers.

**Slider pages.** `slider_open` takes stock's Backlight, Max Volume, Balance and Boot Volume windows as they load, before their init, into the slider page's own form (`patch/slider_page.c`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#progress-and-sliders)), with stock's widgets kept by name.

**Dialogs.** Every question is the confirmation card over the page that asked (`confirm`, stock's confirm pop-up dressed as it by `feedback_confirm_dress`: the dialog's background cleared so the page shows, the card painted under its cells, the cells' words painted over the selection by `confirm_rows_paint`; ours on stock's `sortselect_dialog`, as the menu sheet's pickers; [Confirmation card](oled-design.md#confirmation-card)), the toast a pill over the page, and an empty page the empty state, the note under a page's rows its own form (`patch/feedback.c`, `feedback_confirm_dress`, `feedback_toast_paint`, `empty_state`, `feedback_empty`; [oled-design](oled-design.md#dialogs-and-toasts), [Empty and offline](oled-design.md#empty-and-offline)).

<a id="inset-modal"></a>**Menu sheet.** OLED draws its menus as [oled-design.md](oled-design.md#menus)'s frosted page sheet (`patch/menu_modal.c`). Now Playing's More is a stock window, which its asset makes a dialog (`modal_page`: root type `dialog`, the screen's box, no slide), so the window manager keeps painting Now Playing under it; its init (`ringnav_playermore`) sets `to_modal` 0, as sortselect's init does, so `navigator_to` returns rather than running `dialog_modal`'s loop. `modal_frame` hides the title bar, clears the dialog's background, puts the list at y 50 (58 with no header) down to the screen's foot and stacks the rows 32 px high and the screen's width (`modal_row_w`); the header's space is an empty label 72 px high named `_mm_head` at the head of the rows, so it scrolls away with them, and a gap is an empty label 12 px high; neither is a row (`collect` takes only clickable widgets). The header (`modal_head`: name, line under it, cover) is set by the caller before the frame: `qm_open`, `modal_more` (the playing song, `queue_now`), `ringnav_playlistsmore` and `playlist_page_hold`; a picker over a sheet copies that sheet's. A cover is the player's own for the playing song (`now_cover`), else the server library's (`catalogue_cover`) or Cover Flow's cached one (`art_path` by `album_key`), as an album page finds it. The list's content is padded by what lies past the list end (y 282 to 320) and `list_pad` reads that pad (`_list_pad`, `_list_padded`), so `scroll_end` stops the wheel's and a drag's last row on y 282; `sel_height` gives a sheet's rows the height to the list end (`modal_sel_height`) and `fit_top` leaves them unsnapped, since they pass under the sheet's top fade. The list's `item_height` and `default_item_height` go to 0, so the stock layouter stacks each child at its own height and `settings_list` never reads the list as settings rows. `modal_paint`, from `ringnav_paint_bg` on the dialog, draws the page receding and the sheet straight into the screen's 375 x 320 BGRA buffer, as `engine.c`'s `eng_paint` does, within the canvas's clip: on the first paint whose clip is the whole screen, while nothing slides, `sheet_build` reads the page under it there (every window under the dialog has just painted) and makes, once, the 80 rows the receding page can show in (bilinear at 94% about the center, then dimmed) and the material for the sheet's rows (the receding page averaged onto a 94 x 80 grid, three box passes of radius 5 each way, scaled back bilinearly, its color raised 1.6 times from its luma, 28% kept under 6% white or, in Light Mode, under 75% white, plus a hashed grain of +-3 levels), about 540 KB on the heap until the last open sheet closes, when what it drew straight into the buffer is cleared to black and the whole screen is painted again (`modal_gone`, `sheet_repaint`): a page that paints nothing under the status row, Edit Home's, would keep it; the sheet's 40 px top corners are antialiased from a table of their insets. Until then, and on a window's snapshot, it draws the page dimmed in place and a flat `#1C1C1E` sheet. `paint_modal_rows`, on the rows' surface after the selection, draws each row's symbol (`menu_<stem>_<d|l|w>`, `tools/art.py` `MENU_ICONS`), value (ending in an ellipsis short of its label) and direction caret from the props `modal_row` left on it; a destructive row (`modal_red`: `QA_DELETE`, Delete Song, Delete Playlist, a `trash` action of `modal_actions`) sets its label red, white while lit, and `paint_selection` fills its bar `#FF3B30`. `modal_after`, from `ringnav_paint` on the rows' surface once they are painted, draws the header at the rows' scroll and fades the rows into the material by `foot_alpha` from y 266 and, once scrolled, for 14 px under the list's top, the lit row never, all within the rows' box. The scroll indicator is a list's. `paint_selection` keeps a row bar the rows' own width and lights the row of the page under a sheet, which names what the menu acts on, and `bar_title_sync` titles the bar from the page under one (`feedback_under`) and leaves Songs' action row in place, so after a dialog over the sheet that wrote its own title (Delete Playlist's confirm, `feedback_confirm`) closes, the bar names the page again. The menu's row is lit from the pass after it opens (`modal_lit`): a tap that opened it would otherwise hide the selection. Return closes the dialog itself (`modal_back`, in place of stock's `on_common_keyup`, which goes back a page and would close the page under it). The sheet moves through ui_kit.h's `ovm_t` ([Overlay motion](oled-design.md#overlay-motion); `sheet_run`, the one place its timing and easing are given): `modal_frame` registering the first open sheet sets it waiting (`sheet_wait`: progress 0, the rows 280 px low), and its first whole paint, once the material is made, keeps the page alone (`sheet_start`, a 375 x 320 copy, 480 KB until the last sheet closes) starts the rise (260 ms `cubic_out`, `ovm_enter`) and a 16 ms timer (`sheet_tick`) that reads its level (`ovm_level`), moves the rows (`sheet_shift`: the list, or a dialog of rows alone's rows) and paints the screen again; `sheet_frame` draws each frame from the kept page, scaled from 100% to 94% about the center and dimmed by the progress, under the material faded in by it from the sheet's lowered top with its corners, and `modal_after` lowers the header with the rows. Return (`modal_back`, `pick_back`, the hold menu's `qm_back`, Up Next's `un_back`) goes through `modal_close`: with the material and the kept page it falls (180 ms quadratic ease-in, `ovm_exit`, from where a rise left it), `modal_closing` makes `ringnav_keyup` take every key meanwhile, and `sheet_tick` closes the window at its end; with neither, or for a picker over another sheet, it closes at once. A pick closes at once. Under Reduce Motion `sheet_frame` draws the sheet in place and cross-fades the strip above the rows from the kept page, and `modal_after` the rows' box, linear, over `ovm_t`'s 150 ms in and 120 ms out. Up Next (`upnext.c`) is a sheet with `_mm_own` set, so `modal_frame` keeps each row's own height (46 px songs, 24 px Playing Next, 26 px "From"); its header is the playing song (`modal_head` and `modal_head_bars`, which draws `un_bars` after the name), taken again when the rows are (a frame with a new header replaces the old), and a row's cover and Clear's pill round onto the material (`modal_corners`). In More, stock's rows keep their buttons and handlers: the symbol comes from each row's kind (`PLAYMORE_ROWS` by the button's name), AirPlay's and Get Album Lyrics' from their images; stock's Download Cover & Lyrics reads Get Cover & Lyrics; Delete Song moves last behind a gap (its confirm is stock's); A-B Repeat's stock switch image hides and `modal_row_paint` draws the theme's switch on the right column from that image's state (`switch_on`, `switch_off`: `switch_mark` in `patch/list_marks.c`, 40x24 with a 20 px knob, as settings rows' are drawn); Multiple Speed's four buttons hide, insensitive too (stock's hit test skips only an insensitive widget, so a hidden one still took a tap on the row and set its speed; a pick dispatches its click to the button all the same), and its row reads "Speed" with the speed as its value, opening `modal_pick`, a sortselect dialog of the four (the rating picker's too, [Ratings](#ratings)), under which More's rows, sheet and header hide (the dialog stays shown: a hidden window hands the keys to the page under it); a pick sends stock's own speed button for it a click, so stock's debounce, `PLAYSPEED` and the folder speed (`ringnav_speed`) are unchanged. In the hold menu, a setting's value is its choice without the label's word (`qm_value_name`), and Group by flips in place on Center (`qm_run`, which leaves the sheet open and writes the setting rows' values again, `qm_values`). ponytail: the material is made once, so a page that changes under an open sheet (Now Playing's time) shows as it was; making it again on each whole paint would follow it.

The hold menu (`qm_open`) is the same panel: every row takes its symbol by action, and Shuffle, Repeat and Group by are settings, their values on the right column; the set writes Favorites in US English. On Songs (class `0xf001`) the menu has no Sorting row: Songs' order is Settings > Playback > Library > Sorting's Songs picker (`library_settings.c`), and the Shuffle row's Sort bars hide (`action_row`), and the row's wheel stop with them (`shuffle_key`). `patch/song_sort.c` keeps the order: Recently Added is stock's `g_sort_flag` 3 or 4 (newest or oldest first), which `getAllMusic`'s query takes; with the flag 0 (title order) `[IPOD] SONGSORT` and `SONGDOWN` name Title, Artist or Album and the direction, and `songs_load` reorders the loaded list (`song_order`: a stable merge sort of indices by artist, or by album then disc and track, an untagged name last either way, then the records moved into place a cycle at a time, whole, as Play Next moves rows). A pick writes all three keys at once and sets `g_sort_changeflag` (`song_sort_commit`), which Songs reads as it comes back to the top, as after stock's picker. `name_sorted` (`patch/az_index.c`) keeps the fast-scroll letter for titles A to Z alone. Other themes keep stock's picker and order.

A playlist's More (`ringnav_playlistsmore`) is a dialog over Playlists the same way, its rows the list_items in the dialog itself, placed in the panel by `modal_frame` with no list: Rename, Edit Playlist, then Delete Playlist after a gap, which asks first (stock's confirm).

**A page's switch.** The pages have no toolbars (`tools/ipod.py` `patch_asset`), so stock's toolbar switch moves to a row reading On or Off: `ringnav_sleeptimer` on Sleep Timer.

**Final text.** `text_ink` stores a label's final color as what Light Mode's style hook turns into it, so the stored value depends on the half. `light_apply`'s `text_inks` walks the windows at Auto's turn and writes each again.

**Home's pane.** It follows the highlighted row (`coverflow_home_row()`, from `paint_selection` and the wheel): Now Playing's row shows the playing cover and every other row the library's slideshow (`art_source`, [ipod.md](ipod.md#home)).

**Light and dark.** Every scheme has a dark and a light half (`theme_t.schemes`, `theme_t.light`). Light Mode (Off, On, Auto) picks one through `scheme()`, and a scheme's `mode` can keep it to one. theme.xml states a half's drawn-as-stated colors as `light.<key>`/`dark.<key>` (unprefixed: the dark half, stock's terms), and a half it leaves out is the flip of the other's grays. A theme that states no final value has one array serve both of its halves.

**Other keys.** `tools/theme.py` also reads `list.art.*` (x, text_x, text_end, placeholder, radius) and `list.scrollbar.*` (`paint_scrollbar`'s track and thumb while the wheel turns, from a list's border paint, with stock's bar drawn clear; `sb_w` 0 keeps stock's).

### Playlists without a toolbar

With no toolbars `tools/ipod.py` hides `view_navbar` and takes its room for the list, whose `default_item_height` is the Songs pitch with no `item_height`: `children_layouter_list_view` (`0x5fcd44`) then gives each row its own height, so 52 px playlists stack with 32 px action rows. `ringnav_playlist`, after every stock rebuild (`0x4b5444`), dresses the rows (`pl_dress`): the tile row at index 0 hides and each playlist row's art (stock's 52 px image, [Playlist art](#playlist-art)) shows only where the set has row art (`geom(G_ART)`, OLED's; not in the picker), at the page rows' art place (x 22) with the text from x 80 and 60 px narrower, as an album row's, else hides; the parts take `pl_fit`'s places on the page rows' boxes, under a full-width button so the chevron and band are the list's. Stock's count label is re-worded from its own number, so no second query runs. Rows it can't have are added: Select All, New Playlist… and Select Playlists… restacked to indexes 1 to 3, above the playlists (the two modes never show Select All with the other two), then Import Playlists, Export, Delete and Done; the Add to Playlist picker, which has no tile row, gets New Playlist… alone, at index 0. They are shown by `pl_rows` for the mode, each list item tagged with its action (`PL_ACT`), which `pl_rows` reads in one walk, so no row is found by its place. Select All reads Deselect All while `g_allselect_flag` (`0xa4ca30`) is set: stock's Select All (`0x4b46a4`) toggles on it, and a row's mark sets it to whether every row is marked (`0x4b4950`), so a hand-marked full list clears on the next tap. No stock function is replaced. Each row's click runs next pass (the latest click in a pass wins; the action is the timer's ctx) and finds its target by the handler bound to it, in the hidden toolbar or the hidden tile row (`pl_stock`), and dispatches a click there, so `g_navbar_status`, the marks in `p_vector_select_record`, every dialog and the reload stay stock's; `0x4b44d4` and `0x4b45ec` rebuild only the toolbar, so `pl_rows` runs after them, and after each mark on a second click handler. A row is its action whatever scrolled: nothing keys on an index. The separators (`PAGE_TALL`) go on every shown row, playlist or action, but the list's last, in one walk from the end. With nothing remembered (a first open, or a count changed), `reconcile`'s fresh-page row, the first visible, moves past an action row to the first playlist (`pl_first`), as stock's and the iPod's lists hold playlists alone; an empty list stays on New Playlist…. Just after New Playlist made one, it lands on that one instead, as an iPod's list lands on what was added: `ringnav_playlist_create` keeps the new name (`pl_made`) and `pl_first` finds the playlist row whose `p_deque_playlist` record has it, then forgets it. A remembered row comes back by its text (position memory), so the playlists' shift by two rows lands on the same playlist. Between modes `pl_rows` maps the selection: into select mode on the first playlist, out of it a playlist keeps its own, Select All goes to the first playlist and an action row to Select Playlists…. Export reads `g_navbar_status` after its confirm returns, which `dialog_modal` (`0x65271c`) does before an idle closes the dialog (`0x6521dc`), so a marked Export stays marked; that close is what ends select mode (`0x4b58d4`, `EVT_WINDOW_TO_FOREGROUND`), as stock's. Return in select mode runs Done: `0x4f2394`, which would close the page and leave the flag set, is rebound to `pl_keyup`, which falls through to it when no Done target exists; a page destroyed in the mode (held Return to Home, `PL_MARKING` set) clears the flag, and only then. Stock's hit from x 286 opens More outside select mode (`0x4b48a8` branches on `g_navbar_status`, `0x4b4988`), so every row's click goes through `pl_pick` first: a picker's rows pick with a fresh click at x 0, and in the list a tap left of the dots' column (from x 333), the chevron's column (from x 317, `CHEVRON_W` from the edge) with it, opens the playlist the same way. The dots sit at the right edge, centered on the picker's tick (x 346), as the other trailing marks and values do, since only the selected row has a chevron; on that row the chevron shows in their place, and a tap opens the playlist out to the edge (its More is the hold's). The picker draws no chevron, since a pick adds and closes. Stock's relayout of a playlist row keeps `pl_fit`'s places: `compact_row_layout` hands a `PL_ROW` item's button to `pl_fit`. The dots and marks are `paint_radio`'s; stock's `img_more` keeps its name for the hold menu, its image emptied as a ring. The bar reads the toolbar's first label, which stock writes with the last list opened (`g_navbar_name`); `pl_rows` writes what the mode is.

**Playlists' add mode and memory.** `PLAYLIST_ADD_MODE` is one global that only a mode 2 pick clears, and the page reads it as it comes back to the front, so a page below a picker rebuilt in the picker's form. `ringnav_playlist` keeps each window's own in a prop and writes it back before each rebuild. Opening a playlist writes `g_local_classinfo_save` (`0x4b4be8`), which `context_now`'s scope hashed, so the page lost its row on the way back; its scope is the add mode alone, so the picker keeps its own row.

## Page transitions (iPod)

Stock V1.36 carries AWTK's window animators and uses one: `saverscreen_page.bin` has `close_anim_hint` `slide_left(duration=200,easing=cubic_out)`, the only hint in the stock assets (the lock window, which the build leaves out: [Screen off and wake](#screen-off-and-wake)). The window manager builds the animator named by a window's `anim_hint` (`window_animator_htranslate_create`, `0x696fb8`, for `htranslate`) when it opens or closes. `navigator_to_with_context` (`0x4f6e74`) opens a page above the rest and `navigator_back` (`0x4f6ffc`) is `window_manager_back`, so the page below stays alive and Return reverses the slide.

iPod sets the hint in its assets ([ipod.md](ipod.md#transitions)). `htranslate` animates two snapshots. `window_animator_prepare` (`0x696498`) paints both pages into offline canvases, through the payload's paint hooks, before `window_manager_is_animating` (`0x6810a4`) becomes true and while the sliding page is the top window; a hinted page is not painted before that, so its snapshot is its first paint. Each frame then blits the snapshots (the page under drifting and darkening: [Page parallax](#page-parallax)) and paints only the status bar. The payload follows the snapshots in four places (`slides()`, `patch/navigation.c`). A surface whose own window is under a sliding top window draws the row it holds and nothing else: loading, recall and settling read the top page's state. A sliding page reveals its remembered row at once instead of by the glide, so it does not arrive mid-glide. Home's art is checked when Home itself is painted, not only when it is the top window. After a touch, a Return by button ends [touch mode](#touch-mode) on a 0 ms timer instead of at once: the closing page's snapshot, painted inside stock's handling of the release, keeps its row hidden, while the page behind shows its own.

## Status bar (iPod)

The background hook also handles top-level widgets, whose parent is the window manager. The status bar widget, which `system_bar_init` stores in the `system_bar` global (`0xa4e8a0`, a size-checked `CONTEXT_DATA` entry), gets one `canvas_fill_rect` in black, `BAR_COLOR` (`#000000`), without a highlight, with the LCD fill color restored.

`label_clock` in the bar shows the device's local time, read once a minute rather than on paint: `clock_show` calls `time` and `localtime_r` (stock libc, with a caller-owned time buffer) for the hour and minute (`struct tm` `+8`, `+4`), applies Auto Light Mode's hour, and arms a timer due at the next minute (`60 - tm_sec` seconds; a minute after a failed read). The label follows stock's 24-hour setting (`g_time24h_flag`): `%02d:%02d` (`18:14`), or, on a bar with its own title (OLED's status row), `%d:%02d` so it clears the title, or `%d:%02d %s`, a 12-hour clock without seconds or a leading zero (`12:05 AM`, `6:14 PM`), through `tk_snprintf`, then `widget_set_text_utf8`. A failed `time` (`-1`) or `localtime_r` (null), or an out-of-range field, shows `--:--`. The minute and the 24-hour setting are kept as a key, so the label is looked up and written only when what it shows changes. Besides the timer, `clock_show` runs at once for a new time zone (`ringnav_timezone`), a time set by hand, and a wake, and the pass after the bar first paints or paints with a new 24-hour setting rearms it at 0 ms; a network time sync while lit shows at the next minute. Nothing else reads the time, so stock threads' `localtime` (one shared static buffer) has nothing to race. Every page and dialog shows it. There is no volume flash: stock `on_wm_keyup_fun` opens `dialog/volume_dialog` on every volume turn (`0x4f333c`).

The same paints run `bar_sync`. `systembar_showface` (`0x5417d0`) sets `img_bt`'s image every tick: a codec badge (`bar_sbc`, `bar_aac`, `bar_aptx`, `bar_aptxhd`, `bar_ldac`, by `bt_showcoding`) while Bluetooth is linked, otherwise `bar_bt` or `bar_btcon`. It also sets `img_battery`'s image (`bar_charge`, `bar_lowcharge` under 15%, else `bar_battery`), `label_battery`'s `%d%%` text and `progress_battery`'s value, and never the battery widgets' visibility. A badge that differs from the last one arms a `CODEC_MS` UI timer, whose steps set `widget_set_opacity` (`0x66d494`, the widget's `+0x34` byte, which `widget_paint` applies as the canvas global alpha) down and back up, switching the image to `bar_btcon` halfway. After that the bar's background paint, which runs before its children, puts `bar_btcon` back over each badge stock sets again, so no badge frame is drawn. A hidden `img_bt` or a non-badge image other than `bar_btcon` ends the flash. `bar_sync` then hides `img_battery` and `label_battery` and shows `view_battery` with `widget_set_visible`, which returns early for an unchanged state and otherwise marks the parent for relayout (`widget_set_need_relayout_children`). The slot is sized to its ink: a percentage is its digit count times the `'0'` advance plus the `'%'` advance, both measured with `canvas_measure_text` on the first battery paint (`BATT_PCT_W` until then). `view_battery` is painted in the background hook from the level (`label_battery`'s text, since stock sets `progress_battery` to 0 while charging) and the charge state (`img_battery`'s image), and is invalidated when those or its displayed mode change. Stock's battery writes land on the hidden `label_battery` and `img_battery`, so they repaint nothing, and the bar paints each second only while something on it changes (a codec badge stock sets again): `ringnav_showface`, after stock's tick and while lit, reads the same level and charge state and, when they differ from what the slot shows, keeps them and invalidates the bar, so the next frame shows them and `bar_sync` has nothing more to repaint. A change while dark waits for the wake's paint. `BATTERY=3` uses a compact 28×15 solid rounded battery (radius 3; stock squares any radius under 3) with dark 13 px digits inside, omitting the percent sign; its body follows the charge-state color. Resizing the slot immediately relayouts its parent row.

## Level bars

The playing song's level bars (the status row's play state, Home's first row in `home_np.c`, Up Next's header through `un_bars`) are one motion in `ui_kit.c` ([oled-design](oled-design.md#level-bars)). `lvl_h16` gives bar `i`'s height at a time `t`, between a user's `lo` and `hi` px in sixteenths: a Catmull-Rom spline through `lvl_keys`, the status row's ten approved frames (0 to 1000 a bar), one every `LVL_STEP_MS` (125 ms), so a 1.25 s loop that passes each frame without stopping; the sums are in thousandths, so nothing needs 64-bit arithmetic on the MIPS. Each user keeps an `lvl_clock_t`: `lvl_run` starts it from the time it held and stops it where it is, so a pause holds the bars and a resume goes on from that height, never a jump; zero is stopped at the loop's start. `lvl_fill` draws a bar of whole pixels with its part-covered top row at that part of the ink's alpha, so a canvas without subpixel boxes still shows a height between pixels (the status row draws its round-ended bars with vgcanvas at the float height instead). Frames come from `motion_loop`: one shared `MO_LOOP_MS` (33 ms) timer calls each user's frame function while it returns 1 (`sr_bars_frame`, `hn_frame`, `un_bars_frame`), and each invalidates only its bars' box (the status row's 10 px play box on the bar, Home's 13 x 13 glyph box on `img_playing`, Up Next's 12 x 13 box where `un_bars` last painted, on the sheet's window); the timer ends with the last loop and never repaints the top window, as `motion_frames` does. A user's frame function says 0 once its bars stop (paused, out of sight, the screen dark, Reduce Motion: `MO_DECOR`), and its own sync starts the loop again (`status_row_sync`, `home_np_sync`, `un_poll` and `un_bars`). ponytail: the cost is measured only in the emulator (qemu-user on a laptop, 2026-11-17, a frame about 47 ms there, so about 20 a second): `demo`'s CPU with the bars moving less with them still was 8.5 points of a core on a titled page, 10.2 on Home and 6.9 on Up Next, where the 8-a-second steps had cost 2.7, 7.3 and 8.6 (Up Next's then repainted the whole header). A Q2 with Bluetooth audio playing, measured over q2remote, would say whether `MO_LOOP_MS` should go to 40 or 50 ms.

## Status row slots

OLED's status row (`patch/status_row.c`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#status-row)) lays its glyphs out right to left from the battery as slots (`status_slot_t`: a width function, 0 while hidden, the gap before the shown slot to its right, a painter): the battery (`SLOT_BATTERY`, stock's `view_battery`, which the bar's right group still places and `paint_battery` paints), the play state (`SLOT_PLAY`, 10 px), Wi-Fi (`SLOT_WIFI`, `SR_WIFI_W` 16 px), a card app's sync (`SLOT_SYNC`, 16 px), Bluetooth (`SLOT_HEADSET`: the rune's 14 px while a device connects or one is connected with no level, a car's glyph at `SR_CAR_W` 19 px, or a headset's `headphones` glyph, 2 px and a 15x8 battery and its nub, 33 px) and Buttons Lock's padlock (`SLOT_LOCK`, 13 px), each `SR_GAP` (6) left of the one on its right. A hidden slot takes no room. `status_slots_left` is the leftmost shown slot's left, the edge `clock_place` ends the clock's box `CLOCK_BESIDE` (7) short of, which leaves 8 px of ground after the digits' ink, and the title's box with it, so a new glyph never wraps anything: the title ellipsizes sooner. `status_slots_paint`, from `ringnav_paint_bg` after the bar's own background (and Split's art rows, an artist's cap, About's header), paints every shown slot but the battery in final colors (`ui_ink_raw`), so Home in Split inks them with the clock over the art (`home_ink`, one ink for the row, [Home](ipod.md#home)). Every glyph is `SR_INK` (11) px tall on the clock's digits' rows, 17 to 27 on OLED's `status_y` 23: a glyph box `SR_GLYPH` (14) tall goes on `cy - 7` with its ink from `tools/art.py`'s `STATUS_TOP` (1), and the slim battery's 12 px body rises `BATT_BODY_RISE` (1) to rows 16 to 27 (`batt_top`). The glyphs are `tools/art.py`'s: Wi-Fi's fan drawn from geometry (`wifi_fan`, `status_wifi`), `wifi-x`, the Bluetooth rune, `headphones` and `car-profile` sized by their ink's height (`status_fit`, `STATUS_FIT`), the padlock as before. Sizes and gaps are `mock_status_icons.py`'s (the user's, 2026-11-16).

The play state is drawn with vgcanvas from `play_bars`' boxes, in Text Primary playing or paused: playing, three 2 px bars with round ends 4 px apart, their feet `SR_BAR_DROP` (5) below the row's center (the digits' baseline), their heights from ui_kit.c's level-bar motion (`lvl_h16`, 3 to 11 px, at `sr.clock`'s time: [Level bars](#level-bars)); paused, the pause, two `SR_PAUSE_W` (3) px bars 11 tall with 0.9 px corners at 0.5 and 6.5 px into the same 10 px box; stopped, none (`bar_status`, any player). Between playing and paused the two cross-dissolve over `SR_XFADE_MS` (250 ms, cubic ease-out) in that box: `status_row_sync` starts `sr.xfade` (`play_xfade_sync`) when the state changes with the slot shown at the sync before (a slot that appears shows its state at once), `play_paint` draws the bars at their stopped frame at the opacity left and the pause over them at the rest, `sr_tick` moves no frame while it runs, and the frames come from ui_kit.c's shared timer, which calls `sr_xfade_frame` (`motion_hook`: the timer repaints only the top window, and the bar is a window of its own) to invalidate the play box alone, once more after the end. The run is `MO_SPATIAL`, so Reduce Motion makes it a cut. Wi-Fi reads stock's own status-bar widget, `img_wifi`, kept off-screen and current by `systembar_showface`: `bar_wifi1` to `bar_wifi4` light the fan's dot, then its two bands (3 and 4 all three), the rest in `#3A3A3C`; off, Smart Wi-Fi's radio off, not connected or `bar_wifi0`, the slot hides. Connected with no internet is `wifi-x-bold`, read as stock's network monitor's word (`networkGetConnectStatus`, `0x5c2bdc`, a load of the state its thread sets) at 0 while the bars say connected. ponytail: that is a link with an address, not the internet; nothing on the Q2 probes past the access point (stock has no such check), so a captive portal or a dead uplink shows the full glyph. A DNS lookup or an HTTP check from a worker thread would lift it. The Bluetooth slot reads stock's link list: its last item at status 3 is a device connected (as stock's rows read it), and a link thread running (`bt_connectstatus` 1) with an item listed is one connecting (the rune in Text Tertiary, `status_btdim`); connected, a car by its Class (`bt_headset_class`, `bt_kind`) shows `car-profile`, a headset with a level (`bt_headset_battery()`, 0-100, -1 for none, read from BlueZ's `org.bluez.Battery1` by `patch/bt_battery.c`, [Headset battery](#headset-battery)) `headphones` and `battery_slim`'s 15x8 battery at that level (red under 20% as the status battery's), any other the rune in Text Primary.
