While a guest plays (`guest_active`, [Guest Play screens](#guest-play-screens)) the slot is the guest's phone in the accent (`status_guest`), and with `out` a Bluetooth device the relay mark and that device's glyph. Stock's own status-bar Bluetooth glyph and its codec badge stay off-screen. A --dev build reads `/mnt/data/q2-status.fake` (`status_fake`, at most every 500 ms) for the emulator, which has no radio or charger: `wifi=N`, `charge=1` and `charge=2` stand in for the Wi-Fi level, a charging cable and a cable holding the battery full (`battery_now`), so those slots can be shown and shot there; a release build has none of it.

The bars ride ui_kit.c's shared loop (`sr_bars_frame` through `motion_loop`) while `bars_moving`: lit, playing, the slot shown, no dissolve running and motion allowed; `status_row_sync` starts it, and each frame invalidates only the play box. A frame timer (`SR_FRAME_MS`, 125 ms) turns the sync arrows while the screen is lit and a sync checks, started by `status_row_sync` from `bar_state_sync` (each bar paint and stock's 1 s showface) and ended by the first tick that finds none; each tick moves their frame and invalidates only their box of the bar (the ring's 16 px). Either repaints only those columns, inked over Split's art there with the cut edges kept (`INK_CUT_*`). `status_row_sync` also keeps a signature of what the slots show (which ones, the play state, Wi-Fi's level or its crossed glyph, the sync's kind and its ring to a fiftieth, the Bluetooth slot's kind and the headset's level, the lock) and returns 1 when it changes, so the whole bar repaints once after the frame and the clock moves. A tap (`status_touch`) finds its slot with `status_slot_at`: a 44 x 40 px target round each shown slot's center (the battery's body's, or its percentage's on Percent), the nearer center where two meet. The battery's toasts its state ([Charging](#charging)); the bars' opens Now Playing (`playback_np_open`, from a 0 ms timer, after the input's dispatch), as stock's `img_state` did before it went off-screen.

## Now Playing (iPod)

`playing_page_init` (`0x53e334`, standard PIC prologue, resumed at `0x53e340`) registers the page's handlers, runs the page update (`0x53cf08`) once and starts a 250 ms widget timer (`playing_timer_start`, `0x53d928`) that runs it again. The update finds each widget with a recursive `widget_lookup`, skips any it does not find, and gets the times from `player_playtime_and_length` (`0x51ee10`): elapsed and total seconds from `mclGetPlayTime` (`0x5be768`), less a CUE track's start, elapsed clamped to the total, both 0 while stopped. It sets `slider_play` to value = elapsed, max = total, and formats both labels with `toolsTimeItoa` (`0x5cef40`): `%02d:%02d`, or `%02d:%02d:%02d` from an hour. `label_playlen` is its only reference to that name.

The hook runs the stock init, then caches `label_ipod_album`, `label_ipod_remain` and the slider, and syncs them. It also caches `img_cover`, whose border paint (after the image) rounds its corners in the page's black with `corner_mask`, each corner pixel at the share of it the arc leaves uncovered ([Rounded corners](#rounded-corners)). Painting the top window or the status bar syncs them again. The page shows no queue position; `MCL_POS` and the queue's length still go into the album's key, so a new song of the same album restarts its marquee. The album is that record's `REC_ALBUM` (the record comes from `queue_now`, which Home's art shares), or, once `player_get_id3info` (`0x51f3a4`) has parsed that record's file, the album it parsed: `g_play_id3_info` (`0xa5520c`, `0xa9c` bytes) holds the parsed path at `+0`, album at `+0x404`, artist at `+0x504` and title at `+0x684` (`now_tag`). For a CUE track (`mclGetCueFlag`: the playing record has a CUE start or end) stock copies the record's tags instead of reading the file: stock's sheet parser (`0x5d2f4c`) gives each track the sheet's `TITLE` as album and the last `PERFORMER` seen (the track's, else the sheet's) as artist. Its copy of the parsed path (`ID3_PATH`, `0x51f5d0`), which every fresh parse reaches before Now Playing's title and artist lines are written, becomes `jal ringnav_id3_path`: an empty album or artist there is taken from the file's own tags (`toolsGetMusicInfo`), so a sheet without `TITLE` or `PERFORMER` (common for audiobooks) shows the book and author instead of Unknown Artist. Album artist is filled the same way. ponytail: only the playing track's tags; Library lists and the database keep the sheet's empty fields (Library's Artists and Albums leave audiobooks out anyway), so Home's and Now Playing's art key (artist, album) can miss Coverflow's cache, keyed on the database's values; fill at scan time if that matters. When a folder play (class 1) reaches its last track with the folder-jump setting on (Folder Skip, the byte `0xa5002b`), `mclNextSong` calls `on_player_autochange` (`0x51eca8`), whose `toolsLoadNextDir` and `player_refresh_playqueue(1)` replace the queue with the next folder's untagged file records, and only the parsed tags name the next album. Every stock folder jump tests class 1, so Coverflow plays its albums as stock's album class `0xff10` and Most Played and Shuffle Songs as `0xf001`. `album_memory` also writes the album into `g_memory_info` (`+0x60d` Unknown flag, `+0x611` name), as `player_load_songlist` does for stock lists, so stock resume rebuilds that album with `getMusicByAlbum`. Home's art keys its Coverflow cache lookup the same way. The remaining time is the slider's max less its value, in stock's format with a leading minus, so it matches the elapsed label and follows a touch drag. Each label is written only when its source changes (position, queue length, album string pointer, or those seconds); `EVT_DESTROY` drops the cache. Stock's total label stays hidden.

**One page.** Stock's navigator opens a `playing_page` over whatever is in front, so a song played from a page Now Playing opened (its artist or album tap, the ⋯ page's Look up, then Shuffle or a song there) would leave the first page under it: covered, its 250 ms timer stopped, still showing the song it last showed, and the page Return comes back to before Home. Once stock's init has built the new page, `ringnav_playing` force-closes every other `playing_page` in the window manager (`np_only`, `patch/nav/now_playing.c`) and leaves the pages between, so Return goes to the artist page and then Home. A page stock refused (headphones required) closes nothing. `play_folder` (`patch/coverflow.c`) also closes a Now Playing in front before it opens one, so that open slides from the page under it.

The V8.6 folder-rollover regression in `test/patch.py` executes stock `player_mainscheduling` → `mclAutoChange` → `mclNextSong` → `on_player_autochange` → `toolsLoadNextDir` → `player_refresh_playqueue` → `mclLoadPlayList`, then stock tag parsing, cover-worker completion and the Now Playing timer (`0x53d810`). Filesystem enumeration, tag decoding, image decoding and the audio decoder are mocked at their boundaries; the harness does not supply the resulting player metadata globals. Equal-sized and one-track sibling folders, reused positions, missing tags/art, consecutive transitions, and delayed scheduler/cover completion pass in Stock and iPod. iPod's paint hooks also verify album text and Home art before and after completion. This does not reproduce a V8.6 regression, so no additional metadata firmware change is made.

**Info page**. The page update fills the info page through `0x53bc78` (its one call, a `bal` at `0x53d308`, after the player status checks): `label_album`, `label_genre`, `label_encode`, `label_year`, `label_bits`, `label_kbps` and `label_sample` as `%s:%s` or `%s:%d…` (`Album:Kid A`, `Bit Depth:16bit`, `Sample Rate:44.1kHz`; `%s:%s` is also wpa_supplicant's literal, so stays), `label_size` as `%s:%.2fMB`, and `label_location` as the bare folder with `/mnt/mmc/` as `SD:/` (it looks up `player_location` and never uses it), a missing value as the first `player_unknown`, which en_US has twice ("Unknown Artist", then "Unknown"). The build makes that call `jal ringnav_np_info` (`NP_INFO_CALL`), which runs it, then rewrites each line: `: ` after the label, a space before `MB`, `kbps` and `kHz` and a hyphen before `bit` after a digit, "Unknown Artist" as "Unknown", and the folder after `player_location`'s label (`getFormatString`), only where the text changes. Its labels **Genre** and **Year** are `LABELS` renames of `genre` (which the search page's tab shares) and `player_era`. The page is not in the swipe: `tools/ipod.py` `np_info_out` takes `view_info` out of the `slide_view` (so the dots count the art and lyrics pages) and makes it the window's first child, hidden, its box the slide's place in the window and its own layout dropped; stock's lookups are by name and deep, so its fill finds the labels there. ⋯'s **About** row (`more_rows` in `patch/onlinematch.c`, `list_row` with stock's `system_about` icon, under OLED's menu sheet the Phosphor `info` symbol) runs `np_about_open` (`patch/np_about.c`): a payload window (`page_open`, `npabout_page`) titled About (`page_title`), into which it moves `view_info` (`widget_remove_child`, `widget_add_child`, stock's own, in `FUNCTIONS`) and shows it, then fills it at once. A payload window has Now Playing's box, so the details stand where they stood on the swipe, or under the page's title where the theme shows it as a first row and the details start above its foot. While it is open `ringnav_np_info` fills the page instead of Now Playing's window, the Genre marquee (`genre_fill`, `genre_over`) runs while About is the top window, Smart Awake holds the screen on it and Enlarged Album Art's countdown stays full. Return (`ab_key`) puts `view_info` back in Now Playing's window, hidden, while both are whole, then goes back a page (`page_keyup`), to ⋯ as its other rows' pages do; a close by any other way puts it back from the destroy event, or, if Now Playing went first (`np_gone` calls `np_about_np_gone`), leaves it to go with the page. No setting or saved state names a Now Playing page: stock opens the page on the art each time, so nothing points at the old third page.

`playing_page`'s labels are the source of About's info grid (`np_info_values`, from `np_grid`): each label gets a hidden `<name>_value` `hscroll_label`, and the view stays hidden. There `ringnav_np_info` renames stock's English "File Size", "Encoding" and "Bitrate" to the grid's "Size", "Format" and "Bit Rate" (another language's names stay stock's) and ends with `np_about_fill` (`patch/np_about.c`). While About is open that reads the values back from the page: the header's title, artist, length (the slider's `max`) and cover (Now Playing's `img_cover` image, drawn scaled with `canvas_draw_image`, its corners rounded into the page's black); the quality line, Lossless or Hi-Res Lossless by codec, bit depth (over 16) and sample rate (over 48 kHz), DSD by codec with its multiple of 44.1 kHz from the bit rate (stock's sample rate for a DSF reads half the DSD rate: a DSD64 file's reads 1411.2 kHz, measured in the emulator), the codec and bit rate for anything else; and the cells, a value empty, `Unknown`, the language's `player_unknown` or 0 left out. Location comes from the playing path, not stock's `SD:/...` folder: a file in a card app's hidden folder is the server's, `Streaming` when it lies straight in the app's `stream/` (q2-subsonic's uncached stream, removed after the list) and `Downloaded` otherwise, as is a file under `Subsonic/` (the app's sync folder); any other card file reads `SD Card` and its folder. The grid is painted, not laid out: one view over the window, `np_about_paint` from `ringnav_paint` with `ui_kit.c`'s `ui_text`, repainted when a hash of what it shows changes. Its header stands from y 46, above the 58 px window, so `np_about_cap` paints the grid again into the status bar's background (`ringnav_paint_bg`, after `artist_cap`), clipped there by the bar, while the page is on top, still and scrolled to its top; a timer repaints the bar once the slide ends, as `cap_due` does for the artist page. `np_about_key`, before `ringnav`'s allowlist (as Spotify's page takes its keys), takes every wheel tick on the page: one scrolls the grid `AB_ROW` (44) px, as far as its last row ending on the list's end (`list_fit_end`, y 282), and none reaches stock's volume. A vertical drag scrolls it too (`ab_touch`, on the grid's view for the press and on the page for the move, lift and abort, as `peq_ui.c`'s `e3_touch`): the scroll follows the finger pixel for pixel from where it went down, clamped by the same `ab_scroll` as the wheel to 0 and the last row's end, and stops at the lift with no momentum, so a flick cannot carry it past either end.

`set_repeatpoint`'s marker placement (`0x53b9d8`) puts the 3x10 A-B markers at x = 50 + t \* 290 / length, y 250. iPod keeps y and patches x and width to `NP_BAR`; a bar laid out elsewhere (OLED's grid) takes them along at the same share of its width (`ringnav_ab_x`). The slider's 44px target is centered on the same bar (window y 255), with the page dots moved 6px up, outside the target. The dots' `slide_indicator` gets its own anchor (`anchor_x` `187px`, `anchor_y` `0px`, the point stock's took: the slide_view's center, above the indicator's middle, so the dots on its top edge). With none, stock centers them on its `indicated_target` as `widget_to_screen` places it, and that subtracts the widget's own `xoffset` property, which `slide_view` sets to the drag during a swipe. The indicator lays its dots out again only after its own layout (any relayout of the window), but then from wherever the slide_view was dragged, so the dots slid with the page until the next layout. Native `slide_with_bar` accepts a press anywhere in that rectangle and grabs the pointer, so a drag stays on the slider outside its bounds. Its dragger is skipped when the `icon` style lookup is empty and `border_color` is transparent (`slider_on_paint_self`, `0x62e080`). The asset clears `border_color` in every state. The icon needs more than leaving it out: the slider's style name (`s_ipod_progress`) has no theme entry, and stock then reads what the inline style lacks from its `default` slider style (the style's state change, `0x6b48cc`: the name's state, the name's `normal`, then `default`'s), whose `icon` is the knob, `rounded_n`, `rounded_o` when focused or over and `rounded_p` when pressed. With an icon stock draws the knob, sizes the dragger to it and fills and seeks half a knob short of each end. `slider_knobless` therefore sets `icon` to a value that's no string in all five states, which reads as none, on every slider `plain_slider` makes: this one, Quick Settings' brightness slider (both with their fill, `slider_fill`) and the four settings slider pages' at their load (`slider_open`). No thumb shows and the fill ends exactly at the value. An empty `icon` in the asset reads as none too, as on stock's own brightness bar, but stock then looks the image up at every paint. `np_fill` sets the fill in every state a press passes through, so a touch keeps the accent.

**Volume.** Outside a scrub the wheel stays on the volume, and stock opens `dialog/volume_dialog`, a full-screen transparent dialog holding `slider_vol` and `label_vol`. Its `highlight="default(alpha=200)"` made the window manager draw everything under it as a dimmed snapshot taken at open, so iPod's `volume_dialog.bin` drops that property (`volume_dialog` in `tools/ipod.py`) and nothing dims. When the paint hook paints that dialog, `vol_paint` draws the volume in the dialog's own paint. With Now Playing directly under it (the window manager's second-to-last child) it covers the band from `slider_play` to `label_playtime` in black, then draws the track (the theme's `playing.scrubber.track`, `TRACK_COLOR` by default, the slider's `bar_size`) and a white fill to `value / max`, both pills like the capsule, and "Volume N" centered in the times' row at `NP_TIMES_PX`; under a status row's set (OLED's) the bar is inset `VOL_SPK_INSET` (24) at each end, its fill white, with the theme's 16 px speakers (`vol_lo_*` and `vol_hi_*`, Phosphor's `speaker-simple-none` and `speaker-simple-high` fill in Text Secondary, `tools/art.py`) centered `VOL_SPK_X` (8) in from each end of the progress bar on its center line, and no text. A paint whose clip misses the number (a repaint of the bar's rows alone) sets `vol_drawn` to -1 too, so `vol_poll` repaints the dialog whole and the number follows the bar within `VOL_POLL_MS`. Without the poll timer, or with the dots already hidden, they are left alone and no number is drawn. ponytail: the paper over the elapsed time's box also covers the art reflection's last rows there (a few percent at most), a faint notch while the volume shows; hiding the two labels under the dialog instead needs a restore when it closes. Over any other window, Quick Settings included, it draws a rounded `VOL_PANEL_*` panel in the fast-scroll letter's style (`FILL_RGB` at `LETTER_ALPHA`, `LETTER_RADIUS`) exactly over Quick Settings' brightness row (the build checks it), its rounded corners clear of the glass corners, with the bar as a pill on a `VOL_PANEL_TRACK` gray track (a non-zero fill at least a round dot) and just the number at its right, at `VOL_PANEL_PX`. `slider_vol` and `label_vol` are hidden in the iPod asset before the first paint, so transition snapshots cannot expose the stock full-screen controls; `slider_vol` is moved onto the area drawn, so stock's partial repaints land on it. Those alone stopped after a tick or two, so while the dialog is up a `VOL_POLL_MS` (16 ms) timer compares `slider_vol`'s value with the one last drawn and repaints the whole dialog when it changed, or while the bar eases after a wheel tick ([Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)); it removes itself once the dialog is no longer on top.

**Dark volume.** With the screen off the wheel sets nothing ([Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)): a tick no page takes reaches `on_wm_keyup_fun`, whose hook drops it dark, and so does a tick over a volume dialog left open past the screen-off, which `vol_keyup` sends on there. Stock's opened the dialog on a dark tick (that tick changes nothing, as lit), and the ticks after it were the dialog's own (`volume_dialog_on_keyup`, `0x4a3688`: a step, the save, its 3 s count restarted, `RET_STOP`). Since V1.34 stock's handler returns 0 at once while `g_backlight_status` is clear, so each later tick went on to `on_wm_keyup_fun` again, and `navigator_to("dialog/volume_dialog")` finds an open window only by that path (`widget_child`, a `strcmp` with the window's name, `volume_dialog`), never matching: every dark tick loaded one more dialog over the last and none changed the volume. A dialog's close timer stops when it leaves the top (`0x12a`) and starts again when it is back (`0x12b`), so once lit the stack came down one dialog every 3 s, each drawn the same; Return or a tap off the bar closed only the top one, and a drag on the bar ended with the dialog under it showing the value it opened with (#303). `VOL_DARK` (`tools/build.py`) removes the branch at `0x4a36b4`, so the dialog's other keys are its own dark as V1.32's were; its wheel ticks dark go on to `vol_wm_keyup`, which opens nothing. A stack could still come from a lit pass: a dialog `navigator_to` has just loaded is the window in front at once, but the window manager's key target (`W_KEY_TARGET`, where `widget_on_keyup` sends a release) only from its open event (`window_base_on_event` focuses it on `0x128`/`0x129`), which the open's idle dispatches, or the end of its animation. A tick dispatched before that goes to the page under it and on to `on_wm_keyup_fun`, which loads another dialog; the loop dispatches every queued event before its idles, so a stalled pass took several ticks and opened a dialog for each, only the last stepped. `ringnav` takes such a tick itself, after stock's lock filter: with the screen lit and the volume dialog in front and not the key target it steps the volume (`vol_step`, the dialog's own clamps and save), sets `slider_vol` and stops the key, so one dialog is all a turn opens. The dialog's 3 s count is not restarted by these ticks; its own, a pass later, restart it.

**OLED's grid.** The grid's `np_art` (150, with `np_bar_y` 228) has `playing_page` move the iPod layout's boxes onto it (`np_grid` in `tools/ipod.py`); every name the payload looks up keeps its widget. `img_cover` sits at the text column on the window's top (y 58 on screen), its corners `playing.art.radius` px (6, `paint_cover`); the title, artist and album boxes start 18 px right of it on line tops 64, 96 and 120, each 2 px wider than its column at both sides for `hscroll_label`'s margins, so the text ends on the right column; `img_fav` and `img_more` sit at the right end of an 18 px line whose baseline is the art's foot (`NP_GRID_ROW_PX`, `NP_GRID_ROW_ASCENT`) on the art's page, More's center `NP_GRID_MORE_INSET` (7) px left of the right column, so its dots end on it. Their images are the theme's (`np_glyphs` in `patch/np_bar.c`, under `playing.modes.icons`; `tools/art.py` `np_fav`, `np_unfav_*`, `np_more_*`, `np_moredown_*`, 20 px): stock's update and click, and `rate_fav_click`, keep setting the heart to `play_fav` or `play_unfav`, so each paint of the window (`ringnav_paint_bg`, before the buttons paint) turns either into the theme's name, the empty heart in the half's ink, and More's five `bg_image` states into the half's dots once per half (`ringnav_playing` binds both through `np_glyphs_bind`). An app's heart (`tidal_fav_add`, `tidal_fav_rm`) stays stock's. `slider_play` runs 6 px high from the text column to the right column with its top at y 228 and a 22 px target, the times 22 px under it in Inter. `img_playmode` stays at opacity 0, centered on y 276, as the target for the theme's shuffle and repeat, which `np_modes` (`patch/np_bar.c`, `playing.modes.icons`) draws 44 px apart about its center, each in Accent Blue when lit, else Text Secondary (`tools/art.py` `mode_*`; repeat-once has its own glyph). They are two controls over stock's one mode: `ringnav_dispatch` hands a click on the target to `np_mode_click` before stock's handler, which stepped Order, Repeat One, Shuffle, Repeat All; the left half toggles shuffle and the right steps repeat Off, All, One (`np_mode_step`). `MCL_MODE` can't say everything two controls can: stock has no shuffle under Repeat One, and its Shuffle (2) never ends, drawing again once every track has played. So Repeat One plays as 1 whatever shuffle says, shuffle with repeat Off or All both play as 2, and the payload keeps the rest (`np_shuf_one`: shuffle under Repeat One; `np_rep_off`: Off chosen under shuffle, All otherwise, as that is how stock's Shuffle plays), saved as `[IPOD] NPSHUFONE` and `NPREPOFF` when either moves and read back on first use (`np_modes_read`), so a restart draws the pair as it was. Shuffle with repeat Off therefore keeps playing after the last track. A change that leaves `MCL_MODE` as it is sends nothing; one that moves it goes through `config_playmode`, as the play mode setting saves it, and so through `ringnav_mode`'s rules: stock Shuffle keeps Shuffle Albums or Folders, any other mode ends advanced play. The page dots sit at y 302; the slide (the lyrics) ends 5 px above the bar. `np_sync` sets the artist and album in `playing.artist.font`'s face as their text allows (`face_font`, `theme_font`'s rule for a named face).

**Quick Settings and prompts.** Stock's pull-down (`on_wm_tsmove_fun`, `0x4f2a4c`) opens `dialog/statusbar_dialog` for a touch that began above y 31 (`g_pressdown_y`, written by `on_wm_tsdown_fun`) and moved 20 px down. It stays out of its own Add and Delete prompts by their flags, but tests `g_poweroff_state` only for 2, and the Shut Down? prompt (`on_wm_keylong_fun`, a modal `dialog/confirminfo_dialog`) is state 1, so Quick Settings opened over it. Return there is stock's (`usable` is false with the state set and another window in front), and it took the windows away under the prompt's modal loop: Shut Down? stayed or came back with buttons that did nothing and `g_poweroff_state` still 1, so only Now Playing worked until a restart (#303). `ringnav_input` passes a pointer-down to stock and then, with a `confirminfo_dialog` in front, moves a `g_pressdown_y` above `QS_PULL_Y` down to it, so no touch on a prompt, the Shut Down? one or one of ours, can pull Quick Settings down. Inferred from the handlers, not reproduced: the emulator mocks the window manager.

A theme with `motion.inplace` moves a level inside a page, with no window animating (`page_push`, `coverflow.c`): after `page_list` rebuilds it, the list_view starts a window's width to the side and animates its `x` to rest. `addon.c` keeps the depth's change in `pg.moved` through its Loading level, so the push falls on the first rows or error; a refresh finds it 0. A folder level moves stock's `tableview_folder` when `ringnav_folder_click` or `ringnav_folder_back` sees `g_folder_layer` change and stay above 0. A level still sliding goes to its rest first.

## Boot resume (iPod)

Stock `home_page_init` resumes when Memory Playback (`g_memory_play`) or car mode (`g_carmode`) is set. `memeory_startplayer` (`0x5211f4`) reads the saved state, rebuilds the queue into a new deque, sets the saved position with `mclSetStartSeekTime` when `g_memory_play` is 2 or in car mode, and returns the track index; it neither plays nor opens a page. Home then calls `navigator_to_with_context("playing_page", ctx)` (the `jalr` at `0x534cf8`) with `ctx` `{queue, index, class, mode}`, mode 2 in car mode and 3 otherwise. `playing_page_init` passes `ctx` to `player_start` unless the class is `0xff`; `player_start` loads the queue, starts the player and pauses it (`mclSetPause`) unless the mode is 2.

iPod makes that `jalr` a checked `jal ringnav_boot`; the delay slot still stores the mode. In car mode `ringnav_boot` makes the stock call unchanged, unless Headphones Required (under Settings order) refuses the start, which then is the paused one. Otherwise it makes the page's `player_start` call without the page, so the queue and track come back paused and Home stays; the saved time is restored in Location mode, while Track starts at the beginning. Home destroys its deque afterwards, as before, since `mclLoadPlayList` copies it. The page's two resets before `player_start` (key-seek mode and a countdown) are page state, set again when it opens. `hciplayer` touches `/tmp/notfile` or `/tmp/notsupport` for a missing or unsupported track; the window manager's `on_wm_timer_dialog` (`0x4f4d18`) turns them into a `msginfo_dialog` toast on any page, and `playing_page_init` only deletes stale ones, so a bad restored track still shows its toast on Home.

In-Vehicle Mode (`SYSSET CARMODE`, `g_carmode`) also ties the Q2 to the car's power, in stock code the payload leaves alone. `on_wm_idle_status` calls `check_cardmode` (`0x4f3c24`) on every pass. In car mode, with no cable (`g_charge_state` 0: `get_battery_capacity` keeps it as `usb_detect` reads the cable, and 0 while `g_last_otgid` is 1, so Charge Limit, which only switches charging, leaves it alone), it sets `g_carmode_state` from 0 to 1; with the cable, from anything above 0 back to 0. `on_wm_timer_dialog` takes 1 to 2, wakes the screen (`awake_screen`), opens `dialog/autoshutdown_dialog` ("Shutdown") and sets 3. The dialog's one-second timer (`0x498f04`) closes it once the cable is back; otherwise it counts down from 10 and at 0 closes it and opens `poweroff_page`, so the Q2 shuts down 10 s after the power goes. Car mode also skips the idle Auto-standby and Auto-shutdown (`check_to_poweroption`, `0x4f3d70` and `0x4f3e40`) and the USB Connected prompt on plugging in (`check_usb_status`). Nothing in demo powers the Q2 on with the cable. Settings → Power's row says both in its caption (`pod_caption`, `patch/settings_pages.c`).

The English stock labels are Memory Playback: Off / Track / Location and
System: In-Vehicle Mode. Home's Now Playing action (`on_home_playing_onclick`
at `0x5343f0`) calls `on_backplay_click` (`0x4f1e84`), which opens the player with
class `0xff`; this skips `player_start` and preserves the paused state. Play/Pause
resumes audio.

## Scrub (iPod)

**Stock audit.** `playing_page` is not a navigation context, so a center release (218, the power key) passed through to `on_wm_keyup_fun`, whose `screen_action` (`0x501f64`) turns the screen off, and a wheel release to the same handler, which changes the volume and opens `dialog/volume_dialog`. The page's own key-up handler (`0x53da5c`) knew only Return and keys 222/223 until V1.36, which gave it the center release too: a second one within 350 ms turns the screen off at once (`power_keyup_detect`, 250 ms until then), a single one does 350 ms later (`power_keyup_pending_custom`), and either stops there. `ringnav` takes the center release on this page before that handler runs, and what it passes on is for `on_wm_keyup_fun`: a release under stock's power-key rules (`g_power_longkey`, `g_ingore_bootkey_flag`, the guard after Standby), whose flags only that function clears, and one during a window animation. So the handler's test for Center never matches (`NP_CENTRE` in `tools/build.py`), and it passes Center on as V1.34's did. Those drive stock's key seek: a long press sets `0xa4e880` (`0x53b4d0`), key-down (`0x53e000`) calls `playing_timer_clear` (`0x53dee0`), sets the mode byte `0xa4e881` to 1, steps `slider_play` 5 seconds within `[0, max]` and writes `label_playtime`, and key-up calls `player_seek_time` (`0x51f234`) with the slider value, then `playing_timer_start` (`0x53d928`). A touch drag takes the slider's handlers from the page's `widget_foreach` visitor (`0x53c5dc`): value-changing (`0xf`, `0x53e1fc`) writes the label and, in mode 0, clears the timer and sets mode 2; value-changed (`0xe`, `0x53dea8`) seeks the same way only in mode 2 (`0x53dbf8`). `player_seek_time` takes track seconds: it adds the current record's CUE start (`+0x48`), pauses DLNA, calls `mclSetSeek` (`0x5bd89c`), then polls `player_playtime` every 10 ms, up to 2 s, until it reaches the target. `player_seek_start` (`0x51f090`) is DLNA's and not used. `slider_set_value` emits will-change (`0xd`) and changed (`0xe`), never changing, so a set value in mode 0 neither seeks nor writes the label.

**Scrub.** On the top `playing_page`, with no window animation or pressed pointer, the key-up hook takes the center button and runs an iPod classic's Center cycle (`np_centre`, no `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` wait): at rest a release starts the scrub; while scrubbing it ends the scrub (`scrub_end`, which seeks) and puts a focus ring on the first stop of shuffle, repeat and the heart (`st.np_stage`, `NP_STAGE_*`; `np_stop_ok`: shuffle and repeat need the theme's pair and no radio, the heart that `np_heart` finds it showing on the art page). A wheel tick moves the ring to the next or previous stop and stays at the ends (`np_stop_next`); it never changes a control. Center works the ringed one: shuffle or repeat steps as a tap on it does (`np_mode_step`) and the ring stays; the heart opens `rate_open`, the rating picker (the menu sheet's, `rate_show`), leaving the page at rest. `np_modes` draws a 2 px Text Primary outline round the ringed control (`glyph_framed`; the heart's, `heart_ring`, the same box drawn as two `round_ring`s with no fill, so the heart shows through: the glyph's ink, its alpha's bounds as `glyph_ink` reads the loaded bitmap, joined with the on dot while it shows, 6 px clear to the stroke; a tap's fading `#2C2C2E` square is the same box 8 px clear, `press_share`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#now-playing)); `NP_STAGE_MS` (`SCRUB_MS`) without a key, Return, a touch or another top window end the stage (`np_cancel`). A theme without `playing.modes.icons` has no ring and goes from the scrub straight to the rating picker. A release `NP_HOLD_MS` (400 ms) or more after its press (`ringnav_keydown` stamps `center_down_at` with the press's time, `chord_gate`'s `centre_at`, which the key's repeats keep: a held Center's key-down repeats every 50 ms, so a stamp at each would make every hold a press), outside a scrub, is a short hold: it replays the release to `on_wm_keyup_fun`, which turns the screen off; stock's long press (Shut Down) never reaches the page. Apple's iPod classic guide (160 GB, "Press the Center button to cycle through these additional items") lists scrubber bar, Genius slider, shuffle slider, song rating and lyrics; the Q2 has no Genius, and its lyrics are a page of the swipe. Outside a scrub, with `dialog/volume_dialog` on top and Now Playing directly under it (`vol_band`, where `vol_paint` draws its band), the keys are the page's: a center release takes the same path rather than reaching stock, which turned the screen off at the first. `scrub_start` closes that dialog with `window_close`, as stock's own tap beside the bar does (`on_volume_tsup_fun`; its close timer is a widget timer, gone with the dialog), so the wheel's ticks reach the scrub and the band no longer covers the bar. The close sends Now Playing `EVT_WINDOW_TO_FOREGROUND`, whose stock handler (`0x53d9f0`) refreshes the page, setting the bar to the player's second, and restarts its timer, so `scrub_start` reads the target and clears the timer after closing. After a paused scrub that refresh drops the bar's held target, as any window closing over the page does, the dialog's own timeout included. Wake is unchanged: a press that wakes the screen never reaches the page, and one within `WAKE_MS` after it is dropped (`wake_gate`), so with the cycle a press soon after waking starts a scrub rather than turning the screen off. Starting (`scrub_start`) calls `playing_timer_clear`, reads the slider value as the target and sets the slider's fill (`fg_color` in the normal, pressed, over and focused states) to white; under a status row's set (OLED's, `V_STATUS_Y`) the fill keeps the accent and `paint_scrubber` draws a `NP_KNOB` (14 px) white knob on its end instead. While scrubbing, a wheel release moves the target by `SCRUB_STEP` (5) seconds times the 100 ms ramp's step (`ramp` keyed on the slider with `WHEEL_RAMP_MS`, so 5 to 40 seconds; the lists' gentler curve does not apply: every tick moves the target), clamped to `[0, max]`. It sets the slider value, writes `label_playtime` in stock's format and syncs the remaining label, marks the target moved if the step changed it (a tick against an end does not), rearms the `SCRUB_MS` (3 s) end and swallows the release. A playing track follows the moved target (`seek_scrub`, `patch/seek.c`): the first move sends `mclSetSeek(target + the record's CUE start)` at once, as the [scan](#scan)'s jumps do, and later ones at most every `SCRUB_SEEK_MS` (200 ms) since the last, a one-shot timer sending the latest target when the wait is over, so a spin of ticks 40 ms apart sends about one seek in five and the music is heard at the target as the wheel turns. Ending, if the target moved, the track plays and the player followed it, `seek_scrub_end` sends the target only if the last seek didn't (a seek to where the player already is would take it back to the target after it played on); otherwise (paused, below, or a target no tick moved, as a [chapter](#podcasts-and-audiobooks) row's) the end commits once through `seek_position`, as before. A playing track's scrub never calls `player_seek_time`, whose wait for the player's second would hold the UI thread on every move. It then restores the accent's light-tone fill. Paused (`mclGetPlayStatus` 3), `player_seek_time` would resume the track (`config_outputchannel`, then `mclSetResume`) to reach the target, so the scrub sends the seek alone, `mclSetSeek(target + the record's CUE start)`, as `player_seek_time` adds it: hciplayer's `mcl-seek` handler (`0x42c614`) mutes the DAC and flags the seek, and its seek (`0x42b070`) leaves the DAC muted while paused, so the track stays paused and plays from the target at Play. Unlike `player_seek_time`, it does not pause DLNA first, so a paused seek is not reported to a DLNA controller. After a seek, `playing_timer_start` waits for `settle_poll` (every `SETTLE_MS`, 250 ms): paused, the player's second stands still until Play, and the page's timer would put the bar back on the old second. The bar keeps the target until `player_playtime_and_length` is within a second of it, the track changes, the player stops, or `SETTLE_PLAY_MS` (2 s) of playing pass without it; a new scrub, the lyrics' wheel or an exit drops the wait (an exit that ends a scrub keeps the one its seek starts). A paused seek is remembered with the player's second when it was sent: reopening Now Playing on the same track, still paused and at that second, puts the bar back on the target and waits again, so a new scrub starts from it; playing or another track forgets it. Without a seek the timer restarts at once. It ends on a center press, the timeout, Return (swallowed on the page), a touch (before the slider sees it, so a drag seeks the stock way), another top window, or the page's `EVT_DESTROY`, which drops the target. After the playing track changed (queue position and path, recorded at the start) the target is dropped: the next tick ends the scrub without moving it, and any other end does not seek. The live seeks are measured in the emulator (`Test/08 position 44k16.flac`): ticks a second apart were heard at once, 5 s on each; a spin of ten ticks sent three seeks about 200 ms apart and played on from the last, with no seek at the end. On a Q2 each seek's DAC mute ([Wired start](#wired-start)) is a short gap per jump, not measured. The mode byte stays 0 throughout. Outside scrub the wheel stays on the volume.

**Lyrics.** The page's 250 ms timer also keeps the lyrics in view: when `mclGetLyricSize()` is positive it finds the current line among `scroll_lrc`'s children (`0x53d4dc`), sums the rows' heights up to three lines before it (stock creates a row 20 px tall, or 25 px a line when its text is wider than 225 px and wraps, `0x53b838`), and calls `scroll_view_scroll_to(scroll_lrc, 0, y, 10)` whenever the view's y offset (`+0x84`, `SCROLL_Y`) differs, so a moved offset lasts one tick. That y is a row top, but `scroll_view_scroll_to` (`0x603008`) clamps it to the end, content height (`+0x7c`, `VIEW_CONTENT_H`) less the view's 178 px, which is no whole number of rows, so near the end the top row was cut through. The call (`jalr` at `0x53d6e4`, `LYRIC_FOLLOW`) becomes `jal ringnav_lyric_follow`: `lyric_pad` first grows the content to the first row top at or past that end plus the view's height, so the end is a row top and under a row of blank space shows below the last line. A content no taller than the view is left as is. The page's refresh (`0x53cf08`) rebuilds the rows (`0x53b67c`, which ends with `scroll_view_set_offset(scroll_lrc, 0, 0)`) whenever `g_forcerefresh_flag` is set: Play/Pause (`playpause_quick_click`), the player's state changes and the page's return to the front (`EVT_WINDOW_TO_FOREGROUND`, `0x12b`) all set it, so the lyrics jumped to the top until the next follow scrolled back. Its one call (`bal` at `0x53d10c`, `LYRIC_ROWS`) becomes `jal ringnav_lyric_rows`, which puts back the offset the view had; the follow moves it if the line changed. Limit: the rebuilt content is its natural height until the next follow pads it, so near the end the relayout's clamp can cut the top row for up to 250 ms, as above. Limits: scroll_view's relayout (`0x604638`) recomputes the height from the children and clamps the offset, which cuts the row again until the next follow, at most 250 ms on. `ringnav_playing` keeps `slide_view` and `scroll_lrc`.

**Lyrics wheel.** Every UI loop pass, `lyric_poll` (iPod, from `ringnav_sleep`) checks for the lyrics page in front: `slide_view`'s value is 1, `playing_page` is the top window, `usable()`, no window animation or pressed pointer, `scroll_lrc` has children and `mclGetLyricSize()` is positive. While it is, `wheel_raw` is set, as for [Vortex](#games), so the wheel posts no ticks and each pass takes the raw travel from `wheel_travel` (200 units a turn). Setting or clearing it zeroes the travel, so nothing from before carries over, and the wheel is back on ticks and the volume within a pass of leaving. The travel moves a target, in sixteenths of a pixel so that slow turns keep their fractions: `LYRIC_ROW_PX` (20, stock's row; a one-row line, `lyrics_row_h`'s 51 px, on the [lyrics page](#word-timed-lyrics)) per tick's worth of travel at the Wheel Sensitivity (`WHEEL_TICK_UNITS` x 50 / `wheel_pct()` units), clockwise down, within `[0, content height - view height]` after `lyric_pad`. A turn moves the lyrics as far as its ticks did, but a pixel at a time instead of a row. Each pass then glides the offset towards the target (`lyric_step`, `scroll_view_set_offset`): a `dt / (dt + LYRIC_EASE_MS)` share of the way left (50 ms, `dt` capped at it), at least a pixel, so the motion eases in whatever the loop's pace. Starting a glide stops any stock scroll animator on the view, a drag's fling among them. While a finger stays on the wheel the lyrics stay where its travel put them; once it lifts (`wheel_held`, which `wheel_sample` sets at a finger's first sample and clears at its lift, raw or not) after travel moved them, the glide's target becomes the row top nearest it (`lyric_snap`), so no row is left cut at the top; the end is a row top already (`lyric_pad`). No key event reaches stock, so the travel itself sets `ringnav_input`'s idle stamp and calls `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 1)`, which keeps the loop at full pace and the screen on; `np_animating` keeps the pace while a glide moves. A tick that reaches the page before a pass has taken the wheel raw goes to `np_lyrics`, ahead of scrub, which glides to the next or previous row's top from the glide's target, so quick ticks add up.

**Lyrics hold.** Moving the lyrics, by wheel travel, a tick, or a finger that dragged `scroll_lrc` (a press that came down on the lyrics page, with `playing_page` on top, and the offset different at its release; stock's scroll animator stops at the press, so only the finger moves them, and a swipe that brings the page in holds nothing), ends any scrub (`scrub_end`, committing a moved target) and holds them (`lyric_hold`, keeping the playing track's `np_track`). Stock's timer keeps running, so the bar, the times and the highlighted line go on, but `ringnav_lyric_follow` returns without scrolling while the lyrics are held on that track, and while a pointer is pressed. A swipe to the art or info page and back keeps the hold; the page's destruction (`np_gone`, leaving Now Playing) ends it, and so does another Now Playing replacing the page before it goes (`ringnav_playing`, as `np_gone` leaves a replaced page alone), as does full screen. Another song (`np_track`: queue place and file, checked every pass while the page exists, on top or not) drops it too and puts the lyrics at the top at once, with no glide, stopping stock's animator (`lyric_top`). So does `ringnav_lyric_rows` when it rebuilds the rows for another song than the last rows' (`lyric_rows_song`): it leaves stock's offset 0 instead of putting back the old one, whatever moved the view since the song changed. Stock's `scroll_view_scroll_to` animates for 300 ms whatever its duration, ignores a new target while an animation whose goal is the top or the end runs, and an animation started with the screen off can still be moving when it comes back on: a follow sent with the last song's rows could otherwise carry the new song's lyrics back to the old place, or move them under a swipe onto the page. Off the page, not held, the follow is stock's `scroll_view_scroll_to`, so the lyrics are on the current line when you swipe back; on the page it glides there instead (`lyric_glide`). Another window on top, the screen off or a touch leave the hold alone. Any other page, or no lyrics, leaves the wheel on the volume. Before 1.4.6 the wheel jumped a row a tick and stopped stock's timer, bar and highlight included, until `SCRUB_MS` after the last tick or a touch, when the page jumped back to the current line. Limits: a drag on the screen stops anywhere, so it can leave the top row cut, and one that ends where it began holds nothing; a song repeated on its own (Repeat One) is the same song, so lyrics held on it stay held.

<a id="lyrics-search"></a>**Lyrics search.** Now Playing's ⋯ lyrics match (`onlinematching_page`) runs stock's `online_lyricthd` on its own thread: `online_setkeyword_info` has filled `keyinfo` (`0xa545f4`: file name, title at +0x200, album at +0x400, artist at +0x500) from the playing track's tags; the thread copies it (`online_getkeyword_info`, under its lock) and searches `title/artist` with `kugou_obtainlyric` (`0x51b3f4`: `mobilecdn.kugou.com` search, then `krc.php`), then `com163_obtainlyric` (NetEase `api/search/pc` and `song/media`, which now want a phone-bound account and return no lyric). Each writes the reply to `/tmp/oslyric_<thread>`, which the page shows. Accepting it (`0x535f24`) turns the file name into `<name>.lrc` (`modifystringtolrcsuffix`, `0x51caa8`: its last `.` on made `.lrc`) and, with a card (`/tmp/mmc_add`), `snprintf`s `cp -rf /tmp/oslyric_N "/mnt/mmc/.downpic/<name>.lrc"` (format `0x7867f0`) for `system()`, then reloads the lyrics (`mclLoadExLyric`); it never saved beside the song. That call (`jalr` at `0x536488`, `LYRIC_SAVE_CALL`; the format's `addiu` before it is pinned) becomes `jal ringnav_lyric_save`: for the queue's local song (the playing one first) whose file name stock turns into that `<name>.lrc`, not a CUE track's, it copies the file to `<path without extension>.lrc` beside the song through `.part`, removes `.downpic/<name>.lrc`, which the loader would show first, and leaves the command `:`, so `system()` does nothing and the reload finds the new file; otherwise (another song, a CUE track, a card that can't be written there) it copies the file to stock's `.downpic/<name>.lrc` itself, through `.part` too, and still leaves `:`: stock's command put the name, a file name or a card app's title, inside double quotes for `/bin/sh` as root, where `$(...)` and backticks still run ([GHSA-qp92-mq7c-6r64](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/security/advisories/GHSA-qp92-mq7c-6r64)). A name with a `/` (no file name has one, but a card app's title may, and `../` would leave `.downpic`) or whose `.downpic` path would not fit 0x208 bytes saves nothing. Limits: a song whose file name another song shares is saved beside the first of them in the queue; stock's "no lyrics" choice still removes only `.downpic`'s copy, and that command, `rm -rf "/mnt/mmc/.downpic/<name>"` for the same `system()`, is taken the same way: its `snprintf` (`0x53650c`, `LYRIC_DROP_CALL`) jumps to `ringnav_lyric_drop`, which unlinks the copy and leaves `:`. Kugou counts as found whenever the transfer completes, so NetEase ran only offline. The entry of `kugou_obtainlyric` jumps to `ringnav_lyric_search` (`patch/onlinematch.c`): it copies `keyinfo` the same way, asks `https://lrclib.net/api/search?track_name=&artist_name=` (percent-encoded, `lrclib_url`) through libcurl with the bundled CA file, parses the reply with demo's cJSON and writes the first result's `syncedLyrics`, less its opening credit lines (`lrc_body`: each line before the first sung one whose text holds `:`, as NetEase's `作词 : X` or `Mix Engineer : Y`, with any blank line among them; a tag line such as `[offset:...]` ends the search and stays, and a result with no sung line is skipped), UTF-8 with a BOM as Kugou's, to the same file; without one it writes nothing, and the page finds no lyrics. When the search finds no synced lyrics and taking the accents off the title or artist changes them (`lrc_fold`: each Latin letter of U+00C0-U+017F and U+1E00-U+1EFF, Vietnamese's among them, and `ơ`/`ư` as its plain letter, strokes and ligatures too, `ł` l, `ø` o, `đ` d, `æ` ae, `ß` ss, `þ` th, combining marks dropped), it searches those once more: LRCLIB's search already matches `é` to `e` but not `ł` or `ø`, and holds some songs only under the plain names ("Hataałii" finds none of its "Hataalii" entries). A reply that isn't a results array (LRCLIB's 503 `ServerOverloaded`, below) is asked again 2 s later, 3 requests in all, as Get Album Lyrics does (`LRC_BUSY`). LRCLIB is the only source: the hook never resumes Kugou's search, whose first result was often another song's (a song LRCLIB lacks got unrelated Chinese lyrics), and returns nonzero so that `online_lyricthd` skips NetEase too, whose `api/search/pc` now answers code -462 (bind a phone) and finds no song. Limits: no duration check, so a live or remastered version's timing may come back; plain-only results are skipped, since stock's loader drops lines without a stamp; the reply is capped at 512 KB (`LRCLIB_MAX`); a sung opening line with `:` in it is cut as a credit, while credits written `作词：X` (no spaces), after a tag line or after the first sung line stay.

<a id="cover-search"></a>**Cover search.** The same page's cover match runs `online_searchcover` (`0x51cbf0`): it clears stock's cover list (`p_deque_onlinecover` `0xa4db5c`, under `ponline_mutex`), adds `scover_default` (the track's current cover) and, when `/mnt/mmc/.downpic/<file name>.jpg` exists, that path, then starts `online_coverthd` (`0x51c624`). The thread copies `keyinfo`, builds the keyword `title&artist` (`artist&album` without a title), URL-encodes it and calls `kugou_obtaincover` (`0x51bf74`), `com163_obtaincover` (`0x51c46c`) and, while the list holds under 12, `baidu_obtaincover` (`0x51bbdc`), then sets `onlinematch_cover_threadflag` (`0x9b3281`). Each source adds image URLs with `online_addcoverlist` (`0x51b7a8`: up to 0x200 bytes, a duplicate string is dropped); Kugou's parser (`0x51bd20`) takes only a `.jpg` URL, only while the list holds under 12, and only if a HEAD (`getDownloadFileLength`) reports under 1 MB or fails. Once the flag is set the page makes one 110 px `onlinecover_%d` image per entry, three to a row, and queues them all (`online_coverlist_init`, `batchadd_onlinecover_task`): stock's cover thread downloads each URL with `curl_http_request` (redirects followed, at most 3, 5 s in all, verified as [Stock HTTPS](#stock-https) describes) to `/tmp/online/ori%d.jpg` and sizes it to 330 px `thumb%d.jpg` (`toolsTidalSpecCover`). Picking another than the first sizes that thumbnail into `.downpic/<file name>.jpg` and `.downpic/s_<md5>.jpg` (`toolsThumbSpecCover`, under `parse_cover_mutex`, `0x536248`); picking the first removes both. Now Playing's cover thread (`player_parsecover_thd`) shows `.downpic/<file name>.jpg` before the song's own art when it exists, by `snprintf`ing `cp -f "<it>" '/tmp/externpic.jpg'` (format `0x782974`) for `system()`: the file name sat inside double quotes for `/bin/sh` as root, so a `$` or a backtick in it was expanded, and a file name with a `$` never showed its pick. That call (`jalr` at `0x51db14`, `COVER_PICK_CALL`; the format's `addiu` in its delay slot is pinned) becomes `jal ringnav_cover_copy`, which copies the file through `.part` and leaves `:`. Stock's other `cp -f` commands, in `parse_albumcovertask_thd`, name only MD5s. The entry of `kugou_obtaincover` jumps to `ringnav_cover_search` (`patch/onlinematch.c`), which adds its own candidates in place of Kugou's search, and the entries of `com163_obtaincover` and `baidu_obtaincover` jump to `ringnav_cover_none`, which returns at once: the song's title and artist reach none of Kugou, NetEase (`music.163.com`) and Baidu (`image.baidu.com`), each asked by stock over plain HTTP. `online_coverthd` is the only caller of the three, and the three the only users of their host strings. With the album (else the title) and artist from `keyinfo` it asks MusicBrainz `ws/2/release/?query=release:"ALBUM" AND artist:"ARTIST"&fmt=json&limit=10` (Lucene-escaped and percent-encoded, `mb_url`; no artist clause without one) and, for each new `release-group` `id`, at most 4, sends a HEAD to the Cover Art Archive's `release-group/<id>/front-500` (5 s each): a redirect (307 today) names the group's front as a 500 px JPEG thumbnail on archive.org (`REDIRECT_URL`), which is added; a 404, no art, adds nothing. Then iTunes Search `search?entity=album&limit=5&term=ARTIST ALBUM` (`itunes_url`): each `artworkUrl100` with its last `100x100` made `600x600` (`itunes_art`), a JPEG. Ours stop once the list holds 10 (`COVER_FILL`); when they find nothing the page offers only the covers it started with. Requests use libcurl with the bundled CA file (DigiCert Global Root G2 signs MusicBrainz and iTunes, ISRG the Cover Art Archive), `Q2POD_UA` (`Q2Muse/<version> (repository URL)`, as MusicBrainz asks), 10 s to connect and 20 s in all (the HEADs 5 s), replies capped at 256 KB (`COVER_MAX`), on stock's cover thread; the images themselves are fetched by stock's cover thread (`curl_http_request`, [Stock HTTPS](#stock-https)). One MusicBrainz request per search keeps under its 1 request a second. Limits: a failed MusicBrainz request skips iTunes too, as a likely sign of no internet, so with Wi-Fi up but none the page waits one 10 s connect timeout more than stock; MusicBrainz answers a busy server with an error, which adds none of its covers; archive.org can take more than stock's 5 s download, which leaves that tile on the default art; the same cover from two services shows twice; only release groups' chosen fronts are offered, not each release's.

<a id="album-lyrics"></a>**Album lyrics.** Now Playing's ⋯ page (`playermore_page_init`, `0x539f60`, hooked by `ringnav_playermore` in `patch/onlinematch.c`) builds 8 rows, each button named by its position; its row click (`0x539dbc`) `atoi`s the name into a table of kinds (`PLAYMORE_ROWS`, `0x786a70`: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1), so Download Cover & Lyrics, kind 4 in `get_playmore_showinfo`, is third. For a playing song on the card with an album tag (not an online queue, `MCL_TYPE` `0xf1`/`0xf2`), the hook adds **Get Album Lyrics** under it in `list_row`'s widgets, with stock's `player_onlinesearch` icon and its rows' 24 px, 253 px label; the button has no name, so stock's click never sees it. A press needs Wi-Fi (`get_wifisignal`), then copies the album's tracks off stock's records (`coverflow_album_tracks`, as Go to Album: the album's songs in disc and track order; a CUE track is left out, as it shares its file's `.lrc`) and starts one worker thread (`album_lyrics`), which outlives the page. A 500 ms timer shows "Downloading N of M" on the row while the page is open, keeps standby and auto power-off waiting (`reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 0)`), then joins the worker and toasts the summary (`album_note`). A press while it runs cancels it ("Cancelling…"); USB storage (`ringnav_usbmode`) cancels and joins it first, quietly. Each track is on its own: a file gone from the card since the library's scan is passed over; one with a `.lrc` or `.LRC` beside it is left as it is; any other is searched exactly as the single search above searches LRCLIB (`lrclib`, shared: the record's title and artist, the first result with synced lyrics, less its opening credits), its lyrics written to `<name>.lrc.part` and renamed to `<name>.lrc` once whole, and then stock's `.downpic` copy for it (`lrc_name` of its file name), which would hide it, removed; a song LRCLIB lacks keeps that copy. LRCLIB answers some uncached searches with a 503 `ServerOverloaded` object (`Retry-After: 1`) instead of a results array, and the same search a moment later with results; the single search and the job both ask again 2 s later (`LJ_RETRY_US`), up to 3 requests a track (`LRC_BUSY`, `LJ_BUSY_TRIES`). Once LRCLIB has answered in the job, a failed request is retried once, 2 s later; two tracks in a row unanswered or still busy end it ("Can't reach LRCLIB", or "LRCLIB stopped answering" after some answered), as does a card that can't be written. A cancel stops a transfer at curl's next progress call (`XFERINFOFUNCTION`). However it ends, no `.part` stays and the lyrics saved before stay. Limits: one album at a time; a song without a title tag counts as not found; LRCLIB down while the internet is up reads as offline; as the single search, a live or remastered version's timing may come back.

**Lyrics from tags.** Stock's `mclLoadExLyric` (`0x5bd384`) clears the list and, unless the queue is online (`MCL_TYPE` `0xf1`/`0xf2`), loads the playing record's `<path without extension>.lrc` or `.LRC`; before them, for source types 3, 6, 12, 13, 15, 21 and 23 (the word at `0xa40000 - 0x413c`, mask `0x3a0b048`), `.downpic/<name>.lrc` (`/mnt/mmc/`, or `/tmp/` without a card), and for play type `0xf0` `/tmp/hifi/`, so a stale `.downpic` copy hides the `.lrc` beside the song (`0x5bbdc8`). It keeps only lines whose `[` is followed by a digit. A file without a byte-order mark that it does not take for UTF-8 it converts from GB18030 first (`iconv` to `/tmp/templyric`). Its test, `mclIsUtf8WithoutBOM` (`0x5bbc4c`, also the lyrics match page's), read only the 6 bytes from the first non-ASCII one and knew no 4-byte character, so a UTF-8 `.lrc` with an emoji, or with a character starting 4 or 5 bytes after that first one (`é` and three letters, then `’`; Korean's one-syllable words), was converted and loaded garbled or cut short. Its entry jumps to `ringnav_lrc_utf8` (`patch/lyrics.c`), which reads the first `LYRIC_TAG_MAX` bytes and checks them with `utf8_text`, the tag check in `patch/xiph.c`; a file that fails it still goes through stock's GB18030 conversion. Limit: a multi-byte character cut by that 64 KB read fails it. `ringnav_lyric` runs it first; when `mclGetLyricSize()` is still 0 for a local song (`REC_TYPE` 8, an absolute path), it opens the file with `taglib_file_new` and reads `LYRICS`, else `UNSYNCEDLYRICS`, with libtag_c's `taglib_property_get`, which demo does not import: its address is the one that call bound in demo's GOT (`TAGLIB_NEW_GOT`) minus `TAGLIB_FILE_NEW`, plus the pinned library's offset, and an entry still holding demo's stub reads nothing. Each line (CR, LF or CRLF), without the spaces at its ends, goes into stock's `stLyricInfo` list (`MCL_LYRICS`, under `MCL_LYRIC_LOCK`) at time `0x7fffffff`, which no track reaches: the page's timer then keeps the first line current and the view at the top, the wheel scrolls it as above, and the line `0x4da628` shows in `label_title` stays the default (both read from the disassembly, `0x53d550` and `0x4da700`). No temporary file is written. Limits: unsynced text only, so an ID3 `SYLT` frame is not read and `[mm:ss]` stamps inside a tag show as text; lines starting past the first 64 KB (`LYRIC_TAG_MAX`) are dropped; the file's tags are parsed once more on every track start without a `.lrc`, on the thread that starts it.

<a id="now-playing-links"></a>**Links.** `np_taps.c` makes the art page's artist (`scrlabel_artist`), album (`label_ipod_album`) and art (`img_cover`) links. `ringnav_playing` registers `np_tap` on the window for the pointer's down, move-before, up-before and abort: the window sees every touch whatever child takes it (the slide_view, its page, a label, or OLED's lyrics column), as `np_time_tap` does for the right-hand time, so the boxes are hit-tested from the window (`np_hit`), in whichever theme's layout the page has. A box counts only while the slide_view rests on its first page (`value` 0) and the lyrics are not full screen. A down on a box lights it; a move more than `TAP_PX` (10, AWTK's drag threshold) from where it came down unlights it, so a swipe never goes anywhere, and an up within `TAP_PX` on the same box starts `npt_go` on the next pass, outside the touch's dispatch. The handler returns 0 throughout, so the slide_view still swipes and the bar, heart and More keep their touches. `npt_go` calls `np_goto` in navigation.c, which runs the hold menu's own `qm_goto` for the playing record (`queue_now`), an album as `QM_LOOKUP_ALBUM`: `playerjumpinfo_page` as ⋯'s Look up Album opens it, never Cover Flow's tracks, which the menu's Go to Album opens under Artist View or an open Cover Flow (an artist still opens as Go to Artist and Look up Artist do, in Cover Flow under Artist View), under the menu's gates: Now Playing on top and usable, no menu up, a Library or folder queue (`MCL_TYPE` 1 or a `0xf000` class), not AirPlay, a card app's song only where its app has a page (`addon_goes`), and `qm_goes`, which the menu's Go to Album and Go to Artist rows share: a tag to go by and the single-instance page not already open (nor Cover Flow showing that album alone). A box that fails the gates is not lit and its tap does nothing. Lit, the label's text is the accent's text tone, or white (Light Mode's ink) when that tone is gray, as Graphite's is next to the line's own gray (`np_tap_ink`; `ringnav_style_color` asks `np_tap_lit`), and the art gets a 15% black fill (`np_tap_dim`, from `paint_cover`, before the rounded corners). Stock binds `img_cover`'s click to Enlarged Art (`0x53cb38`: `navigator_to("bigcover_page")` while the player is not stopped); `ringnav_dispatch` stops that click, so the art's tap is only the link, and a hold opens the full-screen art instead: a down on the art, lit while the album goes somewhere or the full-screen art may open (Now Playing in front and usable, `mclGetPlayStatus` not 1, stopped), starts `npt_hold` `ART_HOLD_MS` (500) later; a move past `TAP_PX`, a lift or an abort stops it. When it runs with the art still lit it unlights it, sets `npt.held` so the touch's lift is no tap, and calls `navigator_to("bigcover_page")`, whatever `g_bigcovermode` (Enlarged Album Art) says.

## Word-timed lyrics

iPod's lyrics page (`patch/lyrics.c`; [ipod.md](ipod.md#now-playing)): large lines, the playing one centered and lit word by word.

**Times.** Stock's `.lrc` parser (`0x5bbdc8`, inside `mclLoadExLyric`) keeps each line's whole seconds (`toolsTimeConvert`, `0x5cedbc`) and the text after its last `]`, A2 word stamps and all. Its `jalr fopen` of the file it parses (`0x5bc30c`, `LYRIC_OPEN`; after the encoding probe and any conversion, so the file is UTF-8) becomes `jal ringnav_lrc_open`, which opens it as stock asked and keeps a copy of its first `LYRIC_TAG_MAX` bytes. After stock's load `ringnav_lyric` parses that copy as it parses a LYRICS tag (`lrc_parse`): leading `[mm:ss.xx]` stamps to the millisecond (`.x`, `.xx`, `.xxx` or `:xx`), and A2 `<mm:ss.xx>` word stamps cut from the text, kept for a line with one stamp as each word's millisecond and byte offset; a UTF-8 byte-order mark is skipped. Every line loses the spaces at its ends (ASCII's space, tab, vertical tab and form feed, no-break, ideographic and zero-width spaces, a byte-order mark; `lrc_trim`, its word stamps' offsets moved with the text), and a blank one goes: an empty line between verses, a line of spaces, a stamp alone (stock's `" "`, an instrumental break) and the empty line CR CR LF line ends leave between every two. So both lyrics pages keep an even spacing between lines; lyrics that are all blank leave stock's result. Synced lines replace stock's list (`deque_clear`, then each line at its whole seconds, under `MCL_LYRIC_LOCK`), so the list never holds word stamps and is in millisecond order; unsynced ones leave it. Every load then sends its synced lines, or none, to the page (`lyrics_publish`): their UTF-32 text, starts and word stamps, and an FNV-1a sum of each line's whole seconds and characters as stock's rows will hold them.

**Rows.** The page's refresh still rebuilds `scroll_lrc`'s labels (`0x53b67c`, `LYRIC_ROWS`), and so does `playing_page_init` (`0x53e524`, before `ringnav_playing` knows the page), so `ringnav_playing` takes the rows its init built too (`lyric_init`). `lyrics_rows` takes the sent table when its sum matches the labels' (`lrc_time` and text), keeps the last one when that matches, and otherwise builds one from the labels (whole seconds, no word stamps), so the page never shows another song's. It lays every line out with `widget_get_canvas`'s canvas in the playing line's face at `LYRIC_OLED_PX` (27, the design's 22): rows of `375 - 2 * LYRIC_OLED_X`, breaking before a space or beside a CJK character, else mid-word, up to `LYRIC_ROWS` (4, which still fit the view) of them, the rest cut. Each label's text is then emptied and it becomes the view's width and its line's rows high, 30 px apart (`LY_PITCH`), plus `LYRIC_GAP` (`LYRIC_SLOT` less a pitch at `LYRIC_PX`'s 34, 21 px, so a line of one row is 51 px, `lyrics_row_h`). `lyric_init` gives `scroll_lrc` the list layout `list_view(x=0,y=LYRIC_SLOT,s=0)` (`tools/ipod.py` gives `view_lrc` and `scroll_lrc` the full 375 px), which stacks the rows after a blank slot. A line's follow target centers its row in the view (`lyric_centre`); `lyric_pad` makes the content the last row's plus the view's height, so the last line can reach the middle. `ringnav_paint` draws each row's line (`lyrics_paint`, the row found among the children), its rows centered in it, `LYRIC_OLED_X` (24) from the left, in Inter (`ly_face`: Medium for the playing line, which also measures every wrap, Regular for the rest), every row in view at full alpha. The playing line is drawn `LYRIC_LIT` with the clip ending at its lit width and Text Secondary (`LYRIC_OLED_REST`) with the clip starting there; other lines Text Secondary; after the rows, the view's own border paint (`lyrics_fade`, from `ringnav_paint`) lays `LYRIC_FADE_PX` (32) one-row fills of the page's ground (`ui_ink`, so white in Light Mode) at the top and foot of what shows of the view, found by intersecting its ancestors' boxes (the window under the status row, the slide above the progress bar), each from clear inside to opaque at the edge, as `marquee_fade` does a label's columns. They paint in the canvas's clip, so a scroll's repaint fades each line where it now is. Cost: 64 calls and at most 2 x 32 x 375 = 24,000 blended pixels in stock's `fill_bgra8888_rect` a full repaint, less in a dirty rect, and nothing per pixel in the payload. With no memory for the table the rows stay stock's, and the [lyrics wheel](#scrub-ipod) moves them as before, a row a tick.

**Follow.** Stock's follow (`ringnav_lyric_follow`) does nothing on the page. Every UI pass with the page in front and lit, else every `LYRIC_FOLLOW_MS` (250 ms, stock's timer's pace), `lyric_follow` finds the playing line, the first of those starting when the last started line did (lines sharing a stamp light together), and targets the offset that centers its row (line 0's before the first starts): glided to on the page, set at once off it, never while held or while a pointer is down. Wheel travel moves a one-row line's height (`lyrics_row_h`, 51 px) per tick's worth instead of `LYRIC_ROW_PX`, so a tick lands on the next row's top, where the snap on letting go keeps it. `lyrics_now` reads the clock on those passes, so its bounds narrow on each second's change; off them (another page, another window on top, the screen off) the follow goes by the whole second (`lyrics_sec`, as stock's), which lets the bounds go, so the clock starts again, wide, when the page is back in front. While `playing_page` is on top and lit, the playing line's rows repaint when its lit width changes, at most every `LYRIC_PAINT_MS` (66 ms, about 15 a second; a word-timed line's width moves nearly every pass, and the idle loop passes every 25 ms), and the last line's when another line starts. Limit: the lit sweep moves in steps of up to `LYRIC_PAINT_MS` of the song, a few pixels at a fast word; the value is a guess.

**Full screen.** Stock's page binds nothing to its lyrics, so `ringnav_playing` binds nothing to its lyrics, so on either layout `ringnav_playing` binds `view_lyric`'s `EVT_POINTER_DOWN` (before children), `EVT_POINTER_UP_BEFORE` and `EVT_POINTER_ABORT` (`np_lyric_touch`). A release within `TAP_PX` (10, AWTK's drag threshold) of its press either way, so no swipe or drag of the lines, with lyrics on (`lyrics_on`) or already full screen, toggles `np_full`: the page's column (`tools/ipod.py` `playing_page`: full width, under the 40 px top row, down to just past the dots; the title is on the art page) takes the whole window: y 0 and the window's height, its dots `NP_FULL_FOOT` (20 px) above the foot, and `view_lrc`, whose `self_layout` fixes it at the slide's `lift` and 178 px, from the top to 20 px above them (`widget_set_self_layout_params`, the old place written back off); the width stays 375, so nothing rewraps. The hold drops, so the follow glides to the playing line. Off, the column goes back to its index, place and `slide_view` height from before (`np_was`). Return ends it as a tap does, and stays on the page (`STOP`). Handlers return 0, as the heart's do: the `slide_view` behind takes a swipe and `scroll_lrc` a drag of the lines as stock does, and either's abort ends full screen, so the pages slide in their column; a touch taken that way is no tap at its lift (`np_tap_x` `1 << 20`). `lyric_poll` ends it off the lyrics page, while a window over the page leaves it as it is; the page's destruction drops it; a page without `slide_view` has no column, so `np_full` does nothing and full screen never starts. Limits: a tap brings back lyrics the wheel or a finger held; any window over the page, a toast or the volume included, ends it; the covered widgets still repaint under the column (the bar every second, a long title's scroll), redrawing the lyrics beneath them.

**Clock.** `player_playtime_and_length` reports whole seconds, which stock's status thread (`mclSyncPlayerStatus`, `0x5bb874`) asks hciplayer for every 200 ms (`{media-info\get-music-info}`, its fourth field). `lyrics_now` keeps the offset from `time_now_ms` to the position as an interval: the first second seen, or one after a jump (a seek, another song), puts it anywhere in that second plus a poll (`LYRIC_POLL_MS`, 250); the next second's arrival while playing puts the position at most a poll past that second, and the two intersect, or restart from that change when they disagree. Paused (`mclGetPlayStatus()` not 2) it holds; on Play it goes on from where it stopped until the next second replaces that guess. It never runs more than a poll past its reported second.

**Lit width.** A line without word stamps is lit whole from its start (`ly_lit`). One with them is lit through them, from stamp to stamp, each at its character's distance along the line's rows laid end to end; before the first, from the line's start; past the last, at `LYRIC_UNIT_MS` a letter (90 ms; three for a CJK character; `LYRIC_MIN_MS`, 800, at least), done by the next line's start. Limits: the clock knows the position to about a poll, 0.1 s either way, and doesn't allow for the output's latency (Bluetooth's); a line longer than four rows is cut.

## Pull-to-search

Pull-to-search starts from the existing touch hook only on a real pointer-down (`0x100`; the stock window manager registers `on_wm_tsdown_before_fun` for that type), while the separate move-before callback (`0x102`) tail-calls the same entry point. It applies to Local Songs (`localmusic_page`), the same list where a set with `home_lib` shows it on Home's window (`scroll_view_localmusic` on `home_page`, in Split), and Internet Radio (`radio_page`): Folder view has no working stock search, so it is excluded. It checks the screen coordinates, list bounds and initial scroll offset, then uses page-owned move/up-before-children callbacks (`0x102` / `0x104`). A downward drag of at least `PULL_CLAIM_PX` (8), greater than its horizontal travel, claims the pointer. The native abort event (`0x107`) clears pressed descendants; a widget-owned suppression flag also rejects late row clicks until the next touch. A floating, non-interactive label overlays the page without changing the list or its indices. Release at `PULL_SEARCH_PX` (48) invokes the stock Local Songs search callback `0x5350d4`, which opens `dialog/search_dialog` without replacing the browsing page; on Internet Radio it calls `radio_search` (radio.c) instead. The stock search dialogs quit on Return even while their edit's keyboard is open, which destroys the edit under the keyboard and freezes demo; `search_key` (navigation.c's `ringnav`) reads the editing target from the input method (`IM_WIDGET`, `+0x04`, pinned against stock's `input_method_request`), since the keyboard is a separate top window and its focus chain does not contain the search edit. It closes the keyboard on the first Return (`widget_set_focused(search_edit, 0)` plus `input_method_request`, since the searchbox dialogs' edit does not close on blur), and the next Return runs stock's quit with the keyboard already shut. Moving back below the threshold cancels activation. Page/surface destruction, backgrounding, close and input interruption clear the gesture. The stock quick-settings start region (`y < 31`) is excluded. The Library has a **Search** row (`ringnav_localmusic`); under `list.entry.ipod` (OLED's) the row and the pull call `library_search_open` (`patch/search_strip.c`) instead, which opens `searchstrip_page`, an iPod classic's letter strip with no keyboard: one sheet the payload paints (`search_strip_paint`), its keys taken in `ringnav` before stock's (`search_strip_key`), the songs from `staged_music(all_songs)` searched for songs by title, artist or album as the playlist editor's Add Songs search is, then artists, then albums (one row per name, case aside). The tab picks the list (`ss_filter`): All takes `SS_GROUP` (32) of each group, so a string most titles hold still reaches the artists in 32 wheel ticks (the strip's list moves a row a tick, with no ramp), its artists and albums deduplicated against those before them in song order; Songs, Artists and Albums take their group whole, the artists and albums sorted by name (`qsort`) and deduplicated in one pass, since checking each of a big library's thousand artists against the rest per keystroke would not keep up. Any song matching means some group does, an artist's or album's song holding the text too, so a submit goes to the results (or, on an empty tab, the tabs) only then. The tabs are `segments_paint` (`slider_page.c`), the segmented control EQ's Simple and Advanced draw, given a 30 px track in the first row under the query. The text is ASCII, a byte a character, and `ss.cur` is the cursor: `ss_type` inserts at it and `ss_erase` takes the character before it, Previous and Next move it, and `ss_typed` draws the query's run of characters that keeps the cursor on its line. The strip is one loop of stops, `ss.stop`: 0 the set switcher, then the set's characters and a space (`ss_run`), then the return key (`ss_stops`); `ss_sets` holds the four sets, every printable ASCII character between them, and `ss.off` is the run's first cell shown, moved by `ss_follow` only to keep the highlight a cell in from either edge of the ten. `ss_turn` steps the stop round the loop; a wheel tick under `SS_GESTURE_MS` (250 ms) after the one before (`ss.turn_at`) belongs to the same turn, and a turn that reached the return key (`ss.halted`) goes no further, so crossing from it to the switcher takes a new turn. The run's letters fade where more of the set lies past an edge by their own alpha (`ss_run_letter`): a character in the 22 px band is drawn a 2 px slice at a time under `canvas_set_clip_rect`, each slice in its own alpha, rather than a gradient of the pill's colour laid over it. Return's press starts `ss_hold_tick` (`search_strip_down`); let go before `SS_HOLD_MS` (600 ms) and `search_strip_key` puts the highlight on the return key, else the tick closes the page (`ss_leave`) and arms `RETURN_RELEASE_LATCH` itself, as stock's long press does, so stock's key-up filter swallows the release; stock's own long press comes at `KEY_HOLD_MS` (700 ms), after the close, and `search_strip_hold` takes it for the page that closed (`ss_hold_closed`, within 400 ms) so the page under it does not open Now Playing. A held Return reaching `compact_now_playing` with no press seen closes the page at once. Previous's press arms `ss_erase_due` 450 ms ahead; each erase arms the next, 500 ms, then 15 % sooner each time down to 110 ms, and the release, its erases made, moves no cursor. `search_strip_owns` keeps a hold of Previous or Next there from scanning the song (`seek.c` `seek_allowed`) and from stock's long press (`ringnav_keylong`). Play/Pause on the strip submits (`ss_submit`): a box's OK, a name's save, Search's results. A drag along the strip runs on `EVT_POINTER_MOVE_BEFORE`, moving the highlight a stop per 19 px as one turn (`ss_slide`), each step popping as a wheel tick; a tap types the cell under it, cycles the set on the switcher, or submits on the return key. Each result row is grayed as other lists' are ([server library](server-library.md#grayed-rows)): `catalogue_unavailable` for a song, `catalogue_artist_unavailable` and `catalogue_album_unavailable` (`group_unavailable`) for an artist or album, the text in `#666666` (the bar's white at 70 % on the selection) and `catalogue_mark_paint` at the right column, the text ending 12 px short of the mark. The key pop is `tools/art.py`'s images for a theme with the key (`pop_images`): the bubble (`oled_search_pop`, one SVG path, nonzero fill, in the accent's top tone) and a strip of a cell per character of the sets in their order (`oled_search_pop_letters`, 24 px Inter Medium, `POP_CHARS`; `ss_pop_cell` finds the cell), each glyph's ink centered on its cell from the face's outlines without snapping; the key under the bubble keeps its character drawn as the strip's letters are, in white at 60 %. The return key's marks are six more (`oled_search_return_<kind>_w` and `_a` for `search`, `go` and `save`, `return_mark` from `RETURN_MARKS`: the user's mock-up's 24-unit glyphs, a magnifier, an arrow right and a check, round stroked and scaled into a 20 px box). Which one shows is `ss_ret_kind`: the kind the caller gave (`STRIP_*` in `peq.h`: an edit's `_strip_return` int prop for `search_strip_box`, `search_strip_return` before `search_strip_text`, or set by Search, Add Songs, Rename and New Playlist themselves), else the magnifier when the text is on the query line (a stock search box, TIDAL's) and the arrow anywhere else. `search_strip_paint` draws the bubble's cells at whole pixels with `canvas_draw_image` over the lit cell, in place of its key; `ss_pop_step` times it on each wheel step and drag step (`SS_POP_MS`, `SS_POP_FAST_MS`) and `ss_pop_due` invalidates only the bubble's box. An artist opens `localmusic/artistinfo_page` with `{0xf001, record}` as Now Playing's Artist info does, an album `coverflow_goto_album` as Era's albums do, and a song plays with `play_folder` as a song list (`0xf001`) of the songs found ([ipod.md](ipod.md#search)). The same key turns on `patch/keyboard.c` for the keyboard every other text box opens (`kb_default_t9`, found as the input method's `IM_KEYBOARD`): `kb_wheel_key`, in `ringnav` after the strip's, takes the wheel and Center while it is up, walking the buttons of the `pages` widget's active child (and the candidates' first) and pressing the lit one with a dispatched `EVT_CLICK`, as a tap; `kb_wheel_bg`, in `ringnav_paint_bg`, clears stock's fills once per keyboard (inline `style:*:bg_color` 0) and paints the ground black and each key's box under the label and icon stock still draws. Stock's `#2B2B2B` ground had lit 2982 pixels under the glass's corners; on black none are ([ipod.md](ipod.md#keyboard)). Under `list.entry.ipod` the strip takes each keyboard instead: `kb_style`, on its first paint or key, arms `kb_strip_due`, which hands the window and the input method's edit to `search_strip_box`.
