Stock's input method frees the keyboard window as its box closes and the next keyboard is often at the same address (0xd889f8 both times on Add Network's password box), so `kb_style` forgets it on the window's `EVT_DESTROY` (`kb_gone`), as `ss_closed` lets the strip go on the same event; matching on the address alone left a box's second opening with stock's T9 keys. A password shows as dots (`ss.secret`, `ss_secret_box`), and no stock edit says it holds one: every box's `input_type` reads back 0, its page's `password` included. A network's own password box (`kbwifipass_dialog`) is the edit named `edit_passwd`; Add Network's two rows both open `editwifi_dialog` (its edit named `edit`, `tr_tips` unset), whose init keeps the context its opener passed, 1 for the password row and 0 for the name, in an unnamed word at `0xa3b070` (`EDITWIFI_PASSWORD`, stored at `0x49a698` and read to pick the hint at `0x49a6b4`). A payload box marks itself: a card app's field titled as a password or showing the app's asterisks (`addon.c` `field_secret`) sets `_secret` on its edit, and the Guest Play hotspot's password calls `search_strip_secret` before `search_strip_text`. The character just typed shows for `SS_PEEK_MS` (1 s), a timer (`ss_peek_due`) repainting the dots when it ends, and moving the cursor ends it at once.

`patch/ipod.json` records the added private prologue and native event ABI instructions alongside the compact sites and assets. The builder checks them against the pinned stock executable and checks the byte sizes of all referenced global flags/values.

## Page parallax

`patch/page_parallax.c` ([oled-design](oled-design.md#motion)). Every sliding window's hint is stock's `htranslate` (`tools/ipod.py` `SLIDE`, the theme's `motion.page`), whose animator (`window_animator_htranslate_create`, `0x696fb8`) snapshots both windows at the start and draws them each frame from its vtable at `0x93b234` (`.data.rel.ro`; `window_animator_t`: duration `+0`, `prev_win` `+0x14`, `prev_img` `+0x1c`, `curr_img` `+0x64`, `open` `+0xac`, `percent` `+0xb4`, eased, `canvas` `+0xb8`, `time_percent` `+0xbc`, 1 at the end). Stock's `draw_prev_window` (`0x696d90`) draws the page under `w * percent` left (the whole way with the new page) and paints any window between the two shifted with it; `draw_curr_window` (`0x696c40`) the new page `w * (1 - percent)` right; `update_percent` (`0x696bd0`) eases `time_percent` (reversed for a close). `tools/build.py` `HTRANSLATE_SLOTS` points the update and draw_prev slots at `parallax_update` and `parallax_prev`, each of which runs stock's own (`PRIVATE_FUNCTIONS` `htranslate_*`) with its change: `parallax_update` runs a close's `time_percent` `PAGE_SLIDE_MS / PAGE_POP_MS` as fast before stock eases it, so a pop ends after 200 ms where a push takes 220 (the animator's end is that time's, read after); `parallax_prev` calls stock's with `percent` scaled to `PX_UNDER_PCT` (30%), then darkens what the new page does not yet cover, black at `PX_DIM_ALPHA` (64 of 255) times `percent`, in both halves as iOS dims. The status row is the system bar's own window, painted over the slide in place, so it stays put; its title is the new page's at once (a `ponytail:` in the file: cross-fading it would draw both pages' titles into the bar). Stock paints the bar first in each frame (`window_animator_begin_frame`, `0x6968f8`), before `window_animator_update` (`0x6961f8`) runs `update_percent`, `draw_prev_window` and `draw_curr_window`, so a paint of the bar sees the frame before. Home in Split has a band the bar paints, the art's and the raised list's rows above Home's window ([ipod: Home](ipod.md#home)), which the snapshots do not hold: with Home under the slide, `parallax_prev` paints the bar again after its draw, with the page under and this frame's `percent` readable through `parallax_slide` for that paint alone. `coverflow_home_bar` and `coverflow_home_strip` then draw the band `parallax_under_x` left, as the snapshot is, clipped to the columns the sliding page does not cover; `coverflow_home_dim` darkens them by `parallax_dim`; and the title (`bar_title_fades`, `theme_titles_paint.c`) shows only over the sliding page, faded to its share, in place, clear of the status row's glyphs. Before, the band was the bar's flat ground for the whole slide, the list's raised top row cut at the window's top, under the closing page's title. The glyphs keep the bar's ink over the art while it slides (`ponytail:` the still bar inks them by contrast with the art under them from the screen's buffer, `home_ink_bar`; the slide's paint draws the art through the canvas and leaves them as they are, so in Light Mode the clock is dark on the art until Home settles). Under Reduce Motion the hint is `fade` (`motion_row`), whose animator is untouched. The page slide is `PAGE_SLIDE_MS` 220 (the theme's `motion.page.ms` and `motion.swap.ms`).

## Swipe back

`patch/swipe_back.c`, after iOS's edge swipe ([oled-design](oled-design.md#gestures)). **Claim.** `ringnav_touch` hands every pointer-down that stock, the A-Z index and Edit Library left alone to `swipe_back_down`; one within `SB_EDGE_PX` (24) of the left edge is a candidate when the top window is a normal `window` (not a dialog, Control Center or the keyboard), no window animates, `usable()` holds, Return would leave something and the press is not on full-screen lyrics or the rating picker (Return stays on the page there). What Return leaves, the layer that moves: on Home, the list one of its rows opened (`coverflow_home_sublist`, what `coverflow_home_back` closes); elsewhere the top window, if a normal window lies under it in the window manager's stack (Home's own list has none, and takes no swipe). The window gets `sb_event` for destroy, close, abort, move-before and up-before, bound once (`_sb_bound`), as `pull_event` is. Stock forwards each move-before to the press's hook too, so only a real press resets the state. The touch is claimed once it has moved `SB_CLAIM_PX` (10, AWTK's drag threshold) right and more right than up or down; a drag that goes `SB_CLAIM_PX` up or down first, or left, ends the candidate and stays the page's, so a list scrolls from the edge as before. The claim aborts the window's pressed widgets (`EVT_POINTER_ABORT`, dispatched recursively, as pull-to-search and the A-Z index do), so a row, a slider or Now Playing's `slide_view` lets go, and every later move and the lift return `STOP`. A sideways drag that starts mid-screen is never a candidate: Now Playing's pages, Cover Flow, the letter strip and the sliders keep it.

**Follow.** Each move puts the layer at the finger's distance from the press (`widget_move`, which moves without laying the children out again; `widget_move_resize` lays a list out, and Home's lists lost their fades and scroll to it). The window manager paints from the topmost normal window up, so the page under a window is not painted until Return has closed the window over it: at the claim `under_snap` paints it once into an offline canvas (`canvas_offline_create`, `widget_paint`, as stock's animator snapshots a window) and keeps it as a bitmap, and `swipe_back_paint`, first in `ringnav_paint_bg` for the swiped window, draws the strip left of it from that bitmap (the window's canvas reaches left of its own box), `parallax_under_x` short of its place and darkened to `parallax_dim` (page_parallax.c's, the push's own drift and dim at the share of the page still in), still and undimmed under Reduce Motion. Each move invalidates the whole window manager, as the strip moves with the page. Home's lists (no window under) uncover black (a `ponytail:`). `test/patch.py` prints the payload's instructions for a move and a glide step on MIPS (`Swipe back on MIPS`), a small share of the 600k frame budget; the rest of a frame is stock's repaint of the moved window. **Lift.** The speed is the last two moves' (none from a sample older than `SB_VEL_MS`, 100 ms). `sb_done`: back past `SB_DONE_PCT` (40) of the layer's width or at `SB_FLICK` (500) px a second right, never flicked left faster than that. Either way the layer glides from where it is over `SB_GLIDE_MS` (160 ms, as iOS finishes an interactive pop faster than a push), eased cubic out (`sb_ease`), stepped by `swipe_back_poll` from each UI loop pass (`ringnav_sleep`); a spring back ends at its place, an abort mid-swipe springs back. **Back.** At the right edge, `go_back` clears the window's `close_anim_hint` (it has already slid out; AWTK reads the property before `anim_hint`, and an empty one is no animation), then gives `ringnav_input` a `KEY_RETURN` press and release, the window manager's own input path, so the chord, lock and every page's Return handling see it as the button's. Afterwards the hint is put back and the layer returns to its place: off the stack if Return closed the window, back in view where Return stayed (a page whose Return moves focus first, as the letter strip's results do). A press while a glide runs starts no candidate.

## Now Playing motion

**Art on pause.** `patch/np_settle.c`, after Apple Music ([oled-design](oled-design.md#motion)). `np_settle_poll` runs on each UI loop pass while `st.np_cover` is set: `mclGetPlayStatus` 3 (paused) against what it last saw. A pause starts the art's `ovm_t` out over `NS_PAUSE_MS` (280), a play in over `NS_PLAY_MS` (320), both `cubic_out`; `ovm_scale(..., NS_PAUSED)` is the art's size, 880 thousandths out and 1000 in, and 1000 under Reduce Motion. A new `img_cover` (a page opening) takes the state at once, so a page that opens on a paused song shows the art small with no run. Stock's `image` draws the cover whole into its box (`draw_type` `scale_auto`, with a black box under it from its style), so while the scale is under 1000 `np_settle_begin`, first in `ringnav_paint_bg`, empties the canvas's clip before stock paints `img_cover`, and `np_settle_paint`, first in `paint_cover`, puts it back and draws the image itself (`widget_load_image`, `canvas_draw_image`) into the box `np_settle_box` gives: the scale's share of the box about its center, the image's shape kept and centered as `scale_auto` keeps it. `paint_cover` rounds the corners of that box (a theme's `playing.art.radius` scaled with it) and `np_tap_dim` dims only it, so the ring the art leaves is the page behind. The frames come from the motion helper's shared timer. A paused page's every repaint scales the cover again, about a millisecond at 132 px (a `ponytail:` in the file: a bitmap kept at the paused size would make it a copy).

**Track change.** `patch/np_skip.c`. The change is the lines' text: `np_skip_begin`, in `ringnav_paint_bg` as Now Playing's window starts a frame, hashes the title's, artist's and album's (`widget_get_text`) and compares the hash with the one the page last painted; the art the page reloads (`np_art_poll`, stock's own reload) lands under the same run. Nothing of the window is drawn yet, so the screen's buffer (`LCD_OFFLINE_FB`, stock's 375 x 320 BGRA `lcd_mem`, a frame's dirty rect drawn over the last) still holds the last frame: the band of rows the art and the lines lie in is copied from it as the old, and a run starts (`motion_frames` for its length). `np_skip_end`, from `ringnav_paint` after the window's children, copies the band as just drawn as the new and makes two boxes again inside the canvas's clip: the art's (from `NS_SHIFT` px left of the art, the margin, to where the lines start) and the lines' (the title's top to the album's foot, to the screen's edge). Each pixel is the page's ground (black, or the scheme's paper in Light Mode), the new over it at its alpha from `NS_SHIFT` px the far side, and the old over that at its own alpha and shift, each read inside its box only (`np_skip_at`: the old `cubic_in` over `NS_OUT_MS` 120, the new `cubic_out` over `NS_IN_MS` 200 from `NS_IN_AT` 60; Reduce Motion a linear `MO_FADE_MS` cross-fade, no shift). Next leaves left; Previous (the queue position one back, `queue_now`) right. New lines mid-run copy the screen as it stands, the run's own frame, so skips never queue. It runs only on the art's page (`slide_view` at 0), on the screen's buffer (a window's snapshot or an offline canvas has another `lcd`) and lit; the two band copies (2 x about 220 KB) are freed at the run's end or when the page changes. The times, the bar and the heart change at once.

**Art into Now Playing.** `patch/art_zoom.c`. `art_zoom_load`, first in `motion_load` for Now Playing's window as it loads, finds the window under it in the window manager's stack (the new window is already in it) and asks `art_zoom_source` for the playing cover on it: the middle square of Home's art pane (`coverflow_home_pane`, while it is in that window and shown; Home's selected row is Now Playing's, whose cover the pane shows), or a dressed album page's header cover (`album_local_on`, `hero_cover_box`). With one, the window's `open_anim_hint` and `close_anim_hint` name `art_zoom` (300 and 240 ms; `fade(duration=150)` both ways under Reduce Motion), and `motion_load` leaves the theme's playing hint off; without one, the open stays immediate (an `open_anim_hint` left from an earlier open is emptied). Both read the hint through `window_hint`, which gives `""` for none: stock's `window_base_get_prop` answers a window's `open_anim_hint` and `close_anim_hint` with its own field, NULL until one is set, and `widget_get_prop_str` returns that NULL rather than its default, so Now Playing loaded new over a list read NULL, and dereferencing it was a SIGSEGV in `art_zoom_load`. `art_zoom` is registered once with stock's animator factory (`window_animator_factory_register`) and builds stock's own `window_animator_t` (`window_animator_create`) over a payload vtable: stock's htranslate `update_percent` (the eased percent, reversed for a close), `az_prev` (the ground, then the page's snapshot at an alpha falling to 0 by half the run) and `az_curr` (Now Playing's snapshot at an alpha rising from 40% of the run, then its art's box from that snapshot drawn at the box between the source cover and the art, `art_zoom_at`, the art's box as `np_settle_box` gives it). A close over a window other than the one it opened from draws the fades with no art.

## Scan

Holding Previous or Next (keys 222 and 223) scans the playing track as an iPod's click wheel does ([ipod.md](ipod.md#previous-and-next); `patch/seek.c`). **Stock.** The buttons' key-down repeats while held (a repeat follows within 258 ms, [held keys](#held-keys)). Off Now Playing, nothing looked at the hold and the release reached `on_wm_keyup_fun`'s `prev_quick_click`/`next_quick_click` (`0x4f2db0`, `0x4f2e54`), a skip. On Now Playing the page's long press (`0x53b4d0`, AWTK's at 1000 ms) sets `NP_KEY_HELD` (`0xa4e880`); each repeat after it reaches the page's key-down (`0x53e000`), which stops the page's timer, sets `NP_KEY_MODE` (`0xa4e881`) and steps `slider_play` 5 s; the release (`0x53da5c`) calls `player_seek_time` with the slider's value once, restarts the timer and stops the key there, so a hold was a silent seek at about 5 s a repeat, committed at the release (measured in the emulator, repeats every 33 ms: the slider ran to the track's end).

**Hold.** `seek_input`, from `ringnav_input` (`window_manager_dispatch_input_event`, before stock's input status and every window), takes the two keys. A fresh press passes on, so stock's input status sees the press and later its release, and arms `seek_hold` `SEEK_HOLD_MS` (500 ms) on, if `seek_allowed`: a local queue (`MCL_TYPE` 1, a folder, or `0xfxxx`, the library) playing or paused (`mclGetPlayStatus` 2 or 3); `media_owner()` 1 and nothing else focused, no q2video or card game; not a game, the playlist editor, a time or sleep-timer field (`games_page`, `playlistedit_page`, `manualtime_page`, `sleepshutdown_page`), nor a dialog other than `volume_dialog` (the restart toast's `msginfo_dialog` among them); lit and `usable()`, or dark without a Buttons lock that takes the skip keys (`g_keylock_flag` with `g_keylock_mode` 2 or 3, as stock's dark filters). The press's repeats are dropped there, so Now Playing's key-down never steps the slider. A press of the other button meanwhile is dropped whole. A release before the hold cancels it and passes, and stock skips. Once the hold fires the press is the scan's (`sk.eat`): `ringnav` stops its release (`seek_release`) before the windows and stock's skip, and clears `NP_KEY_HELD` and `NP_KEY_MODE`, since Now Playing's long press still marked the key at 1000 ms and its own release handler, which would clear them, never runs; `ringnav_keylong` stops the long press itself.

**Jumps.** `seek_tick` runs at the hold and every `SEEK_CYCLE_MS` (500 ms) after (an AWTK timer, `RET_REPEAT`). The first reads the player's second (`player_playtime_and_length`, track seconds) as the target and picks the scan's plan, a row of `seek_phases` (`seek_plan`): heard at speed (below) when `/tmp/q2scan` is there and the track plays, else `SEEK_PLAN_JUMPS`, the stock player's scan, which this paragraph describes. Each cycle moves the target half the phase's speed in seconds (`seek_step(held)`), Previous back: 2 until 3 s past the hold, 4 until 6 s, 8 until 10 s, then 16, within `[0, length - 1]` (`seek_target`), and, playing, sends `mclSetSeek(target + the record's CUE start)` alone, as a paused scrub does, without `player_seek_time`'s wait for the player to report the second (up to 2 s on the UI thread) or its press stamp, which would hold each jump's audio [`DAC_RELEASE_MS`](#wired-start) on the jacks. hciplayer plays on from the target until the next, so each cycle is about half a second of the song at its own speed and pitch: no time-stretching, as an iPod's scan. A jump forward includes the half second heard; a jump back is the step plus it. `np_seek_bar` (navigation.c, beside the scrub it shares) shows it on Now Playing: phase 0 ends a scrub under way and clears the page's timer (`playing_timer_clear`), as a scrub starts; 1 writes the slider's value, `label_playtime` (`clock_text`) and the remaining time (`np_sync`) at each jump. Paused, nothing is sent while held: only the bar moves.

**At speed.** With q2player playing a song it can stretch ([player.md: Scan](player.md#scan)), Next's plan is `SEEK_PLAN_FORWARD`: `{mcl-scan\200}` at the hold, `400` from 2 s past it, `800` from 4 s, sent on the player's socket as the Clicker's clicks are (`seek_send`, `MSG_DONTWAIT | MSG_NOSIGNAL`, only when the value changes). The player runs on by itself, so no seek is sent; each tick reads its second and moves the bar there. From 6 s the phase is `400` with a jump of 8 s a cycle (16 times overall), from 10 s 16 s (32 times), sent as `mclSetSeek` as above, q2player playing on at 4 times from each target. Previous's plan is `SEEK_PLAN_SNIPPETS` (`SEEK_REWIND_SNIPPETS` 1, the default), a CD player's rewind: `{mcl-scan\200}` at the hold and a jump back every cycle, of 1 s for the first 2 s, then 2, 4, 8 and from 10 s 16 s, so the scan goes back at 2, 4, 8, 16 then 32 times, each cycle heard forward at twice the speed from its target; at 0 it sends `{mcl-scan\0}` and waits, the track playing on from its start. With `SEEK_REWIND_SNIPPETS` 0 Previous uses `SEEK_PLAN_BACKWARD` instead, Next's plan with the speeds negative: q2player runs the song backward ([player.md: Scan](player.md#scan)), and a backward run that reaches 0 sends `{mcl-scan\0}` there. The release sends `{mcl-scan\0}` and holds the bar on the second the player reports then (phase 2), not the last tick's: forward, q2player plays on at its own speed from the frame after the last one heard; backward it seeks to that second first. Pausing during a scan ends what is heard (`SEEK_PLAN_JUMPS` from the next tick). `test/fw/test_seek.py` drives the default plans; `test/player/run.py` `test_scan` checks q2player's side, backward included.

**Ends.** The release, or a hold whose repeats stop for `SEEK_LOST_MS` (700 ms: a release lost to a window change), ends the scan: phase 2 holds the bar on the target until the player has it, as after a scrub (`settle_poll`, the scrub's `scrub_to` and `scrub_track`), and a paused track gets its one `mclSetSeek` there (`seek_position`, which also records it as a paused scrub's), so it stays paused and Play starts from it. Next's target stops at the track's last second: the scan sends that, ends the bar's hold (phase 2) and waits; the player runs out into whatever follows (Repeat, List Play, Folder Skip and advanced play decide, as at any end), and when the queue's place changes the scan goes on in that track from its second. Previous stops at 0, plays on from there and waits for the release. A track the player stops, or one with no record, ends it.

Measured in the emulator (`Test/08 position 44k16.flac`, a sine whose pitch steps each second, recorded from the guest's ALSA writes): each stretch is 520-540 ms, every 20 ms window of it on its second's pitch; the jumps went 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, then 29, 33, ... 49, then 57, 65, 73 seconds over an 8 s hold; Previous went back 2 s a cycle, then 4; paused, nothing played and Play started at the target. Not measured: a Q2's own repeats while held (taken from the report above), and how much of each stretch the DAC's mute after a seek takes on the jacks (hciplayer's `mcl-seek` mutes and unmutes once per seek, [Wired start](#wired-start): its mute line lets go 90-100 ms after the unmute), which would leave about 400 ms of each stretch heard. ponytail: a stretch's length is `SEEK_CYCLE_MS`; raise it if the jacks' mute leaves too little. At speed (build b6 under the emulator, q2player, same track, recorded by host time with each PCM stream's frames in order): from 13 s, the hold's first 2 s went 16 to 20 s (2 times), the next 2 s 20 to 28 (4 times), the next 2.5 s 28 to 44 (8 times), then 47 to 95 in 3 s by 8 s jumps (16 times) and 95 to 166 in 2.5 s (32 times), each jump's 500 ms heard for 400 ms after 100 ms of silence (the seek's drop); 555 of the 567 sounding 20 ms windows of the hold were within 2 Hz of a second's pitch (the rest straddle a second's change), and the release played on at 166 s with no gap. Previous by snippets (build b7, `SEEK_REWIND_SNIPPETS` 1) from 96 s stepped back 1 s a cycle for 2 s, each cycle 400 ms heard forward at twice the speed after 100 ms of silence, then 2, 4, 8 and 16 s a cycle, reached 0 about 10 s into the hold and played on from 0. The backward run (build b6, `SEEK_REWIND_SNIPPETS` 0) from 77 s went 76 to 72 in 2 s, 72 to 62, 62 to 47, then 8 s back a cycle to 0, where it turned and played on from 0; the turn backward at the hold's start left 120 ms of silence.

## Manual skip

Manual Next and Previous run `player_change_music` (`0x51fd24`), not `mclNextSong`. At queue index `n-1` (or `0` for Previous) it loads the next (previous) folder itself (class 1 with Folder Skip on), or in List Play wraps to the other end with `mclSetPlayPos`. In List Play, `ringnav_next` and `ringnav_change` stop a library queue (`0xfxxx`) at its last track instead (`list_end`), so the end of an album stops on a manual Next as it does at a natural end; `ringnav_change` returns 0, since its caller toasts -1 (no storage) and -5. In Repeat All with Folder Skip off, every branch calls `mclNextSong(0)`/`mclPrevSong`. While advanced playback is active, `ringnav_change` runs stock with `MCL_MODE` 3 and Folder Skip 0, then restores both, so the hooked `ringnav_next`/`ringnav_prev` choose the track and stock's refresh tail (tags, notifications, Bluetooth headset info) still runs. It writes `MCL_MODE` directly, since `mclSetPlayMode` would end advanced playback. `ringnav_mode` (the hook on `mclSetPlayMode`) ends advanced play through `playback_clear` for a user's stock mode choice, except stock Shuffle (2) while Shuffle Albums/Folders is on, which keeps the groups. `ringnav_prev` clears the `seen` flag of the track it leaves, so the next Next returns to it instead of skipping it. Shuffles draw from `rand_below` (`playback.c`), an xorshift32 seeded once from `toolsRandnum` and `time_now_ms`, because stock's generator alone repeated itself between shuffles started close together (the hold menu lists Next/Previous Album, first, only while `playback_option(0) >= 3`). `player_initconfig` (`0x51e024`) also calls it, re-applying the saved mode when hciplayer reconnects (`player_reconfig`, whose flag `mclParseCommand` sets after a disconnect; the first connection at boot never reaches it); that is no mode choice, so `ringnav_mode` passes it straight to stock, told apart by its return address (`INITCONFIG_MODE_RET`, checked by the build). Earlier at boot, `config_init` calls `config_playmode` (`0x504188`) before Home restores the queue. That call goes through `ringnav_bootmode`, which marks it as restoration so `ringnav_mode` applies the setting without deleting the snapshot; explicit mode choices still clear advanced playback.

Memory Playback's `ringnav_memory` restores the saved snapshot using `getAllMusic(3)`, which avoids the pinyin title sort. A temporary index (8 bytes per library row) is sorted by file path and CUE start/end, then binary-searched for each saved occurrence. Equal identities retain the query's first row. The snapshot still controls queue order, history and playback position; missing files are skipped and unindexed files retain the stock directory fallback. Index allocation failure frees the temporary state and falls back to stock resume without rewriting the snapshot. `test/playback.py` checks those cases and bounds path comparisons for a 256-track restore so a full-library search per track cannot return unnoticed.

## Guest Play

Guest Play lets a guest's phone play through the Q2 to what the Q2 plays to (a car, a headset, or the headphone jack): the phone streams to the Q2 over Bluetooth A2DP, the Q2 plays it on, and the guest's track information reaches the car while the car's buttons control the guest's phone. The system side is `q2-guest` (`patch/q2_guest.c`, a program of its own at `/usr/bin/q2-guest`, linked against the rootfs's libdbus), which owns every decision; the payload (`patch/guest.c`) only starts it, passes the UI's commands and the car's keys to it, reads its state for the UI, and pauses and resumes the owner's music. The screens (Settings > Bluetooth > Guest Play, the prompts, the guest's Now Playing) are built on the contract below and nothing else, so that the two sides can change apart.

### Contract

**State.** `/tmp/q2-guest.state`, written whole by `q2-guest` (a temporary file renamed over it) at every change, and once a second while a guest plays (its position moves). Lines `key=value`, values to the end of the line, a newline in a name read as a space. Keys may be added; none listed here changes meaning or goes. No file: the helper is not running, which reads as `state=off`. demo (`guest_poll`, `patch/guest.c`) looks for the file every 250 ms, but only while the helper may be running: at its first pass (a helper an earlier demo started outlives it), for `GUEST_UP_MS` (30 s) after each start, while commands wait for the FIFO, and for as long as its last look found the file; with Guest Play off it asks for nothing.

| Key                             | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seq`                           | Counts writes; a reader redraws when it changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `state`                         | `off` (switched off), `idle` (on, no guest), `open` (Let a Guest Connect is open, no guest yet), `asking` (a prompt is waiting: Allow Once, Always Allow, Decline), `replace` (a second guest while one plays: Keep, Replace), `playing`, `paused` (the guest paused on their phone)                                                         |
| `enabled`, `name`, `allow`, `leave` | The settings: `0`/`1`; the Guest Play name (empty: the Bluetooth name); `ask` (Ask Every Time) or `trusted` (Trusted Guests Only); `resume` (Resume My Music) or `stay` (Stay Paused)                                                                                                                                                 |
| `window`                        | Seconds left of Let a Guest Connect, 0 when it is closed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `guest`, `mac`, `trusted`       | The guest asking or playing: its Bluetooth name, address, and `1` when it is a Trusted Guest                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `code`                          | Six digits while a first pairing asks the owner to compare codes (G3); empty for a known guest (G4) or a phone that pairs without one                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `countdown`                     | Seconds to the automatic answer while `asking` (Decline) or `replace` (Keep), from 30                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `new`, `newmac`                 | `replace` only: the second guest                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `in`                            | The guest's leg: `CODEC RATE KBPS`, as `AAC 44100 256` or `SBC 48000 328`; `KBPS` 0 when it is not known. Empty before the stream is set up                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `out`, `outmac`, `outcodec`     | Where it plays: the device's name and address and its leg in `in`'s form, or `out=jack` with the other two empty                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `title`, `artist`, `album`, `genre`, `track`, `tracks`, `duration`, `position`, `status` | The guest's song as their phone tells it over AVRCP: text; track number and count (0 unknown); length and position in ms; `playing`, `paused`, `stopped` or what the phone says, empty while an allowed guest's stream is still being set up (`state=playing`: show it as connecting)                                                                                                         |
| `event`, `event_seq`            | The last thing that ended or refused a guest, for its toast; `event_seq` counts them, so the same event twice shows twice: `left`, `lost` (out of range while playing), `declined` (by the owner), `timeout` (30 s with no answer), `refused` (Trusted Guests Only, not trusted), `stopped` (Stop Guest Play), `gaveup` (paused 5 min), `kept` (the second guest turned away), `replaced` (the first guest), `failed` (pairing failed or was canceled) |
| `eventname`                     | The guest the event is about                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `source`, `newsource`           | Where the guest asking or playing (and, for `replace`, the second one) comes from: empty for a Bluetooth phone, else `spotify`, `airplay` or `dlna` ([receivers](#guest-play-receivers)); a receiver's `mac` is `KIND:ID` |
| `netdeny`, `netdeny_seq`        | The receiver the payload must stop, counted: set when a receiver's guest is declined, refused, replaced, stopped or given up on |
| `hotspot`, `hotspot_up`, `hotspot_name`, `hotspot_pass`, `hotspot_ip`, `hotspot_clients`, `hotspot_qr` | The [hotspot](#guest-play-hotspot): switched on, running, its name and password, the Q2's address on it (empty while down), phones joined, and the text for its join QR code |

**Commands.** One line each, written to the FIFO `/tmp/q2-guest.cmd` (`guest_send` in `patch/guest.c`, which starts the helper first when it is not running). A line is at most 200 bytes; an unknown or malformed one is ignored. They are answered by the next state.

| Command                                  | Does                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `on`, `off`                              | The Guest Play switch, saved                                                                                                                               |
| `open`, `close`                          | Let a Guest Connect: two minutes discoverable under the Guest Play name, with the Q2's own pairing prompts (`open` again restarts the two minutes)          |
| `allow-once`, `allow-always`, `decline`  | Answer `asking`; `allow-always` also makes the guest a Trusted Guest                                                                                       |
| `keep`, `replace`                        | Answer `replace`                                                                                                                                           |
| `stop`                                   | Stop Guest Play: the guest is disconnected                                                                                                                 |
| `key play`, `pause`, `toggle`, `next`, `prev` | To the guest's phone (AVRCP); the payload sends the car's keys this way while a guest plays                                                             |
| `name TEXT`, `allow ask`/`trusted`, `leave resume`/`stay` | The settings, saved                                                                                                                       |
| `forget MAC`, `ask MAC 0`/`1`, `rename MAC TEXT` | Trusted Guests: forget one (its pairing too), Ask Before Playing, its name in the list                                                             |
| `net KIND ID NAME`, `net-end KIND` | From the payload: a receiver's session started (asked about, or played at once by the same rules as a phone), or ended |
| `hotspot on`/`off`, `hotspot-pass TEXT` | The [hotspot](#guest-play-hotspot), saved; it runs only while Guest Play is on too, and a new password or Guest Play name restarts it |

**Saved.** `/mnt/data/q2-guest/config` (the settings, `key=value`, the hotspot's switch and password among them) and `/mnt/data/q2-guest/trusted`, one Trusted Guest a line, `MAC`, `ask` (0 or 1), the time it last played (seconds since 1970) and its name, tab-separated, at most 16; the UI reads the list from that file. Both are the helper's: the UI changes them only with commands.

**Payload API** (`patch/guest.c`): `guest_send(line)` sends a command, `guest_seq()` is the state's `seq` (0 with none), `guest_field(key, out, n)` reads one key of it, `guest_active()` is true while a guest plays or is paused. The state is read again at most every 250 ms, from `headset_poll`.

### Rules

- **Approval.** A guest is asked about when it pairs during Let a Guest Connect (with the code when the phone compares codes), and when a paired phone that is not a Trusted Guest, or a Trusted Guest with Ask Before Playing, starts a stream. Allow Once lets it play this time; Always Allow adds it to Trusted Guests (Ask Before Playing off); Decline, or 30 s with no answer, refuses: a pairing is rejected, a stream's phone disconnected. A guest allowed while pairing is not asked again when its stream starts. Trusted Guests Only refuses every guest outside Trusted Guests without asking, except one that pairs while Let a Guest Connect is open, which the owner opened on purpose.
- **One guest at a time.** A second guest while one plays gets the Replace prompt, Keep selected; Keep, or 30 s, disconnects the second; Replace disconnects the first and plays the second.
- **Leaving.** When the guest's stream ends (the phone left, went out of range, Stop Guest Play, or 5 min paused), the owner's music resumes if it was playing when the guest started and the setting is Resume My Music; with Stay Paused it stays paused.
- **Name.** The Guest Play name is the Bluetooth name the Q2 shows while Let a Guest Connect is open; the Q2's own name comes back when it closes. Paired devices keep the name they stored.

### The relay

The audio path is the one proven on a Q2 (Pixel, LDAC 96 kHz in, to an Echo, SBC 48 kHz out, 5 to 10% CPU): two `bluealsa` daemons and `bluealsa-aplay` between them. While Guest Play is on, the main daemon offers only the source role (`-p a2dp-source`), as `/usr/bin/bluealsa2`, the launcher demo starts at each Bluetooth on, reads the switch from the saved settings; a device that is both (an Echo) otherwise connects in the sink role. The helper starts the second daemon, `bluealsa -B sink -p a2dp-sink -c AAC` (SBC is always there; no LDAC or aptX for a guest, which keeps the Q2's decoding cheap) once the car or headset is connected or after 8 s without one, so the outbound device connects first; a guest's stream is a PCM on `org.bluealsa.sink`, which the rootfs's `etc/dbus-1/system.d/bluealsa-sink.conf` lets root own and reach (stock's `bluealsa.conf` allows `org.bluealsa` only). Approved, the helper runs `bluealsa-aplay -B sink -D bluealsa:DEV=CAR,PROFILE=a2dp GUEST`, or `-D plug:hw:0` with no Bluetooth device. Turning Guest Play on while a car is connected restarts the main daemon once and connects the car's A2DP again before the sink daemon starts; a guest coming and going after that leaves the car's link as it is.

ponytail: the owner's player is stopped (`player_save_stop`), not paused, while a guest plays, as a paused hciplayer may hold its PCM (it closes it at a stop, a skip and a cold start: [Bluetooth keep-alive](#bluetooth-keep-alive)) and BlueALSA gives a PCM to one client; it restarts where it was (`player_save_start`). Spotify, radio and video are paused instead. ponytail: with the main daemon in the source role alone, stock's receiver mode is off while Guest Play is on, and so is whatever else of its default profiles `-p a2dp-source` leaves out (the hands-free profile that [Headset battery](#headset-battery) may read); turning it off restarts the main daemon as stock's and connects the car's A2DP again.

### Track information and controls

A car asks bluetoothd for the playing track ([Track metadata](#track-metadata)), which answers from `libbtctl`'s record. While a guest plays, the helper fills that record with the guest's song through the same D-Bus call demo's `btctl_notify_track_changed` makes: `NotifyChanged(i event, ay data)` on `shanling.bluez`, `/shanling/bluez` (bluetoothd's own service, `bluez_main`). Event `0x108` is the track: four 32-bit words (track number, track count, length in ms, the number of text attributes), then the title as a 16-bit attribute id 1 and a 16-bit length with its NUL, then the text and its NUL, then artist (2), album (3) and genre (6), each present only when not empty, as an 8-bit id, a zero byte, a 16-bit little-endian length with the NUL, and the text with its NUL. Event `0x107` is the play status, one byte: 0 stopped, 1 playing, 2 paused. Those are what `btctl_notify_track_changed` (`0x2a3b8` in `libbtctl.so`) and `btctl_notify_playback_status_changed` (`0x2a37c`) build. The guest's song comes from BlueZ's `org.bluez.MediaPlayer1` for the guest's device (`Track`, `Status`, `Position`). When the guest leaves, the payload sends the owner's song and status again (`sendBtHeadsetPlayInfo`, `sendBtHeadsetPlayStatus`).

The car's buttons reach demo's headset worker as before; `headset_command` hands Play/Pause, Next and Previous to the helper while a guest plays (`guest_key`), which calls the guest player's `Play`, `Pause`, `Next` or `Previous`. Stock's receiver page, which opens when a phone starts streaming to the Q2 (`btrecvA2dpFunc`, [Bluetooth receiver](#bluetooth-receiver)), is kept shut while Guest Play is on: the hook at `btrecvA2dpFunc` (`0x4fc72c`) drops its events then, as the receiver page would stop the player and take the headset's keys. Cover art waits for the rebuilt bluetoothd's BIP.

### Guest Play receivers

A guest can also play to the Q2's network receivers (Spotify Connect, AirPlay, DLNA), over the hotspot or a Wi-Fi they share. While Guest Play is on, each receiver's session goes through the same rules as a Bluetooth phone: the payload reports its start to `q2-guest` (`net KIND ID NAME`), which asks the owner (Allow Once, Always Allow, Decline, 30 s, Trusted Guests keyed by `KIND:ID`, Replace while another guest plays) or lets it play at once, and the payload holds the receiver until it may play and stops it when it may not (`netdeny`). A receiver plays to the Q2's own output, which is the car or headset through the main bluealsa daemon when one is connected, so it needs no relay; the owner's local music is stopped by the receiver itself, as without Guest Play.

- **Spotify Connect** (built). librespot's change to `playing` (`spot_take`, [Spotify](#spotify)) calls `guest_net("spotify", "connect", "Spotify Connect")`, which with Guest Play on and the session not yet allowed sends `net`, and `spot_take` pauses librespot (`s` on its socket) and stops there. Once the state says `playing` with `source=spotify`, `guest_poll` sends `P`; librespot plays, `spot_take` runs again and takes the output as before. Declined or refused, it sends `s`. librespot names no user or address, so every Spotify Connect guest is `spotify:connect`, one Trusted Guest for all. While it plays, `q2-guest` reads librespot's status file for the song (to the car through `shanling.bluez`, and the state), ends the session when it says `none` (the phone chose another device), and sends the car's keys to librespot's socket (`P`, `s`, `p`, `n`, `b`).
- **AirPlay** (built). Once a phone plays, stock's `airplay_mainscheduling` (`0x519c28`, run from the UI loop) stops the player and opens `airplay_page` for shairport. Its hook, `guest_airplay`, holds that while Guest Play is on and the session is not yet allowed: `airplayGetFlag` set, it sends `net airplay client AirPlay` once and returns without calling stock, so no page opens and the owner's player is left as it is. Allowed, the next call goes on to stock's. Refused, `guest_poll` calls `airplaySendStop` (stock's: it asks shairport, through their shared memory, to end the session, and waits up to 2 s). The flag down while an AirPlay guest plays sends `net-end airplay`. Shairport 1.1.1 names no client to demo, so every AirPlay guest is `airplay:client`, and the car shows "AirPlay" as the title (`q2-guest`). The car's keys stay demo's (stock's AirPlay page).
- **DLNA** (built). The renderer calls demo's `dmrActionSetPlayURI` (`0x51005c`) and `dmrActionPlay` (`0x50fd50`) on its own thread. Their hooks (`guest_dlna_uri`, `guest_dlna_play`) wait there with Guest Play on: `dlna_gate` reads the state file itself every 250 ms (the UI thread owns `gp`), sends `net dlna renderer DLNA` once unless the owner is already being asked about DLNA, and carries the action out once DLNA's guest plays; refused (`netdeny=dlna`), or after `GUEST_NET_WAIT` reads (35 s) with no answer, it does nothing. `dmrActionStop`'s hook (`0x50fe4c`) sends `net-end dlna`. The controller names nothing demo sees, so every DLNA guest is `dlna:renderer`. The song plays through hciplayer, whose track demo already sends to the car, so `q2-guest` sends none for DLNA, and the car's keys stay demo's.

ponytail: a held Spotify session plays for the moment between librespot's start and the pause; a held AirPlay session may be heard while the owner is asked, as shairport opens the output itself when nothing holds it (no hardware check yet); a DLNA controller waits for its SetAVTransportURI or Play answer while the owner is asked, and some give up on an action after 30 s; a receiver guest's end leaves the owner's music stopped (the receiver stopped it, not Guest Play), and only the car's track display goes back to the owner's song.

### Guest Play hotspot

The hotspot lets a guest with AirPlay, Spotify Connect or a DLNA app reach the Q2 with no Wi-Fi of their own, on a second interface beside the Q2's own Wi-Fi connection. The RTL8733BS driver runs `wlan0` and `wlan1` on its one radio (concurrent mode; stock's driver load already makes `wlan1`), and the rootfs's wpa_supplicant 2.12 is built with its access point mode (`CONFIG_AP` in `WPA_CONFIG`, [third-party](third-party.md#wpa_supplicant)), so it needs no hostapd. Proven on a Q2 with `test/guest/hotspot_probe.sh`: `AP-ENABLED` on `wlan1`, an iPhone joined with WPA2 (CCMP), `udhcpd` gave it 192.168.43.20, ping went both ways, and `wlan0` stayed connected on 5 GHz (5180 MHz) throughout, the access point on the same channel; the access point's wpa_supplicant took 6.0 MB of RSS and `udhcpd` 2 MB.

`/usr/bin/q2-hotspot` (`patch/q2_hotspot.sh`) does it for `q2-guest`: `start SSID_HEX PASSPHRASE` writes `/tmp/q2-hotspot/ap.conf` (`mode=2`, WPA-PSK, RSN, CCMP; the name as hex, so it needs no quoting; readable by root alone) on `wlan0`'s frequency, or 2437 MHz (channel 6) without a connection, addresses `wlan1` as 192.168.43.1 and starts wpa_supplicant on it and `udhcpd` (192.168.43.20 to .50); `check` starts it again on `wlan0`'s new channel when `wlan0` has moved, as one radio cannot serve two, and prints how many phones have joined; `stop` ends both. `q2-guest` runs it while Guest Play and the hotspot are both on, checks every 10 s, and names it with the Guest Play name (Q2 without one) and the saved password, made up at first start as two words and two digits (`tulip-river-42`), changed with `hotspot-pass` (8 to 63 characters, no quote or backslash). The state's `hotspot_qr` is the text of Wi-Fi's join code (`WIFI:T:WPA;S:name;P:password;;`, with `\`, `;`, `,`, `:` and `"` escaped), for the UI's QR code.

A receiver a guest reaches over the hotspot goes through [Guest Play receivers](#guest-play-receivers); whether AirPlay, Spotify Connect and DLNA announce themselves over mDNS on `wlan1` is to be checked on a Q2 with a phone on the hotspot.

## Bluetooth boot reconnect

Stock `platform_init` starts `btctl_create_daemon_thread` (`0x51d248`) before `config_bt_init` calls `openBluetooth`. Registering callbacks at the radio's GPIO write can still miss connections discovered by that thread during startup. `headset_bt_init` initializes the stock Bluetooth lists and installs the stock prompt and A2DP callbacks and `headset_bt_status` (below) before starting the control thread, preserving its thread pointer and return value. The later `initBluetoothParam` call in `config_bt_init` is removed so it cannot erase links discovered during startup. Stock's later registration remains for Bluetooth toggles, with `BT_STATUS` registering `headset_bt_status` there too. `test/patch.py` checks the patched call site, callback order and successful/failed thread-start forwarding.

A headset that connects to the Q2 while stock's link thread waits for another device was lost until Bluetooth was toggled. At boot and at Bluetooth on, `autoLinkBluetooth` (`0x4fbed0`) appends the last device (`BTLINKMAC`) and starts the link thread (`0x4fc798`), which waits up to 15 s for it. Stock's device-status callback (`0x4fc180`) ignores a Connected event (3) from a device not in the link list while `bt_connectstatus` is set, and BlueZ sends that event once. If the incoming event arrived first, auto-link appended its target after it, and `checkBluetoothStatus` judges only the last item: the absent target's failure ran `clearBluetoothStatus`, which wiped the incoming link too. `BT_AUTOLINK` turns `autoLinkBluetooth`'s `bal checkPairDev` into `jal headset_bt_autolink`, which also skips while a listed device is connected (status 3). `headset_bt_status` wraps the stock callback; `headset_bt_init` registers it, and `BT_STATUS` turns `openBluetooth`'s registration into `jal headset_status_register`. A Connected event from a paired, unlisted device is adopted only while the thread waits (`bt_connectstatus` 1, not 2 once it ended or 3 while `checkBluetoothStatus` judges) for the saved device (its target, the last item, equals `BTLINKMAC` at `0xa4c0d8`) and the thread has taken that target and is connecting it (status 5: not 1, before the thread reads it, nor 3, already connected). The device is appended with status 3 and the target set to 4, so the wait ends and stock's success path keeps the incoming device and switches the output. Everything else goes to stock. While the thread waits, stock's Bluetooth page ignores taps (`0x4c43e4`) and stock adds no items, so the wrapper is the only writer besides the thread and the payload's cancel ([Bluetooth page](#bluetooth-page): a tap on the connecting row marks the target 4, as the wrapper does). Limits: no global holds the thread's mode, so a connect or pairing the user starts to the saved device from the Bluetooth page is treated like auto-link (a pairing still switches only when its 15 s wait ends), while one to another device still loses an incoming link as stock does. The target's BlueZ Connect is still pending, so if it powers on within its page timeout both may link; that includes the target connecting between the wrapper's check and its update, which then marks it 4. An incoming link whose event arrives after the thread ended but before `checkBluetoothStatus` ran is dropped as in stock. `test/patch.py` checks both patch sites and the wrapper's adopt and pass-through cases.

**Bluetooth abnormal.** When the controller never answers `rtk_hciattach`, `openBluetooth` (`0x4fa378`) retries, then sets `bt_rtk_error`; `checkBluetoothStatus` (`0x4fd42c`) turns that into `bt_initstatus` (`0xa3a874`) -102; and `on_wm_idle_status`, on its next pass, shows **Bluetooth abnormal** (`msg_btabnormal`) and calls `device_reboot` (`0x4f4288` and `0x4f449c`, its only direct callers). A Q2 whose radio module has failed therefore reboots at every boot, and each reboot was a clean end (`ringnav_clean_end`, through `reboot_save`) that left nothing on the card to say why; Wi-Fi fails with it, as the RTL8733BS is one module (`module_driver/rtl8733bs.sh`). Before that restart the Q2 asks (`patch/bt_stopped.c`): stock's two toasts become `jal bt_stopped_toast`, which shows none (`BT_ABNORMAL_TOASTS` in `tools/build.py`), and `ringnav_reboot` (`patch/playback.c`, the hooked `device_reboot`), with `bt_initstatus` at -102, opens **Bluetooth Stopped** instead of restarting ([oled-design](oled-design.md#bluetooth)): a mode page counting down 10 s, then the restart (`ringnav_reboot_from`, with stock's caller for the record); Not Now (Centre, Return or a tap) closes it and every later call from the loop does nothing, so the Q2 runs on without Bluetooth (and Wi-Fi) until it restarts some other way. The restart first calls `reboot_record` (`patch/system.c`): when `bt_initstatus` is -102 it writes `/mnt/data/q2-crash.log` through `system()`, whole then renamed, as `S90play`'s crash path does ([boot.md](boot.md#rockbox-from-home)): `== date`, `== reboot` with the reason, the status, the uptime and the caller's return address, `== dmesg`, its last 200 lines, and `== stderr`, the last 60 lines of `/tmp/q2-demo.err` when a build keeps demo's stderr there, which is where `rtk_hciattach` says what failed. The next boot moves it to the card as any crash log. Any other status (Restart, a factory reset, the power-off page's long press, the firmware update's countdown) writes nothing. `test/fw/test_playback.py` checks the gate and the command, and runs the command under `sh` with stand-ins. ponytail: the record names the symptom, not the cause; `dmesg` and `rtk_hciattach`'s words are what tell a dead module from a UART or firmware fault.

## Bluetooth LDAC quality

The Quality page's rows are LDAC HQ, LDAC Standard, LDAC Connection (auto), aptX HD, aptX, AAC, SBC HQ and SBC (`g_btcoding`, `[SYSSET] BTCODING`). `switchBtPriority` (`0x4faa34`) sends `btctl_set_ldac_quality` over D-Bus to `bluealsa` (`SetLDACQuality`). bluealsa maps 0x15, 0x16 and 0x17 to the encoder's eqmid HQ, SQ and MQ, and maps any other value to adaptive bit rate. Stock sends 0x16 (SQ, 660 kbps, or 606 at 44.1 kHz) for both HQ and Standard. `LDAC_HQ` rewrites the jump-table dispatch to keep `0x15 + row` in the frame's free `0x14($sp)` slot and loads it in place of the constant. HQ then sends 0x15 (990 / 909 kbps), Standard 0x16, and auto still 0x18. Turning Bluetooth on applies the saved row again, and Rockbox plays through the same daemon.

Auto already uses Sony's native ABR controller, including the intermediate 492 and 396 kbps rates (48/96 kHz), alongside 990, 660 and 330. These are discrete encoder frame sizes, not arbitrary 1 kbps increments. The shipped `libldacBT.so.2.0.19` supports them through `ldacBT_alter_eqmid_priority`; `libldacBT_ABR.so.2.0.0` selects them from queue congestion and raises quality after recovery. Bluealsa's `0x416388` maps Auto to an initial SQ encoder with ABR enabled; its encode loop calls `ldac_ABR_Proc` at `0x41ab00` with the queued packet count, using a 40 ms interval and thresholds 12/8/4. The HQ fix changes the fixed HQ row only; Auto could already recover to HQ. `test/ldac.py` executes the shipped encoder's five rates, the daemon's mode mapping and the ABR controller's congestion/recovery paths. No custom rate controller is added. This does not establish a cause or fix for sustained distortion requiring reconnect, or USB-dongle heat; those need device reproduction.

## Bluetooth AAC

When a headset opens the A2DP stream itself (AirPods taken out of the case), it picks AAC at 44.1 kHz. Stock `bluealsa` is still fed 48 kHz audio and drops about 8% of the AAC frames, so the audio is choppy until Bluetooth is toggled; a connection the Q2 opens picks 48 kHz. The build clears the 44.1 kHz bit in `bluealsa`'s AAC source capability, `c0 01 84 84 e2 00` at file offset `0x317b7` (object type, sampling frequencies, channels, VBR and bitrate). Octet 1 holds 8 to 44.1 kHz with 44.1 kHz in bit 0, so `0x317b8` goes from `01` to `00` and headsets pick 48 kHz, which every AAC sink must support. `ZIP_SHA` pins the stock binary, and `test/build.py` audits the allowed byte changes and checks the manifest's `bluealsa_sha256`.

Manual skips also call ALSA DROP. Stock acknowledges it after sending signal 6, but the encoder flushes PCM later (`0x4147ac`), potentially discarding the next track’s first samples. The patched DROP (`0x40cb50`) flushes the nonblocking FIFO under the PCM fd mutex before sending that signal and acknowledging the request. The encoder’s shared DROP handler discards each audited caller’s partial PCM input, restores full input capacity, and resets its pacing clock through the existing OPEN/RESUME path instead of flushing again. Natural gapless transitions do not issue DROP. `test/bluealsa.py` executes both MIPS paths with a delayed signal and empty, normal and oversized old queues; stock loses new audio and the patched binary preserves it.

A manual skip also left the A2DP stream without packets. On a Next mid-song, hciplayer either sends Drain (the PCM still buffered, about 440 ms, drains, then Drain's 100 ms poll times out) or, when demo pauses it first, PAUSE, which stock answers by polling again without a timeout. About 300 ms later it sends DROP, closes the PCM and opens the next one. Traced on a Q2 (stock 1.5.4, AAC), no packet left for 404 ms. The headset's buffer ran dry, and OPEN/RESUME restarted the encoder's pacing (asrsync) from zero, so the new song played on with the buffer near-empty and crackled. A phone keeps its stream running through a skip. `tools/bt_silence.S`, linked at `BT_SILENCE` in bluealsa's payload, patches the shared `io_poll_and_read_pcm` (`0x4145d0`), which every encoder loop calls (all six callers are A2DP encoders). The build points the signal jump table's PAUSE entry (`0x42d09c`) at Drain's case (`0x4147a0`, a 100 ms poll). When that timeout ends and real PCM was read within `BT_SILENCE_SAMPLES` (192000 interleaved samples: 2 s at 48 kHz stereo, 1 s at 96 kHz), the function still wakes Drain's waiter but returns the requested samples as zeros, and from then on it polls without waiting. The encoder's own pacing sets the rate and catches up the 100 ms in a burst that refills the headset's buffer. The next real PCM ends the fill and re-arms the budget; once the budget is spent it behaves as stock. Without a Drain, a poll still blocks as stock, so a stall mid-song is caught up as before. Traced again, a skip leaves 110–131 ms without packets, which is the 100 ms wait. The small click left at a skip is heard with stock as well; the PCM on either side of the skip had no step in it. ponytail: one budget and fill flag serve every encoder thread, which is fine for one headset at a time. A second stream, or a stream torn down while filling, shares or inherits up to the budget's silence. A pause or stop streams up to the budget's silence before the link goes quiet. Unchecked on LDAC Auto: whether the catch-up burst makes its ABR step down a rate at each skip. `test/bluealsa.py` runs the patched function: stock returning nothing at Drain's timeout and polling unbounded after PAUSE, PAUSE's 100 ms poll, the fill for S16 and S32, Drain's wake, unpaced polls and pacing init, a closed PCM, the budget running out and re-arming, and stock behavior without a budget.

## Bluetooth keep-alive

`hciplayer` closes its ALSA PCM at a stop, a skip and a cold start (a gapless change keeps it open: [USB output buffer](#usb-output-buffer)), and stock starts `bluealsa` (`/usr/bin/bluealsa2`) without `--keep-alive`, so the A2DP transport is released and every song begins with a fresh AVDTP start. True-wireless buds start the primary bud (often the right) first and the other joins a moment later, so one ear began early on every track. The build adds `--keep-alive=5` to that launcher (`BT_KEEPALIVE`): the transport stays open 5 s after the PCM closes, which covers a track change. ponytail: inferred from bluealsa's option and the report, not traced on a Q2; the headset stays in streaming state up to 5 s after a stop, and a pause longer than that still restarts the stream.

## Bluetooth link monitor

A headset that breaks up when the Q2 is in a pocket or across a room leaves nothing behind: the kernel logs nothing when packets stop reaching the headset, and bluealsa only waits. On 2026-11-17 a Bowers & Wilkins Px7 on LDAC Auto (no LDAC: bluealsa's `GetPCMs` said aptX HD, 48 kHz, Delay 2357, so 576 kbps) broke up in repeated walking A/B tests where SBC did not, with discovery off (`Adapter1.Discovering` false). The monitor records what the link did, each second, so a policy that lowers the rate under congestion or distance can be built on evidence (the plan is below). The one thing it changes is the headset link's packet types: it allows EDR on the A2DP sink's link (**EDR** below).

**Where.** In `q2guard` ([Overheat guardian](#overheat-guardian)), a process of its own, so the UI and the player do no extra work: q2guard sleeps between its 5 s ticks in `bt_sleep` (`patch/q2bt.c`), which reads the controller's byte counter at each tick and, once an A2DP stream runs (`bt_detect_step`: `BT_START_BPS`, 4 kB/s handed to the controller in an interval; SBC's least is about 25), wakes every second to write a line. The PMIC's 1 s die-temperature window ([Overheat guardian](#overheat-guardian)) waits in `bt_sleep` too (`bus_sleep`; its first window's 50 ms polls do not, as their sum is the time it logs), so the lines go on through it, a sample there only lengthening the wait, and the main sleep is the tick less the window, so q2guard's tick stays 5 s with both. The stream ends after `BT_QUIET_MS` (30 s) under that, so a stall, the radio taking nothing for seconds, is sampled through, and a pause ends it once the [keep-alive](#bluetooth-keep-alive) has let the transport go. The lines go to their own log beside the heat log, `/mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-bt.0`, moved to `.1` at 1 MB (`BT_FILE_MAX`; the two hold about four hours of streaming), through the same RAM ring and writing child (`log_flush`, which `heat_flush` also uses): to the card every minute while a stream runs, and at once at its START and STOP.

**The line.** `TIME up=S kbps= acl= wq= rssi= lq= tpl= afh= err= wtx= wrx= cpu= ba= own= h= er= ew= fcc= done= fly=`, "-" for what was not read; notes `START h=HANDLE mtu= bufs= raw=ok|none`, `ENCODER ba-a2dp-aptx-hd`, `CODEC aptX-HD 48000 Hz delay=235.7 ms`, `LINK h=HANDLE`, `LINK ptype=0x0018 status=0x00 h=HANDLE` (**EDR** below) and `STOP`. What each field is, and why it was chosen over the alternatives:

- `kbps` and `acl`: bytes (as kbit/s) and ACL packets a second handed to the controller, from `HCIGETDEVINFO`'s `hci_dev_stats` (`byte_tx`, `acl_tx`, counted by the H5 UART driver as it writes), one ioctl on an unbound HCI socket. This is the codec's real rate, so it also shows LDAC's ABR steps, which bluealsa does not report. It includes L2CAP, AVDTP and RTP headers and H5's framing.
- `wq`: the largest `Wmem` in `/proc/net/l2cap`, the bytes an L2CAP socket has waiting, which is the A2DP socket's (signalling is idle). An L2CAP packet is charged to the socket until `hci_send_frame` orphans it on its way to the driver, and the kernel holds packets only while the controller has no free ACL buffer (`acl_cnt`, returned by Number Of Completed Packets), so `wq` above zero means the controller's buffers (`bufs` of them, `mtu` bytes each) are full: the radio is not getting packets to the headset as fast as the encoder makes them. This is the controller's occupancy without listening to every completion event. bluealsa shrinks the socket's send buffer (`Couldn't set socket output buffer size` in its strings: three packets), so `wq` saturates at a few kB. It is what bluealsa's `TIOCOUTQ` reads for LDAC's ABR, seen from outside. `SIOCOUTQ` itself needs the socket, which only bluealsa and bluetoothd hold.
- `rssi`, `lq`, `tpl`, `afh`: Read RSSI, Read Link Quality, Read Transmit Power Level (current) and Read AFH Channel Map on the ACL handle (`HCIGETCONNLIST`, looked up again each line and written as `h`, with a `LINK` note when it changes: a codec change reconnects the headset on a new handle while the stream runs on, and on 2026-11-18 a handle read only at the START left every reading "-" after the first switch), sent each second on a raw HCI socket bound to hci0 only while a stream runs, filtered to Command Complete (`bt_cmd`, `bt_event`; answers waited for 150 ms at most). For BR/EDR the RSSI is the controller's distance from its golden receive range, in dB (0 inside it, negative below), not an absolute dBm; Link Quality is vendor-defined (Realtek's scale unknown); the transmit power shows power control raising it as the headset moves away; `afh` is how many of the 79 channels adaptive frequency hopping still uses, which falls when Wi-Fi or other 2.4 GHz traffic takes channels. BlueZ's `Device1.RSSI` was not used: it is set only from inquiry results while discovering, which nothing does during playback. `hcitool rssi`, `lq`, `tpl` and `afh` on the Q2 send the same commands, for a check by hand.
- `err`: transmit errors since the last line (`err_tx`).
- `fcc`: Read Failed Contact Counter, the fifth command: packets in a row the controller flushed undelivered when their flush timeout ran out. It counts only on a link with an automatic flush timeout; with none set (the controller's default, infinite) it stays 0 and the controller retries instead, which shows in `done` and `fly`.
- `done`, `fly`: packets a second the controller says it delivered (Number Of Completed Packets, event 0x13, read off the same raw socket, whose filter takes it with Command Complete), and packets in its buffers now: `acl_tx` less the completions since the socket opened, from the least difference seen (`bt_fly_step`: the count at the opening is not known, and the buffers empty whenever the link keeps up). `fly` over `done` is how long a packet waits in the controller: the radio retransmitting, the headset not acknowledging, shows as `done` falling and `fly` at the buffer count (`bufs`) before `wq` grows. The events come about one for each few packets, so about a hundred reads a second on aptX HD.
- `wtx`, `wrx`: wlan0's kB/s each way (`/sys/class/net/wlan0/statistics`). The RTL8733BS is one module for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth ([hardware](hardware.md)): Wi-Fi traffic takes airtime from Bluetooth through the module's coexistence arbitration.
- `cpu`, `ba`, `own`: all cores' busy percent (`/proc/stat`), bluealsa's and q2guard's own CPU in percent of one core (`/proc/PID/stat`, written `ba=9.0`; as a second holds 100 clock ticks it moves in steps of 1.0, and logs written before 2026-11-18 have the tenths, `ba=90`, which `tools/q2bt.py` reads as the same), so a stall from the Q2 not feeding the encoder (the UI, a scan) is told apart from the radio's, and the monitor's own cost is in the log.
- `er`, `ew`: bluealsa's encoder thread, found by the name bluealsa gives it (`ba-a2dp-sbc`, `ba-a2dp-aptx-hd`, ...: `bt_encoder_thread`), in ms a second: on a CPU and waiting for one, from `/proc/PID/task/TID/schedstat` (`bt_schedstat`; with no schedstat in the kernel, `er` from its ticks and `ew` "-"). An encoder on a CPU for most of the second could not keep up; one waiting for a CPU was kept from one; one mostly asleep was waiting, for PCM when the socket had room (`wq` 0) or for room when it had none. The thread ends at a codec change and another, named for the new codec, starts: that is noted at once (`ENCODER`), and bluealsa is asked for the codec then.
- The codec: `dbus-send ... GetPCMs` in the background at the START, when the encoder thread changes and every minute (`BT_PCMS_MS`), its A2DP source PCM's Codec, Sampling and Delay (`bt_pcms`), noted when it changes, as `bt_battery.c`'s loop already asks every 30 s for the rate.

**EDR.** On 2026-11-18 the RTL8733BS (UART H5) and a Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3, both able to use EDR 2 Mbps, were found on multi-slot basic-rate packets: aptX HD's packets of about 778 bytes took 16 slots each, so the link carried at most about 96 a second, 96% of the airtime, with nothing left for a retransmission. The kernel's default packet-type mask (0xcc18) does not forbid EDR, and `hcitool cpt MAC DM1,DM3,DM5,DH1,DH3,DH5` changed nothing; `hcitool cpt EC:66:D1:CF:59:3F DM1,DH1` at 06:15:05Z (Change Connection Packet Type, OGF 1 OCF 0x000F, mask DM1|DH1 = 0x0018 with the EDR "shall not use" bits 0x3306 clear) moved it onto EDR: it then sustained 96 packets a second with 1 or 2 in flight, which DH1-only basic rate cannot carry, and a walk had 6 seconds with a dip in 152, against 19 in 120 before. So the monitor sends that command itself (`bt_edr_step`, the same bytes), once to each ACL handle of the A2DP sink while a stream runs: on the first line once the sink is known, and again on the new handle after a codec change's reconnect. The sink is the device bluealsa streams to, its address read from the path of the `a2dpsrc` PCM in the same `GetPCMs` answer as the codec (`bt_pcms_sink`) and matched in `HCIGETCONNLIST` to a classic ACL link (`bt_acl_handle_of`), so a phone (the Car Remote, or one streaming to the Q2, an `a2dpsnk` PCM) and every LE link are never sent it. On the first stream after boot that is a second or two in, when `GetPCMs` has answered. The raw socket's filter also takes Command Status (0x0F) and Connection Packet Type Changed (0x1D), and `bt_edr_event` notes the outcome in the q2-bt log, `LINK ptype=0x0018 status=0x00 h=2`, or `ptype=-` with the controller's status when it refuses; the first outcome, and any unlike the last, also goes to the unified log (source `bt`, a warning unless it is 0x0018 accepted). A handle is never sent it twice, accepted or refused, so a controller that refuses or a link that does worse is not asked again each second; the record is cleared at a stream's STOP, as a headset that reconnected in a pause may come back on the same handle number, so a refusing controller is asked at most once a stream. There is no setting: it is always on. The saturated line (**Reading it**) says which rate a walk got. ponytail: a codec change's reconnect gets it at the next line, so its first second or so is on whatever the controller chose.

**Not counted in bluealsa.** Stock bluealsa (bluez-alsa 2.x) writes A2DP packets to a blocking socket and waits (`poll` for `POLLOUT`) when it is full; it never drops one, so the socket's queue is where a stall shows, and the PCM FIFO behind it backs up into hciplayer. A counter of those waits would say what `wq` says, at the cost of more hand-assembled MIPS on the audio path ([Bluetooth AAC](#bluetooth-aac)'s patches), so none was added. The PCM side is not counted either: the FIFO from hciplayer could be measured only by opening it (`/proc/PID/fd/N`), which makes the sampler a reader of the pipe and so changes what hciplayer sees when bluealsa closes its end, and hciplayer's blocking in `write` is not told apart from its other waits in anything `/proc` gives; `er` and `ew` with `wq` say which side waited.

**Cost.** Each line is one ioctl, four HCI commands and their answers, and about a dozen small `/proc` and `/sys` reads; the parsing and the line take about 0.7 µs on the build machine (a C loop over `q2bt_core.c`, 2026-11-17), and nothing is read while no stream runs except the one ioctl every 5 s. q2guard runs at `nice -5`, so this is a short burst each second, mostly asleep in `poll`. `own` measures it on the Q2: `tools/q2bt.py`'s summary prints its mean (q2guard's whole process, the heat log's 5 s work and the die temperature's window included) for each codec. With no Bluetooth socket (the emulator) `bt_sleep` tries again a minute later and otherwise sleeps as before. ponytail: `own` has the kernel's 10 ms tick resolution, so a single line reads 0 or 1.0%; only a stream's mean is meaningful. A flush already running when a stream starts or stops takes its note at the next minute's flush, not at once.

**Reading it.** `tools/q2bt.py q2-bt.1 q2-bt.0` (or `-` from `adb exec-out`) cuts each stream into one segment per codec (at an `ENCODER` note, or at a `CODEC` note naming another codec, which can come up to a minute late: then the seconds since the last gap in sending go to the new codec) and prints each with its median rate, every stall with the 10 s before it and which signals moved over them, and a per-codec summary (seconds streamed, link, encoder and source stall seconds, seconds with the socket's queue backed up, median and lowest RSSI, bluealsa's and q2guard's CPU in percent of one core); `--all` prints every second. A second is behind when the controller was handed under 80% of its segment's median: a **link** stall when something waited in the socket (`wq` > 0, the radio's), an **encoder** stall when nothing did and the encoder thread was on a CPU 800 ms of the second or waited 100 ms for one, a **source** stall when nothing did and the encoder slept (the player's PCM late). Each segment logged with `done` and `fly` also gets a **saturated** line: in the seconds the controller held all its ACL buffers (`fly` at `bufs`) the radio was the limit, so the median `done` then is the link's capacity, set against the most basic rate (DH5, DH3, DH1, each with the headset's return slot, in 1,600 slots a second) and EDR 2 Mbps (2-DH5, 2-DH3, 2-DH1) carry for packets of the segment's size (`capacity`, `slots`): at most 10% over basic rate's ceiling says basic rate, past halfway to EDR's says EDR, between them undecided, and under 5 such seconds too few. For aptX HD's packets of about 790 bytes that is 100 a second on basic rate (96 needed: 96% of the airtime) and 160 on EDR (60%); the Q2 has no 3 Mbps. HCI says nothing of the packet type a link uses (the two radios agree it between them), and the host does not forbid EDR (`hciconfig ptype` lists the EDR types only when they may not be used), so this is how a walk tells which one the Q2 and the headset settled on. The reconnect at a codec change (the idle gap and up to 3 slow seconds either side) is a switch, and nothing sent with nothing waiting is idle (a pause), as is a slow second beside one: neither is a stall.

**Capturing an A/B walk** (on a Q2 with this build, from WSL with Windows' `adb.exe -s Q2CODA`, [adb](adb.md)):

1. Check the counters before walking, music playing to the headset: `adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell 'hciconfig hci0 | grep bytes; sleep 2; hciconfig hci0 | grep bytes; cat /proc/net/l2cap; hcitool con'` shows TX bytes growing, an L2CAP table with a `Wmem` column and the ACL link; `adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell 'hcitool rssi MAC; hcitool lq MAC; hcitool afh MAC'` answers for the headset's MAC. A minute into playing, `adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell 'tail -n 3 /mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-bt.0'` shows lines after a START and a CODEC; a field that reads "-" on every line is a signal this Q2 does not give, worth knowing before walking.
2. Note the Q2's clock (`adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell date -u`); the log is in UTC.
3. Walk the route with the first choice (Quality: LDAC Auto, which on the Px7 is aptX HD), Q2 in the pocket for one leg and in hand for another, noting the UTC time of each leg and each break-up heard. Stop the music at the end: the STOP is written to the card within seconds.
4. Change Quality to SBC (an `ENCODER` note marks the change within a second), play, and walk the same route the same way.
5. Pull and read: `adb.exe -s Q2CODA exec-out 'cat /mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-bt.1 /mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-bt.0 2>/dev/null' > walk.log; python3 tools/q2bt.py walk.log`. Match the stalls to the break-ups heard; the heat log (`tools/q2heat.py`) has the busiest processes for the same minutes.

What the walk should settle before Phase 2: whether the heard break-ups are link stalls (and so `wq` is the trigger), which of RSSI, transmit power, AFH and Wi-Fi moved in the seconds before them, how far ahead, and what the monitor cost (`own`).

**The first walk** (2026-11-18, 04:36 to 04:50 UTC, the Px7, `tools/q2bt.py`): SBC (260 kbps) 234 s with no stall and nothing ever queued; aptX HD (614 kbps on the link) 96 s with 10 link-stall seconds and the socket's queue backed up (5.7 to 9.2 kB) in 55 of them, the rate swinging 323 to 723 kbps as the radio fell behind and caught up; no encoder or source stall in either. bluealsa used 1.4% of a core on SBC and 8.9% on aptX HD, the same 8.8 to 9.7% the heat log's `top` shows with the headset beside the Q2, so a backed-up link does not make it spin: it waits in `poll`. The user heard aptX HD break up with distance and SBC not at all. The RSSI and the other HCI readings were lost after the first codec switch (the stale handle above), so how far the signal had fallen is for the next walk.

**The aptX encoder.** bluealsa links libopenaptx 0.2.1 (`/usr/lib/libopenaptx.so.0.2.1`, 21 KB, integer only; SBC is built into bluealsa, AAC is fdk-aac 2.0.2, LDAC Sony's). Run under Unicorn on the shipped library (2026-11-18), it takes 105 M instructions per second of 48 kHz stereo for aptX and 109 M for aptX HD, which at 1.2 GHz is the 9% of a core measured on the Q2. aptX and aptX HD cost the same; aptX HD's extra two bits a sample cost the air 576 kbps against 384, not the CPU. A quarter of the time is the adaptive predictor's 24-tap coefficient update, where the shipped build (GCC, MIPS32r2, using `madd`) moves its 64-bit accumulator in and out of HI/LO on every tap. The same source built with clang 18 for MIPS32r2 encodes bit-identically and takes more (117 M at -O2, 123 M at -O3 with or without unrolling), so no faster build is to be had from flags; a source change keeping the accumulator in HI/LO might save about a tenth, or a SIMD path if the X2000 has one (its `/proc/cpuinfo` ASEs, unread), and either is two to three percent of one core, which nothing in the walk needed. ponytail: measured in instructions, not cycles: HI/LO latency on XBurst II would make the shipped loop slower than its count says, by an amount only a Q2 can show.

**Plan: Phase 2, adapting the rate (not built).** Lower the bit rate when the link is congested or the headset distant, for every headset, not tuned to one. What each codec allows on this stack:

- **SBC**: the bitpool, carried in every frame's header, can change frame to frame within the range the headset accepted (2 to its maximum, usually 53: at 48 kHz joint stereo, 8 subbands and 16 blocks that is about 357 kbps, 35 about 249, 23 about 177), with no renegotiation and no gap. The finest and safest lever; bluealsa's SBC encoder has no runtime setter, so it is a bluealsa patch or a new bluealsa.
- **AAC**: the encoder's bitrate (fdk-aac `AACENC_BITRATE`) can change between frames, 320 to 256, 192, 128 kbps, seamless to the headset; the same bluealsa patch question.
- **LDAC**: Auto already does it (Sony's ABR on queue depth, 990, 660, 492, 396, 330 kbps: [Bluetooth LDAC quality](#bluetooth-ldac-quality)); the fixed Best and Standard could be moved to Auto's controller or stepped with `SetLDACQuality`.
- **aptX and aptX HD**: fixed rates (352 or 384, 529 or 576 kbps) with no lower setting; the only reduction is another codec (aptX HD to aptX, to AAC or SBC), an AVDTP reconfiguration: the stream suspended, closed and opened again, a gap of about a second, and how stock's Quality change performs it (a reconnect or a reconfigure) is to be read in `switchBtPriority` before relying on it.

A policy would read the Phase 1 signals each second in q2guard, or in bluealsa itself where the queue is known exactly: congestion as the share of the last few seconds with `wq` above zero and `kbps` short of the codec's rate, distance as RSSI and transmit power trending toward their limits, interference as `afh` falling with `wtx`/`wrx` busy.
