The policy is `requested && ready && g_last_otgid != 1 && (g_usbdac_chargeflag == 1 || (cable == 1 && g_usbmode == 0))`:
USB DAC Charging On permits charging, as does a detected cable with USB Storage selected.
`g_last_otgid` 1 is the Q2 as a USB host: stock's `check_otg_status` (`0x4f3408`), with the ID pin
(`PD18`) low (and only once [OTG host power](#otg-host-power)'s wait is over), turns the bus power on (`PC20` high) and the charger off (`PE22` high) by writing the
pins directly, and `get_battery_capacity` reads no cable while it lasts. Each USB pass reads `PE22`
back and writes the policy again when the two differ, so without that term the guard turned the
charger back on within the same pass (seen in the emulator with the pins recorded, 2026-11-17:
`PC20=1`, `PE22=1`, then `PE22=0` in the same millisecond), charging the battery from the Q2's own
bus power; Charge Limit's hand-back did the same. `test/fw/test_usb_charge.py` covers both.
An unknown setting, failed enumeration or a timeout never establishes a dedicated charger. With
Audio and DAC selected and charging Off, an unidentified wall charger is therefore inhibited too:
select USB Storage or turn USB DAC Charging On. No charger-type detector or PMIC register changes
are added. Disabling battery charging does not establish zero USB current to the system.

The choice is stock's `g_usbdac_chargeflag`, saved as `PLAYSET USBDAC_CHARGE`. Stock's `config_init`
(`0x504234`) reads it with `toolsReadConfig`'s default `"1"`, keeps 0 or 1 and makes anything else 1,
and only the DAC screen's switch writes it (`!flag`, then `switch_charge_enable(flag)`; the code at
`0x52d454`, inside `airplay_page_init`'s range). A missing key is therefore On, but the
`/release/assets/default/raw/config.ini` that `config_init` copies to `/mnt/data` when there is none
(first boot, a reset) holds `USBDAC_CHARGE=0` in V1.32, V1.34 and V1.36, so a Q2 nobody asked reads
Off, the same line the switch writes for a chosen Off. `ringnav_usb_config` (`dac_default`) settles
it after stock's read: until `Q2POD DACCHARGEOWN` is 1 it sets the flag and the key to 1 and writes
`DACCHARGEOWN=1`; from then on the key is the user's, so a saved Off is kept, and a reset (a new
`config.ini` without the mark) starts On again. ponytail: an Off chosen under 1.8.1 or earlier is
turned On once at the update, as nothing on the Q2 tells it from the factory line; the changelog
says to turn it Off again. A per-device record of the switch would have had to exist before the
update to do better.

**System settings → Power → USB DAC Charging** (`usb_charge_row`, from `ringnav_powermanager` after
Charge Limit, stock's `usb_chargeswitch` icon) is that same flag and key, usable with no cable in.
A toggle flips `g_usbdac_chargeflag`, writes `PLAYSET USBDAC_CHARGE` and calls
`ringnav_usb_charge(!st.charge_held)`: it asks for charging as `charge_poll` hands it back outside
the USB and AirPlay pages (on, unless Charge Limit holds it off), so the policy above applies the
new choice to PE22 at once, an earlier Off request from the DAC screen's switch is replaced, and
Charge Limit's hold still wins. Off only matters with Audio and DAC: USB Storage with a cable in
keeps charging. The DAC screen's switch reads the flag when it builds, and the row reads it again
on the Power window's `EVT_WINDOW_FOREGROUND`, so a change on either shows on the other.

`switch_charge_enable` is guarded (`charge_apply` calls `toolsGpioSetValue` itself). Stock's direct `toolsGpioSetValue("PE22", ...)` writes (`into_poweroff`,
`device_reboot`, `device_standby`, `check_otg_status`) and other GPIOs pass through, so power-off, reboot
and Standby still release the pin for a charge with the Q2 off; the next `ringnav_usb_status` poll
inhibits again. `S90play`'s `rockbox()` sets PE22 low before Rockbox starts, which never drives it. A mutex serializes
the policy and GPIO writes. A caller's disable request remains disabled through detection and
mode reconciliation, so the existing charge-limit hold is not undone by these paths. Detection
rechecks PE22 and corrects a mismatched readback. `ringnav_usb_status` reconciles immediately before
stock gadget dispatch, covering a storage-to-DAC transition without waiting for the next poll.
The stock USB audio descriptors, radio behavior and kernel remain unchanged.

Stock's `systembar_showface` picks `bar_charge` from the cable flag alone while the charger is not Full (and the plain icon once a DAC link is up with charging off, or at Full), so a cable held off by this guard or by Charge Limit showed as charging. `usb_charge_held` is 1 while the last PE22 write was the inhibit; `bar_charging` (navigation.c), which the status bar's battery and the dark bar's key read, is `bar_charge` and not held, and a held cable under 15% shows low. ponytail: the pin's state, not the charger's: a cable too weak to charge still shows charging; `/sys/class/power_supply/battery/status` would tell, but `get_battery_capacity` keeps only 0 to 2 in `g_power_chargestate`, so a Discharging read leaves the last value there.

The four hooks use the pinned V1.36 build's symbol/address and PIC-prologue/GOT checks. Source
changes are exercised by `test/fw/test_usb_charge.py`.

### OTG host power

Stock's `check_otg_status` (`0x4f3408`), called once a second from `on_wm_idle_status` (its only caller, `0x4f43dc`), reads the ID pin `PD18` with `toolsGpioGetValue`; when its role `PD18 == 0` differs from `g_last_otgid` it writes `PC20` (bus power, 1 on) and `PE22` (charger, 1 off) to that role and stores it, then on a host pass follows a USB DAC through `/tmp/usb_add` and `/dev/snd/pcmC1D0` (`g_otg_status`). Nothing else in demo writes `PC20` high: `into_poweroff`, `device_reboot` and `device_standby` write it 0 with `g_last_otgid`. `get_battery_capacity` reads no cable (`g_usbdet_value` 0) while `g_last_otgid` is 1, and the dwc2 controller follows the same pin (`13500000.otg/id_status`). The cable sense `PD17` (`usb_detect`: 0 is VBUS on the port) reads the Q2's own bus power as well as a computer's.

A pin log on the Q2 (2026-11-17, build p32b, every 0.5 s) showed the fault: after each unplug `PD18` read 0 with no cable in, stock turned `PC20` on in the next pass (within 0.53 s every time), and `PD18` stayed low for 5 to 19 s. A cable put into a computer in that window met the Q2 powering the bus: `PC20=1` with VBUS on, the battery Discharging, nothing enumerated, until `PD18` read high (dwc2: "Do port resume before switching to device mode") and stock turned `PC20` off in its next pass. Plugs that worked were those made after `PD18` was back to 1.

**The ID pin floats.** The port D registers (read on the Q2, 2026-11-17; offsets from the X2000 GPIO map: `INT` 0x10, `MSK` 0x20, `PAT1` 0x30, `PAT0` 0x40, `EDG` 0x70, `PEPU` 0x80 pull-up, `PEPD` 0x90 pull-down) have `PD18` as a GPIO input with neither pull (`PEPU` `0xC7F83F3F`, bit 18 clear; `PEPD` 0). `PD17`'s bits read as `usb_event.c`'s both-edge request asks (`INT` 1, `EDG` 1), which places 0x70 as `EDG` and the map as the X2000's. The kernel's built-in device tree lists `PD16` to `PD19` under `gpd`'s `ingenic,gpio-sleep-pullup`, a pull-up during Standby only; nothing pulls `PD18` up awake, and `cmd_gpio get_func PD18` read `input pull_hiz`. `S12usbcharge` (`patch/usb_charge.sh`) runs `cmd_gpio set_func PD18 input pull_up` at boot (`soc_gpio.ko` offers `pull_up`, `pull_down`, `pull_hiz`); `cmd_gpio get_func PD18` then reads `input pull_up` and `PEPU` `0xC7FC3F3F`. That did not last: demo's `platform_init` (`0x51cd94`, from `application_init`) sets the USB pins up after `config_init` with `toolsGpioInput(name, pull)` (`0x5d1cdc`: `gpio_set_func` with `input` and `pull_down` for 1, `pull_up` for 2, `pull_hiz` otherwise), and gives `PD18` 0, so a build with only the S12 line read `input pull_hiz` 34 s after boot (2026-11-17 22:36). `ID_PULL_UP` (`tools/build.py`) turns that call's `move $a1, $zero` (`0x51d33c`) into `li $a1, 2`, so stock's own call sets `input pull_up`; `test/build.py` checks the word in the built demo. A Standby and wake kept it, and `usb_record_wake` sets it again at every wake (from `ringnav_standby`, as `toolsIntoStandby` returns) all the same. With it on, 4 of 5 quick replugs into a computer enumerated at once with `PD18` high throughout, about half before.

**The line is still driven low.** With both pull-ups on and nothing attached, `PD18` goes low once, for 2.1 to 4.3 s, starting 2.7 to 11.8 s after VBUS leaves the port, the Q2's own bus power ending included (`q2-pull-state.log` 21:0x, every 0.5 s; `q2-ab-state.log` 22:43, every 0.25 s); there is no free-running cycle, so something on the board crosses a threshold as the VBUS net discharges. The Q2's port is USB-C with no ID contact, the role logic is not identified (no Type-C controller is on any I2C bus: only the CW2015, two Hynitron touch parts, the CS43131 and the AXP2101), and nothing in demo, the device tree or the init scripts touches a role or mode pin: demo's GPIO names in port D are `PD17`, `PD18`, `PD20` and `PD22` to `PD26`, and the kernel's dwc2 has `usb_role_switch` code but the device tree gives no `usb-role-switch`, and its `connected`, `dwc2_mode` and `id_status` attributes are read-only (mode 0444, no store). A USB-C laptop will not attach as a source onto a live VBUS, so a cable put in while the Q2 powered the bus enumerated nothing; and on 22:43 a 6 s settle alone made a loop into an empty port: the pulse let stock power the bus, the bus power's end was another VBUS removal, and the next pulse 7 s on powered it again.

`ringnav_otg_status` (`patch/usb_otg.c`) hooks `check_otg_status`. In device role (`g_last_otgid` not 1) a high ID runs stock's pass as before (its device path ends a DAC's output). A low ID read within `OTG_BLANK_MS` (15 s) of VBUS leaving the port (`PD17` going high, or the bus power ending) is ignored until it reads high again; any other low runs stock's pass only once `PD18` has read 0 and `PD17` 1 on every pass for `OTG_SETTLE_MS` (6 s). VBUS on the port, a high ID, or passes more than `OTG_GAP_MS` (5 s) apart (a Standby) start the wait again. The bus power is a trial: with nothing on the host port (`/sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1`) `OTG_TRIAL_MS` (8 s) after it came on, `ringnav_otg_status` writes `PC20` and `PE22` 0 and `g_last_otgid` 0 as stock's device pass would (the charge guard then sets `PE22` its own way), records `otg-trial-off`, and tries no more until a cable's VBUS is seen with the bus power off or the Q2 wakes from Standby. In host role stock runs every pass and turns `PC20` off in the pass `PD18` reads high. The X2000's CPM is also held: `USBPCR` (`0x1000003c`) bit 29, the PHY's ID pull-up always on, and `USBRDT` (`0x10000040`) bits 24 and 23, the controller's ID from its register set to device (`otg_hold`, busybox `devmem` read-modify-writes as tested on the Q2 2026-11-17: `id_status` and `GOTGCTL`'s ConIDSts stayed device through a pulse), at boot after `platform_init`, at every wake (the PHY's init writes `USBPCR` again) and whenever the bus power ends; bits 24 and 23 are cleared just before stock's pass is let through, so a real adapter's device enumerates. A USB DAC or drive on an OTG adapter gets bus power about 6 s after it goes in, or 6 s into boot. `test/fw/test_usb_otg.py` replays the logged sequences over a model of stock's pass and the pins: the p32b unplug-replugs, the floating lows, the pull-up's pulses and the 22:43 pulse never power the bus, the 22:43 pulse under the settle alone does, a trial with nothing enumerated ends and is not repeated until a cable, and the adapter's path keeps its power while a device is on the host port. `test/build.py` runs `S12usbcharge` with a stand-in `cmd_gpio` and checks `ID_PULL_UP` in the built demo.

ponytail: an OTG adapter put in within 15 s of unplugging a cable is taken for the board's pulse until it is put in again; an adapter whose device does not enumerate within 8 s (or an empty one) loses its power until a cable is plugged in or the Q2 sleeps and wakes; a DAC unplugged from the adapter leaves the empty adapter powered; and a power-only accessory on an adapter never enumerates, so it gets 8 s of power. An OTG power option (Auto, Always) would lift the last. The [USB record](#usb-record) shows each trial's end. The hook uses the pinned V1.36 PIC-prologue/GOT check.

### USB record

`patch/usb_record.c` writes a line to the card's `.q2pod/q2-usb.log` (moved to `q2-usb.1.log` at 128 KB) at each start (`boot`, from `ringnav_platform_init`, `platform_init`'s hook, once stock has set the pins up), for each cable edge (`usb_ui_status`: `in`, `out`), the same 5 s later (`in+5s`, `out+5s`, from `usb_ui_poll`), each change of OTG bus power (`otg-on`, `otg-off`, around stock's pass in `ringnav_otg_status`), and each Standby (`standby` just before `toolsIntoStandby`, `wake` as it returns and `wake+5s`, all from `ringnav_standby`; the card is unmounted by then, so these wait in the ring): the wall time and demo's millisecond clock, `PD18`, `PD17`, `PD19` (an input with a pull-up beside them that stock never reads, in case it is the role chip's), `PC20`, `PE22`, `g_last_otgid`, the dwc2's `id_status`, `dwc2_mode` and `connected`, `power_supply/usb/online`, the UDC's state and whether a device is on the host port (`/sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1/idVendor`). `boot` and `wake+5s` also run `cmd_gpio get_func PD18` (into `/tmp/q2-pd18.func`) and end with its answer (`pull=input_pull_up`); one that is not the pull-up is set again and the line's word is `boot-pull-off` or `wake+5s-pull-off`. With the card away lines are held in a 4 KB ring (`card_store.c`'s log), and `usb_record_poll` tries to put them on the card every 5 s (`USB_FLUSH_MS`), so the `boot` line is there soon after the card mounts, not only at the next event. `tools/q2usb.py` reads the two files and flags `BACKFEED` (bus power on with VBUS or a computer's answer seen, or a computer within 3 s of it going off), `EMPTY` (bus power with nothing enumerated), `NOENUM` (a plug not enumerated 5 s on: a charger, or a plug that failed) `IDLOW` (the ID low 5 s after an unplug) `PULLOFF` (a `-pull-off` line) and `WAKEDROP` (a link up at `standby` that is not 5 s after the wake, or the controller in host role at the wake).

Each line also goes to the [unified log](#unified-log) as a `usb` line from its event word on (`ulog`), so it sits in time with the rest; the record's own file stays as it is, for `tools/q2usb.py`.

**At a wake.** `device_standby` (`0x5021bc`) writes `PC20` 0, `PE22` and `g_last_otgid` 0, unmounts the card and USB drive, removes the Wi-Fi and card modules, and calls `toolsIntoStandby` (`0x5d1110`: `mem` to `/sys/power/state`), which returns at the wake; the rest of `device_standby` brings them back and never calls `check_otg_status`, which runs again on the next status pass. The bus power therefore comes back only through `ringnav_otg_status`'s wait, and a computer's VBUS on the cable stops that. The controller's role at the wake is the kernel's: on 2026-11-17 21:27 a wake on a laptop logged `dwc2 13500000.otg: Do port resume before switching to device mode` and the link dropped and came back as a new address (the dwc2 had resumed in host role, so the ID read low as it woke), while a wake at 20:45 kept the link. demo cannot hold the dwc2's role: its `dwc2_mode` and `id_status` attributes are read-only and the device tree gives no role switch. The `standby`, `wake` and `wake+5s` lines record the ID, the controller and the link either side, so the next one shows whether the role chip's ID pulse, not demo, causes it.

## Battery History

**System settings → Power → Battery History** (`patch/battery.c`; the row after In-Vehicle Mode, `ringnav_powermanager`). `charge_poll` hands `battery_tick` the level (`g_power_capacity`) and the cable (`g_usbdet_value`) every `CHARGE_POLL_MS`, screen on or off, so no thread or timer of its own. With the cable out, a level below the last row's is a new row (the time from `wall_time` and the level); the first poll after the cable comes out, or after a boot without it, starts a new history with one row. A level more than `BH_REBOUND` (3) over the last row's also starts again: the Q2 charged while powered off, which demo never saw. A level of 0 or over 100 (not read yet) is ignored. Within a history the level only falls, from 100 at most to 1, so `BH_ROWS` (100) rows always hold it: the record is a fixed 808 bytes, the card's `.q2pod/q2-battery`, written whole (temp, fsync, rename) once a row through `card_store.c` ([Where Q2 Muse writes](#where-q2-muse-writes)): with the card away the rows are kept in RAM and written at the next tick it is back, and the flash's `/mnt/data/q2-battery` from earlier releases is read until then, so the flash is never written. At the first tick or page open it is read once; one that is short, of another layout (`BH_MAGIC`), with more rows than it holds, or whose levels don't fall row by row is dropped and the next tick starts again. Standby is a suspend to RAM and `charge_poll` runs only in the UI loop, so a drop during Standby is one row at the wake (stamped then), and the graph steps there. ponytail: a charge of 3% or less while powered off reads as the same history, and a gauge jump of more than 3 points up while unplugged restarts the record; revisit if a lost history is reported.

The page (`battery_page`, `CTX_DYNAMIC`; 33 v3, [oled-design](oled-design.md#battery-history)) is a graph over the whole page: `page_list` with one row only titles the status row (the list stays hidden) and a view below it is the graph's, which `battery_paint`, from `ringnav_paint`, fills: the reading the wheel is on (`bh_readout`: `Nov 16, 3:10 PM · 51%`, the status bar's 12- or 24-hour form), faint lines at 100 and 50% and the axis at 0% labelled in 15 px Text Tertiary, the level as steps from the start to now in the accent's light tone over a faint fill, through `ui_ink`, so it follows the theme and Light Mode, the reading's hairline and dot, and **Export Log**, the shared gray `ui_button`. The x axis is time up to now; if the times don't run forward on one clock (set or lost mid-history, `CLOCK_SET`) the rows are spaced evenly instead, and a now on the other side of `CLOCK_SET` from the rows ends the axis at the last row. A time before `CLOCK_SET` (September 2020, scrobbling's test) is a clock never set: such a reading reads as hours and minutes since the start, `+1:15 · 97%`. The wheel moves along the readings (`battery_key`, from `ringnav` before the lists: clockwise to the newer, held at either end), and the newest stays the reading as rows join unless the wheel left it on an older one; Center and a tap on the button export, so the button is the page's only action and never wears the focus ring. **Export Log** writes the rows to `/mnt/mmc/battery-log.txt`, each day's date (`11 Nov 2026`) over its rows as `99% | 12:00`, or a `Clock not set` line first, whole through `blob_io`'s temp and rename; not while `usbmode_page` is open (the card is a computer's), without the card mounted, or with under 1 MB free, each with a toast. The toasts show in the button's place, so the button gives way while another window is on top. While the page is open each new row repaints it (`widget_invalidate_force`); nothing is built again.

<a id="usb-pages"></a>
## USB pages

What a cable into a computer shows (`patch/usb_ui.c`, the look in [oled-design](oled-design.md#usb)). Stock starts a gadget the moment a cable is in (`check_usb_status`, hooked as `ringnav_usb_status` in `usb_charge.c`, which calls `usb_ui_status` around it) and, once a computer configures it, opens `usbmode_page` in the mode Quick Settings' USB tile last chose. A cable in with no remembered choice keeps stock out (`g_usblink_status` 3, which stock's next pass leaves alone until the cable is out) and starts stock's storage gadget with no card in it, only to learn whether a computer answers: one that configures it within `USB_PROBE_MS` (3 s) gets the chooser, "Use USB For" (Charge Only, Transfer Files, USB Audio and, in a `--dev` build, USB Debugging) and Always Do This; nothing answering is a charger (`usb_charger_in`, [Charging](#charging)'s toast). Transfer Files and USB Audio hand back to stock (`g_usbmode` for this cable, `g_usblink_status` 0), whose `usbmode_page` is drawn as a mode page: a solid circle and its glyph, a title, a line and Stop, the gray button ringed under the focus rule (Center, as Return, leaves the mode). Charge Only stops the probe; USB Debugging stops it too, which in a `--dev` build hands the controller back to the ADB gadget ([adb](adb.md)), and opens its own mode page, whose Stop parks that gadget. In a `--dev` build with the ADB gadget already on the controller, that gadget is the probe and nothing is stopped. When the cable is seen, and the probe's gadget's stop at a cable out, are in [USB cable events](#usb-cable-events). A remembered choice (`Q2POD USBPICK`, saved by Always Do This) skips the chooser, Transfer Files and USB Audio in their own mode for the cable, and holds until a mode page's Stop (Center) forgets it (`usb_forget`, back to asking); Return only leaves. The saved mode (`USBPICKMODE` in older builds) no longer drops it. **The USB picker** (`usb_pick_open`, `usbpick_page`, CHOICE in `contexts.inc`) is opened by Settings > General's USB row (`usb_ui_row` from `ringnav_systemset`, its value `usb_ui_value`, written again on every change while the row is there) and by Control Center's USB row while a cable is in (`usb_ui_cable`, `g_usbdet_value` 1): Ask Every Time, Transfer Files, USB Audio, Charge Only and, in a `--dev` build, USB Debugging, the remembered choice carrying stock's `select` image (the theme's check) and its note painted in a footer view under the rows (`usb_pick_paint`). A pick is remembered through the one path the chooser's Always Do This takes (`usb_remember`, which `usb_apply` calls: `USBPICK`, and for Transfer Files and USB Audio stock's `SYSSET USBMODE`); Ask Every Time writes `USBPICK` 0 (`usb_forget`). With no cable in nothing else changes, so a link stock's mode-exit prompt still holds is left alone. With a cable in the cable takes the pick at once (`usb_switch`): what it had is let go first, stock's mode by force-closing `usbmode_page`, whose `EVT_WINDOW_CLOSE` runs stock's `usbmode_exit` (bound by `usbmode_page_init` through `0x542ad0`; it stops the gadget, mounts the card again and sets `g_usblink_status` 3 itself, `0x542918`; `window_manager_close_window_force` reaches the default window manager's forced close, vtable `0x9b42b0` + `0x30` = `0x69c460`, which dispatches that event at `0x69c558`), a stock gadget still waiting for a computer by holding the link and stopping its script, USB Debugging's page by closing it and parking its gadget for Charge Only; then `usb_apply`, and USB Debugging runs `q2adb-gadget unpark`, as a stop of stock's gadget may have left it parked. `usbmode_page` gone by any path leaves the cable charging only (`usb_mode_gone`: `u.choice` Charge Only). Leaving Transfer Files while its page is up and the computer has not ejected the card asks first on the confirmation card (`usb_pick_answer`), so a copy in progress is not cut off unasked. Toasts: Unplugged, OK to Disconnect (the computer's eject while the mode page is not on top, `usb_ui_ejected` from `usb_poll`) and USB Audio Ready. In a `--dev` build adbd's question about an unknown computer ([adb](adb.md#authorization)) is "Allow USB Debugging?" on the confirmation card (`auth_open`, `auth_card_answer`): the key's fingerprint, the switch row Always Allow, Cancel and Allow.

<a id="usb-cable-events"></a>
## USB cable events

A plug-in or unplug is acted on in the UI pass after it happens (`patch/usb_event.c`), not stock's next second or two. Stock reads the cable from GPIO `PD17` (low while VBUS is in) in `usb_detect` (`0x4ff220`), called only from `get_battery_capacity` (`0x4ff258`), which only `systembar_showface` calls, on the status bar's 1000 ms timer (`systembar_timer_start`, `0x541f2c`); `on_wm_idle_status` then runs `check_usb_status` only on a pass where `toolsstimer` (`time(NULL)`) has moved to a new second. Up to two seconds passed between the cable and anything reacting, and a cable out and back in within that time was never seen at all. `usb_event_start`, from the first `usb_ui_poll`, asks the kernel's GPIO character device for both edges of line 17 of `/dev/gpiochip3` (GPD, base 96; `GPIO_GET_LINEEVENT_IOCTL`; PD17 is a plain input that no driver holds, its interrupt bit clear in GPD's `INT` register) and starts a thread that blocks on the line's file. Each edge is read with the kernel's timestamp (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), the contacts' bounce slept off (`USB_SETTLE_MS`, 20 ms), the burst's other edges drained, and a count bumped (`usb_event_wait`). `usb_ui_poll`, every UI pass (`ringnav_sleep`), takes a new count (`usb_event_take`) and runs stock's own read, `get_battery_capacity` (which sets `g_usbdet_value` and resets the power-off timers as its timer would), then `ringnav_usb_status`, so `usb_ui_status` and stock's `check_usb_status` see the cable in that pass. The read stays stock's (`/dev/gpio` through `toolsGpioGetValue`), so the event only decides when; stock's timer and second-gated check stay as the fallback, alone if the line cannot be requested. demo's log gets a line per change: `q2 usb: cable in, seen after its edge, N ms` (or `out`), `(stock's once-a-second read)` when the timer saw it first, then `a computer answered the probe after the plug, N ms` or `no computer answered: a charger`. While the probe waits, `usb_ui_poll` reads the UDC's state every `USB_PROBE_LOOK_MS` (100 ms), so the chooser follows the computer's answer, not stock's next second. A cable out stops the probe's storage gadget whether it still waited or its chooser was up unanswered (`usb_probe_stop`, `probe_up`): left running, it kept configfs mounted and the ADB gadget parked, and the next cable's `storage_config.sh start` failed ("usb configfs already mounted"), seen on a Q2 on 2026-11-16 as replugs the Q2 did not react to. In a `--dev` build the ADB gadget, when it is on the controller (`/sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/q2adb/UDC` set), is itself the probe: a computer sees one device at the plug, and USB Debugging or Charge Only keep it; Transfer Files and USB Audio swap in stock's gadget as before ([adb](adb.md#the-usb-gadget)). Each burst also ends the UI loop's idle (`loop_wake`, [The UI loop's wait](#the-ui-loops-wait)), so a plug-in is seen on the pass it starts, dark or lit. `test/fw/test_usb_ui.py` covers the burst, the pass that acts on it, the probe's look and the unplug's stop.

`PD17` also reads low while the Q2 itself powers the bus as an OTG host (`PC20` high), so an edge then is the Q2's own power, not a cable. After an unplug the ID pin `PD18` can read low for seconds; [OTG host power](#otg-host-power) keeps the bus power off until it has settled low with `PD17` high and ignores a low read within 15 s of VBUS leaving, so a cable put back into a computer in that time is a device's, not met by the Q2's 5 V.

## Save Diagnostics

A `--dev` build's Settings > General > About starts with a **Save Diagnostics** row, first so it is in sight as the page opens (`patch/diagnostics.c`, added by `ringnav_about`; `about_rows` in `settings_pages.c` leaves its click alone while the table's other rows get `about_click`, which does nothing). Center or a tap runs one shell command (`diag_script`) that writes `/mnt/mmc/q2-diagnostics.txt` beside itself as `.tmp` and moves it into place, then syncs, so a device problem can be read from the card on a computer with no shell open: the build's version (`Q2POD_VERSION`), `date` and `/proc/uptime`, each `/sys/class/udc/*/state`, each configfs gadget under `/sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget` with its `UDC`, its functions, the functions its configs link and a storage function's LUN file, the configfs, FunctionFS and card lines of `/proc/mounts`, both battery gauges (the CW2015's `cw2015_capacity` and `cw2015_voltage`, which the firmware reads, and the AXP2101 supply's unused `capacity` and `voltage_now`: [hardware](hardware.md)), `ps`, `dmesg`'s last 300 lines, and the last 100 of `/tmp/q2-demo.err` and 300 of `/tmp/q2-demo.log`, where demo writes and q2player, which demo starts, writes too. It reads no `config.ini`, Wi-Fi setting or key and lists nothing on the card. Each save replaces the last. With no card in `/proc/mounts` the command writes nothing and exits 2. A toast says where it went ("Saved to SD card: q2-diagnostics.txt"), "No SD card", or "Couldn't save diagnostics". A release build has no row: `Q2POD_DEV` 0 leaves `diag_about_row` empty, and the compiler drops the rest.

## First boot

**Q2 Muse's defaults, once.** A Q2 flashed with this release, from stock or from any earlier q2-coda build, starts on Q2 Muse's own settings, none of the old ones kept (the user's, 2026-11-15: a Q2 kept stock's Enlarged Album Art on after flashing). S90play's start (`BOOT_HOOK` in `tools/build.py`) checks for `/mnt/data/q2-defaults` (`DEFAULTS_MARK`) before demo starts; without it, it copies the config a reset copies (`/release/assets/default/raw/config.ini`, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, every section: PLAYSET, SYSSET, Q2POD, IPOD and the rest) over `/mnt/data/config.ini` through a `.new` file, synced and renamed, then writes the mark. With the mark there, a later update keeps the user's settings. The build adds one section to that file, `[IPOD]` with `KEEPLIT=1` (`DEFAULT_IPOD`), so Smart Awake starts on, as a missing key reads too. Only `config.ini` is replaced: saved Wi-Fi networks (`wpa_supplicant.conf`), Bluetooth pairings, the library's database and ratings are other files and stay. `test/build.py` runs it under the host's sh: the first boot puts the defaults in place and keeps the Wi-Fi file, the next keeps a changed setting.

Stock's `config_init` (`0x503d0c`) reads `SYSSET LANGUAGE` (`0x5047f8`); missing, it sets `g_guideflag` and the first boot opens stock's language guide (`guide_page`), where Q2 Muse's wheel and Center are off (`usable()` in `patch/navigation.c`). The `config.ini` that a first boot or a reset copies to `/mnt/data` has no such key, so every reset went through the guide. Q2 Muse is English only (Settings has no Language row), so the build writes `LANGUAGE=2`, English, at the top of that file's `SYSSET` (`default_config`, `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE` in `tools/build.py`) and the first boot lands on Home. A `config.ini` already on `/mnt/data` is left as it is.

<a id="config-ini"></a>
## config.ini

The `config.ini` stock copies to `/mnt/data` at first boot or a reset ends on `NAVHIDE=0` with no newline, and stock's `toolsWriteConfig` (`0x5d0284`) appends a section it does not find as `"[%s]\n%s=%s\n"` at the file's end. So the first section written after a reset ran on from that line: `NAVHIDE=0[Q2POD]`, from `usb_charge.c`'s `DACCHARGEOWN` early in `config_init`. `toolsReadConfig` takes a section only at a line's start, so neither it nor its keys were ever read: `synclink.c`'s `SYNCLINKOWN` a moment later appended a second `[Q2POD]`, and the next boot found no `DACCHARGEOWN`, set USB DAC charging On again and wrote the key into the second copy, so an Off chosen in the first session after a reset was lost once (seen in the emulator from a clean `config.ini`). Both of stock's functions take a key's first line in any section of that name, so a file with the section twice still reads. `toolsWriteConfig` is hooked (`ringnav_ini_write`, `patch/config_ini.c`): before stock writes, the file is read whole (up to 16 KB; a larger one is left alone), a line not starting with `[` that ends in `[Q2POD]` or `[IPOD]`, the two sections the payload adds, is split before the header, every line gets its newline, and under a header so split a key that a later section of the same name also holds is dropped, since the later line is the one stock has been reading and writing; a key only the split section holds comes back. A file that changes is written to `config.ini.tmp`, synced and renamed over it (`peq_save_file`); a sound file is only read. ponytail: a value that itself ends in `[Q2POD]` or `[IPOD]` would be split too; no key the payload or stock writes holds one, and telling the two apart would need the file's history. A split section whose every key was dropped stays as an empty header, which both functions pass over.

## Where Q2 Muse writes

The Q2's built-in storage (`/mnt/data`, UBIFS on raw NAND) wears with every write, and a synced write of a few bytes still rewrites at least a page and the index above it. Q2 Muse writes there only what the Q2 needs to boot with no card: anything written often and of use only with the card in (it is about the card's songs, or it is a history) lives on the card, in `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod`, through `patch/card_store.c`; and the settings a wheel steps are written once they settle.

**`card_store.c`.** A *blob* is a file written whole (temp, fsync, rename) to the card. With the card away (out, or lent to a computer as USB storage: `card_mounted` reads `/proc/mounts`), a write keeps the newest copy in RAM, bounded by the blob's cap, reads return it, and `card_blob_flush`, called from the record's own poll, writes it once the card is back. A mounted card that refuses a write is reported to the caller, which retries as it did on the flash. A blob names the flash file it replaces: while the card has no copy that file is read (so a Q2 that boots with no card still has its history), and the first read with the card in copies it there; the flash file is left as it was and never written again. Dropping a blob leaves the card's file empty, which reads as none, so the old flash copy is not read again. A *log* is appended to; with the card away its lines go to a RAM ring (the oldest whole lines dropped to fit, counted), appended to the card in order before the next line once it is back, after a line saying how many were lost. Only stdio, `rename`, `mkdir` and the heap, so a separate program (the heat recorder's `q2guard`) can link it with its own `card_mounted`.

**Settled settings.** `config.ini` is rewritten whole (about 1.5 KB) by stock's `toolsWriteConfig` for every key saved, and a wheel turn on the volume saved one per step. `write_int_config`'s hook (`ringnav_write_config`) holds the keys a wheel steps, `PLAYSET VOLUME`, `BT_VOLUME`, `MAXVOLUME`, `BOOTVOLUME`, `BALANCE`, `SYSSET LIGHTNESS`, `Q2POD AIRVOL` and `XFADESEC` (`config_hold`, `patch/config_ini.c`), and `power_poll` writes each `CONFIG_SETTLE_MS` (3 s) after its last change (`config_settle`), so a turn is one write. Stock's own volume dialog saves through the same hook, so its steps settle too. What is held is written at once before the payload reads one of them back (`config_value`, `ringnav_output`'s read of the other output's level), at Standby and at a clean end (power-off, Restart, an update, Rockbox). ponytail: a forced restart or a flat battery within 3 s of the last step loses that step, the value before it coming back at boot; and a stock reader of these keys between a step and its write (none is known: stock reads them at `config_init`) would read the one before.

| File | Holds | Written | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config.ini`, wheel-stepped keys | volume, limits, balance, brightness, crossfade length | 3 s after the last step | flash, settled |
| `config.ini`, other keys | settings | once per change | flash (boot reads it) |
| `.q2pod/ringnav-queue`, `-elapsed` | the queue snapshot and its second | each track change; every 30 s playing | card |
| `.q2pod/ringnav-resume` | long tracks' places | every 60 s on a long track, a pause, a track change | card |
| `.q2pod/ringnav-plays` | play counts | each counted play | card |
| `.q2pod/q2-battery` | Battery History | each percent fallen | card |
| `.q2muse/logs/q2-log.0` to `.3` | the [unified log](#unified-log) | batched: every 1 to 5 min, at once on an error, a warning, a snapshot | card (RAM while it is away) |
| `.q2pod/q2-usb.log`, `.1.log` | the [USB record](#usb-record) | each cable edge, 5 s after it, each OTG power change | card |
| `q2-state` | the [state record](#watchdog) | a change once it has held 5 s (a burst is one write); a run's first line and Standby's at once | flash: it must outlive a forced restart before the card is mounted |
| `q2-stall`, `q2-cf-trace` | a stall's, a cold Cover Flow open's record | only on a stall or a cold open | flash, for the same reason |
| ratings, sorts, library and Home order, games, EQ presets, Car Remote pairings, `adb_keys`, `boot-target`, the boot logo, Wi-Fi networks | user data and what boot needs | once per deliberate change | flash |

Stock's own writes are its to make: its settings pages' `config.ini` keys, Memory Playback's record at power-off, `database.db` on a library update, `wpa_supplicant.conf` and Bluetooth pairings.

## SyncLink

SyncLink is Shanling's phone remote for its Eddict Player app: a nearby phone browses the library, plays, changes settings, reads and sets the Wi-Fi network's name and password, and starts an over-the-air update. None of its listeners asks for a password: on Wi-Fi, `responseLogin` (`0x5ada40`), the handler of its login message, answers any caller and marks the session logged in. q2-coda keeps it off unless the user turns it on (`patch/synclink.c`). It cannot be removed: demo needs `libSL.so` (Bluetooth RFCOMM and LE GATT), `libWL.so` (Wi-Fi) and `libprotobuf-lite.so.15` to load, and the message handlers are demo's own code.

**One switch.** Stock's **Wireless → SyncLink** page, no longer reached from Settings (stock's page, `systemset_synclink_page_init`, `0x4d2df4`) is **Off**, **Bluetooth** or **Wi-Fi**: `g_synclinkflag` (`0xa4cbad`) 0, 1 or 2, saved as `SYSSET SYNCLINK`, which `config_init` reads at boot (`0x5049c0`, anything over 2 read as 0) and nothing else writes; the default `config.ini` stock copies in at first boot or a reset says `SYNCLINK=0`. Every start of a listener is stock's, behind that byte:

- Bluetooth: `start_btsynclink` (`0x527990`, `startSyncLink`: `BS_startRfcommServer` and `BLE_startServer`, and `btctl_set_synclink` for bluetoothd's own SyncLink mode) from `checkBluetoothStatus` (`0x4fd558`) only at 1; `addMessage`'s restarts after a phone leaves (`0x523638` on) at 1 (one LE restart at 1 or 2), and `synclink_mainscheduling`'s LE restart at 1.
- Wi-Fi: `synclink_mainscheduling` (`0x527a70`) calls `startWifiSyncLink` (`WSL_startServer(1751, "Shanling Q2(<mac>)", serial)`: the TCP listener on port 1751, a UDP socket on 1751 and the multicast group `239.250.255.225` that answers discovery as `shanling_synclink`) only at 2, with the Wi-Fi switch on and the network connected, and stops it when the link drops. Connecting to a network starts nothing by itself: `wifi_action_connect` and the other Wi-Fi actions only stop it (`stop_wifisynclink`) at 1 or 2.
- The page: choosing Bluetooth or Wi-Fi stops the other, sets the byte, saves it and starts the one chosen (`0x4d2754`); Off stops both.

`initSyncLink` (`platform_init`, after `config_init`) only makes the three transports' objects and their event loops; in the emulator it opens no network socket.

**Off on upgrade.** A Q2 that had SyncLink on keeps it on through a firmware update, since `/mnt/data` is kept. `synclink_default`, from `config_init`'s hook (`ringnav_usb_config`, `patch/usb_charge.c`) before `platform_init` goes on to Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and `initSyncLink`, turns it off once: until `Q2POD SYNCLINKOWN` is 1 it sets `g_synclinkflag` 0, saves `SYNCLINK=0` if it was on, and writes the mark. After that `SYNCLINK` is the user's, and a choice made on the page stays, as `Q2POD DACCHARGEOWN` does for [the DAC's charging](#early-usb-dac-charging-guard). ponytail: a SyncLink the user turned on on purpose before this firmware goes off once too; the changelog says so, as no file tells the two apart.

**Retired.** SyncLink has no row Settings leads to: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are Settings' own rows, so stock's Wireless page, which held SyncLink's, is not reached (the user's, 2026-11-15), and its listeners stay off after the one-time off above. Its caption under the row went with it.

**What off costs.** Eddict Player can't reach the Q2, and its over-the-air update with it; **Network Update** on the Q2 is separate and works. Nothing else needs it: AirPlay (`shairport`), DLNA (`libdmr.so`), USB DAC, Bluetooth output to headphones or a car, and the Q2's own settings never call SyncLink. SyncLink over Wi-Fi is one of [Smart Wi-Fi](#smart-wi-fi)'s reasons to keep the radio up, so off also lets the radio sleep sooner. Its Bluetooth mode changes how bluetoothd answers AVRCP and AVDTP (`g_synclink_mode` in bluetoothd's `avctp.c`, which logs `"AVCTP: SyncLink Mode | disconnect connect from %s"` and takes another branch on an incoming control link), so with it on a car's track buttons and metadata may stop while the audio plays on; read from the code, not seen on a device.

`test/fw/test_synclink.py` boots `config_init`'s hook with each saved choice (on before the mark, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi: off; on after it: kept; never on: only the mark) and lays out the Wireless list with its caption. In the emulator (a --dev build, the network connected), stock's `SYNCLINK=2` from older firmware opened TCP 1751, UDP 1751 and the multicast group; after `synclink_default` none is open after boot or after the network connects, and choosing Wi-Fi on the page opens all three.

## Smart Wi-Fi

**System settings → Power → Smart Wi-Fi** (`Q2POD SMARTWIFI`, off by default; the row after Charge Limit). With it on and the user's Wi-Fi switch on, `smart_poll` (from `power_poll`, every `SMART_POLL_MS`, 1 s) turns the radio off once nothing has needed the network for `SMART_IDLE_MS` (5 min), and back on as soon as something does. An associated radio with nothing to do still keeps its SDIO bus busy (about 90 interrupts a second at a few packets a minute, measured with local FLAC and the screen off, before 1.3.0's power save), so local listening pays for a link it never uses.

Both directions go through stock's own switch, `wifi_switch` (`0x5191b8`), as Quick Settings and the Wi-Fi page call it (`wifi_switch(1)`, a toggle of `g_wififlag`). Off removes `/tmp/wpasupplicant_initsuccess`, stops SyncLink's server (`stop_wifisynclink`, which needs `g_wififlag` still set), clears the switch's flags and `wifi_name`, runs `networkStop` and sets `wifilink_timeout` to 30; stock's `network_checkstatus` then sends `rtwpriv wlan0 pm_set ips=1`, as after the user's switch. On runs `networkStart(1)`, the background `wifi_connect.sh &`. The switch's last act, both branches', is its tail call `write_int_config(g_wififlag, "SYSSET", "WIFI")`; the `write_int_config` hook (`ringnav_write_config`, `smart_config`) drops that write for Smart Wi-Fi's own toggles and passes any other on, so `config.ini`, a reboot and the user's own switch stay stock's. A `SYSSET WIFI` write it passes is the user's (Quick Settings, the Wi-Fi page): Smart Wi-Fi forgets it had the radio off and counts `SMART_IDLE_MS` from the tap. With the row off, or the user's Wi-Fi off, a radio Smart Wi-Fi had off comes back, unsaved, and nothing more happens. Rockbox's own Wi-Fi stop ([Rockbox from Home](boot.md#rockbox-from-home)) is unaffected: demo restarts and reads `WIFI` from `config.ini`, which Smart Wi-Fi never wrote.

`smart_ready` keeps to stock's own conditions for its switch: `networkStart` and `networkStop` act only when `initNetworkModule`'s type (`NET_TYPE`, `0xa500d4`, no symbol; `NET_TYPE_READS` in `tools/build.py` pins both reads) is 2, Wi-Fi; the first scan taken (`wifi_initstatus` 0) and no connect half done (`wifi_connectstatus` not 1), as Quick Settings and the Wi-Fi page require; and never in test mode, while powering off or in the first-boot guide, where `on_wm_timer_networkstatus` also leaves the network alone.

Needing the network (`smart_needed`): a USB cable in; AirPlay or DLNA on (Network service); [Car Remote](#car-remote) on (`coda_rc_enabled`, the switch, session or not: the phone connects over TCP when the car starts, so the radio has to be up before it, and the TCP session dies with the radio); [SyncLink](#synclink) over Wi-Fi (`g_synclinkflag` 2, off unless the user turns it on) or a SyncLink session, Wi-Fi transfer; a stock stream queue of the types `on_wm_timer_networkstatus` (`0x4f5168`) stops once the link drops (`mclGetPlayType` 2, 3, 0xf1 and 0xf2: Tidal's), playing, paused or stopped, as stock would otherwise stop a paused one and lose its place; Spotify's librespot running (`spot_running`); an Internet Radio station; a card app started (`addon_running`: launched, or restarting after Retry, until it stops by itself, Stop Streaming Services or Rockbox; one stopped for USB storage counts once it starts again, as the cable holds the radio meanwhile); a scrobble upload, the user's or the automatic one (`scrobble_busy`); Network Update's download or an Apps job (`netupdate_busy`); Get Album Lyrics (`album_lyrics_busy`); a Tidal download (`tidal_busy`); an action held for the link (below); a time sync pending on a link (`g_syncnettime_flag`, cleared after one attempt); and a network page open anywhere in the window stack (`net_page_open`: Streaming and its services' pages but Tidal Downloads, a card app's page and its QR code, System settings' Apps, AirPlay's, Network service, SyncLink, the Wi-Fi page and its dialogs, Wi-Fi transfer and the online lyrics and cover search). A new link counts as a use, so a fresh connection gets `SMART_IDLE_MS` before Smart Wi-Fi acts, time sync first. A radio that never associates (out of range, scanning) goes off after `SMART_IDLE_MS` too.

Waking. Streaming's page (`ringnav_stream`) and the Wi-Fi page (`systemset_wifi_page_init`, hooked as `ringnav_wifi_page`, before it builds its switch from `g_wififlag`) bring the radio back at once. Users that check the link once when they start would fail during the 3 to 8 s reconnect, so they wait for it through `smart_wifi_wait`, up to `SMART_CONNECT_MS` (15 s), then go on as they would have. The link is up once both the status bar's bars (`get_wifisignal`, which the payload's own actions check) and the network monitor thread's connect status (`networkGetConnectStatus`, which stock's check) say so: each comes from its own poll, about a second apart. A server song pressed with Local + Server ([Server library](#server-library)) waits that way too, before its app is started. Internet Radio's directory fetch and a station's start wait that way ("Connecting to Wi-Fi…", "Connecting…"; a station started from the side buttons too). An automatic scrobble upload due while Smart Wi-Fi has the radio off reads `[SCROBBLE] AUTO` from the card, wakes the radio if it is on, and goes at the next minute's check; a wake that brought no link, or `AUTO` off, waits `SA_RETRY_MIN` as a failed upload does, so an unreachable network is tried every half hour, not held on. A press that needs the link is held (`smart_hold`; Network Update, the Apps rows, Get Album Lyrics and Upload Scrobbles through `need_link`, which says "Connect to Wi-Fi first" when no link is coming): it toasts "Connecting to Wi-Fi…", and a 500 ms timer runs the action once the link is up, or `SMART_CONNECT_MS` on (to fail as it would have), if the page it was pressed on is still the top window past stock's self-closing overlays (toasts, `msginfo_dialog`, and the volume, `volume_dialog`, which a wheel turn opens over a toast) once no page is sliding; otherwise it is dropped. One waits at a time: a press while one waits takes its place, so the action runs once, and it runs unheld (`sw.held`), so a radio that could not come back fails it as before rather than holding it again. The payload's are Spotify's row (librespot never retries a Connect login or an mDNS registration that failed at its start), a card app's row, Upload Scrobbles, Network Update, the Apps page's rows and its opening check, and Get Album Lyrics. Three stock actions that check the link once and show `msg_notnetwork` without it are held the same way, each hooked at its entry (none has a symbol): Streaming's Tidal row (`0x540f7c`, the row click `stream_page_init` binds, on Streaming's page and in Home's Split Streaming list, whose Library list beside it names its rows by index too, so the row is found again in `scroll_view_streamsset`), Network service's Wi-Fi transfer (`0x4cce64`, row 2 only: DLNA and AirPlay switch at once, and stock starts their services once there is a link) and Now Playing More's Download Cover & Lyrics (`0x539614`, given More's window; More is no network page, so only this press wakes the radio). None reads its event, and the two rows are found again by name (stock names each row's list_item and button by its index and reads only that name), so nothing pressed is kept but the page. Quick Settings shows Off while Smart Wi-Fi has the radio off, as it is; a tap turns it on and saves it, as stock's does. The Wi-Fi page wakes it first, so its switch shows the user's setting (Off only when `smart_ready` refuses the wake).

`test/patch.py` runs stock's `wifi_switch` from the payload's toggles against the user's tap (the same calls in the same order, without the write), stock's `network_checkstatus` after it, the row, each keep-alive case, the Wi-Fi page, the automatic upload's wake, the held stock actions (stock's own code for the Tidal row and Wi-Fi transfer, and the Tidal row on Home), a press that joins the wait for Upload Scrobbles, Network Update, an Apps install and Get Album Lyrics, Spotify's and Internet Radio's waits. `test/fw/test_smart_wifi.py` runs the idle count on the host, and Car Remote on holding the radio through it. ponytail: on Home the held Tidal row runs while Home is still the page in use, as Spotify's row does, even if the Streaming list has given way to another of Home's lists. ponytail: `network_checkstatus` sends `ips=1` only once its latch (`0xa4db39`) is set, after a connect, so a radio that never associated is left in whatever power state the driver chose. While stock refuses its switch (`smart_ready`), a wait that outlives `SMART_CONNECT_MS` can start one more.

## Watchdog

The X2000's hardware watchdog (`module_driver/soc_watchdog.ko`, loaded at boot; `/dev/jz_watchdog`, libhardware2's `watchdog_start`, `watchdog_feed` and `watchdog_stop`) is never started by stock, so a demo whose UI loop stalls, or a stalled kernel, stays dark with every button dead until a 15 s Center hold cuts the power: `S90play` only reboots once demo is _gone_ (stock's `checkappprocess.sh` likewise), and a hung demo is still there. `wdt_poll`, from `power_poll` on every UI loop pass, opens the device on the first pass and starts it counting `WDT_MS` (60 s, `patch/offsets.inc`; ioctl `0x8004570d`, an `int` of milliseconds by pointer), then feeds it (`0x2000570f`) every pass, so a stall that long reboots the Q2. The driver counts on the RTC clock, through a suspend, so `ringnav_standby` stops it (`0x2000570e`) before stock's suspend and starts it again after. The driver's `close` is a no-op, so a demo that ends would leave it running: `ringnav_clean_end` stops it on a clean end (`into_poweroff`, through the hooked `save_memoryplay_info`; `device_reboot` and the firmware update dialog, through `reboot_save` in `patch/playback.c`; `rockbox_open`), and nothing is fed or recorded after. No device, or a refused start, leaves stock's behavior. The driver's prescaler caps a start at about 23 minutes. ponytail: the UI loop is the only feeder, so a stalled worker thread is not caught; a legitimate pass longer than `WDT_MS` would reboot. The known long ones, on the UI thread, are `importPlayList` reading every song's tags (stock's Import Playlists row and card apps' imports, through `addon_m3u_dir`) and a folder add loading each directory (`qm_tracks`): `ringnav_wdt_long` restarts the count at `WDT_LONG_MS` (15 min) as they begin, and the next pass, after they return, at `WDT_MS` again. Another long pass found later needs the same call. A hang inside Standby's suspend or resume is not caught: the watchdog is stopped across it.

**State record.** `state_poll` (the same pass) keeps `/mnt/data/q2-state`: one line, `screen:on|off power:running|suspending cable:in|out battery:N play:stopped|playing|paused out:jack|bluetooth|usb`; rewritten (flushed and `fsync`ed) only when the line changes. A change of the screen, cable, battery, playback or output is written `STATE_SETTLE_MS` (5 s) after the first one not yet written, as the latest line, so a burst (a wake that starts playback, say) is one write and the flash sees at most one every 5 s; a change undone within it writes nothing. What the boot check rests on is never held: a run's first line (the file's being there is the forced-restart mark), the power field, `power:suspending` just before Standby's suspend and `power:running` after it, and a clean end's removal. ponytail: a forced restart up to 5 s after a change leaves the line before it, which the crash log then reports. A clean end removes it. One still there at boot means the last session ended in a forced restart (or the battery ran out), and `S90play` puts it in `q2-crash.log` ([boot.md](boot.md)) before that is copied to the card, so a report of a dead Q2 says what it was doing. A Coverflow open that never finished leaves `/mnt/data/q2-cf-trace` ([Build](#coverflow)), which goes in after it as `== cover flow`; boot removes that file either way. On a `--dev` build, `WHEEL_LOG_HOOK` appends `/mnt/data/q2-wheel.log` (the wheel's stale-press notes, `stale_note`, [Hooks](#hooks)) to the card's `q2-wheel.log`, kept apart from the crash record so a note never replaces one.

**Stall record.** After the watchdog's reset, `q2-crash.log` says only that demo did not end, which reads the same as a stalled kernel, a 15 s hold or a flat battery. So once `wdt_poll` has started the watchdog, it starts a thread (`stall_watch`) that wakes every `STALL_POLL_MS` (5 s, `patch/offsets.inc`). `wdt_poll` counts the passes; when the count hasn't moved for `STALL_MS` (20 s), and again at `STALL_AGAIN_MS` (45 s), the thread writes `/mnt/data/q2-stall` and `fsync`s it (`stall_write`; the second appends). It counts from its first wake after the last pass, so up to 5 s short. Each record has these lines:

- `age N ms`, since the pass.
- `toasts N`: `toast()`'s dialogs open, nested ones counted (`st.toasts`).
- The UI loop's thread, which is demo's main thread, so `/proc/self`'s: `state` (the letter after the last `)` of `stat`), `wchan`, and `syscall` (the number and arguments, then `sp` and `pc`; `-1 sp pc` outside a call; `running` on the CPU, with no registers).
- `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo`, and `pgmajfault` and `workingset_refault_file` from `/proc/vmstat`.
- When `syscall` gave an `sp`, the stack words from there that could be code addresses, of the 160 up to the main stack's top (`stat`'s `startstack`), as a `q2remote --prof` line (`tid state pc ra words`, `ra` 0). `tools/q2remote.py prof` names only the samples it takes live, so a saved line's words are looked up by hand: `llvm-nm` on that build's `patch.elf` and `demo` names those in demo (linked at `0x400000`). They are read in place: from a blocked thread's `sp` to that top is its own stack, mapped, and an `sp` 8 MB or more below it is not the main stack's (`mmap`'s area starts at least 128 MB down), so it is left alone. demo imports no `lseek64` for `/proc/self/mem`.

The thread uses only `open`, `read`, `write`, `fsync`, `close` and `unlink` on buffers on its own stack (6.7 KB, kept out of `.scratch`): no stock call, no allocation, no lock the UI thread takes. A pass after a record removes it, as a stall that recovered isn't what it is for, and so does a clean end (`ringnav_clean_end`): Rockbox's demo, started again by `S90play`'s loop with no boot between, would never remove one written just before. Nothing is written while the watchdog is stopped (Standby's suspend, a clean end) or stretched (`ringnav_wdt_long`). At boot `S90play` appends it to `q2-crash.log` as `== stall`, after `== cover flow`, and removes it either way. Reading it: D with the two counts climbing between the records and `MemAvailable` near 0 is memory thrash; R with flat counts, a loop on the CPU; S in a futex wait, a deadlock; D in a driver with flat counts, a kernel or driver hang. ponytail: `wchan` reads `0` on a kernel without `CONFIG_KALLSYMS`, and a library's addresses on the stack line need that boot's `/proc/<pid>/maps`.

## Overheat guardian

`q2guard` (`patch/q2guard.c`, its decisions, log line and log rotation in `patch/q2guard_core.c`, `patch/q2guard.h`, the PMIC's die temperature in `patch/q2guard_pmic.c`; the log's RAM ring is `patch/card_store.c`, linked as `patch/q2guard_card.c`) is a helper process of its own, so that it keeps watching when demo is hung: `S90play` (`BOOT_HOOK`, `tools/build.py` `GUARD`) starts it before demo, `nice -n -5`, in a loop that starts it again 2 s after it ends, with the build's version and how the last session ended (`clean`, `forced` when `/mnt/data/q2-state` is still there, `stall` with `/mnt/data/q2-stall`; read only, before those are moved to `q2-crash.log`). A `flock` on `/tmp/q2guard.lock` keeps it to one; the file holds its pid. It is also the [unified log](#unified-log)'s writer. Every 5 s (1 s once powering off) it reads the temperature (the AXP2101 PMIC's die on the Q2, below) and the CPU's busy share from `/proc/stat`, and `guard_step` decides; it writes nothing to `/mnt/data`, and to the PMIC only the two registers below.

**Sensors.** Read from the stock V1.36 kernel (`vmlinux`, base `0x80010000`) and its device tree: there is no thermal core and no hwmon, so no `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp` on the Q2. The AXP2101's `battery` supply (`axp2101_charger.c`; its desc built at `0x80536e40`) has twelve properties: present, voltage_now, energy_full_design, status, capacity_alert_min, temp, capacity, temp_alert_min, time_to_empty_now, time_to_full_now, manufacturer (`X-POWERS`) and capacity_level; no `current_now`. Its `temp` (`get_property` `0x80535418`, case 51) reads two bytes of a PMIC register and returns the second raw: the low byte of an ADC count, not tenths of a degree, so it varies within 0-255 and would pass a naive plausibility check; `temp_alert_min` is the constant 85. The device tree sets `pmu_chg_ic_temp = 0` and no TS (thermistor) limits. `read_temp` takes the PMIC's die while its reader is on, else a thermal zone, then a hwmon input, then the battery's `temp` unless its manufacturer is `X-POWERS`, so a Q2 whose PMIC reader is off reads none and watches the CPU.

**The die temperature** (`patch/q2guard_pmic.c`, `pmic_sample`). The AXP2101 (I2C bus 6, address `0x34`; `/dev/i2c-6` with `I2C_SLAVE_FORCE`, as `axp20x-i2c` owns the address, one SMBus byte transaction at a time) has a 14-bit ADC channel for its die: enabled by `0x30` bit 4 (power-on 0, and the stock kernel never writes `0x30`), the result in `0x3C` bits 5:0 (high) and `0x3D`, read high first; `T = 22 + (7274 - raw) / 20` C (XPowersLib and Rockbox; the datasheet gives only 0.1 mV a count). The stock kernel's power-key probe writes `0x34 = 0x40`: `0x34` bits 7:6 with `0x36` bit 6 are the ADC's debug mode `ch_dbg_en`, and 001 is "VBAT uses all channels", so the die channel never converts. Each sample is therefore a window: read `0x30`, `0x34`, `0x36` and `0x50` and go on only if they are as stock leaves them (`0x30` `0x03` or `0x13`, `0x34` mode 01 or 00, `0x36` bit 6 clear, `0x50 = 0x10`: the TS pin detached from the charger); set `0x30` bit 4 (read, modify, write, read back) at the start and whenever it is found clear again; write `0x34` with its mode bits cleared (bits 5:0 are read-only VBAT data), wait 1 s (`PMIC_WINDOW_MS`), read `0x3C`, `0x3D`, `0x3C`, and write `0x34` back as it was, tried three times and written whatever the reads did. A pair whose two high bytes differ, or a count of 0 (no conversion yet), is no reading. Any register not as expected turns the reader off for good with no write; three I2C errors in a row (over samples) too; a restore that fails three times too, leaving mode 00, the chip's own default, until the next boot rewrites `0x40`. Each is a `SENSOR pmic off: ...` note, and the CPU watch takes over. The first window also polls the pair every 50 ms and logs when its first conversion landed (`SENSOR pmic first conversion after N ms`), the measurement a shorter window would rest on. On a Q2 on 2026-11-17 (charging, in hand), outside q2guard with `i2cset`: before, `0x30 = 0x03`, `0x34 = 0x51`, `0x36 = 0xbf`, `0x13 = 0x03`, `0x50 = 0x10`; with the channel on and mode 00, raw 6952, 6950, 6950, 6947 (38.1 to 38.3 C, falling counts as it warmed), charging and the battery voltage unchanged, and `battery/temp` read `raw & 0xFF`, which confirms the kernel's `temp` is the low byte of this pair (q2guard still never trusts it). The bit in `0x30` survives a reboot (it resets only on the PMIC's power-on reset), so a Q2 that ran this firmware shows a varying `battery/temp` after a downgrade. The emulator has no `/dev/i2c-6`: the reader is off from the start (`SENSOR pmic none`), and the boot ends in the No Temperature Sensor card as before. ponytail: the window is 1 s, the device's first test's own wait; the first-conversion note says how much shorter it can be.

**Rules** (`guard_step`, temperatures in tenths of a degree). A reading counts only within 0..100 C and within 3 C of the last one that counted (a die moves tenths of a degree in 5 s; a jump is a misread); three bad, missing or jumping in a row put the sensor down, and so does one that reads a single value for 60 readings (5 min), before it was trusted whatever the load, after it only while the CPU's busy share swung 40 points or more meanwhile (a real die moves then; an idle one may sit still). Down says why in its note (`SENSOR none usable: none read`, `out of range`, `jumps`, `constant`, `stuck while the load changed`). It is trusted once two readings differ, and after going down as soon as it reads and varies again, with no old reading to jump from. A misread neither counts towards a threshold nor breaks a run of readings over one. Trusted: three readings in a row at 55 C or more toast "Q2 is getting hot" once, again only after it fell below 50 C; three at 62 C or more begin the power-off, which nothing undoes (cooling during it included). **These thresholds are proposed, for the user to approve before release**, and are for the PMIC's die, not the battery. Why these numbers: the AXP2101's own limits are far above (charge-current thermal regulation at `0x65`'s threshold, 100 C by default; over-temperature level 1 at 125 C, `0x13 = 0x03` on the device; shutdown at 145 C, datasheet 6.7.4.3), so they protect the chip, not the battery or a hand, and the guardian has to act long before them. The die sits on the board beside the battery: on battery power the PMIC dissipates little and the die is within a few degrees of the board, and while charging its linear charger heats it, up to about 15 C over the board at 0.5 W (`θJA` 30 C/W, datasheet table 5-4; an upper bound, as the board spreads the heat). A lithium cell is rated to about 45 C charging and 60 C discharging. So 62 C on the die is a battery at about 60 C at worst on battery power, and nearer 50 C while charging; 55 C warns with 7 C to spare. The one reading so far is 38 C charging in hand, 17 C under the warning. Not yet measured: the die against the battery in a long hot run (playing on the charger in a warm room), which would show whether the warning comes too early while charging. The old thresholds (50 C and 58 C) were set for a battery or skin sensor the Q2 does not have. The CPU is logged and never powers off. Not trusted (down or not yet decided): the mean busy share over the last 24 samples (2 min); at 85% or more a 60 s countdown with Cancel; Cancel stands it down until the share stays under 50% for 12 samples (1 min), and the countdown's end begins the power-off. A sensor that comes back ends a countdown.

**demo's side** (`patch/heatguard.c`, `heatguard_poll` from `power_poll` every 500 ms). q2guard writes `/tmp/q2guard.state` every sample, `seq=N card=none|warn|nosensor|loadwarn|off left=MS state=... t=DECI beat=N`; demo answers in `/tmp/q2guard.ack`, `ack N` and `cancel N`. Each new `seq` shows once, through `confirm` (feedback.c), tried again on the next poll while another card is up: `warn` a toast; `nosensor` "No Temperature Sensor" with one OK; `loadwarn` "Q2 has been working hard" with Cancel and Shut Down, counting down `left` to Shut Down; `off` answers `ack`, pauses the music if it plays (`player_play_pause`), shows "Q2 is too hot. Shutting down to cool off." counting down 10 s, and then opens stock's `poweroff_page` (its `into_poweroff` saves the queue), at the same time from the poll if the card couldn't show. Where `/usr/bin/q2guard` is installed, a state whose `beat` hasn't moved for 30 s, once demo has run a minute, is "Overheat protection isn't running", once. `hg_confirm` and `hg_toast` are the tests' seams, 0 on the Q2.

**Power-off.** From its start q2guard writes the log out; with no `ack` in 5 s (demo hung) it kills `hciplayer` and `q2player` (demo owns the player's socket, so there is no pause to send) and powers off as soon as the log write has finished; in any case 30 s after the start. Before `sync` and `reboot(RB_POWER_OFF)` the last lines go out in at most 3 s, never past the 30 s. A `reboot` that returns is logged once and tried again every second. On the emulator the guest's `reboot` either ends the sandbox's pid namespace (its power-off) or is refused, depending on which process of the sandbox asks.

**The heat log.** A line (`heat_line`) every 30 s, every 5 s while warm (45 C), plugged in (`ac/online`), at least 50% busy or counting down: the UTC time, uptime, the temperature, the PMIC's die temperature and its ADC count (`die=`, `adc=`: what the PMIC read, the guardian's verdict aside), the battery's raw `temp`, the level (CW2015) and mV, `battery/status`, the cable, the UDC's state and the configfs gadget bound to it, backlight on and brightness, Wi-Fi (`wlan0` up) and Bluetooth (`hci0`), the CPU clock if `cpufreq` exists (it doesn't on the Q2), the CPU busy since the last line, the top three processes by CPU over that time (`top_three`, `/proc/[pid]/stat` utime and stime), demo's threads, the process count and the guardian's state; notes of their own for BOOT, SENSOR, WARN, LOADWARN, POWEROFF, NOANSWER, CARD and POWER. Lines are held in `card_store.c`'s `card_log` (a 64 KB RAM ring, `HEAT_RAM`, the oldest whole lines dropped and counted) and go to `/mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-heat.0`: every 5 min, every minute while fast, and at once on a note, by a forked child so a card that hangs never stops the watching. The watching process's `card_mounted` (the function `card_store.c` asks) is false, so `card_log_append` only ever holds; the child sets it true, so its `card_log_flush` appends the ring to the file in order, and the watcher drops what the child was given once the child exited 0 (if the ring moved meanwhile it keeps it all: a line twice beats a line lost). `heat_flush` rotates first: a `.0` that has reached 256 KB (`HEAT_FILE_MAX`) moves to `.1`, so each file ends below 256 KB plus one flush (at most 64 KB) and the two hold at most about 640 KB. While the card is away (not mounted read-write, or a configfs `mass_storage` LUN holds a file: USB Transfer Files) or a write fails, the lines stay in RAM and no child is started; the next write that gets through starts with `== N lines lost while the card was away` if the ring had to drop any (`tools/q2heat.py` reads it as a GAP note). Read it back over adb with the one-liner in [adb](adb.md#use). The [Bluetooth link monitor](#bluetooth-link-monitor) keeps its own log beside it, `q2-bt.0` and `.1`, through the same ring and writing child.

**What it costs.** Nothing here runs between ticks: no thread, one `usleep`, so 12 wakeups a minute (60 while powering off), and a quiet Q2 spends them on a few small reads. A tick reads `battery/temp`, the thermal zone, hwmon and `manufacturer` (each a missing file or a few bytes), `/proc/stat` and `/tmp/q2guard.ack`, and writes `/tmp/q2guard.state` (tmpfs, temp and rename); on the Q2 it also opens the PMIC's window: nine SMBus byte transactions (seven reads, two writes) and a 1 s `usleep` inside the 5 s tick, so 24 wakeups a minute instead of 12 (the first window polls every 50 ms, once a start). A log line adds about fifteen sysfs and `/proc` reads and one `/proc` walk, an open, read and close of `stat` for each process (`scan`, at most 512), the one cost that grows with the process count; it is a line every 30 s, or every tick while warm, plugged in or busy. A flush is one `fork` of this small process (its biggest part is the 64 KB ring) plus an append and `fsync` on the card. Measured on the emulator (qemu user mode, about 16 processes): 0.00 s of CPU in 60 s at the quiet cadence, 0.01 s in 60 s (0.017% of a core) at the 5 s one. A line is about 190 bytes: 0.5 MB a day at the 30 s cadence, 3.3 MB a day at 5 s, all on the card; the Q2's flash is never written. Memory is the ring's 64 KB, allocated at the first line, and the binary.

## Unified log

One log for the whole Q2, on the card: `/mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-log.0` to `.3`, beside the heat log and the [Bluetooth link log](#bluetooth-link-monitor), never on the flash (the user's, 2026-11-17). Before it, demo's stderr and the players' went to `/tmp/q2-demo.err` (release) or `/tmp/q2-demo.log` (`--dev`), in RAM and gone at every power-off, emptied whole past 512 KB, with no time or level on a line; only a crash moved a slice of them to the card, in `q2-crash.log`.

**A line** (`patch/ulog_line.h`, `ulog_line`): `2026-11-17T14:35:02Z 5123456 W usb cable in, seen after its edge, 9 ms`, the UTC time (the Q2's clock: 1970 until Wi-Fi or a computer sets it), the uptime in ms (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), a level (`E` error, `W` warning, `I` the rest), a source (`ui`, `player`, `usb`, `bt`, `wifi`, `guard`, `kernel`) and the message, one line, control characters as spaces, cut at about 500 bytes.

**One writer.** `q2guard` ([Overheat guardian](#overheat-guardian)) is the log's only writer, with its own code in `patch/q2log_core.c` (`patch/q2log.h`): its ring is a `card_store.c` `card_log` (`ULOG_RAM`, 64 KB, the oldest whole lines dropped and counted while the card is away), written by the same forked child as the heat and Bluetooth logs, so a card that hangs never stops the watching, and a card lent to a computer or pulled leaves the lines in RAM until it is back, then written in order after a `== N lines lost while the card was away` line if the ring overflowed. The writes are batched: with the heat log's flush (every 5 min, every minute while warm, plugged in or streaming, at once on a heat event), and at once on an `E` or `W` line, at most every 30 s for a run of them (`WARN_GAP_MS`). A flush that finds `q2-log.0` at 256 KB or more (`ULOG_FILE_MAX`) first moves `.2` to `.3` (the old `.3` goes), `.1` to `.2` and `.0` to `.1` (`ulog_flush`): about 1 MB in all, a file never split mid-line.

**Its feeds**, each read once a tick (5 s) in `q2guard`'s watching process, bounded, never blocking:

- **demo** (`patch/ulog.c`, `ulog(level, src, msg)`): demo never touches the card log. `ulog` writes a whole stamped line to demo's stderr, so it is in `/tmp/q2-demo.err` (release) or `/tmp/q2-demo.log` (`--dev`) as before, and `q2guard` passes it through as it is (`ulog_is_line`). USB's cable lines (`usb_ui.c` `usb_log`) go through it, their text as it was without its `q2 usb:` prefix, which the source replaces.
- **q2player's own lines**: stamped as demo's are (`player/main.c` `plog`, source `player`): each song demo hands it (`set-songurl`, `set-nexturl`, `set-gapless`, with the path or URL, a URL's query left out as it carries an app's token) and each `mcl-stop`, `I`; its crashes ([Player crashes](#player-crashes)).
- **the player and stock's helpers**: `hciplayer`, `q2player`, `rtk_hciattach`, `wpa_supplicant`, `udhcpc` and `wifi_connect.sh` inherit demo's stderr, so their lines are in the same file without a stamp: `q2guard` stamps them when it reads them (up to 5 s late) and guesses the rest from their words (`ulog_guess`): `E` for one that names an error or failure (`error`, `fail`, `cannot`, `unable`, `refused`, `timed out`, ...), `W` for `warn`, else `I`; the source by who it names, the player first (`hciplayer` holds `hci`; its mplayer's own lines name `mplayer`, `playback` or an `audio codec`), then Bluetooth (`bluealsa`, `rtk_hci`, `hci0`, `bt` as a word of its own), Wi-Fi (`wpa_`, `wlan`, `udhcpc`), USB, else `ui`. `ulog_tail` reads from where it stopped, at most 16 KB a tick, and holds a line's start until its end arrives. In a `--dev` build that file also holds stock's stdout, so all of it comes in too.
- **the kernel**: `/dev/kmsg` (the kernel's ring, read without consuming it, unlike `/proc/kmsg`), non-blocking, at most 64 records a tick; only the kernel's own (facility 0) at warning or worse (`ulog_kmsg`: priorities 0 to 3 `E`, 4 `W`), at the record's own uptime. A record overwritten before it was read is skipped (`EPIPE`). Where it does not open (the emulator's sandbox), the log says so once.
- **the guardian**: its heat-log notes (`BOOT`, `SENSOR`, `WARN`, `LOADWARN`, `POWEROFF`, `NOANSWER`, `CARD`, `POWER`) as `guard` lines, `W` for the ones that warn or go wrong.

A `q2guard` started again (S90play's loop, `last=respawn`) reads demo's file and `/dev/kmsg` from their present ends: the one before it read the rest.

**Repeats.** A run of one line (the same level, source and message) is the line once and a count: the rest are counted, not written, and `last line repeated N more times`, at the last one's time, goes in when another line comes or before a flush (`ulog_repeats`), and a repeat is no `E` or `W` line to flush for. The emulator's demo prints `gpio: failed to open device` seven times a second: before this it was 2171 of 2400 lines in 5 minutes, 200 KB.

**The roll** (`tools/build.py` `BOOT_HOOK`, and `LOG_HOOK` for `--dev`). demo's file is held open `O_APPEND` by demo and everything it starts, so it cannot be renamed under them: once a minute, past 256 KB (2 MB for the `--dev` file), S90play copies it to `.1` (the one before goes) and empties it. `ulog_tail` sees the file shorter than where it had read to and reads the rest of `.1` from there first, then the emptied file from its start. ponytail: a line written between the copy and the emptying (microseconds, once per 256 KB) is lost to both; and a file refilled past the old offset within one tick would not be seen as rolled (256 KB in 5 s). The crash log, Save Diagnostics (`patch/diagnostics.c`), the Bluetooth abnormal reboot's record (`system.c` `reboot_record`) and `q2remote.py log` read `.1` and the file together, so a tail just after a roll is still whole.

**Snapshots.** A snapshot (`ulog_snapshot`) is a `snapshot WHY` line and what the Q2 was doing, each a `guard` line: `/proc/meminfo`'s totals, `/proc/loadavg`, and the last heat line's state (temperature, battery, cable, screen, radios, the top three processes). Taken at:

- a **power-off**, **Restart** and **firmware update**: demo's `ulog_end("power-off")` (`ringnav_savequeue`), `ulog_end("restart")` (`ringnav_reboot_from`) and `ulog_end("update")` (`ringnav_checkfw`), once a run: a `shutdown: WHY` line, the request written to `/tmp/q2guard.snap`, a SIGUSR1 to the pid `q2guard` keeps in `/tmp/q2guard.lock` (through the shell's `kill`: demo imports none), and a wait for the answer, the request removed, `ULOG_END_MS` (2 s) at most. The signal ends `q2guard`'s sleep (`bt_sleep` returns on `guard_woke`), so it reads the feeds, takes the snapshot, writes all three logs out within 3 s (`flush_final`) and removes the request;
- a **crash**: S90play, once the crash log is written, asks the same way with `crash demo exit N` (`E`), and waits 3 s at most before the reboot;
- a **heat event**: the warning, the load warning and the protective power-off (`W`), once that tick's heat line is made;
- a **SIGTERM** (busybox init's, a second before its SIGKILL, when the system goes down another way): `snapshot shutdown signal`, the logs written out, `q2guard` ends.

With no `q2guard` to answer (none running, or a stale pid), nothing waits and no request is left.

**The boot marker.** Each start writes `boot build=V last=clean|forced|stall|respawn` (S90play's word, as the heat log's `BOOT`): `clean` when the last session ended through a clean end, `forced` when `/mnt/data/q2-state` was still there (a forced restart, a flat battery, or a crash, whose snapshot says which), `stall` with a stall record; `W` for all but `clean` and `respawn`.

**Reading it back.** `q2guard --dump` (also in release builds) asks the running `q2guard` for a flush (a `flush` request: no snapshot), waits for it (6 s at most), then prints `q2-log.3` to `.0`, oldest first: `adb exec-out q2guard --dump` ([adb](adb.md)). `tools/q2log.py` reads it, alone or merged by time with the heat and Bluetooth logs (`--adb` reads all three), and filters by level and source.

**What it costs.** No process, thread or wakeup of its own: each 5 s tick adds an `open`, `lseek` and `read` of demo's file (nothing read when it has not grown) and one non-blocking `read` of `/dev/kmsg` that finds nothing; a snapshot reads `/proc/meminfo` and `/proc/loadavg`. Memory is the 64 KB ring, the 16 KB read buffer and 512 bytes held for a line's end. Measured on the emulator (2026-11-17, a `--dev` build, `BLUETOOTH=0`, a pool slot, `smoke.py`'s walk four times over in 5.3 minutes: Library, Now Playing with a song playing, Cover Flow, four Settings pages, Control Center, Search) against the trunk's build doing the same: `q2guard` used 0.10 s of CPU against 0.03 s (qemu user mode, which counts its translation too: about 0.8 s an hour more, 0.02% of a core); the card took 7 flushes against 1 (about 80 an hour, each an append and `fsync` of a few KB to `q2-log.0` and `q2-heat.0`, set by the 30 s gap for the errors the emulator's stock code prints) and 13 KB of `q2-log` (about 150 KB an hour: the 1 MB covers about 7 hours of that use, longer on a Q2, where the emulator's missing devices do not fail). A release build reads only demo's stderr, without stock's stdout, so it writes less.

## Modal dialog close

A modal dialog (every toast, `msginfo_dialog`, and the confirms) runs its own loop in `dialog_modal` (`0x65271c`); when the loop ends, stock queues the close (`0x6521dc`: `window_manager_close_window` on the dialog's parent) with `idle_add` and the bare dialog, not `widget_add_idle`, whose idles `widget_destroy_sync` (`0x6759b8`) removes with the widget. A dialog freed before that idle ran was read from freed memory. A `q2-crash.log` of 2026-11-10 (1.7.6) shows it: demo's SIGSEGV at `0x680554` (`window_manager_close_window`, reading the window manager's `0x94` from `0x43030000`), `ra` `0x739520` in `idle_info_on_idle`, through that close's tail calls, 2 s after a Standby resume while playing, at a track change. That call (`DIALOG_CLOSE` in `tools/build.py`) is now `ringnav_dialog_close` (`patch/system.c`), which queues `dialog_close` instead: it closes the dialog only while it is still one of the window manager's children, as `widget_destroy` takes a window out of its parent before it frees it, and otherwise does nothing.
