`ringnav_sleep`'s idles (above: `IDLE_SLEEP_MS` lit, `SCREEN_OFF_SLEEP_MS` and `DARK_IDLE_SLEEP_MS` dark) are `loop_wait` (`patch/loop_wake.c`): a `poll()` on an eventfd (o32 `eventfd2` and `poll` through `lw_syscall`; demo imports neither) instead of `sleep_ms`, so whatever brings the UI work ends the idle at once, and `loop_span` lets an idle run longer while nothing needs a pass sooner. Without an eventfd (the kernel refused one, or a host test) it is the `sleep_ms` it replaces, the same length.

What ends the wait (`loop_wake`, from any thread: an 8-byte write): every event `ringnav_queue_event` queues, which is every key, wheel tick, touch and SyncLink key and every timer or idle another thread hands AWTK (`main_loop_queue_event` is the queue's one way in); the wheel's raw samples while the loop idles (`loop_wake_touch` in `wheel_sample`: Cover Flow's thumb and the selection bar's lean read that travel with no event); a headset key `headset_worker` queues; a BlueZ volume signal `bt_vol_event.c` counts; a USB cable's edge `usb_event.c` settles; and a Cover Flow half the loader has read. Everything else a pass picks up is read by a per-pass `*_poll` or a stock timer and rides the wait's bounds below: a worker thread's result, another process's file (q2guard's state, Car Remote's commands, Guest Play's), stock's globals (a Bluetooth link, the player's status).

How long (`loop_span`): never less than the idle it replaces, so a timer already due, or a suspended one, never makes the loop pass more often than before. Longer only when the loop has its eventfd and none of these holds: a timer of `LOOP_ANIM_MS` (50 ms) or less runs (a frame: `ui_kit.c`'s motion loop and the level bars at 33 ms, a marquee's or a spinner's step); the widget animator manager has an animator (its own timer runs every 8 ms whether or not, so it counts only then: `AM_FIRST`); more idles wait than the fewest seen (stock's `on_wm_idle_status` repeats every pass, so it is the floor; a new `idle_add` runs on the next pass); stock's key lockout counts down (`KEY_LOCKOUT`, which `on_wm_timer_setup_state` steps every 100 ms; the wheel's ticks wait on it). Window animations, input in the last `IDLE_MS` and Now Playing's motion already keep the loop at stock's pace before an idle starts. Lit, the idle then runs to the next AWTK timer due (the timer list walked at `TM_LIST`, a timer's start and period at `TIMER_START` and `TIMER_DURATION`), at most `LOOP_LIT_MAX_MS` (250 ms), and not past a pass that left the screen dirty (the top window's native window has dirty rects, `NW_DIRTY`, cleared by each paint's `native_window_clear_dirty_rect`: a poll changed a label after this pass painted). Stock's own 100 ms timer `on_wm_timer_setup_state` runs lit and dark, so a lit idle wait is at most about 100 ms in practice. Dark, stock's timers already ride the dark idle late (a 100 ms timer ran every 250 ms dark and quiet), so the wait does not follow them: it runs to `LOOP_DARK_MAX_MS` (1 s) while `dark_slow` holds (the player polls already run a second apart; not near a track's end, nor for A-B Repeat, Car Remote or another player), input has been still `IDLE_MS`, and no stock stream queue plays (`mclGetPlayType` 2, 3, `0xf1`, `0xf2`, whose network state stock's 500 ms `on_wm_timer_networkstatus` follows). Animations are untouched: a frame timer, an animator or a window animation keeps every idle at its old length, so their frames come as before.

Measured on pool emulator slot 1 (`BLUETOOTH=0`, Car Remote off except in the lit Home and dark idle baselines, whose pace it does not set, 60 s a state, demo's main thread's sleeps ended per second), `release/p32` at `9afab913` then this change: Home lit, a track paused, 45.5 to 28.4 (the loop's passes about 35 to 15 a second; the rest of the thread's wakes are its waits on stock's player locks); dark, idle, the DAC off, 5.1 to 2.1; dark and playing 11.0 to 6.2 (the emulator's 25 s tracks keep the player polls quick for their last 10 s); Now Playing lit and playing, 65.5 to 56.4, and a list lit with the level bars moving, 46.5 to 47.5, both at their frame timers' pace as before. A wheel tick to the framebuffer's change on lit, paused Home, from the input's write: median 9.3 ms (p90 10.8) after, 11.4 ms (p90 26.8) before. Frame gaps unchanged: the level bars on a list median 42.7 ms before, 42.9 after; bars and marquee median 36.5 ms before, 35.1 after (p90 53.2, 53.6); Home's art drift and a Centre press's row and page slide within run-to-run noise. ponytail: a source with no wake (a worker's result, q2guard, a Bluetooth link's end) is seen at most `LOOP_LIT_MAX_MS` late lit, which stock's 100 ms timer bounds to about 100 ms, and at most `LOOP_DARK_MAX_MS` dark and slow (headset disconnect's pause included); give such a source a `loop_wake` call where it lands if that shows.

### Cover threads

Stock's two art threads, started by `platform_init`, polled for work with nothing to do: `parse_albumcovertask_thd` (the Library's album grids, artist pages and folder rows) every 50 ms and `player_parsecover_thd` (Now Playing's art) every 100 ms, 30 wakeups a second on every lit screen. Each loop's only `usleep` (`COVER_WAITS` in `tools/build.py`) is a jal to `patch/cover_wake.c`: a thread with work keeps stock's pace between its tasks; one with none parks in a futex wait on a generation word of its own, `COVER_WAIT_S` (5 s) at most, and a request wakes it.

- **Now Playing's art.** The thread's work is the first byte of `g_play_cover_info`, the start flag. Only `player_set_coverinfo` sets it (`player_get_id3info` on a track change, `get_onlineid3info` through `tidal.c`'s `app_coverinfo`, and two stock page handlers at `0x52c7c8` and `0x5360f8`), and `player_get_coverinfo` clears it: those three are the only functions that reach the struct (its one GOT slot; no page-relative reference). `player_set_coverinfo` is hooked (`HOOKS`): `cover_set_info` runs stock's, then wakes the thread.
- **The Library's art.** The thread's work is `plist_albumtasklist` (a libcstl list, under `actasklist_mutex`) not empty while `albumcover_taskstate` is not 2 (a page scrolling pauses it), or a state of 3 to 6 (a cover cache to clear, then 0). About 35 stores to the state in 25 stock functions set it (a producer such as `local_albumcover_task` pushes its rows, then stores 1; a page's scroll stores 2 and its end the state it saved), with no one function to hook, so `ringnav_sleep` calls `cover_wake_poll` at the start of every UI pass: while the thread is parked and has work, it wakes it. A request made on the UI thread, as the pages' are, is seen in the pass that made it; one from another thread (`loadclasspthread`, a Tidal list) by the next pass.
- **No lost request.** The waker moves the generation before it reads `cover_parked`, and the thread marks itself parked before its last look at its work and waits only while the generation is the one it read first, so a request lands in that look or in a wake. ponytail: a request from another thread while the UI loop is stalled waits for the loop's next pass or the 5 s timeout.

Measured on a pool emulator (`BLUETOOTH=0`, 60 s a state, against the trunk at `d3f243fa`): the two threads' wakeups fell from 1,800 a minute to 24 (the timeout) on lit Home, Now Playing, Songs and Cover Flow scrolling, demo's from 7,857 to 6,019 on Home and 8,989 to 7,099 on Now Playing. Covers come sooner: Next to Now Playing's cover parsed 412 ms on average before, 323 after (12 changes each); Library > Albums' request to its first cover 181 ms, 151 after. Cover Flow loads its own art (`coverflow_loader.c`) and is unchanged.

### Charging

The status row's battery (`list_marks.c` `battery_slim`, from `navigation.c` `battery_now`'s key) fills to the level whatever the cable does; it once filled to the end while charging, which hid how much was left. Its fill is green while a cable charges it, with Phosphor's lightning (fill, 7 px, Text Primary) on the body's center and a 1 px gap in the Canvas cut round it where it crosses the fill (`tools/art.py` `inset_glyph`, `battbolt_d` and `_l`); green with an upright plug in the bolt's place (`plug_glyph`, drawn on whole pixels rather than from Phosphor, `battplug_d` and `_l`) on a cable that holds it full (`g_power_chargestate` 2) or at [Charge Limit](#charge-limit); white, or red under 20%, on a cable that charges nothing (USB DAC charging Off). The cable is `g_usbdet_value`, not stock's icon: `systembar_showface` picks `bar_charge` for a cable only while `g_power_chargestate` is not 2 (`0x541e2c`; at 2 it is `bar_battery`), and the plain icon over a USB DAC link with its charging Off (`g_usblink_status` 2, `g_usbmode` 1, `g_usbdac_chargeflag` 0), so a battery Full on the cable read as unplugged and was drawn white with no glyph (seen on a Q2 on 2026-11-17: status Full, 100%, VBUS in). `g_usbdet_value` is 0 while the Q2 is a USB host (`get_battery_capacity`), so its own bus power never counts. A charger too weak to keep up would make it orange with Phosphor's warning in the bolt's place (`battwarn_d`, `_l`), from `charging.c` `charge_weak`. ponytail: nothing reports that, so `charge_weak` is always 0 and the orange state is never reached. Searched: the kernel's AXP2101 driver (`axp2101-power-supply`; its strings name the battery's status, level, voltage, temperature and times to empty and full, and the BC1.2 detection enable `pmu_init_bc_en`, but no input current limit or charger type it reports), stock's `demo` (it reads only `battery/status` and `voltage_now`, plus the bq25890 paths of Shanling's other players) and these docs. A real signal, such as the PMIC's input-limit state or the battery's current going negative while it says Charging, would lift it; a guess from the level would not.

A tap on the battery toasts its state (`charging.c` `charge_tap`, from `status_row.c` `status_touch`, which takes `ringnav_input`'s pointer events turned upright from the panel's portrait axes: x is the event's y, y 319 less its x): a press inside a 44 x 40 px target round the body's center (the slot's, on Battery: Percent) (`SR_TAP_W`, `SR_TAP_H`; `status_slot_at`, in the bar's own pixels, the screen lit and `usable`; where it meets the level bars' target the nearer center has it) whose lift lands within `SR_TAP_SLOP` (12 px) of it and still on the same slot. The touch goes on to stock, so a pull down from the row still opens Control Center. The words come from the key the battery shows (`charge_words`): too weak, held at Charge Limit ("Charge Limit Reached (80%)", `CHARGE_STOP`), full, charging, under `BATT_LOW_PCT` (20%, where the fill turns red) "Low battery", else "Battery" and the level. The toast waits for the next UI loop pass (`charging_poll`, from `usb_ui_poll`), as the USB toasts do, and is `toast_icon`'s: 16 px each side, a 15 px glyph, 8 px before the words.

The cable's own feedback (`charging.c`, its look in [oled-design: Plug-in screen](oled-design.md#plug-in-screen)). `usb_ui_status` calls `charge_plugged` at every cable put in after its first pass (`det_known`): a cable already in at boot is no plug-in, as a plug-in screen then would turn the screen off under the boot. With the screen off (`g_backlight_status` clear; Buttons Lock is the dark screen's alone, so a locked Q2 is a dark one), the next UI loop pass (`charging_poll`, from `usb_ui_poll`, not stock's USB pass) lights it as `keylock.c`'s card does (painted first, then `enable_fb` and `screen_action(1)`) and paints the plug-in screen over the top window and the status bar (`charge_paint`, from `ringnav_paint`) for `S1_MS` (3 s), a frame every `S1_FRAME_MS` (50 ms), then turns the screen off again (`screen_action(0)`). Not while a video or a card game has the screen. A key or a touch while it shows (`charge_gate`, in `ringnav_input` after Buttons Lock's) ends it with the screen left on and is dropped down to its release; a window opening over it (the chooser for a computer, `awake_screen`) ends it the same way, so the screen stays on for that. Its level is `g_power_capacity` at the plug-in. With the screen on there is no screen: `usb_charger_in` (a cable no computer answered within `USB_PROBE_MS`, or a remembered Charge Only) toasts the battery's state as a tap would (T1, "Charging · 62%"); a computer gets the chooser instead. `system.c`'s `charge_poll` toasts "Charged to 80%" (`charge_limited`, T3) when Charge Limit first holds charging off on a cable, and `charging_poll` toasts "Charger too weak" (T6) when `charge_weak` turns 1 on a cable, which nothing does yet. Unplugged (T2), OK to Disconnect (T4) and USB Audio Ready (T5) are [USB pages](#usb-pages)' (`usb_ui.c`). Every one waits for the next pass (`feedback.c` `toast_later`, shown by `toast_later_poll` from `usb_ui_poll`; the last asked for wins) and shows only with the screen on.

A cable in also chirps in the headphones (`charge_plugged` → `clicker.c` `clicker_chirp`): `{mcl-click\charge}` on the player's socket, which q2player mixes into what it plays as it mixes the Clicker's clicks ([player-plan: The Clicker](player-plan.md#the-clicker)), a 340 ms tick and two rising blips. The Q2 has no speaker but the MCU's buzzer, which can only click, so the chirp is never the buzzer's. It is sent under Clicker Headphones or Both, and only while q2player plays a song (`player_mixes`); paused, stopped or on the stock hciplayer there is none: q2player's PCM is closed then, and hciplayer keeps its PCM (`hw:1,0`, no `dmix`) open and muted while paused and mixes nothing while it plays ([Key Tone](#key-tone)), so a sound of its own would have to open the device under the player or stop it. Mixing while it plays and skipping otherwise disturbs nothing.

## ALSA startup lock

The stock ALSA 1.1.6 library can deadlock with an ioplug behind `plug`. Preparation locks the wrapper while the ioplug callback unlocks and relocks its slave, leaving a slave mutex owned by the setup thread, so the writer blocks at its first write. `q2video` sets `LIBASOUND_THREAD_SAFE=0` in its own process before opening ALSA. Its PCM calls are sequential: setup precedes the writer, and drop, prepare and close follow joining it. BlueALSA's locks, the local player, the codecs and the services are unchanged.

To reproduce the old hang and verify the fix against the stock MIPS library, run `python3 test/alsa.py BUILD QEMU_MIPSEL`. The regression covers one and two plug layers and rate conversion.

## Audio writes and the queue checkpoint

The shared audio writer keeps partial ALSA writes and retries the remaining frames after an underrun, instead of discarding unwritten samples. Native tests exercise partial writes, zero progress, recovery and lost outputs. This is independent of the ALSA startup lock workaround.

Queue and traversal changes commit the full queue snapshot, for queues up to `SAVE_LIMIT` (999) tracks; a larger one keeps no snapshot (it would be rewritten whole on every track change), so a reboot resumes it as stock does. `ringnav_memory` reads none larger either, so a damaged header asks for no more memory than a real snapshot takes (about 1 MB; `QUEUE_LIMIT`'s would be 68 MB). Version 3 snapshots carry Play Next's pending list after the history (count, then indices). A version 2 file, written before the list existed, restores its one run (`forced`, `force_end` in its header) as the list, in order; the next save writes version 3. Without advanced play a local queue (folder, `MCL_TYPE` 1, or library, `0xfxxx`; not AirPlay) is kept too, while Memory Playback or car mode is on (the only readers; off, the save returns without touching the file, and one left from before is rewritten within 5 s of the setting coming back on, as the queue's hash no longer matches `saved_queue`, or at power-off), as a version 4 snapshot: version 3's layout with the queue's own order twice, nothing seen, no history or Play Next list, the cursor at the track. `ringnav_memory` loads it without `rebuild`, so it comes back as it was, still without advanced play; stock's Memory Playback record could only rebuild a queue from its class and source album or folder, so a queue grown with Play Next or Add to Queue came back as the whole library at the same track. Play Next and Add to Queue mark it dirty; stock's own edits (View Queue's delete) are seen by hashing the whole queue (`queue_hash`, `saved_queue`) each save, at most every 5 s and every 30 s while playing on, after the `SAVE_LIMIT` check. An empty queue saves nothing, so the UI loop's first passes at boot don't drop the snapshot before Home restores it, and nor does a position outside the queue. The snapshot and its checkpoint are on the card, `.q2pod/ringnav-queue` and `ringnav-queue-elapsed` ([Where Q2 Muse writes](#where-q2-muse-writes)): a queue's songs are there too. With the card away a save is kept in RAM (a snapshot up to `QUEUE_HELD_MAX`, 256 KB; a larger one fails and is retried as below) and written at the next poll that finds the card; a dropped snapshot leaves the card's file empty, which reads as none, so the flash's `/mnt/data/ringnav-queue` from earlier releases, read and copied to the card once while the card has none, is not restored again. Elapsed-only changes atomically replace the 16-byte `ringnav-queue-elapsed` checkpoint, which applies only when it matches the snapshot's checksum and position. The UI loop writes it every 30 s while the same track plays on and within 5 s of a pause, seek or track change, and retries a failed write every 30 s (a full snapshot rebuilt and synced each time, so a failing card isn't hammered every 5 s); power-off (`ringnav_savequeue`) writes the exact second. A crash mid-track resumes up to 30 s early. The progress check itself runs at most every five seconds (`playback.poll_stamp`), so UI passes between checkpoints do not repeatedly take the playback-time mutex.

**Reboots.** Stock writes Memory Playback's record (`save_memoryplay_info`, `0x521058`: play class, track, second and the album or folder the queue came from, through `write_memory_to_file`) only from `into_poweroff`, the power-off page's. `device_reboot` (`0x502004`: Power's Restart, a long power-key press on the power-off page, and `on_wm_idle_status`'s Bluetooth recovery) and the firmware update never call it, so after a TF card update or Network Update the Q2 resumed the queue and second of the last power-off, however long ago. Both now save first (`ringnav_reboot` and `ringnav_checkfw` in `patch/playback.c`), through the hooked `save_memoryplay_info`, so the snapshot's exact second is written too. The update saves when its dialog opens (`dialog_checkfw_dialog_init`, `0x49982c`, after stock's confirmation, both rows'), since that init stops the player before its thread (`0x499548`) runs `update_firmware` and the countdown's `device_reboot`. A stopped player (`mclGetPlayStatus` 1) saves nothing, as stock's save skips it, so that later `device_reboot` leaves the saved place alone and the snapshot keeps its second. When the reboot is stock's Bluetooth recovery (`bt_initstatus` -102), `ringnav_reboot` first leaves `q2-crash.log` ([Bluetooth boot reconnect](#bluetooth-boot-reconnect)).

## M4B recognition and audit

Stock has two audio extension checks: folder enumeration at `0x5d4cac` and recursive scanning at `0x5d69fc`. Both also feed playlist loading. `ringnav_audio_extension` accepts `.m4b` case-insensitively and otherwise calls the original `strstr` with its original format list. The builder asserts the original import load and call bytes before replacing each call; `audio_extension_calls` records both edits in the manifest and packaging audit. The installed TagLib already sends M4B to the MP4 constructor, and the decoder probes the original MP4 container. Neither needs a binary dispatch change. Cover extraction has a separate extension dispatcher in `libtag_c.so.2.0.1`, which stock recognizes as MP4 artwork only for M4A/MP4. `patch_m4b_cover` in `tools/build.py` checks the whole library hash and adds a case-insensitive M4B comparison that reaches the existing MP4 image extractor. Its 48-byte appended segment is read/execute only, uses relative branches and GP-relative data, and preserves the other formats. Now Playing retains stock’s external folder-cover fallback when embedded extraction fails; Coverflow retains its folder-image fallback. Files and paths are preserved. `test/m4b.py` executes the native metadata and cover dispatchers at two load addresses, while `test/patch.py` covers the patched checks, short-book persistence and shared resume/count exclusions.

## Headset controls and volume

`patch/headset.c` restores the AACP handshake and AVRCP input from `6799d59`, without the battery state or connection card. One generation-tagged worker uses nonblocking socket/input I/O and one `select` over both descriptors, up to 1 s a pass, so a still connection wakes it once a second. It rescans for the AVRCP input (the `/dev/input/event*` node whose name ends in ` (AVRCP)`, read to uinput's 79 characters with `EVIOCGNAME(80)`: a 64-byte read cut a long name before the mark, so a headset named past 55 characters never had its keys read) each pass for the first 10 passes, then every 2nd, and retries AACP every 5th. It drains the AACP socket each pass (AirPods send other reports between ear reports), validates complete ear packets, retries discovery throughout a connection, queues only key presses, and closes descriptors on disconnect. The UI loop discards stale generations and dispatches commands every 100 ms. No player API runs on the worker.

The internal dispatcher chooses video, radio, Spotify, then the stock local/Tidal player, independently of the visible page. Explicit play/pause operations and session identities support ear detection; the number of buds originally worn (counted, since the report's primary/secondary slots swap when the primary leaves an ear), a manual-command epoch and the player/session identity gate automatic resume. Recent AVRCP pauses are coordinated with ear reports, and duplicate commands are suppressed. Player starts, track changes, manual controls and disconnects invalidate pending resume. Video retains its commands and adds idempotent `a`/`r` pause/resume, an atomic pause-state file and a separate `g` gain command. Radio resumes the current station by restarting it.

Bluetooth output remembers `PLAYSET BT_VOLUME` independently of wired/USB's stock `PLAYSET VOLUME`. The `write_int_config` hook routes volume saves to the active output's key; the `mclSetOutputWay` hook saves the departing level and restores the incoming one before stock switches output, clamped to the volume limit, then applies it to the mixer. A missing or invalid saved level inherits the current volume. Stock boot volume behavior keeps the wired key. While receiving Bluetooth audio from a phone, the gear's Playback and its submenus accept normal wheel navigation; the receiver player and volume dialog keep stock volume control. A headset's own volume (its absolute volume, below) moves the Q2's on any page and with the screen off: [Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)'s rule is the wheel's alone. A headset's change shows at once with the screen lit, as a wheel's does (`vol_show`, `patch/volume.c`, from `bt_volume_poll`): the volume dialog in front takes the value and its 3 s start again (stock's close count, `VOL_DIALOG_COUNT`, zeroed as its own keyup zeroes it); Control Center's slider eases to it (`level_follow`); Playback's Volume page (`xfade_open` 4) and its row follow it (`xfade_volume_shown`); over any other window stock's `dialog/volume_dialog` opens on it, Now Playing's band or the panel (`vol_paint`), so for 3 s the wheel is the volume there as on Now Playing. Not with the screen off, over a video (its own volume) or over another dialog (a confirmation card), whose keys the volume dialog would take.

**Bluetooth → Link Volume** (`Q2POD BTVOLLINK`, `bt_vol_link`, a `pod_rows` switch after Resume on Connect, last in the Bluetooth page's Audio group; stock's word was Control Device Volume) never chosen, follows the device connected now (`bt_link`, `patch/nav/rows_settings.c`): on for headphones and headsets (its Class of Device, which the battery loop reads, `bt_headset_class`, is `bt_kind`'s headphones: major Audio/Video, minor 1, 2 or 6), off for a speaker, a car or a device whose Class is not known yet. A device whose own volume tracks the Q2's turns down with it, so a low Q2 volume plays thin through a speaker's weak amplifier stage; headphones have no such stage and are expected to follow. A choice saved (`BTVOLLINK` 0 or 1) applies to every device; the switch shows what applies now, and a click saves the other way from there. Off, the Q2's volume is stock's software gain alone and the device keeps its own volume, never read or written (`bt_audio_ready` is 0, so `ringnav_btvol` passes the levels straight to stock, `headset_gain` is `g_volume` and `bt_volume_poll` stops), and Rockbox's launch leaves the device's volume alone too. The Class arrives with the battery loop's first read, a few seconds into a connection, so headphones start linked from then. On, the rest of this section applies. A switch while Bluetooth plays resets the sync and re-applies the volume at once (`headset_volume_reset`, `device_set_volume`): off, stock's gain comes back; on, the next poll writes the Q2's level to the device.

With it on, volume starts by writing the Q2's saved volume to the headset, unless the headset's level already reads as it, so a level of the headset's own that reads as the same volume is left alone. The Q2's 0 to 100 reaches the headset's 0 to 127 on a curve (`bt_vol_curve`, `bt_vol_avrcp`, `patch/nav/playback_power.c`): 0 silent, 100 its top, and between them 127 × 10^(−40 dB × (100 − v) / 100 / 20), the same 0.4 dB a step, never rising slower than 127 v / 400 (below v 58, where AVRCP's whole steps are coarser than the curve's), and at least 1 above 0. A straight 127 v / 100 put the top half of the Q2's range in the headset's last 6 dB on a headset that takes the value as a gain, so half volume was already loud. Half volume is now 16 of 127, 80 is 51, 90 is 80. A headset level reads back as the volume whose curve level is nearest, the lowest of those sharing it (`bt_vol_q2`), so a level the Q2 wrote reads back as a volume that writes the same level. ponytail: 40 dB is a choice for a headset that takes the value as a linear gain, as the Px7 seemed to; one with its own taper on the value comes out quieter in the lower half, and `bt_vol_curve` is the one table to change. Polling then consumes headset changes, maps 0–127 back to 0–100, enforces the configured limit, saves Q2 state and shows the change (above). The change comes by BlueZ's signal (`patch/bt_vol_event.c`): bluetoothd emits `PropertiesChanged` on `org.bluez.MediaTransport1` when the headset's absolute volume moves, by its keys or by our write. On the first ready pass `bt_volume_poll` starts a thread that connects to the system bus (`/var/run/dbus/system_bus_socket`) and speaks the wire protocol itself, as demo imports neither libdbus nor gio nor `dlsym`: SASL `EXTERNAL` with its uid, `Hello`, and `AddMatch` for that signal from `org.bluez` with `arg0` the transport's interface; then it sleeps in `recv`, frames each message the bus sends by its fixed header and counts each signal whose header names `PropertiesChanged`. The UI loop's next pass sees the count change and reads the level (`btctl_transport_get_volume`) at once, so a lit change opens the volume overlay on that pass (within 8 ms, 25 ms idle); a burst (the wheel's own writes echoed back, a held key) reads at most once every `BT_VOLUME_EVENT_GAP_MS` (400 ms, the old lit pace). With the signal subscribed, the timed read is a fallback every `BT_VOLUME_FALLBACK_MS` (5 s), lit or dark, for a stack or headset that sends none; the dark volume limit is held on the signal too. A headset that refused absolute volume keeps `BT_VOLUME_SLOW_MS`. No bus, a refused login or the bus gone ends the thread, and the timed reads take over as they were without it: 400 ms lit, `BT_VOLUME_LIMIT_MS` dark under a volume limit, else `BT_VOLUME_SLOW_MS`. The match also passes the transport's other properties (`State`, `Delay`), each one read that finds the level unchanged. Remembering the accepted absolute value prevents feedback loops. Confirmed headset volume uses full helper gain except at zero; unsupported or failed reads/writes restore software gain. Spotify, radio and video consume the same effective gain. The AAC 48 kHz capability fix remains in place.

`test/patch.py`'s headset cases run routing, ear counts and slot swaps, single-bud listening, first reports, manual cancellation, player/session changes, duplicate commands, malformed reports and volume limits against the MIPS payload. `test/headset_io.py` runs the actual worker with simulated kernel I/O, including late input discovery, handshake, draining queued reports, release/repeat filtering, cleanup and stale reconnect reports. `test/fw/test_bt_vol_event.py` checks the login, `Hello` and `AddMatch` bytes, the framing (split reads, two in one, an oversized message dropped, a big-endian sender's), the pace with the signal, and the overlay opening on the pass after a signal with the clock unmoved; where the machine has `dbus-daemon` and dbus-python it also logs in to a real daemon and hears a signal sent by a process owning `org.bluez`, while another interface's is filtered out.

## Resume on Connect

Two paths start playback when a headset connects. Stock's `checkBluetoothStatus` (`0x4fd42c`), once a headset's A2DP comes up with the Q2 as the source, runs `player_save_stop` (saves `mclGetPlayStatus` unless stopped, then `mclStop`), `config_outputchannel(2, 3)`, `device_set_volume` and `player_save_start(0)` (`0x4fdcbc`). That restarts the saved local or Tidal queue unpaused, so a paused queue plays, and a stopped queue with a stale saved status starts over Spotify or Internet Radio (`mclStartPlayer`'s hook yields them). AirPods also send AVRCP PLAY as the link comes up, which `headset_command` turns into a start for whichever player is active.

**Bluetooth → Resume on Connect** (`ringnav_btrows`, hooking stock's list builder `0x4c3ef8`, which rebuilds the whole list on every search and link change; `Q2POD RESUME` in `config.ini`; On, 1, is stock's behavior) is Off by default. With Bluetooth on, the row is in the page's Audio group after Headset Volume ([Bluetooth page](#bluetooth-page)), text only and 78 high like stock's rows; with Bluetooth off it isn't added. The jalr at `0x4fdcbc` becomes `jal ringnav_bt_connect_start`, which, unless a card game has the sound (A game with the sound, under Card apps), with the setting On calls `player_save_start(0)` as stock; Off, it lets a playing queue go on, reloads a paused one paused (`player_save_start(1)`, as stock's disconnect does) and starts nothing for a stopped queue or while a stream owns playback. Off, `headset_command` also drops PLAY (200, 207, or 164 while nothing plays) within `CONNECT_HOLD_MS` (5 s) of the link, which covers the worker's AVRCP discovery (about a second) and the headset's PLAY after A2DP setup; a press after that plays. Ear detection is a separate path: the first ear report after a connect never resumes, and putting worn buds back resumes only what removing them paused, with the setting either way. AirPlay and DLNA keep their senders' control (stock skips the restart while AirPlay plays).

## Wi-Fi page flows

Settings > Wi-Fi is stock's page (`systemset_wifi_page_init`, its list rebuilt by `wifimenu_rows_build`, `0x4d5950`), with `patch/wifi_flows.c` hooked onto four of its pieces: the switch and Search Again rows' click (`wifimenu_switch_row`, `0x4d61e0`; stock names the rows `0` and `1`), a network row's click (`wifimenu_network_row`, `0x4d62d8`; the button named by its scan record's index in `wifi_showlist`), the list's builder, and `network_checkstatus` (`0x518cf0`, stock's 500 ms Wi-Fi poll from `on_wm_timer_networkstatus`).

**A join that is trying.** Both click handlers return at once while `wifi_connectstatus` is 1, and a join stays at 1 for up to a minute: `network_checkstatus` counts `wifilink_timeout` down from 30 per poll and, with the radio still associated (`networkGetPhysicStatus` 1), grants one more 30. So the switch could not turn Wi-Fi off, nor a row be pressed, until the join gave up. Now the switch ends the join first, with the steps stock's own timeout takes (`networkDisconnect`, `wifi_name` cleared, status 0, without the toast), and stock's click then turns Wi-Fi off (`wifi_switch`'s off clears the rest and stops `wpa_supplicant`). The joining network's own row ends the join the same way and the list is rebuilt, the row idle again; another row stays stock's. Search Again during a join says "Connecting to Wi-Fi…". Control Center's Wi-Fi circle ends a trying join the same way (`wifi_flows_cancel_join`, called by `cc_act` before it clicks stock's switch), so a tap or Centre there turns Wi-Fi off at once too.

**Search Again.** Stock's click runs `wifi_scan`, which starts the scan and sets `wifi_searchtime` to 10; the page's timer counts it down and rebuilds the list when it reaches 0. OLED's "Searching..." line is written only when the list is laid out (`wifi_rows.c` `wifi_rows_pre`), so a search showed nothing until it had ended, and the row seemed dead. `wifi_busy_show` writes the line as the click returns.

**A failed join asks again.** Stock's timeout returns 2 from `network_checkstatus`, and its caller turns that into "connect failed" (`msg_linkerror`) and nothing else; the password tried was saved by the join (`networkAddSsid`), so the next tap on the network joined with it again unasked. While a join tries, the hook samples `wpa_supplicant`'s `wpa_state` from `g_wifiStatus` (`+0xd8`, written by stock's monitor thread from `STATUS` once a second): a join that reached `4WAY_HANDSHAKE` (or `GROUP_HANDSHAKE`) and never `COMPLETED` was refused its key, as `wpa_supplicant` judges it (`events.c` `could_be_psk_mismatch`), and reads "Wrong password"; one that never got there reads "Couldn't connect". When the failed network asks for a password and the Wi-Fi page is in use, the hook returns 1 (the page rebuilds, no stock toast) and a timer opens stock's password entry (`kbwifipass_dialog`) for it, its empty box's tips the reason. A password entered replaces the saved one (`wifi_action_deleterecord`, then `wifi_action_connect`); Cancel, or an OK with no password fit for the network (`networkCheckSsidPassword`; Return can give one, empty), keeps it. The entry opens from a timer, as stock's own dialogs open from `on_wm_timer_dialog`: opened from `ringnav_sleep`'s polls it took no input until it closed. An open network's failure, or one off the page, keeps stock's toast.

**Forget and Reset.** Stock's Forget is a tap on a saved row's right end (`check_wifinextaction`'s x range 276 to 375), which the wheel cannot reach. Play/Pause held on a saved network's row (`wifi_flows_hold`, from `ringnav_keylong`) asks "Forget *name*?" on the confirmation card, then runs stock's `wifi_action_deleterecord`. **Reset Network Settings**, the list's last row on and off, asks on the card and puts `/mnt/data/wpa_supplicant.conf` back to the shipped one (`/release/assets/default/raw/wpa_supplicant.conf`, no network in it) rather than removing it as stock's Reset Settings does before its reboot: `wifi_connect.sh` starts no `wpa_supplicant` without the file. With Wi-Fi on it goes off first and comes back searching, and stock's saved list is read again (`networkClearSsid`, `networkGetSsidList`).

`test/fw/test_wifi_flows.py` holds each flow. In the emulator, which has no radio, a stand-in `wpa_cli` in the slot's rootfs printing a scan (stock reads `wpa_cli scan_result > /tmp/scan_result` and skips its first line, `Selected interface`) lists networks, and `Q2EMU_WIFI=0` lets a join time out.

## Wi-Fi transfer

Stock's Wi-Fi transfer page (thttpd on port 8888, `/usr/share/web`: `index.html`, `js/index.js` on jQuery File Upload 5.40.1 and five CGIs) is patched in place by `patch_web` (`WEB` in `tools/build.py`: exact replacements, each checked against the audited stock file, and no Chinese may be left). Every string is in English. The extension filter (client-side only; `upload.cgi` takes any file) adds the formats Q2 Muse's pages read: M4B, MP4, M4V, MKV, AVI, MOV, MPG and TXT (EQ presets). The breadcrumb, which `index.js` builds as HTML from the folder path, takes each folder's name as text (`_esc`, `ESC_JS`): a folder named like markup would otherwise run as script in the page, with the page's access to the card.

**Folders.** **Upload Folder** is a second file input with `webkitdirectory`, sharing the upload widget (`fileInput`). A picked folder's files carry `webkitRelativePath` (`Album/CD1/01.flac`), a dropped folder's (the plugin walks it; patched to call `readEntries` until it returns none, as Chromium gives at most 100 entries a call) `relativePath` (`Album/CD1/`); either way the file goes to the current folder plus that path, and its dot files (`.DS_Store`, macOS's `._` copies) are skipped silently. Stock's `upload.cgi` only moves the part into `path` (`mv "%s" "%s" -f`), so `_mkdir` first makes each folder with stock's `create` (`mkdir "%s"`, no `-p`), parents first, once per batch (`_made`, cleared when the batch stops): one that exists fails harmlessly, and a folder that really couldn't be made shows as its files' upload errors. A file's row shows the upload panel as it is added and can be canceled while its folders are made; the panel hides (and `_made` clears) only once no row is left, since the plugin's `stop` fires whenever no upload is in flight, also between files that wait on a folder. The five CGIs the page calls are Q2 Muse's own (**Safe file manager**), so a name holding `"`, `` ` `` or `$` now uploads and is kept as typed.

<a id="safe-file-manager"></a>**Safe file manager.** Stock's five file-manager CGIs (`usr/share/web/cgi-bin/{create,delete,list,download,upload}.cgi`, built on the CGIC library) build a shell command from the request and hand it to `system()` — `create` runs `mkdir "%s"`, `delete` `rm -rf "%s"`, `upload` `mv "%s" "%s" -f` — with the `path` field or the uploaded file's name in the `%s`. A name holding `$(…)` or a backtick therefore runs as a command, as root, and `download` and `list` open and list a `path` that climbs out of the card with `../`; the web root's `/create` … `/download` are symlinks to the same `cgi-bin/*.cgi`, so both routes reach the sink. `tools/build.py` replaces all five with one busybox-ash script, `q2cgi` (`assets/web/q2cgi`, installed as `/usr/bin/q2cgi`), which each `cgi-bin/*.cgi` runs ([Privileges](#wi-fi-transfer-root)), so every route reaches it with no bypass. It dispatches on the basename of `SCRIPT_NAME` and performs each operation with argv — `mkdir -p -- "$d"`, `rm -rf -- "$d"`, `cat -- "$f"`, and for an upload `head -c … > "$out"` and `mv` — never a shell command built from the request, so shell command injection is structurally impossible rather than filtered. `validate` URL-decodes each path (from the query or the POST body; a multipart field is taken raw), refuses a NUL, control characters (which could also inject an HTTP header), any component that begins with a dot (one rule that covers a `..` traversal, a `.` self-component that would otherwise let `rm`/`mkdir` reach the card root, and a hidden file such as `.scrobble.ini` — so hidden files are refused for a direct `download`/`delete`/`list`, not only hidden from the listing), any path not under `/mnt/mmc`, and a duplicate `path` field; `confine` then resolves the path's deepest existing ancestor with `realpath` and re-checks it is under the card, so a symlink on a non-FAT card (the SD card can be NTFS, which the stock mdev script mounts with `ntfs-3g`, or reformatted) cannot redirect an operation off-card where the purely lexical `validate` could not see it. `hidden` then covers a hidden entry asked for by another name: FAT32 keeps an 8.3 short name beside every long one and the kernel resolves either, in any case, so `.scrobble.ini` is also `SCROBB~1.INI` and `.spotify` `SPOTIF~1`, names the dot rule passes (by them a hidden file was read, replaced and deleted on a FAT32 image, and a file put in a hidden folder). It walks the path's existing components and refuses one that is the same file (`[ -ef ]`: device and inode) as a dot-entry of its folder, holding the component open meanwhile, because vfat numbers an inode at its first lookup and may give it another once it has left the cache. Names aren't compared, so an ordinary name in another case, or an ordinary file's own short name, works as before; an upload's whole destination is checked as well, so a file named like a hidden file's short name can't replace it. exFAT keeps no short names. `confine` makes the same test of the place a symlink leads to, because `hidden` holds a component only against the dot-entries of its own folder: through a link in another folder to a hidden one (`Music/peek` to `/mnt/mmc/.spotify`, possible on an NTFS card) that folder was listed, read and written. A hard link (NTFS has them, for files only) can also give a hidden file an ordinary name in another folder, and that name is left to work: the page can't make one, telling it from any other file would take a walk of the whole card at every request, and through it the hidden file is only read, under the name its owner gave it (an upload renames a new file over the name and a delete unlinks the name, so neither changes the file; in the hidden file's own folder such a name is refused, as a short name is). A hidden entry's short name is refused (400) where a name that isn't there is not found (404), so whether it exists can be told. That is left, as FAT tells it anyway: a new long-named entry takes the next free short name (a new `spotifyprobe` is `SPOTIF~2` when `.spotify` holds `SPOTIF~1`) and answers by it. The dot rule also takes a name to be stored as asked. vfat's `uni_xlate` mount option turns `:002e` into a dot, but the card is mounted without options (the stock mdev script's `ntfs-3g`, else a plain `mount`, and the player's own `mount %s /mnt/mmc`), and vfat then refuses a `:`. An upload's file name is refused if it holds a `/`, begins with a dot, or holds a control character. Because the operation is argv, a name holding `$`, `` ` ``, `"` or `\` is stored and served exactly as given — where stock's shell mangled it — so the client-side name check `index.js` already applies is the only limit on names. The replies match stock's: `create`/`delete` answer `{}` as JSON, `list` the same JSON array of `{path,name,ctime[,size]}` objects (sorted client-side by `ctime`), `download` the file with its `Content-Disposition`/`Content-Length`/`application/octet-stream` headers, and `upload` a small JSON body (the jQuery File Upload widget only reloads on success). The script runs as root under the stock busybox ash, like the CGIs it replaces, and answers nothing until the request carries the session cookie the PIN gets (**PIN**, below). thttpd gives a CGI `PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/ucb:/bin:/usr/bin`, so the applets resolve. The device busybox (v1.31.1) has no `stat` applet (verified on the stock binary under qemu), so a size comes from `ls -ln` field 5 — which `ls` fills from `stat(2)` without reading the file, so a listing of large media stays cheap — and an mtime from `date -r`; `realpath` is called through `busybox` so `confine`'s resolver never depends on a PATH symlink. The listing omits dot-entries and `System Volume Information`, as stock's does. `CONTENT_LENGTH` must be a positive integer (so a negative value cannot turn `head -c` into an unbounded read) and the `create`/`delete` body is read as exactly `CONTENT_LENGTH` bytes, 64 KB at most: bounded, so one request cannot exhaust the device's RAM, and never to end-of-file, because thttpd gives a CGI the client's socket as stdin unless it already holds part of the body, and the socket stays open until the answer (a POST whose body followed its headers in a second segment, and every GET, went unanswered by stock's thttpd). An upload is streamed, so the file's bytes reach the card once and it needs free space of its own size, as stock's did (#341's first version stored the whole request and then copied the file out of it, which took twice the space). The page sends the `path` field and then the one file (`sequentialUploads`), so everything before the file's bytes is a few short text lines: ash's `read` takes them one byte at a time, which leaves the file's bytes in stdin, and `wc -c` counts what it took (ash's `${#}` counts UTF-8 characters, in any locale). `read -n 8192` bounds a line and 64 KB the lines together. Each field is a line of its own, so an LF in a value ends the line early and the next line is then not the boundary, which refuses the upload: in #342's parser, an LF sent in the `path` field passed a line of its own for the content's offset, and the sender's envelope was stored as the file. A part other than `path` and the file, a second `path`, or a file before the `path` is refused too. The destination and name are checked before a byte is written; then `head -c` copies the rest of the request (the file and `\r\n--boundary--\r\n`) to `/mnt/mmc/.q2upload/out.<pid>`. A file shorter than that rest (the client stopped) or an ending other than exactly that boundary is refused. `dd if=/dev/null of=… bs=1 seek=<size>` then truncates the boundary off, with no copy, and `mv` renames the file into place on the same card, so a reader never sees a half-written file under the real name and a failed write leaves none. A work file an interrupted upload leaves behind, whose owner PID is no longer in `/proc`, is reaped on the next upload. ponytail: a crafted body with a second file part stores it as bytes of the first file (only a scan of the whole file after writing it could tell; it writes no second file, and a sender can put any bytes in a file anyway); a request whose fields come in another order, or which ends without the final CRLF, is refused, as every browser and curl send the page's order and that ending; a name holding a `/` is refused rather than making folders, since the client sends folder structure through the `path` field.

<a id="wi-fi-transfer-pin"></a>**PIN.** Stock serves the card to anyone on the same Wi-Fi network while the page is open: no login, and the page's whole UI is the five CGIs. `patch/wifi_transfer.c` hooks the two stock functions that bracket a session. `switch_wifitransport` (`0x519b30`; 1 runs `thttpd -C /etc/thttpd.conf` through `toolsSystemd`, 0 runs `killall -9 thttpd` and sets `g_wifitransport_flag`) is called with 1 by `systemset_wifitransport_page_init` and with 0 by the page's `EVT_WINDOW_CLOSE` handler (`0x4d7600`), so the server lives exactly as long as the page; `ringnav_wifi_transfer` writes a new session before thttpd starts and removes it after thttpd is killed. A session is `/tmp/q2wifi` (mode 0700, on the `/tmp` tmpfs, so never on the card or in flash): `pin`, six digits, and `token`, 32 hex digits, both read from `/dev/urandom` (the PIN is a 32-bit draw below 4,294,000,000, the largest multiple of a million under 2^32, taken mod a million, so every PIN is equally likely; a draw over the line is taken again). If `/dev/urandom` can't be read, no session is made and thttpd isn't started, and the page says so. `ringnav_wifi_transfer_page` (the page init's hook, after stock's) hides the page's picture (`img_wifitransport`) and puts the PIN in its place, in 56 px type as two groups of three under a line naming it, so it sits between the title and the address (the 320-pixel screen has no room under the address). q2cgi checks before anything else: with no `/tmp/q2wifi` every route answers 403; `cgi-bin/auth.cgi` (q2cgi again, through an inode the build adds beside stock's five) takes the PIN as a POST field and answers it with `Set-Cookie: q2s=<token>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`; every other route answers 401 unless one of the request's `q2s` cookies (thttpd passes `HTTP_COOKIE`; it passes no other request header a CGI could use) is the token. The PIN is sent once, in a POST body, never in a URL; the cookie is what rides on every request after, including a download's plain navigation, which a same-site cookie still gets. `HttpOnly` keeps it from script on the page, and `SameSite=Strict` keeps another site the browser has open from sending a request with it (stock's page could be driven from any web page the user visited, by a form posted to the Q2's address). Secrets are compared as their SHA-256 digests (`sha256sum`, a busybox applet on the Q2), so the time a comparison takes says nothing about how much of a guess is right. Tries are limited by folders: `auth` claims one of `try.1` to `try.5` with `mkdir`, which is atomic, before it reads the PIN, gives it back (`rmdir`) when the PIN is right and keeps it when it is wrong, so five wrong PINs, however many are sent at once, leave none and every later try answers 429 until transfer is turned off and on again, which makes a new PIN. A browser that already has the cookie keeps working through a lockout, so someone else guessing can't cut off the user, only use up the tries; the page then shows **Locked** in place of the PIN (`wifi_transfer_poll` sees `try.5`). A wrong cookie, a malformed one or none is not a try: the token is 128 random bits, so there is nothing to guess. The web page (`PIN_JS`, `PIN_HTML` in `tools/build.py`) opens a PIN box on any 401, so a page left open across a restart of transfer asks for the new PIN, and says how many tries are left after a wrong one. Six digits and five tries give a guesser one chance in 200,000 per session. ponytail: the connection is plain HTTP, as stock's is, so anyone who can read the Wi-Fi's traffic (an open network, or a member of a WPA2-Personal one who captured the join) sees the PIN's POST and the cookie; TLS would need a certificate the browser trusts, which a device with no name and an address from DHCP can't have. Tested by `test/wifi_transfer_cgi.sh`'s PIN cases.

<a id="wi-fi-transfer-idle"></a>**Idle off.** Each admitted request touches `/tmp/q2wifi/seen` and holds `busy.<pid>` while it runs (removed by its `EXIT` trap). `wifi_transfer_poll` (from `power_poll`, once a second while a session is live) restarts its count when `seen`'s mtime changes or a `busy.<pid>` names a running process, and after 10 minutes of neither (`WT_IDLE_MS`, counted on `time_now_ms`'s monotonic clock, so a time sync can't end it early) closes the page with `window_close`. That is the close handler Return would reach, so stock stops thttpd and the hook removes the session; a toast says why. A long upload or download is one request that is busy for as long as it runs, so it is never cut off. Requests that fail the PIN check don't count, so a stranger's requests can't keep transfer on.

<a id="wi-fi-transfer-root"></a>**Privileges.** Stock's `/etc/thttpd.conf` said `user=root`, so thttpd 2.29 parsed every request as root, before any PIN check. The build makes it `user=www-data` (`THTTPD_USER`; uid 33 in stock's `/etc/passwd`, `WWW_DATA`): thttpd binds :8888, writes its pid file and opens `/tmp/thttpd.log` as root, then drops to www-data (checked with stock's binary under qemu: `Uid: 33 33 33 33`, the page and its scripts served as before), and demo's `killall -9 thttpd` still ends it. thttpd can't then read `/tmp/q2wifi` (root's, mode 0700), so the PIN and token stay out of its reach. The card can't follow it: the stock mdev script (`/etc/mdev/add_removesd.sh`) mounts it with `ntfs-3g`, or a plain `mount`, with no `uid=`, `gid=` or `umask=`, and `usbmode_exit` mounts it again the same way after USB storage (`mount %s /mnt/mmc`, loaded at `0x542a28`), so a FAT or exFAT card is root's with mode 755; vfat ignores new owners on a remount, and a second mount of the same device shares the first's. So each of the six CGIs is `patch/cgi_root.c` (`q2cgi-root`), mode 4755 (`CGI_MODE`; thttpd runs a CGI only if it is world-executable): a set-uid root program that refuses any caller but www-data or root, takes all of root's ids (real and saved too, so the caller can't signal it), init's resource limits, every signal at its default and none blocked, umask 022, thttpd's working directory and descriptors 0 to 2 alone, and runs `/usr/bin/q2cgi` with the six variables q2cgi reads (`REQUEST_METHOD`, `SCRIPT_NAME`, `QUERY_STRING`, `CONTENT_LENGTH`, `CONTENT_TYPE`, `HTTP_COOKIE`, the first of each) and a fixed `PATH`. A caller can therefore give q2cgi nothing a request to thttpd can't. thttpd 2.29 sets no time limit on a CGI (a CGI that slept 40 s finished under stock's binary), so the CGI being root's where thttpd can't signal it loses nothing. Checked end to end on the build's own rootfs, in a user namespace with uids 0 to 65535 and a `binfmt_misc` that runs MIPS set-uid programs as their owner: thttpd at uid 33, the PIN, a create, an upload and a download of names holding `$(id)` and a backtick, a list, a delete, a `../` refused, and q2cgi's 403 with no session; `test/fw/test_cgi_root.py` checks the refusals, and under root what the script is given. ponytail: www-data is a smaller foothold, not a wall. Kernel 5.10.21 has public local escalations (Dirty Pipe, CVE-2022-0847, needs nothing but a pipe), so code run in thttpd is root one step later; and the card holds card apps and the TF-card update, which root runs. Owning the card's mount by a dedicated uid at both mount sites would let the CGIs drop too.

<a id="wi-fi-transfer-tls"></a>**Plain HTTP.** No TLS: a browser trusts a certificate only for a name or address a public authority vouched for, and the Q2 has neither (an address from DHCP, no name on the network), so HTTPS with a certificate made on the Q2 would show the browser's full-page warning at every session, which teaches clicking through it. What protects a session is its PIN (shown only on the Q2, new each time transfer is turned on), the lockout after five wrong ones, the `SameSite=Strict` session cookie, the 10-minute idle stop and the server living only while the page is open (`switch_wifitransport`, [PIN](#wi-fi-transfer-pin); `test/fw/test_wifi_transfer.py`). Someone who can read the network's traffic can still read the files moved and take the cookie for that session; use transfer on a network you trust, or USB.

Checks in `test/build.py`: the three files in the image are `patch_web` of stock's, listed in the manifest's changed assets; `/usr/bin/q2cgi` is `assets/web/q2cgi`, the six CGIs are one `q2cgi-root`, mode 4755 and root's, and `thttpd.conf` is stock's with `user=www-data`.

## Quick-settings holds

Holding Wi-Fi or Bluetooth for `QUICK_HOLD_MS` (550 ms, the house hold) opens `systemset/wifi_page` or `systemset/bluetooth_page`. `ringnav_quick_settings` adds pointer-down handlers to the stock images. Release, movement over 10 pixels, pointer abort, keys, window close, background or destruction cancels the one-shot timer. A successful hold aborts the native press before closing the dialog and suppresses any late click, so it cannot also toggle the radio or open Playback settings. Ordinary taps keep their stock click handlers.

Holding Playback (`img_playset`) the same way opens `playset/equalizer_page`, the path stock's Playback EQ row opens (`0x4bd114`), after closing the panel. Pulled down over the page a hold opens (anywhere in the window stack), the hold only closes the panel (`cc_page`, `patch/control_center.c`): that page is already the goal. Stock's navigator would stack a second copy on it, so Return took two presses to leave Settings > Wi-Fi (the emulator, 2026-11-17), and `peq_ui.c` keeps one EQ page's state, so a second `equalizer_page` over the first would leave the first dead. Quick Settings gets the touch hold only; a held Play/Pause there is stock's, the wheel walking its rows.

Under Control Center (`patch/control_center.c`) every toggle holds the same way. `cc_open` gives each of its own clear buttons that has a settings page `quick_hold(button, QUICK_CC + stop)`, and `quick_long` hands those to `cc_hold` after closing the page: Wi-Fi `systemset/wifi_page`, Bluetooth `systemset/bluetooth_page`, AirPlay `systemset/netservice_page`, Car Remote `carremote_open`, Smart Wi-Fi `systemset/wifi_page` and EQ `playset/equalizer_page`, each through `cc_page` (not a second one); AirPlay's tap opens `systemset/netservice_page` the same way. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth need buttons of their own too: stock's `label_wifi` and `label_bt`, hidden, still take a touch (the dialog's hit test skips no hidden widget) and lie over the two switches inside `view_menu`, so a tap or hold on those circles reached the label, never the switch (the device and the emulator, 2026-11-17); the buttons, made after `view_menu`, are found first, and a tap there clicks stock's switch as Center does (`cc_act`). Center held as long with the ring on such a stop does the same: `cc_keydown` (from `ringnav_keydown`) arms `cc_hold_due` once, a held key's repeats leaving it be, and once it fires the release is swallowed (`cc_key_release`, in the key filter before every page's own keys), so neither the stop nor the page then in front sees it. A shorter press drops the hold on its release and acts as a tap. The sliders and the Now Playing block have no hold.

## On-The-Go

Library > Playlists is dressed by `pl_dress` with no select mode and no action rows but **On-The-Go** (`pl_otg_row`, while Settings > Playback > Library's `Q2POD OTG` is 1, the default): its tile, its name and its count, read by `otg_count` (`getMusicByPlayList(100)` through `staged`). The playlists' rows are `pl_oled_row`'s: 44 px (`PL_OLED_H`), the art image 36 px (`PL_OLED_ART`) at x 22 and the text from x 66 (`pl_oled_fit`, which `compact_row_layout` calls again on each relayout), stock's dots and other images hidden, a `list_into` image for the chevron, "N songs" in 16 px (the design's 13). The art is the playlist's own picture only (`playlist_art` with `PL_ART_OWN`: no 2x2), else a server playlist's cover (`catalogue_playlist_cover`: the app's `covers/pl-<pid>.jpg`, by the playlist's `cat.serverlists` row, the mapping read once per list built by `catalogue_playlist_covers`); with neither the image is empty and `pl_tile_paint` draws the tile under the `PL_TILE` prop (1 playlist, 2 On-The-Go), two int compares for every other widget painted. `pl_pitch` keeps the list at 44 px. A row's Center opens `playlist_page_open` (`pl_pick`) instead of stock's song list.

**On-The-Go's songs** are rows of stock's `playlist` table with `cd_num` 100 (`ON_THE_GO`) and no header: headers are ids 0 to 99 (`ringnav_playlist_create`, the catalogue's), and every reader of the headers asks `id <= 100` for headers or `cd_num = N` for one list's songs, so nothing lists it as a playlist, while stock's `batch_add_file`, `checkPlayListExist`, `getMusicByPlayList` and `sort_playlist_addtime` and our `ple_mutate` (whose bound is now `ON_THE_GO`) take it as any list's. It lasts in `database.db` across a restart. `otg_save` makes the header "On-The-Go N" (`ringnav_playlist_create`, the first N it doesn't refuse as taken) and moves the songs to it in one statement (`update playlist set cd_num=id where id>100 and cd_num=100`), so their ids and order stay; `pl_made` lands the list on it. `otg_clear` deletes the rows. Stock's Update Local Music drops `songtable` only, and Import replaces playlists by name, so neither touches it. ponytail: Export leaves it out, as it has no header.

**A playlist's page** (`playlist_pages.c`, `playlistsongs_page`) is `page_list` rows: Shuffle (when it has songs), Add Songs, and for On-The-Go Save as Playlist and Clear, then the songs in the playlist's own order (`sort_playlist_addtime`). `pv_paint` draws an action row's glyph (`plact_<name>_<a|w>`, `tools/art.py` `PL_ACTIONS`) and keeps its label in the accent, white on the selection, and right-aligns a song's artist, narrowing the title's label to end 8 px short of it. Clicks run on the next pass (`pv_run`). A song plays as stock plays a playlist's own list: `g_local_classinfo_save + 4` set to the `cd_num`, then `play_folder(songs, i, 0xff13)`, so Now Playing's Delete takes it out of this list (`deleteMusicFromPlaylist`), not the library. The page reads its songs again on `EVT_WINDOW_FOREGROUND`. A Play/Pause hold on a song (`playlist_page_hold`, from `ringnav_keylong`) is a Library song's whole menu (`qm_song_hold` in `navigation.c`: `QM_COVERFLOW` over the page's own list, `qm_held`, with Go to Album as well), then Remove from Playlist (or On-The-Go), `QA_REMOVE`, last after a gap in red, which asks on the [confirmation card](oled-design.md#confirmation-card) ("Remove "Two"?", "It stays in your library.") and on Remove runs `playlist_remove` (`ple_mutate`) on the song held, if it is still that row (`pv_remove_answer`).

**Menus.** In the menu sheet `qm_open` builds a song's menu as Play Next, `QA_OTG` (Add to On-The-Go, `playlist_add(r, ON_THE_GO)`) or, with On-The-Go off, Add to Queue, then Add to Playlist…, Favorite, then the Go to rows; a playlist's (`QM_PLAYLIST`) as `QA_PLAY` (its songs, `qm_collect`, played as its own list), Shuffle, `QA_RENAME` and `QA_DELETE` after a `modal_gap`. A playlist row's hold finds the playlist by its button's name, stock's index, as OLED's rows have no dots. Add to Playlist… is `playlist_pick_open`: the song copied into a one-record deque, the headers read (`getAllPlayList`), `modal_actions` with New Playlist first; a pick adds (`playlist_add`: stock's batch add through a private one-entry selection, checked with `checkPlayListExist` after) and toasts. New Playlist creates "New Playlist N" from the count plus one. Rename opens the letter strip (`search_strip.c` `playlist_rename_open`, `ss.rename`), which saves through `playlist_rename` (name and filename, as stock's, refused when another playlist has the name); Delete asks through stock's confirm (`playlist_confirm`) and runs `playlist_delete`. Each sets `g_delete_flag`, so the Playlists page reads its rows again when it is on top.

## Add Songs

`add_songs.c` (`addsongs_page`) is one sheet the page paints itself, as Search's strip is: a stack of up to four levels (the chooser; Recently Played, `getAllRecentRecord`; Recently Added, `getAllRecentAddRecord`; Artists, `getAllArtist` or `GetAllAlbumArtist` as Playback's Artists says; Albums, `getAllAlbum`; Songs, `all_songs`; an artist's songs, `getMusicBySonger` or `getMusicByAlbumArtist`, and its albums, each once by `album_cmp`, `coverflow_newest`; an album's tracks, `coverflow_album_tracks`), each a deque through `staged_music`, so a list of any length costs its records and no widgets. Its keys come before stock's in `ringnav` (`add_songs_key`): the wheel moves the selection and keeps it whole above y 282, Center acts, Return pops a level and leaves from the chooser. A tap acts on its row, a drag scrolls a row per 32 px. A cover row's picture is `catalogue_cover`'s for a server album, else Cover Flow's cached cover (`art_path(album_key)`), a `#2C2C2E` square till it exists. The A-Z index past `AZ_MIN_ROWS` is az_index.c's own column and bubble, driven through `az_mark` (the letter from the selected row on a fast spin, or the finger's on the right edge, which jumps to `az_target`).

**Marks.** `add_songs` reads the playlist once into `as.was`, and `as.now` starts the same: each a set of keys, a song's path hashed with its CUE start (`as_key`), `AS_MAX_KEYS` (4096) at most. A song is in before and now (check), added now (plus), or in before and not now (minus). Center (`add_songs_toggle`) adds through `playlist_add`, or takes the song out by finding its entry in a fresh read of the playlist and `playlist_remove`, and changes `as.now`. Add All adds each song not in now. Search's strip in its pick mode (`add_songs_search`, `ss.pick`) lists songs alone, found by title or artist, and hands a Center to `add_songs_toggle`, its rows marked by `add_songs_mark`.

## Local playlist editing

The other themes keep stock's Playlists page and this editor; OLED's playlists are [On-The-Go](#on-the-go)'s pages and menus, with no Edit Playlist. `ringnav_playlistsmore` extends stock `localmusic_playlistsmore_page_init` (`0x4b6614`). Its context is the index into `p_deque_playlist`; the container's `REC_DISC` (`cd_num`) fixes the editor's destination. Stock Rename and Add to Playlist routes remain in use, while New Playlist's allocator and Delete are replaced (`ringnav_playlist_create`, `ringnav_playlist_delete`); the More page's Delete row is relabelled Delete Playlist, as it deletes the whole list; the label is set as its translation key (`widget_set_tr_text`; no language has it, so it reads as given), which a re-translation keeps. The added Edit Playlist row reuses the Rename icon and the stock rows' list item, 335px button, 52px icon, 20px label and spacing. The runtime `playlistedit_page` uses the shared `page_open` / `page_list` helpers, its own staged records and a local song picker. Touch/Center song actions include adjacent movement and removal confirmed on the confirmation card (`ple_remove_answer`, Cancel first); Add Songs leaves the picker open after each stock batch addition, checking a fresh load before reporting success. Add Songs' first row opens the same T9 box as Internet Radio's pull-down (`edit_create`, named `search_edit` so `search_key` closes the keyboard before Return destroys it); the picker filters case-insensitively on tagged title, artist and album, and keeps the query while several songs are added. Holding Play/Pause on a playlist row opens its [queue menu](#queue-menu), whose last row, More…, opens `localmusic/playlistsmore_page` with the playlist index from the row's `img_more<n>` dots, as the dots themselves do (the list's row index also counts Import and Export, and a row without dots keeps stock's hold); the shared `playlist_page` add picker is excluded by `PLAYLIST_ADD_MODE`. Stock duplicate checking runs before addition. The picker ticks a song the playlist already holds (same path and CUE start, matched against the staged entries in memory, no query per row) with stock's `select` check at x 340, the caption shortened to stop before it; a successful add ticks its row in place. A private one-entry libcstl selection vector lives for demo’s lifetime, so adding never rewrites a covered stock picker’s global batch selection. Done/Back exits; destroy cancels pending work and releases both deques.

Playlist creation (`ringnav_playlist_create`) allocates a free header ID from 0–99 under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, independent of the displayed name order. Stock's allocator assumed ID order and could reuse an occupied ID after name sorting. Duplicate names keep stock's `-2` result; database failures roll back and show “Could not create playlist”. Delete Playlist asks for confirmation, then removes the header and its entries in one transaction. It sets stock's reload flag and shows “Playlist deleted” only after a successful commit; failure keeps the playlist and shows “Could not delete playlist”. Music files and the current playback queue stay intact.

Stock `getMusicByPlayList` (`0x50b6c8`) selects `playlist` records with `id > 100` and the destination `cd_num`. V1.34 gave playlists a Sort: by `g_playlistsort_flag` (`SYSSET PLAYLISTSORT`) the function hands over `sort_playlist_first_alphabet` (0, by name) or `sort_playlist_addtime` (Time added: the stored order, V1.32's only one, and the default, which an unset or out-of-range key also gives). The page, its play and the M3U export follow the Sort; Edit Playlist reads `sort_playlist_addtime` itself (`ple_query`), since a move swaps two neighbours' ids, which means nothing in a list sorted by name. `getAllPlayList` (`0x509b20`) lists the playlists themselves with `select * from playlist where id <= 100`; `ringnav_library_query` appends `order by name collate nocase, id` to exactly that query, so Library → Playlists and Add to Playlist list them by name (stock Rename updates `name` and `filename` together). It also adds explicit `order by id asc` to that exact stock query, including its export (`saveExternM3uFile`) and later playback callers. `ple_mutate` opens the existing SQLite library, takes `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, validates both entry IDs, playlist membership, path and CUE bounds, then swaps IDs through a verified free ID above the table maximum. Every update/delete checks `changes() == 1`; errors and failed commits roll back. Removal uses entry ID, so duplicate paths and CUE segments remain distinct. Only the chosen entries change; records omitted from a view keep their IDs. UI reload and selection movement follow successful commits. No live playback queue is rewritten, and no schema is added.

Previous/Next press, repeats, native delivery, long press and release are consumed while the editor is open, including under a success/error toast; movement requires the editor to own the top window. One press moves once; a release latch survives page closure. The wheel retains ordinary row selection. `test/patch.py` exercises the MIPS editor with SQLite transactions at the import boundary, including rollback, stale selections, ignored writes, duplicate/CUE entries, isolation, limits, picker behavior, touch actions and selection retention. Hardware reboot, stock export/import round trips and subsequent playback still require device validation before release.

## 1.3.5 audio and input fixes

Swap L/R (`Q2POD SWAPLR`, default 0) follows Mono Audio in settings. `crossfade.c` publishes `/tmp/q2swap` using the existing atomic shared-int pattern. The float PCM filter swaps after EQ and mono, before Crossfade; q2video swaps S16 after soft gain and mono for video, radio and Spotify’s helper. Spotify uses that helper on the headphone DAC when either switch is on, with the existing sink-restart limitation. Neither option changes DSD/DoP or AirPlay.

The stock title sorter queries `toolsQueryDbTableAndSort` (`0x5daf44`), now scoped through `ringnav_sorted_query` just like the other Library queries. Folder loads and stored playlist records retain their scope. Bluetooth absolute volume keeps the larger requested channel gain on the headset and normalizes each software channel against it. Reconnect/read-back uses `device_set_volume` to retain stock Balance rather than applying equal gains. `bt_volume_poll` reads the headset's volume back on BlueZ's signal and every `BT_VOLUME_FALLBACK_MS` (5 s) besides ([Headset controls and volume](#headset-controls-and-volume)); without the signal, every 400 ms lit, and dark every `BT_VOLUME_LIMIT_MS` (1 s) while a volume limit has to be held on the headset's own keys, else `BT_VOLUME_SLOW_MS` (2 s). A headset that refuses absolute volume, or can't report it (a read above 127, as before its AVRCP is up), gets the 2 s pace lit too, so its reconnect `device_set_volume` isn't repeated 2.5 times a second. ponytail: without the signal, dark, the headset's own keys can pass the limit for up to 1 s before it is pulled back.

`ringnav_input` handles the disconnected USB confirmation before stock input routing. During a Now Playing animation it applies fresh wheel volume directly and consumes the event; held list-navigation ticks are discarded. Once the animation ends, normal stock feedback resumes.


## Release signatures

q2-coda's releases are signed, so a GitHub account or repository taken over can't ship code that Network Update or the App Store runs as root. The key is Ed25519. Its private half lives in the maintainer's password vault and never in the repository; its public half is `assets/signing/q2-coda-release.pub`, which `tools/build.py` (`signing_key`) reads into `stock.h` as `Q2POD_SIGN_KEY`, and `patch/release_sig.c` keeps as `release_key`. A release build refuses to run without that file, and `--signing-key` (another public key, for a test build whose private half is at hand) requires `--dev`. The manifest records the key (`signing_key`), and `tools/release.py` refuses a package built with any other.

A signature covers a short ASCII message, never the file itself, so the Q2 hashes a 55 MB `update.tar` in 64 KB pieces (`sig_hash_file`) rather than holding it in memory:

- `update.tar`: `q2-coda-update-v1 TAG SHA512\n`, `TAG` the release's tag and `SHA512` the file's SHA-512 in lowercase hex. The tag is in it so that an older release's file and signature, published under a newer tag, fail. Its signature is the release's `update.tar.sig`, 64 bytes ([Network Update](#network-update)).
- `sources.list`: `q2-coda-sources-v1 SHA512\n` over every byte before the list's last line, which is `signature ` and the 64-byte signature in hex ([Q2 Shelf](#q2-shelf)).

`tools/signing.py` writes the same messages; [releasing](releasing.md#signing-a-release) has the commands. Monocypher 4.0.2 (`patch/monocypher/`, BSD-2-Clause or CC0: its `LICENCE.md`) checks the signature (`crypto_ed25519_check`, RFC 8032's Ed25519, which `openssl pkeyutl -rawin` makes) and hashes with SHA-512; `release_sig.c` adds SHA-256 for the App Store's pins. Its four files are Monocypher's own, unchanged (the release tarball's `src/` and `src/optional/`, SHA-256 `38d07179738c0c90677dba3ceb7a7b8496bcfea758ba1a53e803fed30ae0879c`, the same as GitHub's 4.0.2 tag but for the version line), and `--gc-sections` keeps only what the checks use, about 26 KB. `test/fw/test_release_sig.py` checks that a good signature passes and a flipped byte in the file or the signature, another tag, another key and no signature fail; `test/patch.py` swaps `release_key` for a test key in the emulated payload, whose private half it holds.

ponytail: the key can't be rotated without a release signed by the old one: a Q2 trusts only the key it was built with. A compromised private key is the one thing a signature can't survive; the next firmware would have to carry a new key, and be installed from the card by hand.

## Network Update

General's **Software Update** row (`ringnav_systemset` in `patch/navigation.c` binds it to `sw_update_open`, `patch/sw_update.c`) checks online and the SD card at once ([SD Card Update](#sd-card-update) for the card's half and the page); this is the online half, in `patch/netupdate.c`. **The check** (`netupdate_check`, on `sw_update.c`'s thread `sw_net`, only while `g_wififlag` is set) makes two header-only requests of at most `NU_CHECK_S` (5 s, connect and all) each: `releases/latest`'s redirect for the tag (as in step 1 below; a tag that isn't newer is `NET_LATEST`), then the tag's `update.tar`, following its redirects, for `CURLINFO_CONTENT_LENGTH_DOWNLOAD`, the size the offer shows. Any failure (no link, no DNS, a timeout, a code other than 302 then 200) is `NET_FAILED`, which only adds "Couldn't check online · Try Again" under the card's answer. Stock's own System Update page (`systemset_fwupdate_page_init`, hooked by `ringnav_fwupdate`) is no longer on General; should it open, stock's row builder (`0x4c8660`) names each row's button by its index, and stock's click (`0x4c84cc`) runs `atoi` on the name: 0 is the TF card update (`0x4c7eb4`), 1 Shanling's plain-HTTP server (`openwin.shanling.com:9000`, `/tmp/versioninfo`, `download_ota_thd`). The hook renames the second button "2", which stock's click ignores, and binds it to `sw_update_open`.

**The download**, Download and Install on the offer (`netupdate_start`): one pthread (`worker`) runs three transfers through demo's libcurl, all verified against `/etc/scrobble-ca.pem` (`SSL_VERIFYPEER`, `SSL_VERIFYHOST` 2; `easy` sets what every transfer shares), and checks the release's signature ([Release signatures](#release-signatures)):

1. A header-only request for `https://github.com/312-dev/q2-coda/releases/latest` (`Q2POD_REPO`, another repo's with `tools/build.py --update-repo`), without following the redirect. The tag is what follows the last `/` of `CURLINFO_REDIRECT_URL` (`netupdate_tag`, `.../releases/tag/TAG`), 1 to 31 of `A-Za-z0-9._-`, as it goes into the next two URLs and the signed message; anything else is no tag ("Can't reach GitHub"). A tag equal to `Q2POD_TAG` (`VERSION` in `tools/build.py`; empty in `--dev` builds) says "Latest firmware installed", as stock's updater would refuse that tag anyway. A beta of that version says so too, though its update identity differs (`BETA`), so its testers install the release itself from the card; Network Update offers them the version after it.
2. `releases/download/TAG/update.tar.sig` (`signature`), through `/tmp/q2-update.sig`, deleted once read: 64 bytes, the release key's signature. A 404, or any other length, is "Release not signed: not installed", and nothing more is fetched. q2-pod's upstream releases (DiamondBond/q2-pod) carry no signature, so a q2-coda Q2 never installs one; a Q2 pointed at them with `--update-repo` refuses every update.
3. `releases/download/TAG/update.tar`, the tag's own asset rather than `releases/latest`'s (the one the signature names, if the latest release changes in between), following the redirect to GitHub's asset host, into `/mnt/mmc/update.tar.part`, flushed and `fsync`ed. curl fails a body shorter than its `Content-Length`, and a transfer under 1 KB/s for 30 s ends. Then the part is read back from the card, the bytes stock will flash, through SHA-512 a 64 KB piece at a time (`sig_update`; the row says "Verifying…", `nu.verifying`), and only if the release key signed `q2-coda-update-v1 TAG SHA512` is it renamed over `update.tar`. Any failure deletes the `.part` and keeps the old `update.tar`: "Can't reach GitHub" (curl or no redirect), "No update for this build" (not 200), "Can't write to the card", "Signature check failed: not installed" (the file, the tag or the signature changed since signing, or another key signed it).

Software Update's page polls it every 250 ms (`netupdate_poll`, from `sw_update.c` `sw_dl_tick`): the percent from the transfer's progress callback and `nu.verifying` for its page, `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 0)` while it runs so standby and auto power-off wait (the screen still sleeps), and, once it ends, the thread joined and its state, which the page says (`netupdate_said`) unless it is `NU_DONE`, when the card's check runs on the new file. Leaving the page calls `netupdate_cancel`, which sets `nu.cancel`, which the progress callback returns, so curl stops ("Download cancelled"), and which the signature check reads after each 64 KB; a cancel that lands after the transfer finished still deletes the `.part` and reads as cancelled: the state is settled after `fclose` and the check, so a press while the card takes the whole part's `fsync` (seconds on a slow card, the label at 100%) or during "Verifying…" says "Download cancelled", not "Can't write to the card". The header request has no progress callback, so a cancel there waits for it (30 s at most), then skips the download. Leaving the page drops the label (`EVT_DESTROY`) and cancels, as the card may be unmounted or shared over USB next. A tag not newer than the build's (`strcmp`, as tags are single-digit `x.y.z`) is "Latest firmware installed", so an older release is never offered; `--dev` builds take any tag. After the rename the card's root directory is `fsync`ed (demo imports no `sync`), so the new entry is on the card before stock flashes. When it finishes on the page, `fwupdate_tf` runs [SD Card Update](#sd-card-update): its checks, its confirmation and stock's flash. Elsewhere it says "Update downloaded: use SD Card Update".
