`tools/release.py` uploads `update.tar` and `update.tar.sig` under fixed names (`ASSET`, `SIGNATURE`), which `NU_ASSET` names in each tag's `releases/download/TAG/`. `github.com` chains to USERTrust ECC (Sectigo E46) and the asset host to ISRG Root X1; both roots are in the bundle.

ponytail: only releases that carry the fixed-name assets and a signature can be fetched, and a CA change at GitHub needs a bundle refresh. The card needs room for the new tar (about 55 MB) beside the old one. The signature binds the file to its tag, not to "latest": someone holding the repository could still hold back a newer release, though never install an older one over a newer build. A `--dev` build takes any signed tag, an older one too. Checking the signature reads the whole part back from the card (seconds), on the worker, so the UI keeps going. Plugging in USB storage mid-download unmounts the card under the write (the card-corruption risk of any card write); the `.part` then fails and is deleted. Leave USB unplugged until it finishes.

## SD Card Update

Software Update's card half (`patch/sw_update.c`, the look in [oled-design](oled-design.md#software-update)). `sw_update_open` starts the online check's thread (above) and then this one; `sw_tick` waits for both, and `sw_offer` weighs their answers apart: low battery stops either; the internet's update is offered first, with "Install from SD Card instead" when the card has one too; else the card's, with "Turn on Wi-Fi to check online" (`ON_OFF`) or "Couldn't check online · Try Again" (`NET_FAILED`, which runs the online check again and keeps the card's answer) under it; a card file that can't be used says why; else You're Up to Date. The wheel moves between the offer's button and that line (`sw_update_key`, from `ringnav`'s key handler), and taps hit either (`sw_touch`). Stock's row (`fwupdate_tf`, `0x4c7eb4`) asked first (`msg_confirmupdate` in `confirminfo_dialog`), then ran its checks, then opened `checkfw_dialog`, whose thread does the work and whose 1 s timer reports it; every answer was a message dialog. The hook (`ringnav_fwupdate_tf`, no trampoline: none of stock's function runs) checks first and asks only about an update stock's updater would take; the flash is still stock's `checkfw_dialog`. The download ends in the card's check alone (`ringnav_fwupdate_tf`'s path, `ON_NONE`), which asks Install Update? at once ([Network Update](#network-update)).

1. **Stock's checks**, `check_updatefw_exist(SW_CARD, SW_FILE)` (`0x5034f0`, exported), on the UI thread as stock calls it: -15 when `g_charge_state` (a cable in, `usb_detect`'s) is 0 and `g_power_capacity` is under 16 ("Charge to Update", "Needs 16% or a charger · now N%", `SW_BATTERY`); -2 with no card mounted (`toolsCheckMountNew`: "No SD Card"); -11 when `update.tar` can't be read ("No Update Found"); -12 under 0.1 GB free (`getDiskMemoryInfoAndSetFormat`'s GB, rounded to hundredths: "Not Enough Space", "Free 100 MB on the SD card"), as stock's tar unpacks the update beside it. Each opens its mode page at once (`swupdate_page`, `sw_stock_answer`).
2. **The tar**, read on a thread (`sw_check`, `sw_check_file`) while the page shows "Checking for an Update…" with a twelve-spoke spinner, as `update_firmware` (`0x5028e0`) will take it after `tar xvf`: its first member must be `firmware_v20.info` (at most 1 KB), whose first line, trimmed, is `Shanling Q2` and whose second, trimmed, holds a `V`; an equal version is "You're Up to Date" (stock refuses it with -14: `Q2POD_FW_TAG` is the patched version literal, [building](building.md#versioning)); then each member's header in turn, the MD5 of `recovery-update/xImage` against the third line's first 32 characters and `rootfs.squashfs`'s against the fourth's (stock's `strncmp`), streamed through demo's libcrypto 64 KB at a time. Anything else (another model, a missing image, a wrong MD5, a file cut short) is "Update Can't Be Used". Return leaves the page and sets `swu.cancel`, which the thread reads after each read. An 80 ms timer (`sw_tick`) turns the spinner and joins the thread, then acts on the answer only once the check's page has stopped sliding in (`window_manager_is_animating`), so a fast check still shows the spinner before its answer.
3. **Install Update?** on the confirmation card (`sw_ask`, `feedback.c` `confirm`) over the check's page: the update's name from its tag (`sw_update_name`: `V1820` is Q2 Muse 1.8.2 (`SW_PRODUCT`, the one product name), `V1822` 1.8.2 beta 2, a dev tag "Q2 Muse Dev", anything else the line itself) in the title, "55.6 MB, over TAG. Takes about 2 min;" and "your music and settings stay." as its body, Cancel (selected) and Install and Restart. Either answer closes the check's page (`sw_answer`); Install and Restart then, from an idle callback once the card is done, runs `navigator_to("dialog/checkfw_dialog")` as stock's function did. No card (another up) closes the page.
4. **Restarting to Install** is stock's `checkfw_dialog` (`ringnav_checkfw` in `playback.c` saves the place, then `sw_update_restarting` hides its `scrlabel_checkfw`): its thread stops the player, unpacks the tar to `/mnt/mmc` (`tar xvf ... -C mnt/mmc`, relative to demo's working directory, `/`), checks it as above and, at 1, marks mtd6 for the recovery (`ota:kernel2`) and restarts; the recovery flashes. The page's bar is the two images' bytes unpacked so far (`SW_PARTS`) of their sizes in the tar (`swu.parts`), stat'ed every 250 ms. Should stock's own check fail after all, its `dialog_quit` code comes back from `navigator_to`: 9 "No Update Found", 13 "You're Up to Date", 18 "Update Can't Be Used".

`test/fw/test_sw_update.py` covers the tar check (tars built as `tools/build.py` builds them), stock's answers, the names and the flow; `test/patch.py` runs the hook and the pages on the real payload.

ponytail: the check reads the whole 55 MB once more before stock's updater unpacks and checks it again, a few seconds the user sees as the spinner; skipping it would mean asking before knowing whether the file is any good. The bar stays full while stock checks the unpacked images and counts down its 3 s, which it reports nothing of.

## Card apps

Card apps (`patch/addon.c`, apps on the card, or carried in the firmware ([Bundled apps](#bundled-apps)), that Q2 Muse knows only by their folder: q2-deezer, q2-soulseek, q2-filebrowser, q2-subsonic, q2-podcasts, q2-lma) draw their pages over Q2SPOT/1, as Spotify's browser does ([librespot.md](librespot.md)). Each row's kind sets what a press does: `list` opens a level (its uri the op, its context the argument), `action` sends its uri with the context and toasts the reply, `needslib` is an `action` that needs Streaming Songs on (below), `search` opens the T9 box, `sort` opens a level as `list` does (below), `remote` the QR code page, `local` plays a song or a folder from the card, a path under `/mnt/mmc/` with no `..` segment as a playlist's lines must be (context `album`: in track order, by name), `page` shows another window of the same list (below), `field` opens the T9 box for a value the app keeps (**Fields**, below), `info` nothing; `position` is the op a held Play/Pause sends, and a reply message `refresh` asks again every 2 s. A `progress` row (`progress_row`) is inert as `info`, Play/Pause held included: its title on the left and subtitle on the right of one line, over a flat 8 px bar of its `position` in permille (clamped to 0–1000, text that isn't a number as 0), kept in the bar's `_pml` prop for `addon_paint`: a square rectangle the caption's width, a dim gray track (`PROGRESS_TRACK`, #3A3A3A) filled from the left in the accent's light tone, as Spotify's bar, with no rounded ends and no knob; at 0 it draws no fill at all. Firmware without the `progress` word shows it as a plain title and subtitle row, so an app sends `info` with a text bar there. A press is queued for the next timer pass as a row index (`pg.go`), so any rebuild of the rows (`show`: a refresh that changes them, an error page's [Retry, Stop], a pop or push) drops it rather than let it land on whatever row now has that index. ponytail: a short first page that `append` rebuilds drops it too, the row kept or not; the press is just made again.

**The QR code page** (`qrcode_page`, `qr_open`, `qr_paint`) is a `remote` row's page: the app's phone page, from its status file, read again every 500 ms while the screen is on. With a code and no `step` it draws the code (`qr`, `qrsize` rows of hex, the leftmost module the high bit) on a white plate centered under the status row, 166 px with two quiet modules each side, the app's `note` under it ("Scan with your phone" without one), and dimmer the address (`addr`) and PIN (`pin`) for a phone that types it in; without an address (no Wi-Fi) or a file (not running) it says so. Once the file has a `step` the page is a mode page instead ([oled-design](oled-design.md)): one solid circle with its glyph (`MODE_GLYPHS` in `tools/art.py`, `modepage_<step>`), drawn by `feedback.c`'s `mode_page_paint`, the file's `title` and `line`, the stack centered between the status row and the screen's foot. `phone` (the phone has the form) and `check` (the server is being asked) are the accent's, `done` green, `fail` (not reached) and `error` (anything else) red; `done` closes the page after `QR_DONE_MS` (1.5 s), so the app's page, now signed in, shows. The status row names the app (`addon_qr_title`), and the wheel does nothing there, as on every page but a playback screen ([Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)). An action whose live level's refresh puts a `remote` row under the cursor opens the page at once (`pg.qrnext`), so a sign-in row takes one press. While the page is open `/tmp/q2-<id>.qrpage` exists, removed as it closes, so an app knows the page was left by the file going, not from the pauses in its page's refreshes, which the screen turning off also makes. The `signin` word in the caps says the firmware does all of this; an app keeps writing `note` with each step for older firmware, which draws only the note, beside the code.

**Search in the title bar.** A list whose first row is of kind `search` shows it as a magnifying glass at the right of the title bar, in line with the page's name, as stock Tidal's (`s_img_search`), instead of as a row: `take_find` takes the row out of the reply's rows when the reply arrives (`lv_t.find`), and `find_icon` keeps the title centered on the screen in a box ending at the glass's box, x 73 to 302 (with a sort icon, at its ink: 95 to 280, below), so a longer title scrolls clear of them; it then adds a 50 px image after the rows, at x 302 in line with the rows' chevrons (`row_into`), and marks it clickable (an image sends no click otherwise; stock Tidal's `img_search` is clickable in its page too). A tap is queued as a row's press is (`G_FIND`) and opens the same T9 box (`search_box`, the row's press too); closing the box rebuilds the page, icon included. Only the first row of a level's own reply moves, its title and subtitle no longer shown, and a sole Search row stays a row so the list isn't left empty. A search row further down stays a row. A More… level is a level of its own and a `page` row's window is the level's reply, so their first row is taken; a later `pages` page is appended to the list, so a Search row there stays a row. Under a theme without a title bar (`page_title_h` 0, OLED's, where the name is in the status bar) the row stays as it was. No capability word: apps need no change, and older firmware shows the row. Not covered: the icon takes taps only, so the wheel and buttons no longer reach search on such a list.

**Sort in the title bar.** A row of kind `sort` (the `sort` word, below) is a `list` row: a press opens its uri as a level, its context the argument and its title the level's, and it has the chevron (`opens`, `open_list`). Where the first Search row was taken (`lv_t.find`), a `sort` row right after it (now the first) is taken too (`take_sort`, `lv_t.sort`), unless it is the last row left: its six fields are kept in `pg.sort`, pointers into the shown reply, which lives as long as the level is ready, and `find_icon` adds a second 50 px image left of the glass, in stock's Sort style (`s_img_order_navbar`, the Sort of stock's Songs page, image `song_order`), clickable, and the title's centered box ends where the sort's ink starts, 95 to 280. The sort's image is made before the glass's: their boxes overlap at 302 to 315, and a tap goes to the child made last, so the glass keeps all of its box. A tap is queued as a row's press is (`G_SORT`) and opens the kept row's level exactly as its press would. The icon's place is set by the glyphs' ink, not their boxes: stock V1.36's `navbar_search` and `song_order` are 50 px images whose ink (alpha above 0) is columns 15 to 35 and 15 to 34, so at `FIND_X` 302 the glass's ink is 317 to 337, 37 px from the screen's edge (in line with the chevrons), and at `SORT_X` 265 the sort's is 280 to 299: midway between the end of a centered 150 px title (a section's "Newly Added 1/5" at 20 px, ending at 262) and the glass, 17 px from each. Light Mode recolours the glyphs but keeps their alpha. `s_img_search` centers its image in the box (no draw type: AWTK's center), while `s_img_order_navbar` sets draw type 0, from the box's top left, so the sort's box is 50 px high and centered on the title's line, `(h - 50) / 2`, which puts both glyphs at the same height. A `sort` row anywhere else (no Search row taken before it, further down, the sole row left, a later `pages` page, or a theme without a title bar) stays a row; `page_to` counts a Search and a Sort row kept as rows before Previous page. A refresh whose sort row comes or goes rebuilds the list. Not covered: as the glass, the icon takes taps only.

**An action in flight.** While an action's request is out (`pg.act`), `go` sends nothing for another press of an `action` row: the app has usually done the first by then, and a second request would cancel it (`req_send` calls `req_cancel`), so its toast never came and a toggle pressed twice undid itself. Nothing else changes: a `list`, `sort`, `page`, `local`, `remote` or `search` row, the title bar's icons, a section swipe and a held Play/Pause's op go ahead as before, taking the request's place (the app has done the action; its toast is lost), and Return, the wheel, the volume and the player keys are not the page's to hold back. Return still pops the level or leaves the page, dropping the request as before. When no reply has come after `BUSY_MS` (400 ms, checked by the page's 250 ms tick), `busy_row` writes **Working…** over the pressed row's detail, or over its title when the detail is empty (under a theme with separators the empty detail's label lies under the centered title), as the App Store's rows say Installing…; `got`, and `action` for an op that takes the request's place, write the row's own text back before the reply's toast, so it clears on an answer, a refusal and a failure alike, and a live level whose reply doesn't change is left as it was. A reply within `BUSY_MS` changes nothing on screen. A list drawn again while the action waits (`show`, such as the search box closing) has its own texts, so `show` clears `pg.busy` and the next tick says Working… again.

**Live lists.** An action on a live level (the app's last reply for it said `refresh`) leaves it shown: once the action's reply has come, the level is asked again rather than after `ADDON_LIVE_MS`, after the toast when the reply has a message (2 s) and at once when it has none, with no Loading… page in between, so a choice page's mark moves as soon as the app answers (written in place when every row keeps its shape, else the list drawn again, its row kept selected) and pressing the current choice changes nothing on screen. A refused action, or one on a level that isn't live, reloads it as before. A `refresh` reply that differs from the shown one is written into the shown rows in place when it has the same rows (`same_rows`, on the reply as `take_find` and `take_sort` left it): as many, on one page, each of the same kind, uri and context (so a press queued on a row still does what it did), each with a detail where it had one and none where it had none, More… there or not as before, a first Search row and a Sort row after it taken or not as before, and as many covers (`art_rows`, a count). `relabel` then walks each row's children: its `hscroll_label`s are the title and then the detail, each set only when its text changed, then given the face that text needs (`theme_font`, `ROLE_TALL` and `ROLE_META`, the roles `page_row_detail` set however the row was dressed) and put back to its left end (`xoffset` 0), and a progress row's bar (the child with `_pml`) takes the new permille and is repainted (`widget_invalidate_force`). A label's `text` prop is a wide string, so `widget_get_prop_str` returns NULL for it; the shown text is read with `widget_get_text_utf8`. So the list, the selection, a queued press, a cover's bitmap (the `drop` that lets covers go is skipped) and a long title's marquee carry on while, say, a sync's percentage moves, where a rebuild would start the marquee over every 2 s. When the selected row's title itself changes, `relabel` calls `marq_restart`, which clears `st.marq_row`, so the next paint re-arms the row's marquee (`paint_selection`) for the new text's width; a detail changing leaves the title's marquee alone. Any other change (a row added, removed, or of another kind, uri or context, a detail appearing or going, the first Search row or a cover coming or going) rebuilds the list with `show` as before. ponytail: covers are counted, not compared, so one cover replaced by another in the same reply stays until the next rebuild.

**More….** A level keeps its list's own arguments apart from a page's cursor (`lv_t.base`, the bytes of `args` before it), and More… asks for the list's arguments and the new cursor alone, the op's last argument as Q2SPOT/1 has it. Up to 1.4.1 each More… appended its cursor to the page's arguments, cursor included ("albums 30 60"), which q2-deezer read as the second page again; q2-deezer v3.3 reads the last argument either way.

**Full lists.** A reply whose message is `pages` (the app opts in, as `refresh` does for a live list; [librespot.md](librespot.md)) and whose cursor isn't empty is followed by its next pages (`page_next`): each is asked with the same op, the list's own arguments (`args` up to `base`) and the newest cursor as the last argument, exactly what More… sends. Any other reply with a cursor keeps More…, so apps that don't send `pages` (q2-deezer, q2-soulseek, q2-filebrowser) see no change and no extra requests. A page's rows are appended to the same `page_list` without rebuilding it (`append`): the trailing row is destroyed, the new rows and a new trailing row added, `virtual_h` grown, and `ringnav_select` given the new count, so ringnav keeps the selection and the scroll and the wheel's acceleration and big letter run through the whole list. Limit (`ponytail:`): each page's new count makes ringnav's `load` drop a spin's speed-up and the big letter, as for any list whose count changes, so a spin while pages are still arriving starts slow again at each one; a ringnav call that grows a list in place would keep them. A page that lands while another window is on top (Now Playing, a menu) only records the count and selection: `ringnav_select` skips `load` for a list whose window isn't the top one, which took ringnav's list state and the top list's glide and big letter from under the wheel. While a page is on its way the trailing row is **Loading…**, which a press ignores. The list ends when a reply has no cursor or isn't `pages` (then at More…); at `ADDON_PAGES` (10) replies, or after a failed page (an error status, no socket, or the 15 s deadline), the trailing row becomes **More…** with the last good cursor, the rows already shown kept. Only a first page shorter than the screen is rebuilt (`page_list` shrank its view); pages that arrive while the search box is open are kept and drawn when it closes. A live level (`refresh`) never pages, its 2 s refresh asking for its first page alone. An action, a held Play/Pause, or Back from a deeper level reloads the level from its first page and pages it again; the selected row (`lv_t.sel`) comes back when the page holding it arrives, unless the user has moved off the trailing row meanwhile; once reached or left it is the selection, so a later page never moves it. A last page with no rows leaves the selection on the last row, not past it. The cap is 500 rows because ringnav navigates at most `MAX_ENTRIES` (512) rows of a `scroll_view` and walks every row per wheel event and paint; past that, More… asks for the rest as a level of its own. Only the top level keeps a reply (push and Back let the others' go), so the shown reply lives in `pg`: up to ten replies (`pg.buf`, each `realloc`'d to its own size before `spot_reply` cuts it, where the request had 64 KB) and 500 rows of fields (`pg.f`, 12 KB, calloc'd with the page). Progress rows belong in live lists, which never page.

**Sections.** An app's first level can be a row of sections, such as a music app's Home, Albums and Playlists, the way a phone app has tabs. A first-level reply whose message is `sections` makes each of its `list` rows a section: its uri the op that fills it, its title the section's name and its context the op's argument (other kinds and a `list` row with an empty uri are left out, and so is a context too long for a level's arguments; at most `ADDON_SECTIONS`, 8). Sections are taken once per page: a section whose own reply says `sections` shows its rows as an ordinary list, so a confused app can't make the page ask for the first section again and again. `sec_take` keeps them (`pg.sec`, a level each, calloc'd, freed with the page) and `sec_open` puts the first in the first level's place at once, asked for and titled with its name and, when there are two or more, its position (`Albums 2/3`), so the reply with the names is never shown. A sideways swipe on the page opens the next section (to the left) or the previous one (to the right); there is none past the first or the last. `swipe`, bound on the page's pointer events before its rows see them, works as Pull to search's pull (`pull_event`): a move of `SWIPE_CLAIM_PX` (24 px) sideways and at least twice as far as up or down takes the touch, the rows are sent a pointer abort so the lift clicks nothing, and the moves and the lift go no further; at the lift, `SWIPE_PX` (60 px) sideways and more than up or down changes the section, on the next timer pass (`G_SECTION`), as a row's press does. A move of `SWIPE_CLAIM_PX` up or down before that is the list's scroll, however far it went sideways. Only the first level swipes: a level opened from a section is an ordinary level, and Back returns to the section, asked for again. Leaving and opening the page starts at the first section again. ponytail: the wheel never changes section, on purpose (it moves the selection, as on every list), so the sections past the first are reached by touch alone. A swipe shows no movement until the lift, and a section is asked for again each time it opens (only the shown level keeps a reply), its selected row kept across the swipe; a section paged by `page` rows (**Windows**, below) comes back to its first window.

**Covers.** An app gives a row a cover by leaving a JPEG at `/tmp/q2-<id>.art/<key>.jpg` before it replies: the key is FNV-1a 32 (`hash_bytes` from `FNV_SEED`) over the row's uri, a tab and its context (as the app sent them, before Q2SPOT/1's `%` escapes), written as 8 lowercase hex digits (`art_file`). When `show` draws a level's rows it reads each row's file's header (`art_rows`, `picture_size`, stopping only at a progress row, whose bar belongs to the plain row, with the whole first page counted); if any row has one, the whole list is drawn as stock Tidal's lists are (`art_row`): `ART_ROW_H` (78 px, stock `tidal_*_page.bin`'s `list_view` `default_item_height`) rows, the cover `ART_PX` (64 px) square at the theme's text column, centered in the row's height and scaled to fit (draw type 4, as Cover Flow's), and the title over the subtitle beside it, with the chevron for a row that opens a page and the trailing More… or Loading… row in the same height. A row without a file keeps the cover's room empty, so the titles line up. The app sizes its covers: one over `ART_MAX` (128 px) either way, or whose size can't be read, counts as no cover, as each decoded bitmap stays in demo's memory; one up to 128 px is scaled to fit the 64 px. A row's bitmap is unloaded from the image manager before its image is set, so a file changed since is decoded again. Stock never releases decoded bitmaps, so a list a user scrolled would keep up to 500 x 128 x 128 x 4 (32 MB) until it closed: `art_window`, in `show`, `drop` and the page's 250 ms `tick`, keeps at most `ART_KEEP` (24, about 1.5 MB at `ART_MAX` px) rows' covers decoded around the list's real scroll position (`yoffset` over the row height, so wheel, touch and a fling all count). `[pg.art_lo, pg.art_hi)` names the rows whose bitmaps may be decoded; each tick the range is widened to all a move crossed since the last and the rows now outside the window are unloaded by name (`image_manager_unload_bitmap_by_name`), so the cost is the rows crossing, not the list's length. It is reset wherever the rows are rebuilt (`show`) and when a level's reply is let go (`drop`, unloading only that range while `pg.f` still has the rows, with no dependence on `l->art` and no file read); no row build decodes a cover. A row scrolled back paints by name again: stock's `image` widget paint (`0x627c6c`) keeps only the name (`image_base + 0x78`) and calls `widget_load_image` (`0x66f75c`) into a `bitmap_t` on its stack each paint, which `image_manager_get_bitmap` (`0x65823c`, `0x657e70`) fills from the cache or by decoding, so a released bitmap leaves nothing dangling (the same as `np_art_poll` and Home's cover, `navigation.c`, `coverflow.c`). ponytail: at most `ART_KEEP` covers plus what a fling paints in one 250 ms tick; a cover scrolled back decodes again on the UI thread. A list with a `progress` row is drawn as before, since its bar belongs to the plain row. The protocol is unchanged: an app that leaves no files, or firmware without the `art` word, shows the plain rows. Not covered: the choice is made when the list is drawn, so in practice the first page decides: pages appended later (`append`) keep it, and Back or an action reloads from the first page, so a later page's covers don't count then either (a list rebuilt whole with its pages there, a short first page or the search box closing, counts them); and a cover written after the reply counts only once the list is drawn again, which a live level does only when its rows change, though a row already drawn reads its file again whenever it scrolls back into the kept rows, so an app that deletes the file gets a blank there, the size being checked only when the row is built; and a theme with separators between two-line rows draws none between covered rows, whose height isn't its two-line rows' (`paint_separators`). Checks in `test/patch.py`: no file, another row's key and a progress row leave the list as it was; a cover's row, a row without one and a chevron's, in 78 px rows; and later pages joining as 78 px rows; `test/fw/test_addon.py` checks the key (a `%` in a uri too), the 128 px limit, the choice, and the bitmaps let go.

**Windows.** An app can keep a long list to a window of it at a time instead (the `window` word, below): a card app such as Jellyfin sends a window of a few `pages` replies, the last ending with a **Next page** row instead of a cursor, and a later window's first reply starting with **Previous page**. A row of kind `page` has a cursor of the level's own list as its context (empty: the list's start, no argument sent); a press asks for the list from it (`page_to`: the list's own arguments up to `base` and that cursor) **in the level's place**, not as a level over it, so Back leaves the list instead of stepping back through its windows, and the firmware holds at most one window, which Back from a deeper level asks for alone. uri `prev` slides the window in from the left and selects its last row once its pages are in; any other uri (the app sends `next`) slides it in from the right and selects row 1, the row after its Previous page (past a Search and a Sort row kept as rows, under a theme without a title bar). A page row is a plain list row with an empty subtitle: `row`'s usual path and a list's row height (`row_h`), so in a list drawn with covers it is 78 px with the cover's room empty, as the trailing row. Without the word an app pages as before (up to 500 rows, then More…).

**Capabilities.** Every Streaming scan writes `/tmp/q2-addon.caps` (`ADDON_CAPS`), so a stale or half-written file never outlives the next scan: one line of words, the card-app features this firmware has, as a set (an app tests for a word, and order means nothing). Firmware without a feature lacks its word. `/tmp` is empty after every reboot and firmware update, so the file always describes the running firmware. Older firmware never writes it, so an app that finds no file knows it is on older firmware and falls back. The word `libsource` says the firmware writes Streaming Songs' state to `/tmp/q2-addon.library` and draws `needslib` rows ([Server library](#server-library)). `ahead` (always) says the firmware writes `.ahead` and reads a streaming app's `.stream`, and `grow` (only while q2player is the player: its `/tmp/q2clicks` is there at the scan, `ahead_caps`) that a song may play while it arrives ([Download Ahead](server-library.md#download-ahead-and-the-streaming-state)).

Words: `playlist` (Stream mode plays an `.m3u`), `progress` (the progress row), `pages` (full lists), `window` (`page` rows, **Windows**, above), `library` (**Library update**, below), `sections` (**Sections**, above), `art` (**Covers**, above), `urls` (**Stream mode: URL queues**, below), `sort` (the `sort` row, **Sort in the title bar**, above), `field` (the `field` row, **Fields**, below), `more` (`q2app`'s `more=`, **Now Playing's ⋯**, below), `fav` (**Hearts**, below).

**Stop and Retry.** A page that can't show the app's rows ends in **Stop <name>** whenever the app may be running (launched, a restart pending, or its loop's pid file there): an error page under its Retry, and a level loading or starting for `SLOW_MS` (3 s; a frozen app holds a request up to `ADDON_WAIT_MS`, 15 s). It ends the app as Stop Streaming Services does, a TERM to its loop (`app_stop`), so a frozen app, which can't answer a stop op of its own, stops too; then it toasts and leaves the page. Retry on "<name> isn't running" while the loop's pid file is there (the app running, its socket gone) restarts it: the loop is asked to end, the page waits as for a start (a pending `restart` counts as starting), and `poll_one` starts the app again once the pid file is gone, or after `RESTART_MS` (20 s) regardless; q2-soulseek's launcher kills an app still there 15 s after its TERM. Otherwise Retry asks again, starting the app first if it isn't running. An app whose `q2app` says `stop=0` (`app_t.nostop`, read as text at the scan, as `scrobble=0`, a Windows editor's `\r` taken) has no Stop row: `stoppable` is 0 for it, so a slow level stays at Loading… with no rows (`l->slow` never set), and its error page's second row is **Cancel**, which does what Return does (`pop`, or `navigator_back` from the first level), the app left running. No capability word: older firmware keeps Stop.

**Fields.** A row of kind `field` (the `field` word) is a value the user types, such as a sign-in page's user name and password, whose subtitle the app chooses (the name, `***`). Its press opens the search box (`search_box(i + 1)`: `pg.field` names the row, its title the box's hint); OK with text (`searched`, `G_FIELD`) calls `field_sent`, which sends the row's uri with its context, when not empty, and the text as the last argument, as the level's own fetch (`l->id`, `pg.act` 0), then lets the shown reply go and shows the level's Loading… page: no `push`, nothing titled with the text, and the selected row kept (`search_box`'s `keep_sel`). `got` takes the reply as the level's: `ok` draws its rows, anything else is the level's error page, whose Retry is the level's own `fetch`, so the text is never sent again; a `refresh` and Back ask the level's own op too, and the app answers with the page as it stands. The row is checked again when OK comes (still `K_READY`, still a `field` at that index, a uri), so a reply that landed under the box sends nothing. A text of 64 bytes or more, a plain search's too (`searched` reads into a 256-byte buffer, wiped after) is not sent, with a "Too long" toast: a cut password would be the wrong one. Done sends `searched` twice (EVT_IM_ACTION and EVT_VALUE_CHANGED), so `pg.field` stays set when the text is refused (`field_sent` and `search_box` clear it) and the toast waits for no pending `go` (its modal loop would run it under the edit's own handler): the second call must not toast again or send the text's first 63 bytes as a `search`. ponytail: a text of 256 bytes or more closes silently, as stock's `widget_get_text_utf8` writes nothing for a text that does not fit; a field that long is not worth a bigger buffer. A field's request (`req.field`) that finds no socket while the app starts or restarts is the level's error page ("<name> isn't running", Retry and Stop or Cancel), not the wait a level's own fetch gets, which would ask the level's op and drop the text unsaid. The text never reaches a title, a toast or a file: `pg.term` is cleared once it is in the request, the worker clears the request's bytes past the reply once it has ended (`memset`), and `req_send` clears the buffer itself when no worker starts, so the freed buffer keeps none of it. ponytail: the T9 box shows the text while it is typed, as for a search (AWTK's password edit isn't tried with the T9 keyboard); a text is at most 63 bytes (`pg.term`), checked at OK rather than with the box's `max_length`, which isn't tried with T9 either.

**Now Playing's ⋯**, below).

**Stop and Retry.** A page that can't show the app's rows ends in **Stop <name>** whenever the app may be running (launched, a restart pending, or its loop's pid file there): an error page under its Retry, and a level loading or starting for `SLOW_MS` (3 s; a frozen app holds a request up to `ADDON_WAIT_MS`, 15 s). It ends the app as Stop Streaming Services does, a TERM to its loop (`app_stop`), so a frozen app, which can't answer a stop op of its own, stops too; then it toasts and leaves the page. Retry on "<name> isn't running" while the loop's pid file is there (the app running, its socket gone) restarts it: the loop is asked to end, the page waits as for a start (a pending `restart` counts as starting), and `poll_one` starts the app again once the pid file is gone, or after `RESTART_MS` (20 s) regardless; q2-soulseek's launcher kills an app still there 15 s after its TERM. Otherwise Retry asks again, starting the app first if it isn't running. An app whose `q2app` says `stop=0` (`app_t.nostop`, read as text at the scan, as `scrobble=0`, a Windows editor's `\r` taken) has no Stop row: `stoppable` is 0 for it, so a slow level stays at Loading… with no rows (`l->slow` never set), and its error page's second row is **Cancel**, which does what Return does (`pop`, or `navigator_back` from the first level), the app left running. No capability word: older firmware keeps Stop.

**Fields.** A row of kind `field` (the `field` word) is a value the user types, such as a sign-in page's user name and password, whose subtitle the app chooses (the name, `***`). Its press opens the search box (`search_box(i + 1)`: `pg.field` names the row, its title the box's hint); OK with text (`searched`, `G_FIELD`) calls `field_sent`, which sends the row's uri with its context, when not empty, and the text as the last argument, as the level's own fetch (`l->id`, `pg.act` 0), then lets the shown reply go and shows the level's Loading… page: no `push`, nothing titled with the text, and the selected row kept (`search_box`'s `keep_sel`). `got` takes the reply as the level's: `ok` draws its rows, anything else is the level's error page, whose Retry is the level's own `fetch`, so the text is never sent again; a `refresh` and Back ask the level's own op too, and the app answers with the page as it stands. The row is checked again when OK comes (still `K_READY`, still a `field` at that index, a uri), so a reply that landed under the box sends nothing. A text of 64 bytes or more, a plain search's too (`searched` reads into a buffer one byte larger than `pg.term`, so a full one was cut) is cleared and not sent, with a "Too long" toast: a cut password would be the wrong one. A field's request (`req.field`) that finds no socket while the app starts or restarts is the level's error page ("<name> isn't running", Retry and Stop or Cancel), not the wait a level's own fetch gets, which would ask the level's op and drop the text unsaid. The text never reaches a title, a toast or a file: `pg.term` is cleared once it is in the request, the worker clears the request's bytes past the reply once it has ended (`memset`), and `req_send` clears the buffer itself when no worker starts, so the freed buffer keeps none of it. ponytail: the T9 box shows the text while it is typed, as for a search (AWTK's password edit isn't tried with the T9 keyboard); a text is at most 63 bytes (`pg.term`), checked at OK rather than with the box's `max_length`, which isn't tried with T9 either.

**Now Playing's ⋯.** An app's `q2app` can say `more=<op> <title>` (`app_t.more`, read at the scan, a trailing `\r` taken). Each queue an app's `.play` starts (`stream_start`'s `play_folder`, or `urls_start`'s `app_urls_play` when it returns 1) notes the app and `playback_loads` after its load (`qa`). The click on Now Playing's `img_more` (`ringnav_dispatch` in `patch/navigation.c`, before stock's handler, and the hold menu's More…, which clicks it through `stock_dispatch_trampoline`) asks `addon_more` first: while `playback_loads` is still `qa.loads` (no queue loaded since), the app has a `more` and its binary is still on the card (as `addon_goto` asks), it closes the app's page if one is open (as `addon_goto`) and opens the page at `op`, no arguments, titled `title` or the app's name (`page_at`), and the click goes no further (STOP), so stock's `playermore_page` never opens; otherwise stock's ⋯ opens as before. An op of 16 bytes or more, or none, leaves ⋯ stock's. ponytail: a stock reload of the app's own queue steps `playback_loads`, so ⋯ is stock's after it until the app plays a queue again; it errs toward stock's page. Checks in `test/fw/test_addon.py`: the click opening the page or stock's, the keys, the queue's mark.

**Stream mode.** An app that plays as well (q2-deezer's Stream mode) writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.play`, "<seq> <folder>": a hidden card folder (under `/mnt/mmc/.`, no `..` segment) it fills with a list's songs named in play order ("01 - Title [id].flac"), each renamed into place once whole. `stream_poll`, every `ADDON_POLL_MS` while the app runs, follows it: a new one is played from its first song once one is there (a 0 ms timer: the folder's songs by name, `app_album_songs`, through `play_folder` as a local album, Now Playing opening); while the queue playing is still the folder's (its first song's path in it), songs named after the last one queued join its end through `playback_queue_insert`, as Add to Queue; and the path of the one playing goes to `/tmp/q2-<id>.playing` (`blob_io`), from which the app fetches a couple ahead and deletes the ones long played. Once another queue plays, the session is left; a new seq starts again. A session is one app's (`sm.app`): each app's `.play` is kept hashed in its slot (`app_t.play`), and only a change to an app's own starts one, so two apps' files left in `/tmp` (q2-deezer and q2-subsonic keep theirs while they run) never take the queue from each other at every poll. The folder is listed only when its mtime changes (`stream_newer`, `sm.seen`), not every poll; an mtime within a second of now is scanned again on the next poll, as a file could land later in that second. A song that is added and then rejected (no `stSongInfo` for it yet) is picked up only at the folder's next change. Songs are queued by name after the last one queued, so a song that finishes downloading before an earlier one is never queued. The library scan skips hidden folders (`SCAN_DIRS`: the folder walk's `"."` test is `ringnav_scan_dir`, which skips any name starting with a dot, as Folder view's list does), so streamed songs never join the Library.

**Stream mode: a playlist.** `.play` may name a playlist file instead, "<seq> <path>.m3u" (`.m3u` in any case): it must be on the card: any path under `/mnt/mmc/` without a `..` segment, a hidden folder or not. A `.play` path of 160 bytes or more (`sm.dir` holds 159), or a `.play` of 190 bytes or more (`raw` holds that much, so its path may be cut), is refused in either mode, as cut it would name another file or folder. q2-subsonic writes one per queue, `/mnt/mmc/.subsonic/stream/queue-<seq>.m3u`. It is UTF-8 with one absolute card path a line; `#` lines (`#EXTM3U`, `#EXTINF`) and blank lines are ignored, and a leading BOM and CRLF line ends are taken. Its songs are queued in its order, wherever on the card they are (synced ones in their album folders, streamed ones in the app's folder). `m3u_songs` reads the file whole (up to `M3U_MAX`, 256 KB; of a longer file, it reads one byte more and drops the last line whose newline it didn't read, so a cut line is never taken as a path or waited for) and goes on from the entries it has already passed (`sm.next`); an entry not there yet (`access`) is waited for (`sm.want`), and nothing after it is queued before it, so order holds while streamed songs land out of order. A line off the card (not under `/mnt/mmc/`, or with a `..` segment: `/../`, a trailing `/..`; a name with an ellipsis, "Hello... (Live).flac", is fine, `dotdot`) is passed over, as is a file there that its folder's listing (`app_album_songs`, `REC_TYPE` 8) doesn't take as a song; neither is waited for. Nor is a line of 512 bytes or more (`sm.want`, `sm.first` and `sm.playing` hold 511), so a path the buffers would cut is never waited on forever. The app changes the file only by writing it aside and renaming it into place. Entries are counted, not compared: the ones already passed (`sm.next`) are never read again, so the app keeps every entry before the one waited for as it was (appending is always safe), and may rewrite the rest. An entry the firmware waits for (a card path under 512 bytes, its file not there) is never passed while it is missing, so from the first such entry on, the app may drop or replace a song that won't come (a download that failed, a synced file deleted since), and the songs after it then play. To change an entry before it, the app writes a new seq. At most `M3U_BATCH` (32) folders are listed a poll (a song's folder, `app_album_songs`, unless the song before it was in the same one), so a long list's start doesn't stall the UI, however many albums it spans; the rest follow on the next polls. The first batch plays as a folder's first song does; later ones join the queue's end through `playback_queue_insert`. The session is identified by its first song's path (`sm.first`) and by its queue's load: `playback_loads` counts `mclLoadPlayList` calls (`ringnav_load`); `stream_poll` notes it as the session starts, and `stream_start` again after its `play_folder`, whose load is synchronous. Once the queue's first song is another, or any queue has been loaded since (a Library or Folder play of the same album is the user's, even though it starts with the same file), the session is left, before its first song too (`S_WAIT`, and `stream_start` checks again): a song that lands later never replaces a queue the user started meanwhile. A stock reload of the same queue ends it too: it errs toward leaving the user's playback alone. A session still waiting for its first song (any mode, URL queues too) is also left once the user moves to another song of the queue playing (`moved_on`: `playback_picks`, which `playback_pick` counts at a manual Next or Previous, a Shuffle Albums or Folders group skip, an Up Next pick and a car remote jump, never at a skip nobody pressed): on the device a shuffled server song finished downloading half way through the song Next had played, and played over it. The song waited for stays on the card. Folder mode keeps its own test for a session that plays (the queue's first song in its folder) and no load test: a hidden folder can't be played from Library or Folder view, so the test would gain it nothing. The file is read again only when its mtime changes, the song waited for lands, or a batch filled (`m3u_ready`). Folder mode wakes for any new name that isn't hidden or a `.part` or `.tmp`, so `.m4a`, `.opus`, `.ogg`, `.wav`, `.ape` and `.dsf` stream too; whether a file is a song is stock's listing's call (`ringnav_audio_extension` over stock's format list). In either mode no folder is listed while a library scan runs (`library_scanning`, coverflow.c: its thread started and not done), the scan dialog's own loop included, as a listing (`toolsLoadDirectory`) refills `tools_pdeq_directory`, which the scan's thread fills too; nor while its window (the user's Update Local Music page, `updatemusic_page`, or its dialog, `updatemusic_dialog`, which a library request opens without the page) is still open after it, as `play_folder` would open Now Playing over it (`scanning`): nothing is armed or queued until both are over, a `stream_start` that finds one running clears `sm.seen` so the next poll after it looks again, and `.playing` still follows the song playing. A user's Next on the last song queued while the playlist waits for its next entry (`sm.want`, still downloading) does not reach stock, whose Next on a queue's last song wraps to its first (a radio's seed, played again; the device, 2026-11-17): `addon_next_waits` (from `change_music`) notes `playback_picks` in `sm.skip` and moves Now Playing to the waited song at once: a record of its path and file name, named by `card_record_tags` (below), shown as a pressed server song is (`catalogue_np_show`, `np_press`: the song playing stops, and `np_stream.c`'s spinner turns from the song's own `.stream` line), with no toast; the poll that queues the waited song plays it (`player_start_queue`). With stock's player that is once the app's download is whole (it renames it into place), as stock skips or hangs on a file still arriving; with q2player (`grow` in the caps) once `START_MS` of it is there (`stream_startable`), as q2player waits at the end of the bytes there are. Any other move of the user's meanwhile (Previous, a pick) changes `playback_picks` and drops the wait, and the player's parse of that song ends the pressed one's display. The user's words, 2026-11-17 23:56, of the toast this replaces: "why doesn't it go to next song and show it buffering? it shouldn't reject".

**Stream mode: URL queues.** An app that streams (a Jellyfin app, say) can have stock's Tidal player play its songs instead of saving them to the card. It writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.urls` whole (temp + rename) and names it in `.play` as `<seq> /tmp/q2-<id>.urls`; only the app's own file there is taken (`sm.urls`). The file is `#Q2URLS/1<TAB>start=<index>` (and `<TAB>now=1` for a queue whose app is to be told what plays, below), then one line a song, `<url or card path><TAB><title><TAB><artist><TAB><album><TAB><cover url><TAB><seconds>` (no field holds a tab or a line break; a field missing is empty; a line with no URL is passed over, and so is one whose first field is neither a web URL, `http://` or `https://`, nor a card path, under `/mnt/mmc/` with no `..` segment, the rule a Stream mode playlist's lines pass: a server's string reaches stock's player as nothing else; a cover is fetched by stock's cover thread with curl, so one that isn't a web URL is dropped; `seconds` is optional and not read yet), read up to `AU_MAX` (256 KB, a last line cut there dropped) and kept up to `AU_SONGS` (5,000 songs, the rest of the file passed over; `start=` counts the songs kept, so a skipped line doesn't move it). A line whose URL or card path is `AU_PATH` (1,024) bytes or more, each `}` counted as five, is passed over: stock's `mcl_tidalStartPlayer` and `mclStartPlayer` both `strcpy` it into a `0x600`-byte stack buffer (`0x5bf9a8`, `0x5c023c`), then expand every `}` to `%0x7d` in place, unbounded (`toolsReplaceString`). `stream_poll` starts it on a 0 ms timer, as a folder's first song (`urls_start`, not during a scan or its dialog), and the session ends there: the queue is stock's. `app_urls_play` (`patch/tidal.c`) builds stock Tidal records as `load_titaltracks_ex` (`0x48670c`) does: an 88-byte `stSongInfo` zeroed, `REC_TIDAL_ID` `app:<gen>:<n>` (the queue's generation and the song's place), `REC_NAME` and `REC_TITLE` the title (`Unknown` without one, since stock prints them with `%s`), `REC_ARTIST`, `REC_ALBUM` and `REC_COVER` when given, `REC_PATH` empty for a URL or the card path, `REC_TYPE` 8 and `+0x38` `0xf1`, each `malloc`'d. `_deque_push_back` copies the record and `toolsFreeStSongInfo` frees the original, as stock does. It plays them as a Tidal page does, `play_folder(q, start, 0xf1)` (Now Playing with `{q, start, 0xf1, 2}`), and keeps the URLs (`au`) by generation.

For a `0xf1` queue `mclStartPlayer` calls `get_tidal_trackurl` (`0x483f28`, hooked as `ringnav_tidal_track`), which for an `app:` record (the queue's record at `MCL_POS`) does what stock does around a track itself (`app_track`), so the id never reaches Tidal's API or stock's stream thread: offline it returns `networkGetConnectStatus()` (`0x483f54`); online it calls `tidal_playurl(0)` and `mclStop()` (`0x483ff8`), then on a detached thread hands the URL to stock's `mcl_tidalStartPlayer` past the `tidal_start` hook (`stock_tidal_trampoline`), and then, as the stream thread does after it (`0x487b38`, `0x487b64`), pauses if `savestartbt` was set and sets `transposition` to 1, which arms Now Playing's online tick (`get_onlineid3info`, its notifications and auto-advance). These threads start one URL at a time (`au.start`), as stock's one thread does, and a later start drops one still waiting (`au.play`); an id from a queue replaced since has no URL, and the player stays stopped. A start also drops one still waiting, and a stream thread's Tidal fetch still in flight (`tidalfurlstart`, as stock at `0x483f5c`), so the last Now Playing asked for wins; a job waiting is dropped too when a queue has loaded since (`playback_loads`). A card-path record arms stock's auto-advance flag itself (`tidal_playurl(1)`: `mclAutoChange` only moves on with `-0x426c` above 0, which the stream thread's `transposition` sets for a URL), waits for a stream still inside stock's start to finish (`au.start`, its 100 or 150 ms start sleep), and returns, and `mclStartPlayer`, which has no `mclStop` on its local path, writes its own play command after it, playing `REC_PATH` as a local file, so its Now Playing is a local file's: no `get_onlineid3info`, no cover by URL. Next, Previous and a song's natural end come through `mclStartPlayer` the same way. Only stock's idle tick (`player_mainscheduling`, on the UI thread) reads the flag, and a UI-thread start is running before the tick's next pass; ponytail: a start from another thread (`player_save_start`'s jack and Bluetooth restarts) could in principle be passed by that tick while the player is stopped. `tidal_play` never sees an `app:` id, the trampoline being past its hook ([Tidal cache](#tidal-cache)). The cover: `get_onlineid3info` calls `player_set_coverinfo(REC_COVER, REC_NAME, 4)` at `0x493708`, and type 4 fetches from Tidal's image server with Tidal's session; `COVERINFO_CALL` (`tools/build.py`) turns that `jalr` into `jal app_coverinfo_call` (`move $a3, $s1; j app_coverinfo`), which passes type 2 for an `app:` record instead: curl to `/tmp/dlnadownpic.jpg` on stock's cover thread, scaled to 320 px. The stock routines this calls by address (`APP_URL_CALLS`, checked against the demo's symbols at build time) are not in `FUNCTIONS`, so `test/patch.py` runs them as stock's. Stock gives the rest: Now Playing's spinner shows while a `0xf1` stream buffers (`mclGetCacheBuffer() <= 0`, `0x53cf70`), and the player seeks with HTTP ranges (a Jellyfin `/Audio/{id}/stream?static=true` URL answers them). None of `get_tidal_trackurl`, `mclStartPlayer`, `mcl_tidalStartPlayer` or `get_onlineid3info` checks for a Tidal session, so no Tidal sign-in is needed. The capability word is `urls`. ponytail: a stream that fails leaves the player stopped, and it doesn't skip on (`mclAutoChange` returns at status 1, `0x5c1170`); online match and scrobbling skip `0xf1` queues, as for Tidal; an app's queue isn't kept for the next power-on; there is no gapless playback for `0xf0`–`0xf2`; Now Playing's heart is stock Tidal's for a song whose line names no item (**Hearts**, below). Checks in `test/patch.py`: a queue's records and start, another app's or a stray `.urls` never read, a start offline and online (the URL on its thread, the pause and tick after it, a later start or a queue loaded since dropping an earlier one), a card song arming the advance, a Tidal fetch stopped, a Tidal track still stock's, a replaced queue's old ids, files that aren't a queue, over-long URLs and card paths passed over, and the cover's type.

**Stream mode: lyrics for a URL queue.** Stock's lyrics loader and the tag lookup in `ringnav_lyric` (`patch/lyrics.c`) skip a `0xf1` queue, so a streamed song had none. The app can leave each song's lyrics, as its server gives them, in `/tmp/q2-<id>.lyrics/<n>.lrc` beside its queue, `<n>` the song's place among the songs kept (counted from 0, as the id's). The app empties the folder before naming a new queue and writes each file whole (temp + rename): a file carries no generation, and it is read once. `app_urls_play` keeps that folder with the queue (`au.lyr`: the queue's path with `.lyrics` for `.urls`), and for a `0xf1` track whose id is `app:<gen>:<n>` of the latest queue, `ringnav_lyric` reads `<n>.lrc` (`app_lyrics`, `file_text`: its first `LYRIC_TAG_MAX` bytes, a UTF-8 mark skipped) with the parser a tag's lyrics take, synced or plain. An id from a replaced queue, a Tidal track or a song with no file gets none. ponytail: the file is read once, as the track loads; a song whose file the app hasn't written yet (a skip far ahead just after the queue starts) shows none until it is played again. Checks in `test/patch.py`: synced and plain lyrics, an older queue's track, a song with no file and a Tidal track.

**Hearts.** Stock's heart click on Now Playing (`0x53c968`, `img_fav`'s, which `rate_bind` swaps for `rate_fav_click`, [Ratings](#ratings)) refuses queue types 2, 3 and `0xf2`; for `0xf1` it calls `tidal_collection` (`0x488d2c`), which toggles stock's `isFav_playing` byte and starts `addFavouriteTrack` or `removeFavouriteTrack` on a thread with `atoll` of the record's id (0 for `app:…`: Tidal's API, without a session), then sets the image `tidal_fav_add` or `tidal_fav_rm`; any other type is `manage_myfav` and `play_fav` or `play_unfav`. Now Playing's update (`0x53cf08`), on a track change or a forced refresh, draws a `0xf1` track's heart from `isFav_playing` (`0x53d178`), which otherwise only Tidal's favorites thread (`tidalGetFavoritesIdsThd`) sets, started by `get_tidal_fav_flag` (`0x493458`) when the Tidal page or its More opens, not per track. A URL queue's line may carry two more fields: the song's item, the app's own id (`au.items`; an empty one, or one of `AU_ITEM`, 128 bytes, or more, is none), and its heart (`au.fav`, `1` a favorite, a CR after it taken), kept per queue with its app's id from the queue's path (`au.app`). `app_track` sets `isFav_playing` as every `app:` song starts, before its URL or file goes to the player, so the page's update draws it: `au.fav` for one with an item, 0 for any other. A queue loading (`ringnav_load`) clears it again when an app's song set it last (`app_fav_load`, `au.hearts`), so a Tidal queue played next doesn't show the last app song's heart; stock's own value is left alone. A tap on the heart asks `app_fav` first: for a `0xf1` record whose id is `app:<gen>:<n>` of the latest queue with an item, it appends `item\t<0|1>\t<item>` to `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/fav.log` (`addon_fav`, `patch/addon.c`), then flips `au.fav` and `isFav_playing`, and `rate_fav_click` sets the image as stock's click would, stock's never called; a press the card refuses changes nothing and toasts "Favorite not saved". An `app:` record with no item (its line named none, or its queue was replaced) returns -3: the tap only toasts "This app has no favorites", so an app's song never reaches Tidal's API. Any other song's tap is stock's, as before. For a song on the card, each change Q2 Muse makes to My Fav (the heart, the picker's 5 in or out, the queue menu's Favorites rows and `rate_album_favs`) goes through `fav_told` to `addon_fav_path`, which reads every card app's `q2app` (each `.<id>` in the card's root: no scan needed, and a press is rare) for `favdir`, one folder name in the card's root (a Windows editor's `\r` dropped; empty, `.`, `..` or one with a `/` names none), and appends `path\t<0|1>\t<path>` for the first whose folder holds the song; a refusal toasts "Favorite not sent to the app", and an album's songs stop at the first. An album's Off tells the app only of songs that were in My Fav, so a song liked on the server and never hearted on the Q2 is not unliked. Each press is one `fwrite` of an LF and its line, appended on the UI thread with no fsync, as `scrobble_append`'s listen (the LF first ends a line a cut write left, so it never joins the next press); the app takes the file by renaming it ([librespot.md](librespot.md)). The word is `fav`. ponytail: stock's own batch-select Add to My Fav and its queue delete don't tell the app (the next change through Q2 Muse does, for that song); a synced song's heart is the Q2's, not the server's; a streamed song's heart is its queue's, so a change made on the server meanwhile shows only in the app's next queue; stock's `notifyFavor` (`0x525c70`, after its own toggle) isn't called for an app's press. Checks in `test/fw` (`test_tidal.py`, `test_addon.py`, `test_nav_library_pages.py`): the fields kept (a CRLF line, a field after them), the press flipped and written, an app's song without an item and every other song's heart, a refused press, the start's flag and a load clearing it (through `ringnav_load`), the favdir rule, a press after a cut one, and the synced song's line from the heart, the picker's 5 and 0, the hold menu's rows and an album's (stopping at a refusal; Off only for songs that were in My Fav); in `test/patch.py`: the start's `isFav_playing` and a load clearing it.

**Stream mode: what a URL queue plays.** An app that reports plays to its server (Jellyfin's `/Sessions/Playing`, Progress and Stopped) has to know which of its songs plays, and how; the queue is stock's once it starts. A queue whose header holds `now=1` (a field of its own: a tab before it, a tab or the line's end after; `au.now`) is told in `/tmp/q2-<id>.now`, `<seq><TAB><n><TAB><playing|paused|stopped><TAB><sec><TAB><length>` ([librespot.md](librespot.md) has the app's side). `urls_start` hands the session's app and its `.play` seq (`sm.seq`: up to the first space or control byte, 23 bytes at most) to `now_start` once `app_urls_play` played the queue; an earlier queue whose file says it plays is written `stopped` there first, whichever app's it was. `now_poll`, in `addon_poll` every `ADDON_POLL_MS` whether the app runs or not, asks `app_urls_at` (`patch/tidal.c`) for the song's `n`: the record at `MCL_POS` of a `0xf1` queue (`MCL_TYPE`), as `get_tidal_trackurl` finds it, whose id is `app:<gen>:<n>` of the latest queue (`au.gen`) with `au.now` set; and reads the state and position as the sleep timer does (`mclGetPlayStatus`, `player_playtime_and_length`, `media_owner`). It writes the line whole (`blob_io` through `/tmp/q2-now.tmp`; tmpfs, so cheap on the UI thread) only on a change: another song, state or length at once, a position at once while paused or after a seek back, else after `NOW_STEP_S` (5 s); nothing while nothing changes, and nothing before the queue first plays. Another queue or player (`app_urls_at` -1, `media_owner` not 1) writes `stopped` at once, the player stopped `NOW_STOP_MS` (3 s, so not between songs, as `sleep_check` counts) writes it after that, once (`nw.live`); playing again writes `playing`. `addon_stop` writes `stopped` at once: Home's Rockbox row (`rockbox_open`) kills demo right after it, `/tmp` kept, and Stop Streaming Services stops a `0xf1` queue after it. A demo restarted with `/tmp` kept (a crash, the watchdog) starts with `nw` zeroed, so `now_sweep`, at the first `addon_poll`, turns the state of every `/tmp/q2-<id>.now` (a valid id) that says `playing` or `paused` into `stopped`, the rest of its line kept: an app never sees a play that never ends. `n` is the songs-kept index the record id and the lyrics use, so it needs no per-line field. Never the URL: it carries the app's token. ponytail: a stream that buffers past 3 s before it plays reads as `stopped`, then `playing`, for the same song; the position is the player's, so a seek forward under 5 s while playing is told at the next 5 s step. Checks in `test/fw/test_addon.py` and `test_tidal.py`: the header field, the song, states and steps, a stop between songs and a real one, another queue, player or older queue, a queue that didn't ask, the next queue (the same app's or another's), `addon_stop`, a restart's sweep, and the seq.

**Library update** (`patch/addon_library.c`). After a sync an app can ask for Update Local Music and the import of its playlists, so the user does neither by hand. It writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.library` whole (temp + rename): `<seq>` on its first line (at most 23 bytes; the file's end ends it when no newline follows), then `scan`, `import <path>` and `add <path>` lines, LF or CRLF, each path a `.m3u` (any case) directly in `/mnt/mmc/_explaylist_data/`, with no `/` in its name (so never `..`; a name with an ellipsis is fine), that exists, and whose playlist name (the file's name less `.m3u`) is at most 63 bytes (`LIB_NAME`). That limit is stock's: `ringnav_playlist_create` cuts a longer name into `char title[64]` and skips its duplicate check, so the stored name would never match the file's again, `import` would never replace it and `add` would never find it, and every sync would add another copy (a name in Chinese, Japanese or Korean reaches 64 bytes at 22 characters). `import` replaces a playlist of the same name, for a name the app owns (one it imported before); `add` imports the file only when no playlist has its name yet, and otherwise leaves that playlist alone, so a playlist of the user's with the same name is never replaced.

`addon_poll` calls `library_poll` once a pass, every `LIB_POLL_MS` (500 ms), for every app on the card (`addon_id`) whether it runs or not, so an app that exits right after its sync is still served, and no app's poll drives another's request. It reads each app's first line alone (the file's first 62 bytes); a seq that app hasn't had taken (each app's last one is kept, by id, in RAM; a seq `.done` already answers, as after demo restarts for Rockbox from Home with `/tmp` kept, is taken as done) reads the whole file once, and that read's own first line must be the seq: a file gone between the two reads, or replaced by a newer seq, is looked at again at the next poll, so no seq runs another's lines and none is answered without its own. The request is then checked whole: an error is written at once and nothing runs. A seq of 24 bytes or more, or an empty first line, is never run: it is answered `<seq> error Seq too long`, or ` error Missing seq` (no seq, so the line starts with a space), written again only once `.done` no longer holds that answer. One request runs at a time; a newer seq is taken once it is done.

The answer goes to `/tmp/q2-<id>.library.done`: `<seq> ok`, or `<seq> error <why>`, where `<why>` is `No memory card` (`/tmp/mmc_add` missing, or the import returned -2), `Unknown request: <line>`, `Not a playlist in /mnt/mmc/_explaylist_data: <path>`, `Name too long: <name>`, `Not found: <path>`, `Request too long` (the request fills `LIB_MAX`, 32 KB: more than 300 imports of the longest names), `Couldn't start the scan` or `Couldn't import <name>` (both below); then one `exists <path>` line for each `add` left alone, after an error too. It is built whole in one buffer and written with `blob_io` through `/tmp/q2-library.tmp`, renamed only once all of it is written and synced (`/tmp` full would cut the `exists` lines, and the app would take a user's same-named playlist for its own); otherwise `<seq> error Couldn't write the answer` is written the same way, and if that fails too, the temp is removed and nothing is published. The request is read into heap (`libup.list`, `LIB_MAX` for the request and `LIB_ANSWER` after it for the answer), taken at the first request and kept; its files are then moved to its start, each as its op (`i` import, `a` an add not looked up yet, `e` an add left alone) and its name, NUL-ended.

The scan and the import each wait for the same check (`library_safe`): nothing plays, as `ringnav_sleep`'s quiet check has it — the player, Spotify, the radio or a video (`media_playing`), AirPlay (`airplayGetFlag` 2) or the Bluetooth receiver (`bt__recv_pageflag` 2) — since the scan dialog's init, `dialog_updatemusic_dialog_init`, calls `player_stop` unconditionally at `0x4a2d78`, which stops paused playback too and loses its place: so the scan alone also waits while a local song is paused and the screen is on (`mclGetPlayStatus` 3 and `g_backlight_status`); with the screen off it goes ahead and stops the song, as Library → Update Local Music does; no scan runs (`library_scanning`, coverflow.c's: `SCAN_THREAD` set and `SCAN_DONE` clear); and every open window, the window manager's children less the status bar (`system_bar`), is on an allowlist of windows that show no library records: `home_page`, `stream_page`, `streamconf_page` and `streamsvc_page` (Streaming's Configuration and its provider pages), `addon_page` and `qrcode_page` (a card app's page and its QR code), `playing_page` (Now Playing, which plays its own copies, `mcl_pdeqplaylist`), and System and Playback settings' own pages, `sysset_page`, `display_page`, `backlight_page`, `lighttime_page`, `keylock_page`, `language_page`, `datetime_page`, `autotime_page`, `manualtime_page`, `standby_page`, `powermanager_page`, `sleepshutdown_page`, `about_page`, `bluetooth_page`, `btquality_page`, `btadjustvol_page`, `wifi_page`, `wifiset_page`, `netservice_page`, `playset_page`, `audiosetting_page`, `playmode_page`, `replaygain_page`, `filter_page`, `dsdoutput_page`, `memplay_page`, `usbvol_page`, `maxvol_page`, `bootvol_page`, `balance_page` and `equalizer_page`. Any other window holds the request until it closes, so the check fails safe: a dialog (`library_poll` also runs inside every modal loop, a toast's or a confirm's, and no request starts there); stock's Library pages, whose rows are records of the lists the import reloads (`p_deque_playlist` and `p_deque_showlist`, `load_localclass_list(0xf00b)`), so a press on one afterwards would take the wrong record; Q2 Muse's own library pages, which keep records read from the database the scan rebuilds; the user's own Update Local Music (`updatemusic_page`, awaiting its OK: no second dialog); USB storage; firmware update, reset, Wi-Fi transfer and the App Store; and any page added later until it is listed.

A request with neither line reports `ok` at once and runs nothing. The scan opens stock's own `dialog/updatemusic_dialog` (a zeroed 16-byte context, as stock's four callers do), a modal dialog: its init starts the scan's thread, and its own loop runs until it closes. The state is `L_SCAN` before the call; a `library_poll` from inside that loop (`libup.busy` set) runs nothing but notes the scan it sees (`scan_seen`: the thread running, or `updatemusic_dialog` open), as does a check right after the call. The scan is over once it was seen and is gone; one never seen (the dialog didn't open) is answered `Couldn't start the scan`, never `ok` without a scan. Then the payload loads Library → Playlists' list itself (`ringnav_localclass(0xf00b)`), looks each `add`'s name up in it as stock's replace does (`library_adds`: the file's name less `.m3u`, compared whole with each playlist's), drops the ones found from the import, and calls stock `importPlayList` (`0x5186c8`), as the Import Playlists row does; with nothing left to import it is not called, and no toast follows. Stock stops at a create that fails (-1: a database error, or the 100 playlists' cap) and returns 1 as if done, so afterwards each imported file's name must be in the reloaded `p_deque_playlist`; the first that isn't gives `Couldn't import <name>`. The result is written to `.library.done` first, then toasted ("Playlists updated", or the error): stock's `msginfo_dialog`, like Update Local Music's dialog, runs a loop of its own that polls again, so `library_poll` is guarded (`libup.busy`) and a nested poll runs nothing. For each file stock looks its name up in `p_deque_playlist` (`checkPlayListByName`, a `strcmp` against each playlist's name) and deletes a match, header (`deletePlaylist`) and entries (`deleteAllMusicByPlaylist`), before it creates the playlist again (`createPlayListItem`, Q2 Muse's `ringnav_playlist_create`) and adds the file's songs, their tags read from the files, so a playlist of the same name is replaced, not doubled. `p_deque_playlist` is empty until Playlists first loads it, hence the load: without it the name is missed, the create fails on the duplicate name (-2) and stock adds the songs to playlist -2. The playlist takes the file's name without its extension (`toolsGetDirectoryM3u8` cuts it at the last dot; paths are `/mnt/mmc/_explaylist_data/<file>`), and absolute `/mnt/mmc/...` entries are accepted. Stock lists the whole folder; `importPlayList`'s `toolsGetDirectoryM3u8` call (`M3U_DIR_CALL`, `0x518768`, a `jalr` with `addiu a0, a0, 0x12e0` in its delay slot, which stays) becomes `jal addon_m3u_dir`, which keeps only the records whose path is `/mnt/mmc/_explaylist_data/` and an `i` name of the request while `libup.only` is set, around the app's import alone. Stock's own Import Playlists row is unaffected and still imports the whole folder. Limits (`ponytail:`): a scan canceled with the dialog's Back still reports `ok`, as stock keeps no cancel flag; the import reads every song's tags on the UI thread, as stock's Import row does, so a long playlist freezes the UI for a while.

<a id="artist-page"></a>**An artist's page.** Under a set with the menu sheet (OLED's), a level whose reply has `shuffle` and `radio` actions on an `artist:` context (q2-subsonic's artist page, reached by Go to Artist, Now Playing's artist tap or the app's Artists) is drawn as the design's artist page ([oled-design.md](oled-design.md#artist-page)) instead of as its rows: `artist_view` builds it, `patch/artist_page.c` draws it. `lv_t.lay` says how a level is drawn (`LAY_ARTIST`, and `LAY_ALBUMS` and `LAY_TOP` for the pages its rows open) and `lv_t.stop` which of the pair is lit, so both survive the rebuilds an action or a Back makes. The header (`hero_open`) names the level's title and counts the reply's album rows; its monogram stands 6 px over the status row, so `artist_cap` draws that part in the status bar's background paint and the header's first paint asks the bar to repaint once the page is still. The pair (`pair_open`) is two stops above the list, as Songs' Shuffle row is: `pair_key` runs in `ringnav` after `shuffle_key`, and `pair_holds` hides the list's bar while a stop is lit. Albums is no reply row: its click context is `AR_ALBUMS`, which pushes the level's own op and arguments again as `LAY_ALBUMS`, whose album rows are sorted newest first by the year their subtitle starts with and drawn as `cover_row`s with the app's catalogue cover (`/mnt/mmc/.<id>/covers/<album id>.jpg`, [server-library.md](server-library.md#covers)) when the file is there, a placeholder otherwise; the covers leave the image manager when the level drops its reply. A cover row keeps its reply row's index (`_ar_row`) for `addon_hold`, and `busy_row`, `relabel` and `append` leave a laid-out level alone or draw it again whole. Play/Pause held on the page opens `modal_actions` (menu_modal.c) with the reply's sync rows (`toggle`, `quality`, `sync`), each pressed as its row would be. With the caps word `artist` the app adds the rows of [librespot.md](librespot.md#artist-rows): `artist_view` takes the header's counts and genre from the `about` row (else it counts the album rows), and offers `singles`, `similar` and `songs` as drill-down rows, each opening a level whose `lay` `drill_lay` sets (`LAY_ALBUMS`, `LAY_SIMILAR`, `LAY_TOP`); a count is the number its subtitle starts with (`lead_count`). A song row's album and length come from its subtitle (`song_parts`: the first part of digits and colons is the length, all before it the album) and its cover from the `album:` word its context ends in (`row_album`), read only when that word is there, so an older app's rows show their title alone; `cover_after` draws the album after the title where 30 px are left, and `cover_mono` gives a Similar Artists row its monogram and chevron. The covers of a songs page leave the image manager as the Albums page's do.

<a id="album-page"></a>**An album's page.** Under the same sets, a level whose reply has a `play` action on `album:<id> 0`, a `shuffle` action on `album:<id>` and an `about` info row (q2-subsonic's album page with the caps word `album`, [librespot.md](librespot.md#album-rows)) is drawn as the design's album page ([oled-design.md](oled-design.md#album-page)): `album_view` builds it as `LAY_ALBUM`, before `artist_view` looks for an artist. The header is `hero_open`'s with `hero_cover`: the album's catalogue cover (`album_cover` on the Shuffle row's `album:` id) drawn by `hero_art` cropped square, scaled to 64 px and its corners scrubbed to the color behind, in the header's paint and, for its top 6 px, in `artist_cap`; the header's own destroy lets the decoded cover go. The pair is Play and Shuffle, `lv_t.stop` starting on Play. The song rows (an `action` `play` on a `song:` context) become `track_row`s numbered in the reply's order, their length read from the subtitle (`sub_parts`, `song_parts` without its `album:` check), the number and length painted by `artist_paint`. Play/Pause held anywhere on it opens `artist_hold`'s sync rows, which take an `album:` toggle as an `artist:` one. A reply without all three rows keeps the plain rows, so an older app's album is as before.

<a id="library-album-page"></a>**A Library album's page.** Stock's two album pages, `albuminfo_page` and `playerjumpinfo_page`, are dressed in place (`patch/library_album.c`), as their UI loads (`ringnav_ui_load` calls `album_local_load` before stock's init runs): their navbar and Songs' action row (the Shuffle row) are hidden, the list (`list_view` with its `scroll_view`, or `table_view` with its `music_table_client`) moved under the pair by `drill_list`, and the header and pair made in the window. Stock's rows stay: their clicks, the album track drawing of `song_rows.c`, the hold menu and the playing colors. The header's lines need the songs, which stock's init loads into `p_deque_showlist` after the UI, so `album_local_paint` fills them at the header's paint (`lb_fill`) whenever the page is on top and the songs' count is not the one last read: the first song's album and album artist (else artist), its year (`songtable` by `fileurl`, the first four digits, or `catalogue_np_info` for a server song), the count and the sum of `duration_seconds`. The cover is `catalogue_cover`'s for a server album, else Cover Flow's cached `art_path` of `album_key`. Play is `play_folder` of the songs from the first, as class `0xff10` (Cover Flow's album tracks); Shuffle is `shuffle_play`. `bar_title_of` gives the page no title. One page is dressed at a time: `artist_page.c` keeps one header, so the page dresses again at each `EVT_WINDOW_FOREGROUND` (back from an artist or album page over it), keeping its lit stop. Cover Flow's album tracks keep their own page.

### Card app sync

A card app says what it syncs in its state file (`/tmp/q2-<id>.state`, the file that carries `hold=` and `server=`): `sync=check` while it checks its server or its metadata, `sync=down DONE TOTAL` while it downloads songs (DONE of TOTAL in any unit; q2-subsonic writes bytes), and no key while idle. `poll_one` reads it with `hold=` every `ADDON_POLL_MS` from the read it already makes (`sync_read`; past 20 bits both numbers halve together until the total fits, so the permille is 32-bit arithmetic), a stopped app's key goes with its `hold`, and `addon_sync` answers for the status row: a download ahead of a check, with its permille. The row shows turning arrows (`arrows-clockwise-bold` in Text Secondary, eight frames of a half turn) for a check and a ring filling in the accent from 12 o'clock with `arrow-down-bold` in it for a download ([Status row slots](#status-row-slots)). ponytail: like `hold=`, only the file's first `QR_RAW - 2` bytes are read and an app writes its keys in name order, so a `sync=` behind a sign-in's long `qr=` reads as none; q2-subsonic never signs in and syncs at once.

## Radio

Now Playing's Radio (the antenna in the OLED row under the progress bar, `np_bar.c`) starts an endless radio of songs like the playing one; the car's `StartRadio` does the same ([remote-protocol: Radio](remote-protocol.md#radio)). `patch/song_radio.c` owns it.

**The tap.** `np_mode_click` runs `song_radio_tap` on a timer (a radio's queue opens Now Playing). With no radio playing it starts one seeded by the playing song (`playing`: `mcl_pdeqplaylist` at `MCL_POS`) from its place (`player_playtime_and_length`); on the pill it stops the radio, the songs queued playing on, and toasts "Radio Off". `song_radio_on` is the pill: the app's radio (`addon_radio`, its state file's `radio=`) or the local one.

**A server song's radio is its app's.** `addon_radio_start` (`addon.c`) finds the app: the one whose folder holds the song's path (a streamed file, a Library server row's `cat/` path), else the playing queue's app, when its `q2app` says `radio=1` (the `radio` word in `/tmp/q2-addon.caps` tells the app the firmware asks). It starts the app if needed (`addon_wake`) and writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.radio`, one line, `<seq> start <path>` or `<seq> stop`, only once the app's socket is there (the app takes a request already there at its start as answered, as a `.catplay`). The app answers in its state file, `radioack=<seq> <code>`: 0 started (or stopped), 1 not its song, 2 no radio. `song_radio_poll` reads it: on 1 it plays the local radio of the same song if it still plays, on 2 or after `SR_WAIT_MS` (25 s) it toasts "Radio isn't available for this song".
