The path is the seed: a streamed song (the player's id 0) is its stream-cache file, whose name carries the server's id between its last brackets ([stream_path.h](#car-remote-streams)), and the app reads the id there (q2-subsonic's `songOf`). The app plays the seed then the server's similar songs as a new queue (`.play`), and says `radio=<the seed's title>` while it plays; q2-subsonic asks `getSimilarSongs2` with the song's id, adds more when 10 or fewer are left after the one playing, and leaves out the last 200 songs played or queued (its `radio.go`).

**The local radio**, for any other song, one the app declines, or one whose app is too old to play radios (no `radio=1`: q2-subsonic before q2-v1.0): the library's songs (`staged(songs_unsorted)`, server rows and videos left out) by the seed's artist, then those of its genre (`REC_STYLE`), compared without ASCII case, each group shuffled, none of the last `SR_RECENT` (128) played or queued, `SR_BATCH` (25) at a time. Songs are told apart by their path's FNV-1a (`key`), not `REC_ID`: a queue's records and the library's number one song differently, and by id a radio of a song from Songs queued that song again. The queue is the seed then those (`play_folder`), with Now Playing's shuffle and repeat off (put back when the radio ends); when `SR_LOW` (10) or fewer are left after the one playing, `song_radio_poll` adds another batch at the queue's end (`playback_queue_insert`, an app's Add), and looks again `SR_RETRY_MS` later when it found none. Another queue (`playback_loads` moved) ends it. A new radio that finds nothing but songs played lately forgets them and picks again. One that finds nothing toasts "No similar songs on this Q2 Muse", or, for a server song whose app has no `radio=1` (`addon_radio_missing`), "Update <app> to use Radio": the library rarely holds a server song's artist, and on 2026-11-16 the first message, from q2-subsonic v0.9 on a streamed song, read as the server having no similar songs when it had many.

**The seed plays on.** Once the radio's queue plays the seed (a queue loaded since the tap, its song at the seed's path), it is sought to the place it had at the tap (`player_seek_time`), within `SR_SEEK_MS` (30 s). A song the car names plays from its start, and so does a seed its app had to fetch again (one streamed to the top of its stream folder, which a new list empties).

**While a radio plays** the antenna is the blue pill and shuffle and repeat are dimmed and ignore taps and the Centre cycle ([oled-design](oled-design.md#now-playing)); `/tmp/coda-rc.now` carries `radio=1` for the car.

Checks: `test/fw/test_song_radio.py` (the local radio's order, the seek, the pill and its stop, another queue ending it, the refill with nothing twice, the car's `radio` commands, a streamed song's request carrying its stream path, the server's "none" and a too-old app's toasts), `test/fw/test_nav_painters.py` (the tap runs `song_radio_tap`), `test/fw/test_addon.py` (the app's request and answer), `test/unit/test_coda_rc_daemon.py` and `test_coda_rc_lib.py` (`StartRadio` and `NowPlaying.radio`). ponytail: an artist's radio from the car is one of its songs' radios, so a server-only artist's needs Library on Local + Server; the app's own artist Radio row seeds `getSimilarSongs2` with the artist.

## Bundled apps

The firmware carries the Subsonic app, so it is in Streaming with nothing installed, and it is the firmware's alone: the App Store no longer lists it, and a new version of it comes in a firmware update. `tools/build.py` installs each app in `BUNDLED_APPS` from its release zip, pinned by version, size and SHA-256 and read from `--apps` (`~/.cache/q2-apps`; [building](building.md#bundled-apps)), into `/usr/lib/q2apps/<id>` on the read-only root filesystem: the zip's `.<id>/` files (`q2-<id>`, `q2app`, the icons), a `version` file holding the pinned version (`q2-v1.0`), and the app's own `run` changed by `bundled_launcher` in two lines, each checked to occur once: its data folder is the card's `/mnt/mmc/.<id>`, made if missing, not the launcher's own folder, and `/tmp/q2-<id>.bin` is a link to the image's binary, not a copy (7.9 MB of RAM for q2-subsonic). The app's credentials, catalogue, covers and log stay on the card, as they do for a card install. A `BUNDLED_APPS` entry's last field, `builtin` (Subsonic's is `True`), adds a `builtin` file holding `1` beside the app, which `addon_builtin` reads; a zip that ships one of its own is refused. The manifest records each app's version, zip, SHA-256 and `builtin` (`bundled_apps`).

**Which copy runs** (`addon_dir` in `patch/addon.c`): for a builtin app, always the firmware's, whatever the card holds. A card copy of it, from an App Store install or unzipped by hand before the firmware carried the app (`q2-subsonic`, `run`, `q2app` and the icons in the card's `.subsonic`), is never run or listed, and is left where it is rather than deleted: the folder is the app's data folder too (sign-in, settings, catalogue, downloads), so nothing is deleted from it, and a firmware without the app still finds a working copy there. Each Streaming scan deletes the App Store's tag and file list for a builtin app (`builtin_untag`: `/mnt/mmc/.q2/apps/<id>.tag` and `.files`), so nothing about the old install is left in the App Store's records. With the card's copy out of the way, Radio never says "Update Subsonic to use Radio" for an old card copy (`addon_radio_missing` reads the running copy's `q2app`, the firmware's, which says `radio=1`). For any other carried app, the card's `.<id>` runs when it holds the app (`q2-<id>`) and either the firmware carries none or the card's is newer; else the firmware's. Newer is the card copy's App Store tag (`/mnt/mmc/.q2/apps/<id>.tag`, [Q2 Shelf](#q2-shelf)) against the carried `version` file, compared by `addon_version_cmp`: the dotted numbers after a `v` and a digit (else from the first digit), in turn, a missing one as 0. A card copy without a tag was unzipped by hand and counts as newer, since whoever put it there chose it. So an App Store update past the carried version takes over, and an older install left on the card is passed over without being deleted. `addon_scan` reads both folders and keeps each app's chosen one (one Streaming row), and every reader of an app's manifest (`addon_q2app`: Go to, scrobbling, favorites, the server library's `catalogue.c`, Storage's `storage.c`) reads the chosen copy's `q2app`. Those readers find apps by their folder on the card, so a carried app the card has no `.<id>` for yet is listed in Streaming but not in the Server Library or Storage until its first start makes the folder. ponytail: for an app that is not builtin, a hand install shadows the carried app forever, whatever its version; reading the binary's own version would lift that.

**A new version** of a builtin app ships as a new `BUNDLED_APPS` pin in a firmware update ([building](building.md#bundled-apps), [releasing](releasing.md#the-app-list)); nothing on the card or in `sources.list` changes.

## Server library

With **Streaming Songs** on (`[Q2POD] LIBRARYSOURCE=1`, Settings > Playback > Library, `pod_keys`; Local + Server below), a card app that declares `catalogue=1` in its `q2app` (the [Subsonic app](https://github.com/andsuor/q2-subsonic) does) supplies a music server's songs and playlists, and they join the Library's lists beside the card's. The firmware never speaks to the server; the file formats are the contract in [server-library.md](server-library.md), and all of it is `patch/catalogue.c`. `ADDON_CAPS` carries `catalogue` and `ratings`, so an app writes nothing until it sees them. With Local Only (the default) nothing is read, attached or unioned. `catalogue_poll` (from `addon_poll`, once a second while the setting is on) looks for such apps every 10 s, reads each one's `/tmp/q2-<id>.state` for `server=down`, and starts a job when an app's `catalogue.tsv` has a new `seq` (header `#Q2CAT/1`), or when `library_gen` has moved since the last match (Update Local Music, and the scans after USB storage and Wi-Fi transfer, move it around each stock scan), never while a scan runs or with the card away.

**Streaming Songs and the apps** (`patch/library_settings.c`). The firmware is the only writer of `LIBRARYSOURCE`; apps read the state from `/tmp/q2-addon.library`, `server` or `local` and a newline, written atomically (`blob_io`) at every Streaming scan just before the caps file (so an app that finds the caps word `libsource` finds the file too; every app start scans first) and at every change. A missing file reads as off, so it is never written as a side effect of reading the settings. An app sends its "needs the server's songs" press (q2-subsonic's Show in Library while it is off) as a `needslib` row, whose cells are an `action` row's: pressed with Streaming Songs on, its action goes at once; off, the firmware asks "Show streaming songs?" (Cancel selected, Turn On, Return is Cancel, and a footer naming Settings > Playback > Library > Streaming Songs), and Turn On turns it on as the Settings row does (the key written, `catalogue_changed`, the file written) before the action goes. The ask runs its own loop, so the action goes only if the row is still the same row of the same level (`needslib`). The Settings row turns it on at once; off, it asks "Hide streaming songs?" (Cancel, Turn Off, a footer saying Show in Library pauses) while a catalogue app has its `catalogue.tsv` on the card (`catalogue_kept`), and flips at once otherwise. An app that sees `local` pauses and keeps its records.

**Autostart** (`cat_autostart`). With Streaming Songs on, each catalogue app that is signed in is started in the background once, by the same path as a catplay's start (`addon_wake`: the caps and state files written first, then its `run`), at the first app scan with the card in after boot, and again at the first one after the setting is turned on (`catalogue_changed` clears `cat_started`); it idle-exits as it does from its page, and Smart Wi-Fi keeps the radio up while it runs (`addon_running`). Signed in is the app's card folder holding its `credentials` file, which the firmware looks for and never opens (`catalogue_signed`): the app's status file is in `/tmp`, empty at boot, and signing out deletes the file. A signed-out app, or Streaming Songs off, starts nothing.

**The job** (`cat_worker`, its own pthread and SQLite connection on `/mnt/data/database.db`) writes a whole new `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod/catalogue.db.new`: the old file's tables less the imported app's rows, then the app's file streamed a line at a time (`import_file`; a line over 8 KB is skipped), 64 songs to an insert, in one transaction with the new file's journal off. Server rows go to `serverall` with `songtable`'s columns (ids from `0x40000000`, a 16 M span per app; `fileurl` `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/cat/<album id>/<sid>.<suffix>`, a hidden path no file has, so ratings, favorites, playlists and play counts key on it as on a card path; `filename` the title alone, since stock's Search lists a song by its file name, and a card file's has the title in it) and the rest to `servermeta` (sid, seconds, size, MusicBrainz id, suffix, offline copy, the normalised tags' hashes). The header's `rows=` must equal the `s`, `p` and `i` lines read, so a file cut short is answered `<seq> error Read N of M rows`, not imported as a smaller library. SQL is built against the buffer's end less 64 bytes of slack (`PUT`, `sq`), and a statement that did not fit is never run, so a cut `delete` can't lose its `where`. Then the duplicate match (below), `servertable` (what the lists read) rebuilt as `serverall` less the duplicates, every app's playlists, and the index. The UI thread joins it in `cat_swap`: it detaches `cat` from stock's shared connection, renames the new file over the old, takes the index, answers `/tmp/q2-<id>.catalogue.done` (`<seq> ok <rows>` or `<seq> error <why>`), and bumps `library_gen` so open lists query again. A scan that moved `library_gen` while the job ran leaves the match due again (`cat.gen` is the generation the job started at).

**Duplicates** (`cat_match`, `cat_same`): the card's songs are read from `songtable` once per job and sorted by their normalised title (`cat_norm`: lower case, letters and digits only, a "feat." part and trailing bracketed or dashed edition notes such as "(Remastered 2009)" or "- 2012 Stereo Mix" cut, unless the note says live). A server song is compared only with card songs of its title, and with untagged card files of its size (stat'd once per job). Strongest first: equal MusicBrainz recording ids (`cat_mbid` reads the first 128 KB of the card file for a Vorbis `MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID` or an ID3 `UFID` owned by `http://musicbrainz.org`; when both have one and they differ, nothing weaker is tried); equal size, suffix and a length within 1 s (`ringnav_statx`, taglib's length); equal normalised artist (or album artist), album, title and track and a length within 2 s. A match sets `servermeta.dup` to the card path, which leaves the row out of `servertable` and links its sid to the card file for ratings. A size alone that differs stops nothing: a retagged copy differs. ponytail: a tagged card file whose title differs from the server's is never a candidate, even at equal size; indexing every card file by size would stat the whole card at each job.

**Where it is read.** `stock_db_open` (stock's shared connection, its `0x5c8d30` reopen, and the payload's other opens through it) attaches the file as `cat` while the setting is on and the file exists (the setting as the UI thread loaded it: stock's scan thread opens through it too, and never reads the config file there); `cat_live` attaches it again to a new stock handle. `library_query`'s music loads read `(select * from songtable where <music> union all select * from servertable)` (`catalogue_rows`), and Era's SQL each `from songtable` as the union (`catalogue_union`, with `cat` attached to Era's own connection). Stock's Search (`SearchMusicByName` and its kin, a `like '%<text>%'` query through `toolsQueryDbTable` outside a music load) reads the union too (`catalogue_search`), so server songs are found; its rows are grayed (below, from `p_deque_searchshowlist`, Search's own results, which each tab of its `tab_button_group` fills: `ringnav_search_rows`), and a press on a song goes through `search_track_row_on_click`'s play check. Home's song count (`library_count`, Era's path) counts the union; the Updating page counts `main.songtable`, the card's files the scan walks. Everything off the UI thread (stock's scan thread through `stock_db_open` and `library_query`, the count and Era workers) reads `catalogue_source` as the UI thread loaded it, never the config file. The index (`cat_ix`, built by the job): every server row by its `fileurl`'s 64-bit FNV-1a, and every linked card file by its path, each with the sid, seconds and offline copy, sorted for a binary search, plus a by-sid order for `catalogue.avail` and `ratings.in`.

**Availability.** A server row can play when it has an offline copy (its `local` from the catalogue, then each `catalogue.avail` line in order: `<sid>\t<path>` sets one, `-<sid>` clears it; the file is read on from where it stopped, and whole again when it shrinks or after an import), or when online: `networkGetConnectStatus()` above 0, or [Smart Wi-Fi](#smart-wi-fi)'s radio off or coming back (`smart_wifi_back`), and no app's `server=down`. A press while Smart Wi-Fi has the radio off wakes it (`smart_wifi_wait`) and waits for the link (`cp_link`, polled by `catplay_poll`) before it starts the app or writes the catplay; no link `SMART_CONNECT_MS` (15 s) on, the list plays offline. With Local Only every server row is unavailable (a catalogue playlist kept). **Grayed rows:** `ringnav_table_load`, as stock binds a pooled Library row to its index in `p_deque_showlist`, calls `catalogue_bind`, which keeps the row in a 48-entry set when its record is a song that can't play, or an album that can't (`catalogue_album_unavailable`, when the showlist is albums: `g_class_type` `CLASS_ALBUMS`, or on `artistinfo_page` its classinfo's `0xff01`-`0xff03`): offline, its name (ASCII case folded, as the list's `COLLATE NOCASE` groups it) is no card song's album and none of the server rows of that name has an offline copy (`group_unavailable`). The job keeps, for each group (album; artist, a song's artist and album artist both; genre), every card song's names (`cards`) and every server row's (`servers`), as sorted sets of their `group_hash`, and each server row's four names (`cat_ent.grp`); the names of the rows with an offline copy (`local`) are gathered again on the UI thread when `local_gen` has moved (an import, a `catalogue.avail` line). A name the catalogue doesn't know is the card's. ponytail: by name, so a server-only album sharing a card album's name stays white, and so does a server-only artist named as a card song's album artist. Lists that are not pooled tables but a scroll_view with one row per record in order are grayed as their surface's background paints (`grey_rows`, after `paint_selection`): an album's songs (`albuminfo_page`, `playerjumpinfo_page`: the showlist), Cover Flow's tracks (`coverflow_tracks`: Go to Album lands there with Artist View on), Most Played's and a Ratings list's songs (`page_tracks`: `st.mp_list`, `st.rt_list`) and Search's results (`p_deque_searchshowlist`, which each tab fills with its own rows: `ringnav_search_rows`, with the lit tab), each only when the list holds as many records as the surface has rows, and each row in sight through `catalogue_mark` (a row scrolled out of sight is forgotten, `catalogue_forget`, so a long list never fills the `CAT_GREY_ROWS` slots): a song's record by `song_mark` (below), a row of Search's Artists, Albums or Genres tab (a directory record its tab's callback, `0x506904`, `0x506e94` or `0x506d60`, fills with the name in `REC_ARTIST`, `REC_ALBUM` or `REC_STYLE`) by `group_unavailable` of its group; a grayed row is forgotten when it is destroyed (an `EVT_DESTROY` handler, once per widget, `_catgrey`), so a widget made later at its address is not grayed with it. `ringnav_style_color` runs stock's mapping first (`style_color`), then hands every text color painted at depth 0 to `catalogue_greyed`: inside a grayed row it is `#666666`, or on the selection (`ringnav_row_selected`: the row holds `g_menu.at[st.sel_row]`, or is inside it) the theme's own ink at 70% alpha (`CAT_DIM`), so a grayed row on OLED's Accent Blue bar reads white, not gray on blue; the color is kept per row (`grey_ink`). After the rows, `paint_offline` (from `ringnav_paint`, beside `paint_chevrons`) draws each grayed row's offline mark in that color: Phosphor's `cloud-slash` bold (MIT), rasterised once at 20 px by `tools/art.py`'s `path` and `coverage` into a 20 x 16 table of 16-step coverage in `catalogue.c` (`MARK`), painted a run of equal coverage per `canvas_fill_rect` at the row's alpha times the coverage. It sits in the chevron's column (the row's right less `CHEVRON_W` plus 25), or 28 px left of it on a row that shows a chevron (`offline_x`: a drill row of the payload's under a theme without `chevron_sel`, or the selected row when it holds stock's `list_into`). Before the rows paint, `grey_rows` also has `catalogue_fit` end each grayed row's labels (`label`, `hscroll_label`, four levels down, as deep as an album row's artist in `view_artist`) so their text stops `SONG_COL_GAP` (12 px) short of the mark's ink (`CAT_MARK_W` wide), as a length's does, their own width kept in `_catw` and given back when the row is no longer grayed or the limit moves (the selection leaving a drill row). **Play:** each Library song row and Play All asks stock's `access(path, R_OK)` first and says File Not Found when it fails; those eight calls (`CATALOGUE_ACCESS` in `tools/build.py`) go to `catalogue_access`, which passes a server row that can play now and fails one that can't, as a missing file (stock then says File Not Found and opens no Now Playing; a refused load after a pass would leave Now Playing open on the last song). `ringnav_load` then asks `catalogue_load`: a queue with no server row loads as before; a start row that can't play (reached another way) says "Not available offline" (or "Turn on Streaming Songs to play it") and loads nothing; online, the list is handed to the row's app as `/tmp/q2-<id>.catplay` (`<seq> <start>`, then each row's path) and nothing loads, the app's `.play` playing it through the card-app channel; when that `.play` has not changed in 4 s (`CATPLAY_WAIT_MS`), or offline at once, the firmware loads the list itself. An app that isn't running (none of its launcher's pid file: not opened since boot, or gone after its own 30-minute idle exit) is started first (`addon_wake`: `addon_scan` if Streaming hasn't listed it since boot, which also writes the capability line the app reads at its start, then `launch`, as its Streaming row starts it, after removing a socket a killed app left), and the catplay is written only once its socket is there (`addon_ready`, polled each second by `catplay_poll`): the app reads the catplay file at its start as one already answered and makes its socket after that, so one written earlier would never be answered. The 4 s wait runs from the write; an app that hasn't listened within `CATPLAY_START_MS` (15 s) has its list played the firmware's way. Nothing is started with Local only, offline (the list plays from the card), or for an app whose binary is not on the card; a running app that `addon.c` was not tracking (demo restarted under it) is marked launched, so its `.play` is polled. An app started this way holds Smart Wi-Fi's radio as one opened from Streaming does, until its idle exit; the next press starts it again. The firmware's offline load: card rows, and server rows by their offline copies (the record's path replaced by the copy's), the start moved to the pressed row or the next kept. While a catplay waits, Now Playing shows the pressed song ([server-library.md](server-library.md#now-playing-while-it-loads)): `catalogue_load` keeps a copy of its record (`np_press`), its place in the list and its album's cover (`catalogue_cover`, else `play_defaultcover`), and once stock's press is over (a 0 ms timer, `np_stop`) stops the song playing (`mclStop`): stock's `player_start`, after a `ringnav_load` that loaded nothing, plays the queue it has again, so its time and sound would run on under the new title. `np_sync` (`np_bar.c`) takes the album and "2 of 12" from that record (`catalogue_np_now`) and has `catalogue_np_text` write its title and artist into `scrlabel_title` and `scrlabel_artist`, again whenever their text is not what it wrote last (stock's page update writes `g_song_name` and `g_song_artist` there on its own refreshes); `np_art` gives the cover whenever the art shows another image: stock's page opens on the last song's, and its own reload (the restarted song's cover thread) can replace ours. It ends at the player's next fresh parse (`id3_parses`, counted in `ringnav_id3_path`), when the fallback finds nothing to play, or after `CATPLAY_SHOW_MS` (60 s); then the player's title and artist go back on the page. Stock's update (`0x53cf08`) writes them only while `g_forcerefresh_flag` or `g_autochange_flag` is set, and every library list page's timer clears those flags too, so the flag `np_done` sets from inside Now Playing's update (`np_sync`, after its title) was taken by the Songs page under it and the pressed song's title stayed on the next song (the device, Shuffle Songs then Next). `np_done` still sets the flag and marks `np_back`, and `catalogue_np_text` writes the playing song's title and artist (`now_tag`, the record's name for a missing title, as `g_song_name` has it) once `g_play_id3_info` names its path, which `ringnav_id3_path` writes after the tags. `play_folder` (`coverflow.c`) closes a Now Playing on top before it opens the new one: stock's `navigator_to_with_context` opens a second `playing_page` over the first (an app's first song starting under the pressed song's page), and two pages' updates race for the same flags, the one under winning as often as not. Shuffle Songs plays the whole library through the same load, so offline it leaves the unplayable out. Mid-queue, `upcoming()` (`playback.c`) passes over a row `catalogue_unavailable` refuses. Go to Album and Go to Artist on a server row open the Library's pages (stock's `playerjumpinfo_page` and artist page, by the row's tags), not its app's: `goto_app` (`addon.c`) leaves a catalogue path out, so `addon_goto` declines it, and `addon_goes` offers Go to on it although its path is in the app's folder. Now Playing's info page (`ringnav_np_info`) asks `catalogue_np_info` for the playing path, a server row's or its offline copy's (found by a pass over the index's copies, `cat_copy_of`): the catalogue's genre and year (`style` and `year` of `cat.serverall` by `fileurl`, kept for the last path, as the page fills every 250 ms) replace stock's Unknown, which comes of the Stream Cache file having no `songtable` row, and Location reads `Server`. **Covers:** `catalogue_cover` maps a server row's path (`/mnt/mmc/.<id>/cat/<album id>/<sid>.<suffix>`), or its offline copy's (`cat_copy_of`), to the app's `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/covers/<album id>.jpg` when that file is there. `grid_cover` (stock's Library album rows and grids, Folder's rows: `GRID_COVER`) gives a server row that file through `toolsThumbSpecCover` under the lock its caller holds, and nothing else (no file to read tags from); `coverflow_player_cover` tries it after the folder images and before ffmpeg's embedded probe, through `ff_thumb`, as its lock order wants. The app writes a baseline JPEG of at most 160 px, which stock's decoder takes whole. Durations of server rows are the catalogue's seconds (`durations.c`). A listen of a server song's offline copy (what the app's `.play` and the offline queue both play) counts under its server row's key (`play_count` asks `catalogue_song_key`: the listen_key of the row's `fileurl`, found by the copy's path in the index, the last answer kept until `local_gen` moves; hearts given on Now Playing while the copy plays take the same key through `rate_song_key`, `catalogue_rated` writes the row's sid, and `rate_all` counts the copy's My Fav, which stock's heart keeps by the copy's path, as the row's), so Most Played and Cover Flow's Most Played order, which rank the Library's rows, find it; Most Played's kept tracks take only a counted song's own record (`mp_counted`), never the copy's, so its next open reads the library again. **Cover Flow** (`coverflow.c`): with Local + Server its album queries (`getAllAlbum`, `ALBUM_SQL`, `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`, the Sort ranks, the rated albums) run as music loads (`cf_staged`, `staged_music`), so `library_query` reads the union and the carousel has the server's albums; Local Only runs them as before. An album whose first track is a server row is queued for art only once its app's cover is there (`load_albums`: `catalogue_cover`, one `access` per uncached server album per open), and `build_art` thumbnails that cover into the cache (`thumb`, `ART_SIZE`); a cover that won't decode gets the "no art" marker, and one removed meanwhile none, so the next open asks again. Until then the placeholder shows, with no marker to clear. The centered album's captions are grayed as a row is (`caption_offline`: `catalogue_grey` on the name and artist labels, so `ringnav_style_color` grays their text) while `catalogue_album_unavailable` says none of its songs can play, the name narrowed `CF_MARK_W` (28) a side so it stays centered, and `caption_mark` paints the offline mark in the name's right margin as the covers' view paints; `titles` checks it as the center changes, and the slide's paint again each frame (`album_offline`), so a lost connection grays the centered album at the next frame. A track row of a server album, and Cover Flow's All albums card (`play_all`) and Era's Play All and Shuffle (`era_pick`) whose first song is a server row, check no file before they play (`catalogue_missing`: `access` for a card file, none for a server row), so `ringnav_load` hands the list to the app or says why it can't, where `access` said Storage unavailable.

**Where a song lives** (OLED, [oled-design.md](oled-design.md#song-rows)): the same slots that gray a row carry a mark kind (`grey_mark`: `MK_OFFLINE`, `MK_CLOUD`, `MK_DOWN`), set by `song_mark` wherever a song row is bound or made (`catalogue_bind`, `catalogue_mark`). A row that can't play now is `MK_OFFLINE`, grayed with the offline mark as above; a server row that can play is `MK_CLOUD` (it streams), a card file under a catalogue app's downloads folder (its `q2app`'s `downloads=`, one folder at the card's root, read by `cat_scan`: q2-subsonic's `Subsonic`) is `MK_DOWN`, and the user's own file has none. Only `MK_OFFLINE` changes the row's text color (`catalogue_greyed` and `catalogue_row_ink` skip the others; `cat.noff` counts the offline ones, so a list with none spends no time in `grey_of` per text color). `paint_offline` hands each marked row to `catalogue_row_mark`, which draws the offline mark as before or the theme's own 18 px glyph (`tools/art.py` `MARKS`: Phosphor's `cloud` and `arrow-circle-down`, regular, `oled_mark_<cloud|down>_<d|l|w>`) in Text Tertiary, white on the selection, centered where the offline mark would be; the title, artist and length end clear of either as they do of the offline mark (`catalogue_row_greyed` answers for every marked row). Marks follow the catalogue: with Local only, or before an app's `q2app` is read, there are none.

**Playlists** (`cat_playlists`, in each job, for every app): each catalogue playlist is a stock playlist (a header row with an id 0-99 whose `cd_num` is itself; items above 100 with that `cd_num`), its items a card file's `songtable` row (a synced song's path from its `i` line, or the linked file) or the server row's. `serverlists` remembers which header is whose. A new catalogue playlist whose name a stock playlist already has is compared with it (`pl_twin`: that playlist's items, in order, equal to the catalogue playlist's card files, in order): equal, it is the app's synced `.m3u` twin, and the catalogue playlist takes its place (`twin` 1; its items replaced by the catalogue's); not equal, it is the user's own, and the catalogue's is left out. A playlist gone from the catalogue is deleted, a twin only unlinked. The pass runs in its own transaction on stock's database; a failure there rolls it back and leaves the import as it is, to be tried again at the next job. Turning Local + Server off keeps them, their server rows refused.

**Ratings** ([server-library.md](server-library.md#ratings-and-favorites)): `rate_close`, the heart page's My Fav button, an album's favorites (`ratings.c`) and the queue menu's Add to and Remove from Favorites (`qm_rated`, which clears the song's 1-4 as the heart does) call `catalogue_rated`, which appends `<listen_key>\t<sid or empty>\t<hearts>\t<unix time>` to `ratings.out` of each app with `ratings=1` (the sid a server row's, or a linked card file's; for a Stream Cache copy, its server row's key and sid, `cat_row_of`). `ratings.in` is renamed to `ratings.in.taking` before it is read (lines the app writes meanwhile go to a new `ratings.in`), each line applied unless that song's newest line in `ratings.out` is newer (`rate_keep` by the key; My Fav set or cleared by the path: a server row's or a linked file's from its sid, any other card file's found by its `listen_key` in one pass over `songtable`), then the file is deleted. `catalogue_poll` reads it only while no job runs and the app's `catalogue.tsv` seq is the one imported, so at a boot's first poll, before the import has built the index, a server row's line waits rather than lose its My Fav (its path comes from the index). A server row in My Fav (from `ratings.in`, or the queue menu on its Library row) is a favorite of its Stream Cache copy too, which stock's `checkFavExist` can't see as it checks the copy's own path: `rate_fav` (Now Playing's heart and picker, the queue menu's Favorites and Rate rows) asks `catalogue_row_fav` as well (`select 1 from myfav` by the row's `fileurl`, kept until the row, `local_gen` or `fav_gen` moves; `fav_told`, `ratings_in` and `rate_bind` move `fav_gen`). Now Playing's 500 ms badge tick (`rate_row_heart`) fills the copy's empty heart for it and empties a heart it filled once the row leaves My Fav, or one stock drew from the copy's own path once `checkFavExist` no longer finds it (asked only when `catalogue_fav_gen` has moved since the last tick, not twice a second); `ratings_in` takes a copy's own path out of My Fav with its row's whatever the hearts (`fav_set`'s third argument, the row's `local` from the index), so a copy hearted here and then rated 4 or unstarred on the server shows the empty heart and the server's 4, and five from the server leaves the row in its place, the song in Favorites once; a tap on that heart, a picked rating under five and the queue menu's Remove take the row out (`catalogue_row_unfav`) instead of running stock's toggle, which would put the copy in. ponytail: a row taken out of My Fav by stock's own lists is seen when Now Playing next opens, not while it shows.

**Measured** on the emulator (`q2emu` under qemu-user on a laptop, not a Q2): see [server-library.md](server-library.md#scale).

## Storage

**System settings → Storage** (`storage_open` in `patch/storage.c`, the `storage_page` runtime window; between App Store and System Update, `sysset_order`) shows how the card is used: the line "33.9 GB of 60 GB used", a 10 px bar from the text column to the right column (round ends, the track `#2C2C2E`, then Your Music in white, Downloads in the accent's top tone and Stream Cache in `#6E6E73` from the left, square where they meet with 1 px of track between them), and four rows, each with its 10 px legend dot and size: **Your Music**, **Downloads** (opens its page), **Stream Cache** (opens the app's own Settings, where its size and Clear Cache are) and **Free**, under two footers in Text Tertiary at 13 px ("Your Music is never changed by Sync." and "Downloads stay under the limit you set."). Sizes are MB of 10^6 bytes, as the apps and a card's label count (`mb_mib`: MiB times 1.049, so no 64-bit division), shown as "512 MB" or "24.1 GB". **Storage → Downloads** (`downloads_page`) is a **Limit** row (No Limit, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64 GB, picked in the menu sheet's picker, `modal_pick`) and the app's downloaded items, each with its mark (Phosphor's `arrow-circle-down` in the accent for one the user picked, `arrows-clockwise` in Text Secondary for one the app keeps on its own; `oled_store_<pick|auto>_*`), its size and a chevron when the app has a page for it, which a press opens (`addon_open_at`); Play/Pause held on an item (`storage_hold`, from `ringnav_keylong`) asks the app to remove it and toasts "Removed from Sync". Its footer says so: "Hold Play/Pause on an item to remove it.", or "Nothing downloaded yet." with no item. The rows are `page_row_detail` rows; the header and footers are views above and below the list (as Battery History's graph), and `storage_paint` (from `ringnav_paint`) draws them and each row's dot, mark, value and chevron, under OLED only (other themes show the rows' names).

**The channel.** A card app that keeps downloads says `storage=1` in its `q2app` (the first found is the page's, `st_app`), and the firmware adds `storage` to its capability line. The app writes `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/storage.tsv` whole (temp and rename), tab-separated with the card-app channel's escapes (read with catalogue.c's `tsv_split`, at most 32 KB and `ST_ITEMS` 64 items):

```text
#Q2STORE/1	limit=<MB, 0 for none>	downloads=<bytes>	cache=<bytes>
i	<pick|auto>	<key>	<bytes>	<op>	<arg>	<name>
```

`downloads` is what the app downloaded for the user, `cache` its own folder (Stream Cache, covers, its files). The firmware asks for a change by appending a line to `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/storage.out` (`st_ask`; an LF first ends any line a cut write left): `limit\t<MB>` or `remove\t<key>`, and starts the app (`addon_wake`) to take it; the app takes the file by renaming it, applies it and writes `storage.tsv` again. A limit chosen here shows at once (`so.pending`) until the file says so. While either page is open the file is read again every second (`st_poll`) and the pages rebuilt, their selection kept, when it changed. **Your Music** is measured, never walked: the card's used space (`statfs`: blocks less available, so a card's reserved blocks count as used) less the app's downloads and cache, so it holds every file the user put there, other card apps' folders and the firmware's own (`.q2pod/catalogue.db`, Cover Flow's art) with them. Without such an app, or before it has written the file, Downloads and Stream Cache read 0 MB and open nothing.

## Q2 Shelf

**System settings → App Store** (titled **App Store**; just above Storage; `shelf_open` in `patch/netupdate.c`, the `apps_page` runtime window) installs, updates and removes the apps in [`sources.list`](../sources.list), each from the one release zip the list pins. The firmware names no app but its own three. The list is fetched from `raw.githubusercontent.com/312-dev/q2-coda/main/sources.list` (`Q2POD_REPO`'s, as Network Update's releases, so `--update-repo` moves both), taken only when the release key signed it ([Release signatures](#release-signatures)), and kept as `/mnt/mmc/.q2/sources.list` so the page works offline. The first row, **Check for Updates** (`ROW_CHECK`), runs a check when pressed, so with no list yet it is the one row and fetches the list.

Each line is `owner/repo TAG ASSET SIZE SHA256 [Name]` (`#` starts a comment, `-` before it marks a dropped app), and `shelf_sources` reads up to 16 (`SH_MAX`). The owner is `A-Za-z0-9-`, the repo also allows `._`, and the name defaults to the repo's. `TAG ASSET SIZE SHA256` is the app's pin (`parse_pin`, into `shelf_app`'s `latest`, `asset`, `size` and `sha256`): the release's tag (1 to 31 of `A-Za-z0-9._-`), its zip's name (up to 63 of the same, ending `.zip`; both go into the download's URL), the zip's bytes (1 to 1 GB, `SH_CAP`) and their SHA-256 in lowercase hex. A line is skipped when any of these fail, it has no pin (only a dropped app needs none; a dropped app's pin is let go), its id repeats an earlier one's, or the firmware carries the app as its own (`addon_builtin`, [Bundled apps](#bundled-apps)): such an app is never shown, installed, updated or removed here, whichever list names it, the signed one or the card's copy of an older one, and so never kept as dropped either. `serial N` numbers the list (`shelf_serial`) and the last line, `signature <128 hex>`, is the release key's; neither is an app. `tools/shelf.py` writes the pins, from each app's latest release's first `.zip`, and signs the list ([releasing](releasing.md#the-app-list)).

The list is the store's trust: card apps come from many people's repositories, which no single key signs, so q2-coda's maintainer vouches for each exact zip instead, and the Q2 checks two things. `fresh_list` takes a fetched list only if `sig_list` finds the release key's signature over everything before its last line, and its serial is at least that of the card's list (an older signed list, served again from a repository taken over, would roll the pins back); otherwise "App list not signed: not used", and the page keeps the list it has. `install` downloads only `https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/releases/download/TAG/ASSET` from that list, reads the part back from the card through SHA-256 and goes on only if it is the pin's ("Download doesn't match the list" otherwise, before anything is unzipped). So neither a repository's owner nor anyone holding it can put a new zip on a Q2 without a new signed list, and q2-pod's upstream list, unsigned, is never taken. The id is the repo's name less `q2-`, and must be 1 to 15 of `a-z0-9-`, addon.c's rule, since it goes into shell commands. A card app's folder is `.<id>`, its binary `.<id>/q2-<id>`, and nothing in it is kept from unzip.

Q2 Muse's own apps are matched by the repo's name, so a fork is the same app; another repo whose id would be one of theirs is skipped:

- `q2-rockbox` → `rockbox`: binary `.rockbox/rockbox`, keeps `.rockbox/config.cfg`.
- `q2-rockbox-themes` → `themes`: folder `.rockbox`, no binary, keeps the same file.
- `q2-librespot` → `spotify`: binary `.spotify/librespot`, keeps `.spotify/cache/*` and `.spotify/.cache-size`.

The app rows follow the list's order. Each one shows its app's state as the row's detail:

- **Installed** with a tag in `/mnt/mmc/.q2/apps/<id>.tag`.
- **Update** when that tag differs from the pin's (string equality, not order), or when the app's binary is there without a tag (a manual install).
- Otherwise **Install**.

Rockbox Themes is listed only while `.rockbox/rockbox` is a regular file. The rows are built when the page opens, and again when a job's end changes which (`sh_rows`). Themes says "Install Rockbox first" without Rockbox.

ponytail: a card app keeps nothing from an update. Its settings survive only because its release zip doesn't ship them; an app whose zip ships its settings file overwrites the user's copy on every update. The fix belongs in that app's release, or in a `keep` list here if one ever needs it.

See [the user guide](manual/guide.html#apps) for install, removal, confirmation and cancellation controls.

One pthread runs one job at a time, all transfers through netupdate.c's `fetch` (the same CA bundle and TLS checks, `User-Agent: Q2Pod`, progress and cancel through its transfer callback). Opening the page with Wi-Fi checks: it fetches the signed list, one request, as each app's latest is its pin's tag (no GitHub API request is made). This is skipped if the last check fetched it in the last 10 minutes (`SH_STALE_MS`, kept until power-off). The worker parses the fetched list into `sh.next`, adds back any app it dropped that still has a tag (so it can still be removed), and writes the result to the card: `serial N`, then each app's line with its pin, a dropped one's with a `-` before it and no pin, without the signature (the card's copy is the page's offline and the floor for the next list's serial; nothing installs from it). A dropped app (`shelf_app.dropped`, from that check or a `-` line) has no pin, its last tag is let go, `install` refuses it, and its row shows only while it is installed: with the pins, dropping an app is no longer the only thing between a taken-over repo and a Q2 ([GHSA-8wpr-pmqx-538x](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/security/advisories/GHSA-8wpr-pmqx-538x)), but it is how the maintainer takes an app away. The UI thread adopts it when the check ends, so the rows never change under a job. A list that fails to fetch or parses to nothing leaves the old one in place. So the rows can be the card's list of days ago: after opening with no Wi-Fi, after a row's press stops the opening check, or while the list can't be fetched. An install therefore fetches the signed list itself first (`listed`, through `fresh_list`) and takes the app's pin from it, going on only if it names the app's repo, not dropped: "Can't reach GitHub" or "GitHub is busy, try later" with no list, "App list not signed: not used" with one that fails its signature or serial, "No update for this build" with the repo gone from it. The rows themselves change at the next check.

**Check for Updates** checks inside those 10 minutes, but not within a minute of the last whole check (`SH_RECHECK_MS`): then it says that check's count again without fetching. Its row reads "Checking…" during any check; pressing it then starts nothing, but the check's end answers it. When a check ends with the page on top (not covered, nor stopped by another row's press), `sh_told` toasts the number of apps whose tag file differs from the latest release: "1 app can be updated", "3 apps can be updated". A manual install's **Update** isn't counted, as its version is unknown. With none, after Check for Updates (`sh.manual`, cleared by the next `sh_start`) it says why the list wasn't taken (`SH_NET`, `SH_BUSY` for a 403 or 429, `SH_UNSIGNED`: "Can't reach GitHub", "GitHub is busy, try later", "App list not signed: not used"), or else "All apps are up to date". No list at all, on the card or fetched, is `SH_NET`. The opening check says nothing unless an app can be updated.

An install:

1. Fetches the signed list (`listed`) and goes on only if it names the app's repo, not dropped, taking its pin; then deletes any leftover `/mnt/mmc/.q2/staging` (an interrupted install is retried, never resumed), and needs the pin's size plus 64 MB free (`statfs`).
2. Downloads `releases/download/TAG/ASSET` to `.q2/staging/<id>.part`, then reads it back through SHA-256 (`sig_hash_file`) and stops unless it is the pin's.
3. Lists it with `busybox unzip -l -qq`, restricted as the unpack is: the app's folder only (`.rockbox/*` or `.spotify/*`), never `*/._*` or the kept paths (`.rockbox/config.cfg`; `.spotify/cache/*` and `.spotify/.cache-size`). `shelf_unpacked` rejects an absolute path or a `..` component and a total over 1 GB, and needs at least one entry; the card then needs that total plus 64 MB free.
4. Unpacks with `busybox unzip -o -qq -d .q2/staging/<id>` and the same patterns, so `INSTALL.txt`, `__MACOSX/` and macOS `._` files stay off the card. busybox's unzip matches with `fnmatch` without `FNM_PATHNAME` (so `*` spans `/`), and strips a leading `/` and `../` from names itself before listing and unpacking.
5. Stops Spotify (`SPOT_KILL`) again before touching `.spotify`, in case it was started during the download, lists the staged files with `find <dir> -type f`, and renames each over its target on the card (the same file system), making folders as needed; the app's binary goes last, and only when every other file moved, so `.rockbox/rockbox` is the old file or the new one, never part of one, and never new beside a half-moved set. The list becomes `.q2/apps/<id>.files`, then `sync`, then the tag through `blob_io`. Staging is deleted after every install, whatever the outcome.

Every Spotify job starts and ends with `spot_stop` on the UI thread, so spotify.c forgets the librespot it started and Streaming → Spotify starts the new one (or says it is missing).

**Remove** unlinks the app's binary first (a remove cut short still boots Q2 Muse), then each path in `<id>.files` that no other app's list holds (two fonts are in both Rockbox's and the themes' zips), then each folder left empty, up to and including the app's own, then, for a card app (not in `special[]`), its folder whole (`rm -rf .<id>`, with the login and settings it saved there, which no release lists), then the list and tag. So `shelf_sources` refuses a card app whose id names one of the firmware's own card folders (`reserved[]`: `q2`, `q2muse`, `q2pod`, `tidal`, `coverflow`, `downpic`, `sldp`), as it does Spotify's; `test/peq.py` fails when a card folder in `patch/` is missing from it. Before removing anything, `addon_quit` asks a running card app to end and waits for its loop's pid file to go, up to `QUIT_MS` (20 s), so an app saving its login on its TERM has done so before the folder goes; if USB storage has taken the card meanwhile (`card_mounted`), nothing is removed and the job ends in **Can't write to the card**, so the app is still there when the card comes back. ponytail: one still saving after 20 s can write files back, and the card is checked once, so USB storage taking it during the unlinks still ends in removed. Removing Rockbox removes the themes first, after the same check. Removing Spotify stops it and keeps `cache/` and `.cache-size`, which were never installed by it; [Streaming configuration](#streaming-configuration)'s **Erase Spotify Data** runs on this thread as a job too (`shelf_erase`), stops it and deletes those two.

A 500 ms timer refreshes progress and holds standby and auto power-off during app jobs; `sh_wait` joins the worker and reports its result wherever the user is, including after leaving the page.

ponytail: an app's own runtime downloads, if it makes any, and what it runs once installed, are its own: the pin vouches for the zip, not for what the app does. A new app release reaches Q2s only once the maintainer pins and signs it. Cancel stops the download at once, otherwise it lands after the step it was pressed in (the list or API request, the listing or the unpack); once files move it is ignored. A power cut while files move leaves those moved so far beside the old ones, with the old tag and list; the next install starts over. Staging left by a power cut stays on the card until the next install. A release that drops a file leaves the old one on the card and off the new list. The card is FAT32 or exFAT, which hold no symlinks or special files: busybox fails on one, so nothing checks for them.

### Card apps

Every other app in the list is a card app: it installs through the same rows and runs from **Streaming** through one generic host, `patch/addon.c`. It lists up to 8 card folders `.<id>/` (id: 1 to 15 of `a-z0-9-`, since it goes into shell commands) holding `q2app` (`name=`, `search=`, `qr=1`, `goto=1`, `scrobble=0`: see [Scrobbling](#scrobbling); `favdir=`: see Hearts in [Card apps](#card-apps); `stop=0`: no Stop row, see Stop and Retry; `game=1` and `audio=1`: see Card games below), `run` and `q2-<id>`, and optionally `icon.png` (52 px) and `icon-40.png` (40 px), each at most 128 px either way (`ART_MAX`: demo decodes it whole, so a larger one, or one whose size can't be read, is not used): Streaming's row shows the 40 px icon 1:1, else the other scaled down, else the shared `stream_app` (`addon_icon`); under `list.icons.addon_mono` (OLED's) it grays as Streaming's own icons do (`addon_is_icon` in `ringnav_image_add`). The launcher's loop leaves its pid in `/tmp/q2-<id>` and must remove it as it ends; a TERM to it stops the app. Every wait for an app to end (USB storage's `AWAY_MS`, a remove's or update's `QUIT_MS`) ends when the pid file goes, so a loop that leaves it behind costs each wait its full limit. `run` is started with `system()` on the UI thread each time the app starts (`launch`), so it must return at once: anything slow, such as a copy, goes inside the loop it starts in the background (`&`), and it exits straight away when the loop already runs; until it returns, the screen and buttons are frozen, and a minute of that restarts the Q2 ([Watchdog](#watchdog)). `/tmp/q2-<id>.browse.sock` serves the page over Q2SPOT/1, and `/tmp/q2-<id>.state` holds `hold=1` (standby kept off) and the QR page's `addr`, `pin`, `qr`, `qrsize`, `note`, in any order: `poll_one` and the QR page (`qr_refresh`) read its first 1,534 bytes (`QR_RAW`). ponytail: a `hold=` past them reads as 0. USB storage (`usbmode_page_init`'s hook, `addon_card_away`) asks every app to end at once and waits up to `AWAY_MS` (3 s) in all, on the UI thread (ponytail: an app still saving on its TERM after that can write to the card as USB takes it; the fix is to defer stock's USB-mode call until the apps are gone, without sleeping), then starts each again once the card is back. No app starts while the Apps page installs or removes its folder (`shelf_busy`). Its Streaming row opens no page while the folder is being removed or an update's files are moved into place (`shelf_moving`, stage 3 on), or while an update downloads for an app that is not running (its page would be refused as it started): it says "Wait until the App Store finishes", as its Games row does; a running app's page works during the download. A stop removes a pid file whose loop is gone, but it trusts the pid inside: a loop that died without removing it, its pid since reused, would TERM that process (a `flock` in `run` would close this). The QR page draws up to 49 modules (`QR_HEX`).

**Card games.** A card app whose `q2app` holds `game=1` (q2-fidget, named Buddy) has no Streaming row and needs no `run`: `addon_scan` keeps it in its own by-name list, which Library's Games chooser lists after its own four (`addon_games`, `addon_game_name`; `games.c` `pick_card_game`). A row forks and `execl`s `.<id>/q2-<id>` from the card (`addon_game_start`), as Videos' q2video runs, and the game draws on `/dev/fb0` itself while demo runs on: `ringnav_wm_paint` skips the window manager's paint and `ringnav_input` hands every event to `addon_game_input` instead of stock, except Play/Pause and the side buttons (222, 223), down, up and long, which stay stock's media keys under the Games page unless the game has the sound (below). The rest go as text datagrams to `/tmp/q2-<id>.input.sock`: `k d CODE` and `k u CODE` for a key's down and release, `t d X Y`, `t m X Y` and `t u X Y` for a touch, in the 375 × 320 view's pixels (this hook sees the portrait panel's coordinates, before the window manager turns them, so X is the panel's y and Y is 319 less its x; the pointer types `EVT_POINTER_DOWN`, `_MOVE_BEFORE` and `_UP_BEFORE` less one or not, an abort as `u`). `wheel_raw` is set while it runs, and `game_poll` (from `addon_poll`, each UI loop pass) sends the travel gathered since as `w N` (200 a turn, rising anticlockwise). Return held `GAME_HOLD_MS` (700 ms, timed in `game_poll` from its key-down, since stock makes `EVT_KEY_LONG` after this hook) TERMs the game, and one still there `GAME_KILL_MS` (3 s) later is KILLed, as often as it takes. So does `GAME_IDLE_MS` (2 min) without input, unless Smart Awake (`IPOD KEEPLIT`, `ringnav_smart_awake`) is on, which holds it open and lit with no limit (asked once each `GAME_IDLE_MS`); meanwhile `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 1)` holds the screen, standby and auto power-off. Its end (`waitpid` `WNOHANG`) clears `wheel_raw` and repaints the whole window manager. The child gets `Q2_POPUP` (`popup_env`, `games.c`): the theme's pop-up as the Games page draws it, so a game's menus can match ([librespot.md](librespot.md)); it is built before the fork and set with `setenv` in the child alone (demo imports no `execve` or `environ`), after its files are closed. ponytail: a fork while another thread holds libc's environment lock (stock's `toolsSetTimeZone` sets `TZ`) leaves the child waiting in `setenv`, before its exec, until Return's hold ends it; setting it in demo instead would race other threads' `getenv` and change demo's environment. The capability word is `game`. ponytail: the game runs from the card, so USB storage's prompt, under it, can't be answered until it ends; and the screen can't go dark under it, as for a video.

**A game with the sound.** A card game whose `q2app` also holds `audio=1` (q2-groovebox, named Groovebox) owns the audio output while it runs, as a video does. Before the fork `addon_game_start` runs what `video_play` and `video_start` run: `headset_manual`, `spot_yield`, `radio_stop`, `player_stop` (hciplayer holds the PCM even paused) and, for the headphone output, `dac_take` (power, PCM mode, unmuted, the volume). The binary gets q2video's arguments: the output device, `plughw:0,0`, `plug:bluealsa` or `usb` (`output_device`), and on Bluetooth or USB the volume as a second argument (`NN`, or `hNN` to show only), since the DAC's hardware volume is out of those paths and the game applies the soft volume itself; on the jack there is no second argument. The game opens them as q2video does (`video.c` `sound_open`), which the contract in [librespot.md](librespot.md) spells out: `usb` is the card `/proc/asound/cards` lists as USB-Audio, `plughw:N,0`; hciplayer lets go of the PCM, muting the DAC, a moment after the stop, so the open is retried (2 s on the jack, 5 s on Bluetooth and USB, and up to 5 s more at `snd_pcm_set_params` off the jack, since bluealsa claims its PCM there) and, on the jack, `DAC_MUTE` and `DAC_PCM` are cleared through `/dev/shanling_dac` after it, the mute set again when it closes; `hNN` is applied by the DAC, so the game plays at unity; Mono Audio and Swap L/R are `/tmp/q2mono` and `/tmp/q2swap` (an int each), applied to its output as q2video applies them. Play/Pause and the side buttons then reach it as `k d|u 171`, `222` and `223` (stock makes a key's long press after the hook, so none arrives, and no Play-hold action of stock's runs; power-off is Center's hold, which stock still has). A headset's buttons do nothing meanwhile: `media_key` and `media_set_playing` (headset.c) return while `addon_game_audio` says a game has the sound, as otherwise, with video, radio and Spotify all stopped, a headset's Play (AVRCP PLAY, 200 and 207, which `headset_command` sends to `media_set_playing`, not `media_key`) would reach `player_play_pause` with the player stopped and start hciplayer over the game; a pause still passes, Play/Pause's included, for a Spotify a phone resumed meanwhile. Every other start of stock's player meanwhile fails with -1 as a too-long track's does, silently (`ringnav_start_player`, mclStartPlayer's hook: a jack or USB DAC change and a Bluetooth drop come through `player_save_start`), and a headset's link coming up starts nothing (`ringnav_bt_connect_start`, Resume on Connect either way). Stock's `player_save_start(1)` ignores the -1 and still marks the player paused, on nothing, so the game's end stops it when it finds it paused (`game_poll`), and Play then starts the queue as from a stop. A launched card app's first song waits for the game's end (`stream_poll` keeps `S_WAIT`); stock's own steps before the hook (`config_outputchannel`, the volume) still run. `game_poll` zeroes a counting `g_dacoff_time` each pass, as `video_poll` does, so the DAC stays on, and skips the `GAME_IDLE_MS` close: only the game knows whether it is playing, so the idle close is its own (Groovebox ends itself after 5 minutes stopped and untouched). Return's hold still ends it. Music stays stopped when it ends, as after a video, and the DAC powers off on stock's count. Standby needs the screen dark, which a game keeps lit, so nothing else changes; `media_playing` does not count a game. The capability word is `audio`. Home's Shortcut can open such a game by id (`addon_game_open`, -1 when no card game has the id, which `home_shortcut_open` toasts as not on the card, or as unable to start from it when the binary is there without its `q2app`'s `game=1` or a slot; a failed fork toasts as a failed exec does: Groovebox, [Home](ipod.md#home)). ponytail: a headset's Play could be forwarded as a datagram instead of ignored; a live volume change while it runs is not mirrored (Videos' `video_sync` does that), the game has its own volume gesture; a Spotify a phone resumes meanwhile opens its own PCM beside the game's, as beside a video's.

**Go to on a card app's song.** The hold menu's Go to Album and Go to Artist (`qm_goto`) on a song under `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/` first ask `addon_goto`: when that app's `q2app` holds `goto=1` (the app rewrites the line from its own setting; `goto=0` hides the rows again, as below), its page opens with the Q2SPOT/1 level `goto` (`album` or `artist`, then the song's path) as its first level, titled by the record's album or artist tag (`card_tags` fills the playing song's), and the app answers with that album's or artist's own level; More… keeps both arguments, and Back from it closes the page as from a menu. An app page already open (the song played from it) is closed first, as Coverflow's scoped page (`closed` then `window_manager_close_window_force`); `closed` ignores the late destroy of a page it no longer holds. An app not yet scanned this boot is scanned for its name. A song in an app's folder whose app doesn't have `goto=1` (Tidal's downloads too) has no Go to rows (`addon_goes`): the Library never scans those hidden folders, so stock's pages would be empty. `goto` in `/tmp/q2-addon.caps` tells an app the firmware has it. Checks in `test/patch.py`: the request and its title, More…, Back, the replaced page and its late destroy, and no page for an app without `goto=1`, a song outside a card folder or an id that can't be one.

**Tags.** A card app's songs come from its folder's listing (`card_songs`, `toolsLoadDirectory`) or an `.m3u`, which read no tags, and play as a library queue (`0xf001`). `player_get_id3info` parses only a folder play's file (`MCL_TYPE` 1) and copies any other queue's record into `g_play_id3_info`, so such a song read as its file name by an Unknown artist. `card_tags`, from `ringnav_id3_path` as each song starts, gives the playing record (`queue_now`, its path the parsed one, under `/mnt/mmc/`, no album yet, not a CUE track, whose tags are its sheet's) and the parsed tags its file's title, artist, album and album artist, and the record its track and disc, read as the library scan reads them (`toolsGetMusicInfo`): one TagLib open as a song starts, once a queue, since the record then has its album; a song on the card without an album tag played from a list (Shuffle Songs, Most Played) is read at each start, as stock reads every folder play's. A song without tags keeps its record's. A song a playlist session queues from an app's own folder (a path under `/mnt/mmc/.`: the Stream Cache, never the user's synced albums), and the song a Next waits for, are named before they play by `card_record_tags`: the server row's title, album, artist and album artist when the catalogue knows the download (`catalogue_copy_tags`, by `cat_copy_of`: no file read, and a song not there yet is named), else its file's tags when the file is there, so Up Next and Now Playing read "Take It Easy", Eagles, not q2-subsonic's file name, the title in lower case and the server's id (the device, 2026-11-17 23:51, a radio's Up Next). A record with an album is left. Streamed songs land one at a time, so this is one TagLib open per song as it joins. ponytail: Up Next shows a card app's synced songs (in its folders at the card's root) not yet played by their file names, and holding a song in an app's list has no Go to rows (Now Playing's has); reading a whole folder when it's queued froze the UI for seconds on a few hundred songs. A queued row's cover is its server row's album cover (`catalogue_cover`) or Cover Flow's of its album: with Local Only, or an album whose cover the app has not fetched yet, it is the placeholder.

**Sleep timers.** An app's `/tmp/q2-<id>.sleep` (q2-podcasts' Sleep Timer) holds `until <time>` (seconds since the epoch) or `end`; `sleep_read`, in the app's poll, takes a new request (its contents hashed per slot), and its removal by the app cancels the one it set. Q2 Muse keeps the timer, so it fires once the app has stopped too: `until` is kept as the time left on the boot clock (`boot_s`, `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`), which counts Standby and doesn't move when Wi-Fi sets the clock (stock's NTP), so neither shifts it (a time already past pauses at once; no digits, more than 11, anything after them, or more than a week away, `SLEEP_MAX_S`, is dropped without pausing; a time the Q2 slept through by more than `SLEEP_LATE_S`, a minute, is let go without pausing). `end` waits on the track playing (its place, `MCL_POS`) and follows its elapsed time and length (`player_playtime_and_length`, a pass reading -1 between tracks skipped) every pass: ending by itself (`mclNextSong`'s automatic call, counted in `auto_nexts` by `ringnav_next`, so a VBR file whose length is overstated still counts) or leaving its last `SLEEP_END_S` (2 s) for another place pauses, the next track waiting at its start, and so does starting over in place (repeat one); a move from anywhere else (another track picked, Next, a seek back) waits for that track's end instead, since stock refills the same deque for a new queue (`mclLoadPlayList`), so a pick and Next look alike. A length unknown counts any move on as the end. The player stopped for `SLEEP_STOP_MS` (3 s, as Tidal's: stock reports stopped between tracks for a moment), or another one taking playback (`media_owner`), lets it go. `sleep_check`, every `addon_poll`, pauses with `media_set_playing(0)` (whatever owns playback: the local player, Spotify, radio or a video) and removes the file, the app's sign the timer is over. One timer at a time: the latest request, from any app, replaces the one before; another app's removes the earlier one's file. `sleep` in `/tmp/q2-addon.caps` tells an app the firmware has it. Checks in `test/patch.py`: a timer before and at its time, canceled, already due, slept through, the clock set a day on, a bad or far-off time, a time replaced by `end`, and `end` at the next track, at a natural end before the length's last seconds, at repeat one, after another track picked and a seek back, and at a stop.

## Car remote

Settings > Car Remote lets a phone (the q2-auto-remote Android Auto app) browse the library, start songs and lists, and follow Now Playing while the Q2 plays into the car. The protocol is coda-rc ([remote-protocol](remote-protocol.md), `remote/coda-rc.proto`); this section is how the Q2 serves it.

**Two halves.** The protocol runs in `coda-rc` (`/usr/bin/coda-rc`, `patch/coda_rc.c`, `coda_rc_core.c`, `coda_rc_lib.c`, `coda_rc_ble.c`, `coda_rc_mdns.c`, with Monocypher), a program of its own built by `compile_helper` (`tools/build.py` `CODA_RC_SOURCES`) against the rootfs's libc, SQLite and libdbus. Nothing of it is in demo's payload, so its parser, sessions, keys and buffers cost neither the payload's code room nor its scratch state, and a network-facing service is not in the UI process. demo keeps a shim (`patch/coda_rc_shim.c`, `coda_rc_poll` in `ringnav_sleep`, paced to 500 ms), whose state is a few words: it does what only demo can, and talks to the daemon through files in `/tmp`.

**Off means off.** The switch (`Q2POD CARREMOTE`, 0 by default) is the only thing that starts the daemon: the shim starts it on the first poll after boot when the switch is on (no init script, so the emulator, which runs no init scripts, behaves as a Q2), starts it when the switch goes on, starts it again if it has died (at most every 30 s), and kills it (`/tmp/coda-rc.pid`) when the switch goes off. The daemon runs at nice 19. Off, no port is open and nothing advertises. On, it keeps Smart Wi-Fi from turning the radio off ([Smart Wi-Fi](#smart-wi-fi)), as AirPlay on does.

**Discovery.** While Wi-Fi has an address, `coda_rc_mdns.c` answers mDNS for `_q2muse._tcp` (the records are [remote-protocol: Discovery](remote-protocol.md#discovery)), so Q2 Muse Remote's Wi-Fi tab lists the Q2. It is one socket more in the daemon's poll, no thread: once a second `mdns_poll` reads `wlan0`'s address (`SIOCGIFADDR`), and every 5 s the Bluetooth name from config.ini (`BTNAME`, checked as `bt_name_valid` checks it); a new address or name says goodbye to the old records, closes the socket and opens one on the new address, which announces twice a second apart. A socket the kernel refuses is tried again on a new address or after 30 s (`MDNS_RETRY_MS`), with one log line each time. The socket binds 5353 with `SO_REUSEADDR`, beside shairport's own responder (built into stock's AirPlay receiver, which offers no registration) and librespot's, and joins 224.0.0.251 on that address. `IP_MULTICAST_IF` is not required: qemu-user 8.2 refuses it in every form (EADDRNOTAVAIL, a MIPS probe under the emulator's qemu, 2026-11-17), and without it sends follow the route, which on a Q2 is `wlan0`. `mdns_query` and `mdns_reply` are the packet half, pure and bounds-checked: names are read with compression pointers that may only point back, at most 255 bytes, and any count, length or pointer past the packet makes it malformed (`test/unit/test_coda_rc_mdns.py`, each packet against an unreadable page). `--mdns-if IF` names another interface (the emulator's: it has no `wlan0`), `--no-mdns` turns it off; the host build answers only with `--mdns-if`.

**Transports.** TCP port 7720, and Bluetooth LE: the daemon registers a GATT application and an advertisement with bluetoothd over D-Bus (`GattManager1`, `LEAdvertisingManager1` on `/org/bluez/hci0`), not through `libSL`. stock starts bluetoothd only while Bluetooth is on, so registration fails while it is off (`ServiceUnknown`, `NameHasNoOwner`): the daemon logs `ble: bluetoothd is not running` once and tries nothing more until bluetoothd appears on the bus (`NameOwnerChanged` with a new owner), then registers 2 s later. Any other refusal is tried again every 30 s. Each failure is logged once, not at every try (`log_once`): Bluetooth off used to add two `refused` lines to the log every 30 s for as long as Car Remote was on. `/tmp/coda-rc.ble` exists while the GATT application and the advertisement both stand (`crc_ble_advertising`), for the Pair a Phone page. On a real Q2 (V1.36's bluetoothd, 2026-11-17) registration is refused even with Bluetooth on: `/org/bluez/hci0` has `Adapter1`, `Media1` and `BatteryProviderManager1` but no `GattManager1` or `LEAdvertisingManager1` (`UnknownMethod`), though the adapter reports the central and peripheral roles, so no phone can find a Q2 over Bluetooth yet and every working session is TCP. One BLE session at a time: StartNotify on the event characteristic or a write from a new device opens it, StopNotify ends it. ponytail: the GATT path has run only against a bus without bluetoothd (the emulator) and a bluetoothd without the GATT interfaces (a Q2); why V1.36's bluetoothd registers neither on `hci0` is open, and everything past registration is for the Q2 test plan ([remote-protocol: Testing on a Q2](remote-protocol.md#testing-on-a-q2)), including whether bluetoothd's D-Bus policy lets it call the daemon's objects, and how LE behaves beside A2DP.

**Security.** Every session authenticates before anything but the handshake is answered, and seals every frame after; pairing needs the code on the Q2's screen ([remote-protocol: Pairing and authentication](remote-protocol.md#pairing-and-authentication)). Keys are in `/mnt/data/coda-rc/peers` (0600, never the card). The schema carries no credentials, settings writes, paths or updates. The daemon validates every length and offset it is sent; SQL takes ids only after `arg_ok` refuses quotes, and search text only as a bound parameter.

**The library** (`coda_rc_lib.c`). Each request opens `/mnt/data/database.db` read-only, attaches `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod/catalogue.db` when Library is Local + Server, builds two temporary views over `songtable` (and `servertable`, joined to `servermeta` for its lengths: the two share column names such as `track`, so each column the view takes from them is named by its table), answers and closes, so no lock or schema outlives a request and a rebuilt catalogue (renamed over the old one) is simply opened anew. The tree, its orders and the letter buckets (over 120 entries; a bucket over 500 splits by two, then three letters; year orders by decade) are those of q2-auto-remote's `tools/q2bridge.py`, so the app's `LibraryTree` maps onto it unchanged; titles go out unnumbered, and an album's rows carry their track number in `Item.number` (no other row does), which the app shows as q2bridge's "N • Title". After Folders the Library level lists **Favorites** (`favorites`: the songs in stock's `myfav`, five hearts, by path, in the tracks' orders) and **Recently Added** (`recent`: the `RECENT_CAP`, 100, songs with the latest `time_create`, newest first, never lettered), advertised as `CAP_FAVORITES` and `CAP_RECENT` ([remote-protocol](remote-protocol.md#favorites-and-recently-added)). An id whose list comes out empty answers NOT_FOUND, except a playlist that exists, Favorites and the top folder; the bucketing needs SQLite's window functions, which the rebuilt SQLite 3.54.1 has ([third-party](third-party.md)). Ids: `song:t<id>` for a card song, `song:c<id>` for a server one (the catalogue's ids start at `0x40000000`), `album:` with the folder's FNV-1a hash or the server album's id. Lengths come from Long Songs' cache (`ringnav-durations-v1`, [Song durations](#song-durations)) and the catalogue's `servermeta`. A cover is Cover Flow's 160 px cache file when the phone asks for 160 px or less, else the server app's cover (its 512 px `covers/512/<album>.jpg` for an ask over 160 px when the app has fetched it, else its 160 px one: a 160 px cover looked soft in the car's ~350 px art box, 2026-11-16; the Q2's own screens keep the 160 px ones, as its rows hand the file to AWTK, which decodes it whole on the UI thread into its image cache, 1 MiB a cover at 512 px against 100 KiB at 160), a picture in the folder, or the first FLAC's embedded picture, sent in pieces of up to 4 KB. A playlist row's art is its first song's album's, except a server playlist's (`cat.serverlists`) once its app has its cover, `covers/pl-<pid>.jpg` (Navidrome's collage, [server-library: Covers](server-library.md#covers)): then its art id is `p<pid>` (`plart`, a SQL function that looks for the file, so a playlist whose cover is not fetched yet keeps its first album's), and `GetCover` for it finds the app by `pid` in `cat.serverlists` and sends that file (`pl_cover_find`); a name with `/`, an app id over 15 characters or a pid over 46 has no such art. ponytail: `norm` folds ASCII case only, and the Library's scope markers (`q2-library-scope`) are not applied; both as q2bridge.py does.

**Now Playing out.** The shim writes `/tmp/coda-rc.now` (`key=value` lines: play state, position, length, the song's id, path and tags, shuffle, repeat, volume, the song's hearts, the queue's place, length and version) whenever any of it changes, so once a second while playing, through `blob_io`'s rename. The toast the Q2 Muse showed last is in it for 4 s (`note`, and `noten` counting them; `coda_rc_note`, from `toast`). Its song is the queue's at `MCL_POS`, or a server song pressed and not yet the player's (`catalogue_np_now`), from the press, as Now Playing shows it. On a queue change (its deque, its length or `playback_loads`) it writes `/tmp/coda-rc.queue`, the queue's song ids (a song with no library record, a card app's stream download, also its path, title and artist after tabs), with the place it had then; GetQueue answers the place from `/tmp/coda-rc.now` instead while both name the same queue version, since the queue file is not written again when only the place moves. The daemon reads the file whenever one of the shim's files is renamed into `/tmp` (an inotify watch, `IN_MOVED_TO`, in its `poll`) and pushes what changed to subscribed sessions, the position once a second while playing; its `poll` otherwise sleeps until the next thing falls due (`wait_ms`: the second's tick, mDNS's next look or announcement, the next position push for a phone that follows it, held-back bytes, a command's `ACK_MS`), at most `TICK_MS` (1 s), where it woke every 250 ms. demo's side still looks for the daemon's files every `CR_POLL_MS` (500 ms) on its UI pass, which adds no wakeup of its own: a socket from demo would need the phones' authentication, or one of its own, so the files stay. ponytail: the queue is listed in the deque's order, so under Shuffle its rows are not the play order; up to 5000 are listed.

**Commands in.** Every command goes to the shim, which runs it inside demo. Play, Pause and Play/Pause (`resume`, `pause`, `toggle`), Next and Previous are `media_key`'s, a headset button's ([Headset controls](#headset-controls-and-volume)): they reach whatever plays without passing through a window, since the window in front may take a press of the Q2's own button for itself: a toast's `msginfo_dialog_on_keyup` stops Play/Pause, the wheel's steps and the skip buttons while it is up ("Pixel 10 Pro paired" just after a pairing), and OLED's Shuffle confirmation (`feedback_shuffled`) closes on any key and stops it, for its 1.2 s after a shuffled list starts. Pause and Play press only when the player is not already as asked, and are answered once `media_playing` shows it, or refused after 3 s (`CR_SETTLE_MS`), so an Ack is the player's state, not a press sent. The daemon logs each Transport (`transport <verb>: state ...`) and the shim's answer (`demo: <verb> done` or `not done`) in `/tmp/coda-rc.log`. Playing a list: the daemon writes the list's song ids to `/tmp/coda-rc.list` and `<seq> play <index> <shuffle> <count>` to `/tmp/coda-rc.cmd`; the shim, on a timer (play_folder opens a window), matches the ids against the whole library's records (`staged(songs_unsorted)`, sorted by `REC_ID`), plays them with `play_folder(…, 0xf001)` or `shuffle_play`, and answers `<seq> 0` in `/tmp/coda-rc.ack` (2 while a scan, a card game's sound or USB mode holds it off: the phone gets UNAVAILABLE). Seek is `player_seek_time`; volume is set as AirPlay's is, up to Volume Limit and saved for the output in use. `mode <shuffle> <repeat>` (SetMode, -1 for a mode left alone) goes where the Q2 Muse keeps the pair: while playback.c's extended play runs (`playback_active`), `playback_set`, as the hold menu's Shuffle and Repeat rows ([Queue menu](#queue-menu)), mapped to the nearest Q2 mode; otherwise Now Playing's buttons' `np_mode_set` (`np_bar.c`: stock's `MCL_MODE` and `[IPOD] NPSHUFONE`/`NPREPOFF`), so their icons follow (`cr_mode`). Now Playing out reads the pair from the same place (`cr_modes`: `playback_option` while active, else `np_mode_shuffle`/`np_mode_repeat`). Before, the shim read and set only playback.c's pair, which plays only while active, so a mode changed on the Q2 Muse never reached the car and the car's never moved the Q2 Muse's buttons (2026-11-16). `radio <record id>` (0 the playing song) and `radio stop` are StartRadio's, run on a timer as play's, through `song_radio_car` ([Radio](#radio)). `rate <hearts> <song id>` is `rate_car` (`ratings.c`): the picker's own `rate_song`, through Now Playing's heart click while that page is open so its heart follows, else batch-select's Add to My Fav or `deleteMusicFromFav` as the queue menu's Favorites rows; the hearts go out in `/tmp/coda-rc.now` (`rate_car_hearts`, -1 for a stream), read again on a new song, a My Fav change made here (`catalogue_fav_gen`) or every 5 s, since stock's lists change My Fav without telling. `jump <index> <song id>` plays a queue entry as Up Next's row does (`player_start_queue`, after `press_stamp`, refused while Headphones required forbids it); the playing entry plays on. Rate and jump check the song id first and answer 3 when it is not there, which the daemon sends as NOT_FOUND. Resume ([remote-protocol](remote-protocol.md#modes-rating-the-queue-resume-and-radio)) is the daemon's alone: the shim writes Now Playing before a Play's ack, so the daemon has the new queue's version, and from the ack on, while that version plays, it keeps the list's song in `/mnt/data/coda-rc/places`, rewritten on each song change (the first song at the ack itself, so a list left within a second still has its place).

<a id="car-remote-streams"></a>**A streaming song.** A card app's song streamed without an offline copy plays from its download, `/mnt/mmc/.<app>/stream/<account>/<quality>/<x>/<title> [<sid>].<suffix>` (`x` a hex digit of the sid's hash), with no library record: the shim's id is 0 and its title the file's name (the Q2 Muse's own Now Playing reads the file's tags).
