The daemon's `np_stream` (`coda_rc.c`) looks the path up once per song with `lib_stream_song` (`coda_rc_lib.c`): `stream_sid` takes the sid from the name's last brackets (letters, digits, `-` and `_` only) and the app from the path (`stream_path_sid`, `patch/stream_path.h`, which the payload's `cat_copy_of` reads the same paths with: on the Q2 itself such a download is its server row for the cover, the play key, the hearts and the info page's genre and year), and the catalogue's `servermeta` row for that sid and app, joined to `servertable` by `fileurl`, gives the song id (`song:c<id>`), title, artist, album, length and the album's art id (`akey` of the row's `cat/<album>/` path). NowPlaying carries those, the length only while the player reports none (a stream's is 0 until it has downloaded), and `rateable` from the shim's hearts: Rate takes the server song's id and sends the shim the record's, 0, which it compares, and `rate_car` rates the download through its catalogue row as Now Playing's heart does (`ratings.c` `rate_fav`, `catalogue_song_key`). `cover_find` for a server album with no `covers/<album>.jpg` tries `stream_picture`: each of the album's sids, `glob`bed in `/mnt/mmc/.<app>/stream/*/*/*/*[<sid>].*` (any account, quality and shard folder), and the first FLAC picture found (the user's screenshot, 2026-11-16 14:34: Android Auto showed `hello [VcF5XCDqrNB23RlHx35Z0w].flac`, no artist, 0:00 and no cover; reproduced with the build's coda-rc under qemu-user). ponytail: the cover needs Library on Local + Server (the art id is looked up in the songs view, which holds server albums only then); and the player switches to a stream only once it has downloaded (about 6.7 s for a 20 MB FLAC).

**Pairing on the Q2.** While `/tmp/coda-rc.pair` holds a code, the shim asks on the [pairing card](oled-design.md#pairing) (`patch/pair_prompt.c` `pair_prompt`, the confirm card's): "Pair with Pixel 8?", the code in two groups of three, "Enter this code in Q2 Muse Remote", and Cancel, which with Return or the daemon's 120 s (`CRC_PAIR_TIMEOUT_MS`, the card's bar) writes `/tmp/coda-rc.pair-cancel`. It closes when the daemon removes the file, and `/tmp/coda-rc.pair-end` says whether to toast the phone's name and "paired" ("Pixel 8 paired", `carremote_paired`, with Positive's check-circle; it closes How to Connect too) or "Pairing failed". Guest Play's guest asks on the same card (`guest_ui.c` `ask_card`); `confirm_t`'s `glyph` puts the phone over its title, and a title wider than the card's text column scrolls in it (`card_title`: the house marquee's hold, speed, gap and faded ends, a 33 ms frame timer while the card is up). A file holding another code than the card shows (the daemon ended one code and showed the next between two of the shim's polls) closes the card, and the next poll opens it on the new code (`cr_pairing`, `cr.pair_code`). The code outlives its phone's connection: a session that closes while pairing leaves the code and the card up (`pair_leave` in `coda_rc_core.c`), and a `PairStart` from the same client name within the code's 120 s gets that code again, so a phone that reconnects while the user types is not handed a new one; a wrong code, Cancel, the 120 s or another phone's `PairStart` ends it ([remote-protocol: Pairing](remote-protocol.md#pairing-a-pake-on-the-6-digit-code)). <a id="car-remote-settings"></a>**Settings > Car Remote** (`patch/carremote_page.c`, `carremote_page`) is the switch, its caption under it while selected; while on, Pair a Phone (the accent's top-action row) and a two-line row per paired phone, or, with none, the empty state with Pair a Phone as its button ([oled-design: Car Remote](oled-design.md#car-remote)). That button is a row of the page's own list (`K_CTA`, row 1 after a gap that keeps it under the empty state's words as the switch grows and shrinks; `empty_state` keeps its place but gets no row of its own), painted with `ui_cta_paint` and marked `_rings_itself`, so `paint_selection` draws no bar behind it. Its row reaches only as far past the capsule as the focus ring (`CR_CTA_OUT`, 5 px: the ring's 2 px, 3 px out), so under the switch its foot (y 280) stays inside OLED's list end (282) and the wheel moving on to it scrolls nothing; a foot past the list end by a pixel has `reveal` scroll it and `fit_top` take the list on to the row's top, the switch gone (the user's device, 2026-11-16, with an 8 px band, reproduced on the emulator). The ring (`ui_kit.c` `cta_ring`) is two images for its round ends, `tools/art.py` `cta_ring_end`'s annulus between radii 24 and 22 at 16 x 16 samples a pixel in the half's Text Primary (`ctaring_l_d`, `ctaring_r_l` and so on), and two whole rows of ink along its top and foot between them, so its arcs are graded as smoothly as the capsule's own edge. The row-at-a-time `round_ring` is kept for a set without those images (anti-aliased at any radius, [Rounded corners](#rounded-corners)); before `corner_cover.c` it had no coverage table for radii 24 and 23 and drew them in hard one-pixel steps, the jagged ring the user saw; two one-pixel `canvas_stroke_rounded_rect` pills still stepped unevenly where the strokes met at 6x (the user, 2026-11-16). As the empty state's own list it sat beside the page's, each holding a selection, and `surface_under` gives the wheel no surface when two do: the wheel moved nothing and the switch showed no bar (emulator, 2026-11-16). It reads three files the daemon writes. The peers file gives each phone's id, name and pairing time; `/tmp/coda-rc.online` holds a 9-byte record per authenticated session, the peer id and its link (0 Wi-Fi, TCP; 1 Bluetooth, BLE), written whenever that set changes (`online_poll`) and removed when the daemon stops; `/mnt/data/coda-rc/seen` holds a 12-byte record per paired phone, its id and the wall clock (u32 LE) when a session of it last authenticated or ended (`seen_stamp`, written only when a phone comes or goes, so the flash is not worn; a phone no longer paired is dropped). A row says "Connected over Wi-Fi" (with the Positive dot) or "Not connected · last seen Friday" (today, yesterday, a weekday within the week, else the date; nothing after "Not connected" for a phone not seen since this firmware or a clock never set). Its rows sit at their own heights: the list's `item_height` is 0 and stock's layout stacks them (`cr_fit`), the switch growing for its caption while selected, 10 px before Pair a Phone. Before this, `page_list`'s `item_height` forced every row to the one-line 32 px, so a phone's 52 px row lost its second line (Connected or Not connected) to its row's foot or to the next phone (the user's screenshot, 2026-11-16, reproduced on the emulator). Centre on a phone opens its page (`carphone_page`): Status, Paired (the date), Last Connected (Now while connected), Rename, then Forget Phone in red after a 12 px gap; it opens on Rename. The count each page hands `ringnav_select` is the rows the wheel stops on, the gaps passed (`collect`), so Forget Phone is row 4 and Pair a Phone row 1: a count with a gap in it does not match ringnav's own at its next load, which then drops the selection (`nav/lists.c` `load`), and the phone's page opened on Status that way (emulator, 2026-11-16). Rename is the letter strip (`search_strip_text`), which rewrites the record's name in the peers file; the name is the Q2 Muse's alone (the phone's own is unchanged). Forget asks on the confirmation card, Cancel first, then rewrites the peers file without that phone and closes the page; the daemon closes the phone's sessions within a second. Pair a Phone opens `carhowto_page`: the steps for the one link a phone can find this Q2 Muse on now (`cr_howto_mode`), in Q2 Muse Remote's own words, then what they need. Q2 Muse Remote's Bluetooth tab finds a Q2 Muse only by its advertisement, and its Wi-Fi address tab by the daemon's mDNS (above) or the address typed, so: while the daemon advertises (`g_bluetoothflag` and `/tmp/coda-rc.ble`; the flag so a killed daemon's file is not believed), "Pair a Q2 Muse > Bluetooth", "Pick Q2 Muse, then tap Next", with the Wi-Fi address besides; else, with a Wi-Fi address (`SIOCGIFADDR` on `wlan0`), "Pair a Q2 Muse > Wi-Fi address", "Pick Q2 Muse, then tap Next" (the Bluetooth name, under which the Wi-Fi tab lists it), the address for a phone that does not list it, and "Phone and Q2 Muse on one Wi-Fi" (the app's port, 7720, is coda-rc's, so no port is shown); with neither, "Open Settings > Wi-Fi", "Join the Wi-Fi your phone is on", "Come back here to pair", and no "Waiting for a phone". Bluetooth on is not enough for the Bluetooth steps: on a Q2 whose bluetoothd refuses the registration (above) they could not work. Each poll hashes the mode and the address (`cr_howto_sum`) and paints the page again when they change, so Bluetooth or Wi-Fi coming on turns the steps at once. The Q2 Muse cannot start a pairing (the phone sends `PairStart`), so the page only says how; it closes when a phone pairs, and the toast names the phone ("Pixel 10 Pro paired", with the Positive check). ponytail: no QR code on that page until Q2 Muse Remote can scan one. While a page is open each poll hashes the three files and the switch (`cr_read`) and rebuilds the page when the hash changes (`carremote_poll`, from the shim's poll), the selection kept on its row, so a pairing, a Forget, a rename, a connection or a disconnect shows within half a second.

## 2038

The rootfs is glibc 2.28 on 32-bit MIPS, so stock's `time_t` is 32 bits, and the root certificates in `assets/scrobble-ca.pem` expire between 2035 and 2046.

**TLS.** Every verified libcurl handle (Network Update, Q2 Shelf, Internet Radio, scrobbling, lyrics and covers, Tidal Downloads, and stock's own HTTPS through `ringnav_stock_tls`) checks the server's chain against its CA file and its name, but no certificate's dates: the rootfs's libcurl does its TLS with an mbedTLS built without `MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME_DATE` ([third-party](third-party.md#curl-and-mbedtls)), so a chain still verifies after its roots expire (2035 on) and after the 32-bit clock wraps, and a Q2 whose clock was never set still connects. ponytail: an expired or retired server certificate is accepted too, and there is no revocation check. That is the price of working with a firmware nobody can update. hciplayer's streams are the exception: they do their TLS with the OpenSSL 1.0.1 linked into the player, which checks certificate dates ([Stock HTTPS](#stock-https)).

**Clock.** Linux 5.10 keeps 64-bit time, and glibc 2.28's `time()` truncates it to 32 bits. `wall_time` reads that unsigned, which is right until 2106. Scrobble timestamps use it. The iPod status bar takes it back in 28-year steps, a span over which dates and weekdays repeat, before stock's 32-bit `localtime`, which is right until 2100. ponytail: stock code stays 32-bit. Its clock screens and its network time sync (`ntpdate`, then `hwclock -wu`) will show or write wrong dates after January 2038, and NTP's 2036 era rollover depends on stock's `ntpdate`. Stock's own HTTPS calls go through the same libcurl, so they check no dates either, all but hciplayer's streams, which do ([Stock HTTPS](#stock-https)). Card apps' folder poll (`addon.c`) compares a 32-bit `st_mtime` with `time()`; both wrap together, so only the second of the wrap misjudges a change. librespot carries its own fix (DiamondBond/q2-librespot).
